L01.text: The flight to San Antonio leaves at fourteen fifteen, not at four fifteen.

L02.text: Only fifteen students passed the first test, but fifty passed the second one.

L03.text: How long have you been stationed at this base?

L04.text: Are you coming to the briefing at zero eight hundred?
I wouldn't miss it for the world.

L05.text: Excuse me, where can I get my ID card renewed?
At the personnel office. It's on the second floor of Building Four, next to the post office.

L06.text: Before you clean your weapon, make sure it is unloaded.

L07.text: Would you mind closing the window?

L08.text: Why didn't Sergeant Lopez come to physical training this morning?
He hurt his ankle playing basketball yesterday.

L09.text: The new truck is heavier than the old one, but it uses less fuel.

L10.text: It was a piece of cake.

L11.text: The meeting has been moved from Tuesday to Thursday, at the same time.

L12.text: Can I give you a hand with those boxes?

L13.text: Are you driving to Dallas this weekend?
I was going to, but my car is in the shop, so I'll take the bus.

L14.text: We need two boxes of paper for each classroom, and there are six classrooms.

L15.text: I think the new schedule is much better.

L16.text: If it rains tomorrow, the field exercise will start an hour later.

L17.text: How often do you have English class?

L18.text: It's on the shelf, behind the first aid kit.

L19.text: The jacket was eighty dollars, but I got it for half price.

L20.text: Did the captain approve your leave request?

L21.text: The patient should take one tablet every eight hours.

L22.text: I'm afraid the library is closed until further notice.

L23.text: Do you know what time the dining facility opens?

L24.text: Almost. I just need to check the figures one more time.

L25.text: Private Kim arrived after the formation had already started.

L26.text: I'm not sure I can finish this by Friday.

L27.text: Go straight for two blocks, then turn left at the gas station. The clinic is on your right.

L28.text: Is Lieutenant Brown in her office?
She just stepped out. She'll be back in ten minutes.

L30.text: It's supposed to be cold and windy this afternoon, so bring your field jacket.

L31.text: The bus to the airport leaves every twenty minutes. The next one is at ten forty.

L32.text: Could you tell me where the nearest ATM is?

L33.text: Sergeant Diaz used to smoke, but he quit last year.

L34.text: Should I wear my dress uniform to the ceremony?
Yes. And make sure your shoes are polished.

L35.text: I've been waiting for over an hour, and the mechanic still hasn't called me.

L36.text: Hand in your homework on Monday at the latest.

L37.text: Do you want to eat at the dining facility or go off base?
Let's stay here. It's raining too hard to drive.

L38.text: The training was supposed to last three weeks, but it was extended by one more week.

L40.text: The colonel wants the plan by noon.
Then we'd better get the ball rolling.

L41.text: The store is open from nine to five on weekdays, and from ten to two on Saturdays. It's closed on Sundays.

L43.text: I'd have called you if I had known you were in town.

L44.text: How far is the firing range from here?

L45.text: I can't find the keys to the supply room.
Did you check the drawer of my desk? I usually leave them there.

L46.text: Everyone except the new students has to attend the safety briefing.

L48.text: The temperature dropped from seventy degrees to forty degrees overnight.

L49.text: Have you ever been to New York?

L50.text: I heard you got promoted. Congratulations!
Thanks. I can hardly believe it myself.

L51.text: Please report to the orderly room at zero seven thirty.

L52.text: Why don't we take a break?

L53.text: Did you get the email about the new duty roster?
I haven't checked my email since this morning.

L54.text: Neither the captain nor the sergeant was at the meeting.

L55.text: Can you cover my shift on Saturday?
Sorry, my hands are tied. I'm on duty all weekend.

L56.text: The convoy leaves the base at twenty-two hundred, and the drive to the port takes four hours.

L58.text: Daylight saving time ended last night. Did you set your watch back an hour?
Oh no. It completely slipped my mind.

L59.text: Attention, please. The eleven forty train to Washington will leave from Track Six today, not from Track Two. Because of work on the tracks, the train is running about fifteen minutes behind schedule. We apologize for the delay.

L60.text: I get thirty days of leave a year, and so far I've taken ten in June and eight in August.

L61.text: Did you make it to the finance office before it closed?

L62.text: My flight gets in at nine forty tonight. Could you pick me up at the airport?
Sure, but I'm on duty until ten. Is ten thirty all right? I'll meet you outside baggage claim.
That's fine. It always takes a while to get my bags anyway.

L63.text: The hotel costs a hundred and twenty dollars a night, but the travel office will only pay ninety.
So I'll have to pay the difference myself.

L64.text: Out here, fresh water is delivered every other day, and the last delivery came yesterday.

L65.text: My overtime pay finally came in, three months late. Can you believe it?

L66.text: Did you catch your flight to Chicago last night?
Yes, but I got to the gate in the nick of time.

L67.text: The mail room called. Your package is there, and you have to pick it up before sixteen thirty today.
It's sixteen ten already, and it's a fifteen-minute walk. I'd better go now.
Hurry. I'll answer your phone while you're gone.

L68.text: We ordered ninety sleeping bags, but only seventy came in this morning. The rest will come next week.

L69.text: Hi, this is Sergeant Delgado from the transportation office, calling about your move. The movers can't come on Thursday after all. They'll pick up your household goods on Friday morning instead, starting at eight. Please call me back today to confirm that Friday works for you.

L70.text: How much is a round-trip ticket to Boston?

L71.text: So the cargo plane lands at zero seven hundred, and we finish unloading by noon?
Exactly. I'm glad we're on the same page.

L72.text: The ferry has been delayed by two and a half hours, so it won't leave until seventeen hundred.

L73.text: Captain Brennan, I'd like to take leave from the tenth to the twentieth of next month.
We have an inspection on the eighteenth. Can you be back before then?
Yes, sir. I'll change my form so I return on the seventeenth.

L75.text: It's already nineteen thirty, and all the equipment is packed for tomorrow.
Great. Then let's call it a day.

L76.text: Good evening, everyone. Tomorrow we move to the training area. Breakfast is from zero four thirty to zero five fifteen, and the buses leave from behind Building Nine at zero five thirty sharp. The drive takes about two hours, and the first exercise begins as soon as we arrive.

L77.text: The tires we ordered were delivered on Monday, the day before yesterday.

L78.text: Everyone's waiting for you at the restaurant. How soon can you get here?

L79.text: How many trucks do we need to take forty-eight tents out to the field?
Each truck holds twelve, so four. But the motor pool can only give us three until Thursday.
Then one of them will have to make two trips.

L80.text: It's almost five o'clock. Can you still send me the delivery schedule today?
Sorry, I can't. I'll send it first thing in the morning.

L81.text: This truck is supposed to get an oil change every three thousand miles, and it's gone almost five thousand since the last one.

L82.text: Do I need an appointment for sick call, or can I just walk in?

L83.text: Have they fixed the washing machines in the barracks yet?
Two of them are still out of order, so you might have to wait.

L84.text: Good morning. Here is today's weather for the base. Thick fog will stay with us until about ten o'clock, so drive slowly and use your low beams. This afternoon will be sunny and warm, with a high of seventy-eight degrees. Thunderstorms will move in after nine tonight, so put away any loose equipment before you go home.

L85.text: We've run out of toner for the printer, and the new order won't arrive until Thursday.

L86.text: I need a vehicle this afternoon to bring twenty boxes of uniforms back from the warehouse.
Take the pickup, then, and throw a tarp over the boxes. They're calling for rain later on.
Really? It's so sunny now. All right, I'll grab one from the supply room.

L87.text: How was the food at the new dining facility?

L88.text: You look pale. Are you all right?
I'm a little under the weather, that's all.

L89.text: Unless you've completed the safety course, you're not allowed to drive the forklift.

L90.text: Who's in charge of the office while Major Ramirez is away?

L91.text: How much do I owe you for the coffee and the muffin?

L92.text: Sergeant Miller, the doctor at sick call gave me a note. I'm supposed to rest in my room until tomorrow.
All right. Drop the note off at the orderly room on your way back, and I'll tell the platoon.
Yes, Sergeant. I'll go there right now.

L93.text: My computer is at the help desk for repairs, so I'll be using Sergeant Haddad's until Friday.

L94.text: Listen up. Before you start work in the motor pool today, here are three safety rules. Wear your gloves and safety glasses at all times on the shop floor. Never stand under a vehicle that is held up only by a jack. And if you see fuel or oil on the floor, clean it up right away or report it to me.

L95.text: What's the weather supposed to be like this weekend?

L96.text: The neighbors had another loud party last night. It went on until two in the morning.
That's the last straw. I'm going to talk to the building manager today.

L97.text: While the kitchen is being painted, lunch will be served in the gym instead of the dining facility.

L98.text: Any news on our order for the new radios?
Bad news, I'm afraid. The supply office lost the paperwork, so it was never sent.
So we're back to square one. I'll fill out the forms again this afternoon.

L99.text: You've already signed for your room key, haven't you?

L100.text: Do you think they'll cancel the outdoor ceremony because of the heat?
I'd be surprised if they did. It's only supposed to be in the low eighties.

L101.text: You must wear hearing protection in the generator room, even if you're only going in for a minute.

L102.text: Hi, this is Specialist Okafor at the supply room. The cold weather boots you ordered have finally come in. You can pick them up any weekday between one and four in the afternoon. Please bring the old pair you're turning in, along with your copy of the order form.

L103.text: Could you keep an eye on the phones while I run down to the mailroom?

L104.text: Can I take the van to the training area this afternoon?
Not unless you want to push it. The battery's dead.

L105.text: Have you heard when we're moving into the new barracks? I was hoping it'd be before winter.
It's still up in the air. The building hasn't passed its final inspection yet.
That's too bad. Let me know as soon as you hear anything.

L106.text: I'd rather study in the library than in my room, because my roommate plays loud music all evening.

L107.text: What did you get on the listening test?

L108.text: Do you know why the soccer game was canceled?
Beats me. The weather is perfect.

L109.text: Listen up. Tomorrow's fitness test will start at zero six hundred on the track behind the gym. You will do push-ups first, then sit-ups, and you will finish with a two-mile run. If you have an injury, report to me before the test begins.

L110.text: The instructor didn't collect the tests until every student had finished.

L111.text: Excuse me, which way is the language lab?

L112.text: I'd like to check out these three books, please.
Sure. You can keep them three weeks, but this one's a reference book. It can't leave the library.
Oh. Then I'll just read it here today.

L113.text: We're getting pizza tonight. Do you want to come?
I'd love to, but I really need to hit the books.

L114.text: The post office is on Oak Street, between the bank and the barber shop, and right across from the bowling alley.

L115.text: How many push-ups can you do in two minutes?

L116.text: Did you finish the ten-mile march, Ramirez?
Yes, but I couldn't keep up with the others.

L117.text: Are you going to the gym after class?
It's closed for repairs until Monday. We could run on the track instead, though.
Good idea. It's open until dark, so let's meet at seventeen hundred.

L118.text: Before the radio class on Friday, every student must know the phonetic alphabet by heart.

L119.text: When you plan a route on a map, look at the scale first. On our training maps, one centimeter equals two hundred fifty meters. As a rule of thumb, a soldier with a full pack covers about four kilometers an hour on a flat road, but much less in the hills. So always add extra time if your route goes uphill.

L121.text: Are you going to apply for the instructor course in Texas?
I already did, but it's a long shot.

L122.text: Unless you score at least seventy on the progress test, you'll have to repeat the unit.

L123.text: Excuse me, where is the education center, and is it far? I don't have a car.
It's Building Twenty-two, a ten-minute walk. Turn right at the flagpole and look for the brick building across from the parking lot.
Great, I'll be there before my placement test at nine.

L124.text: Could you repeat the last question, please?

L126.text: Hello, Corporal Haddad, this is Mister Novak, your reading instructor. Tomorrow's class will be in Room Fourteen instead of Room Four, because the projector in our room is broken. Please tell the other students in your group. See you at zero eight hundred.

L127.text: The gym gets too crowded after seventeen hundred, so I usually work out before breakfast.

L129.text: Where were you? We waited for you for half an hour.
Sorry. I was reading in the library and lost track of time.

L130.text: The map says the bridge is two kilometers north of here.
Are you sure? I thought it was south.
Let me look again. Oh, you're right. I was holding the map upside down.

L131.text: My husband had our son's bicycle fixed at the shop on Pine Street.

L132.text: Captain Haddad is on another line right now. Would you like to hold?

L133.text: Are you going to buy those leather boots you tried on?
I'd like to, but they cost an arm and a leg.

L134.text: Attention, passengers on flight seven twenty-two to Norfolk. The fog is too thick for aircraft to take off safely, so all departures are on hold. We now expect boarding to begin at sixteen fifty, about forty minutes later than planned. Please stay near Gate nine and listen for further announcements.

L135.text: After twenty years at sea, Chief Novak is used to sleeping in a narrow bunk.

L136.text: Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes?

L137.text: Excuse me, my flight to Atlanta was canceled. Is there another one today?
The six forty flight this evening is full, but I can put you on the first flight tomorrow, at six fifteen in the morning.
I guess I don't have much choice. Go ahead and book me on that one.

L138.text: Dinner was great. Let me get the check this time.
That's nice of you, but let's go Dutch tonight.

L139.text: We didn't receive Colonel Okafor's message until our radio was repaired the next morning.

L140.text: Can I pay for this with a credit card?

L141.text: Sorry, I have another call coming in. Can we finish this conversation later?
No problem. Let's touch base tomorrow morning.

L142.text: I'd like to return this sweater. It's too small for my son, but I have no receipt.
Then I can't give you a refund, but you can exchange it for a larger size.
That's fine. It was a gift from my sister.

L143.text: Sergeant Miller isn't answering his phone. He must have left it in his car again.

L144.text: Excuse me, is this the gate for flight five eighteen to Denver?

L145.text: Attention all hands. A storm is expected to reach the port tomorrow afternoon, so the ship will leave at zero six hundred instead of fourteen hundred. Shore leave ends at twenty-one hundred tonight. All personnel who are ashore must be back on board by that time.

L146.text: We're having a barbecue on Sunday. Can you and your husband come?
I'd love to, but can I take a rain check? My parents are visiting this weekend.

L147.text: After its engine failed, the fishing boat was towed back to the harbor by a Navy patrol boat.

L148.text: Bravo Two, this is Bravo One, radio check. How do you read me? Over.

L149.text: Do you want to take the kids to the beach on Saturday?
It's always so crowded on weekends. We can never find a place to sit. What about the lake?
Good idea. The kids can go fishing there, and we can bring a picnic lunch.

L150.text: Did you remember to reserve a table for tonight?
No, but I should have. The earliest table they have now is at nine thirty.

L151.text: I'm sorry, but we can't cash this check unless you show us some photo identification.

L153.text: If I borrow ten thousand dollars for a car, how much will I pay each month?
I'd need to check a few details, but a ballpark figure would be three hundred dollars a month.

L154.text: I'd like to mail this package to my daughter in Germany. Her birthday is Friday.
Express takes three days. Regular mail costs half as much, but it takes about two weeks.
Then I'll pay extra for express.

L155.text: Eagle Two, this is Base. Your pickup point has changed, so do not go to the bridge. Move to the old water tower, one mile north of the bridge. The helicopter will pick you up there at fifteen thirty. Base out.

L156.text: I have to be at the hospital by two. Can I take the shuttle?
It leaves at one thirty but makes a lot of stops. Take a taxi to be safe.

L157.text: I'd like to sign up for the evening English class.
Monday's full, but Wednesday has room. It starts at six thirty in Room Eight.

L158.text: Did you hear the dining facility is closing for repairs?
Yes, for two weeks starting Monday. There'll be a field kitchen behind the gym.
At least we'll have somewhere to eat.

L159.text: Your car's ready, sir. New brakes, two hundred forty dollars, parts and labor.
Is that all? That's less than I expected.

L160.text: Excuse me, I ordered chicken, not fish.
I'm so sorry. I'll bring the right one in five minutes.
Please hurry. I have to be back at work in twenty minutes.

L161.text: Are you taking leave for the holidays?
Yes, but I asked for two weeks and only got ten days.
That's too bad. I hope you still enjoy it.

L162.text: I'm looking for a gift for my wife.
How about a scarf? We have some nice silk ones on sale.
She already has too many scarves. What else do you have?

L164.text: The battalion run wasn't canceled, just moved to tomorrow at six.
Even with this weather? Then I'd better set my alarm.

L165.text: I can't find parking near the clinic.
There's a lot behind the chapel.
Isn't that reserved for staff? I don't want a ticket.

L166.text: Tiring. The movers broke a lamp, but they gave me a check for the full price.

L167.text: Are you going to the space travel lecture tonight?
I wanted to, but I have to work until eight.
It doesn't start until eight thirty, so you can make it.

L168.text: I'm thinking about buying a used car.
Have a mechanic check it first. My brother-in-law runs a garage on Elm Street.

L170.text: Ma'am, your bag is five kilos over the cabin limit. You'll have to check it.
All right, but please mark it fragile.
Of course. Here's your claim ticket.

L172.text: Can you help with my resume? I'm applying to be a logistics manager.
Sure. Let's put your supply experience first, then.
Good idea. That's my strongest point.

L173.text: The gym's new hours start at five instead of six.
Great! Now I can work out before formation.
Yes, though it still closes at nine.

L174.text: Are you ready for the history test?
Not really. I don't understand the chapter on the Civil War.
I can explain it to you tonight, if you want.

L175.text: I'd like a room for three nights, please.
We have a double with a lake view for one twenty a night, including breakfast.

L177.text: The convoy leaves at oh five hundred, so the trucks must be loaded by twenty-two hundred tonight.
Then we'd better start right after dinner.

L179.text: How was the Grand Canyon? Did you hike down to the river?
Only halfway. It was too hot to go farther.
You should go back in the spring.

L180.text: Is something wrong with my order?
The blue sweater is out of stock. We have gray or green.
Gray is fine. I'll take it.

L181.text: I need to renew my passport.
It takes about six weeks. When are you traveling?
In three weeks. Can I pay extra for faster service?

L182.text: Since Coach Davis retired, I could coach the kids' soccer team if nobody else wants to.
Oh, the parents would be thrilled!

L184.text: How's your Japanese after a year of classes?
Not bad. I can order food and ask for directions.
That's more than I can do.

L185.text: The colonel wants the report by Friday.
We still need the numbers from finance. I'll call and tell them it's urgent.

L186.text: Welcome to Fort Hood. How can I help you?
I came to see my son. He's in the First Cavalry.
All right. I'll need your ID and his unit information.

L187.text: I'm thinking of taking the bus to New York.
Why not the train? It's much faster.
True, but the bus is much cheaper.

L188.text: Can you come to our barbecue on Sunday? Bring a salad or dessert.
Sure! I'll make my famous apple pie.
Great. We have enough salad already.

L189.text: Only one side. I ran out of paint, so I'm heading to the hardware store.

L190.text: I'd like to see Dr. Lewis this week.
Her first opening is next Thursday, but Dr. Ford can see you tomorrow at three.

L194.text: How much are tickets for the baseball game?
Twenty dollars for regular seats and fifty for box seats.
I'll take two regular ones, please.

L195.text: I want to lose some weight before summer.
Have you tried the spinning class? It's Tuesday and Thursday evenings at six.

L196.text: The radio says a truck overturned near the bridge, so the highway's closed.

L199.text: Where will everyone stay for the reunion?
We reserved a block of rooms at the Holiday Inn for all fifty guests.

L200.text: Can you recommend a book? I mostly read history and biographies.
Then you'll love the new biography of Eisenhower.

L202.text: How long does it take to reach the beach?
About forty minutes by car. The bus takes over an hour.

L203.text: I'd like to return these shoes.
What's wrong with them? I can exchange them or refund you.
They start to hurt after an hour.

L204.text: When's the next train to Washington?
An express at three fifteen, and a local at three forty that arrives about thirty minutes later.

L205.text: Did you hear the general is visiting tomorrow?
Yes, and we have to clean the whole building so it looks perfect.
Again? We just cleaned it last week.

L209.text: Want a ride to the airport tomorrow?
Great. I was going to drive, but airport parking is so expensive.
I'll pick you up at six.

L210.text: Can I see the menu, please?
Here you are. Today's special is grilled salmon, with rice or potatoes.
That sounds good. I'll have it with potatoes.

L212.text: How did the job interview go?
I think it went well. They asked about my experience, and they'll decide next week.

L214.text: I hear you're retiring in December.
Yes, after thirty years. I'll travel and spend time with my grandchildren.

L215.text: What did the doctor give you for that cough?
Some syrup. He said it might take a few days to help.

L216.text: I'd like to rent the cheapest car you have for the weekend.
That's the compact, thirty-five dollars a day.

L217.text: The radios came in, Sergeant, but we got twelve, not fifteen.
Call supply and find out where the other three are.

L218.text: I'm having trouble with the new software. I missed the training because I was on leave.
There's another session on Thursday afternoon.

L219.text: When do we leave for the field exercise?
Monday at oh six hundred. Ten days, if the weather cooperates.

L221.text: Who's driving the van to the airport? You need a special permit for it.
Then not me. I don't have one. Corporal Shaw does, though.

L223.text: Are we still short of cooks in the dining facility?
Two new ones start next week. Until then, I'll borrow some from Alpha Company.

L224.text: Friday's inspection covers the whole building, storage rooms included.
Not just our offices? Then we have a lot of work to do.

L225.text: I need the afternoon off for a dentist appointment. Is there a form?
Not for half a day. Just let the first sergeant know.

L227.text: The heater in our classroom isn't working.
The engineers can't come until tomorrow, so we'll use Room Five today.

L229.text: Is the range open this weekend? I must qualify before my deployment.
Only Saturday morning. Sign up now; slots go fast.

L232.text: I need the computer lab for three hours tonight.
It closes at eight, so come right after dinner, at five.

L234.text: How's your first week? Have you met the commander?
Not yet. She's been away at a conference all week.

L238.text: How far is the training area? Let's leave at six.
Two hours by convoy. Make it five thirty, to be safe.

L241.text: Is the motor pool open late tonight?
Until nine, because of the exercise. Bring your paperwork.
Good. I'll drop the truck off after chow.

L243.text: The captain wants everyone at the brief by eight.
I have a medical appointment at seven thirty. I'll tell the captain myself.

L244.text: How did your son do in basic training?
He graduated last Friday, top of his class. Now he's off to airborne school.

L245.text: Can you show me how to set up the tent? Ground cloth, then poles?

L246.text: The truck's battery is dead again.
That's the third time this month. I'll request a new one.
Thanks. I'll use the other truck.

L253.text: The building phones are down, and my cell gets no signal in here.
Then make your calls from outside.

L254.text: Is the promotion exam all multiple choice?
Mostly. It's a hundred questions in two hours, then a short essay.

L256.text: I left my ID at the office. Can you get me on base?
Sure. I'll call the gate and vouch for you.

L258.text: Do you know how to use the new GPS units?
Yes, I took the class last week.
Could you teach my squad Thursday morning?

L260.text: The barracks air conditioning is broken, and the repairmen can't come until Thursday.
It's ninety-five degrees! Can we get some fans meanwhile?

L261.text: Can I take my weapon home to clean it?
No, weapons stay in the arms room. Use the cleaning area next door.

L265.text: The helicopter needs a new rotor blade. The part arrives Wednesday.
And how long does installation take?
About a day, so it'll fly again Thursday.

L267.text: Is there a PX sale this weekend?
Yes, on electronics, but go right when it opens. They sell out fast.

L268.text: The lead vehicle has a flat tire. Changing it will take twenty minutes.
Then tell the other drivers to take a break.

L272.text: The commander approved your transfer. Report by the fifteenth of next month.
Really? That gives me time to pack.

L273.text: I'm calling about the apartment for rent.
It's still available. It comes partly furnished, with a bed, a table, and a sofa.
Great. Can I see it today?

L275.text: Doctor, I'm always tired. I sleep only five hours a night.
You need at least seven. Let's look at your schedule.

L278.text: How do I join the free math tutoring program?
Fill out this form and bring in your most recent report card.

L279.text: My son has had a fever and a sore throat since yesterday.
Bring him in at three. We'll do a strep test.

L280.text: We need a bigger house now that we have the baby.
Yes. Should we buy or keep renting?
Let's ask the bank about a loan first.

L281.text: Does the Army pay for evening classes?
Tuition assistance covers most of the two hundred dollars per course.
Great. I'll sign up for two.

L282.text: The dentist says I need a filling.
Only when I drink something cold, but I'll get it done soon.

L284.text: I'd like to get in shape, but I'm a slow runner.
Join the running club. They have groups for every level.

L285.text: Good. Our son is fine except in spelling, so the teacher suggested reading together twenty minutes nightly.

L286.text: I lost my wallet with my cards and ID.
Call the bank right away to cancel the cards. The personnel office can replace your ID.

L291.text: I need a doctor today. It's not an emergency, just a bad earache.
Dr. Lin has an opening at four.

L293.text: We spend too much eating out. Let's cook at home more.
Okay. You plan the meals, and I'll do the shopping.

L294.text: My son wants to play football. The school gives new helmets, but I still worry about injuries.
Then let him try just one season.

L296.text: An A in history and a B in math. My parents are taking me out to celebrate.

L298.text: We should save for a house. A down payment is about twenty thousand dollars.
If we save five hundred a month, that's over three years.

L299.text: I'm locked out of my apartment, and the office closed at five.
You can stay at my place until morning.

L301.text: My doctor wants me to lose weight by walking daily and eating less sugar.
I'll walk with you in the mornings.

L306.text: How long will my car be in the shop?
At least three days; we're ordering a part. But I can lend you a small car for free.

L309.text: My credit card bill is huge. I bought new tires and a plane ticket.
Well, you needed both of those, at least.

L311.text: The heating bill was huge last month.
The windows are old and let in cold air.
Should we replace the bedroom windows first?

L312.text: My eyes hurt after reading. My last checkup was three years ago.
You should go again. You may need new glasses.

L320.text: My new job starts at seven.
That's early. How will you get there?
There's a bus at six fifteen. It gets me there just in time.

L329.text: I have a reservation under the name Carter. Could I get a room on a higher floor?
Yes, two nights in a single room. I can give you one on the eighth floor.
Perfect. It's always quieter up high.

L330.text: How was your drive up from Texas?
Long, twelve hours with stops. But my brother came, so we took turns.
That makes it a lot easier.

L331.text: Excuse me, does this bus go to the stadium?
No, you need number fourteen. It stops across the street, by the bank.

L332.text: I'm looking for a dress for a wedding, something light, maybe blue or green.
We have a nice blue one in your size.
Oh, it's lovely. Can I try it on?

L333.text: Are you coming to Mike's going-away party? It's Friday at seven.
I'll be late. I have to work until eight.
That's fine. It's at the Italian place.

L334.text: Our flight is delayed three hours, so we'll miss the connection in Atlanta.
Let's ask the agent about other flights.

L336.text: Loved it, except for one rough day. I felt seasick and stayed in my cabin.
At least it was only one day.

L337.text: I'd like to send a dozen roses to my mother in Ohio. She loves them.

L338.text: Where can I get coffee near the train station?
There's a café inside the station. It opens at five thirty.
Great. My train leaves at six.

L339.text: How was your first day at the new school?
Confusing. I got lost twice, but a girl from math class showed me around.

L340.text: I want a gift for my boss, but he already has plenty of pens.
Then get him a book about fishing. He's crazy about it.
Great idea. I'll buy one today.

L341.text: Can you tell me how to get to the museum?
Go two blocks north, turn right on Pine Street, and it's the third building on the left.

L342.text: We're going camping this weekend. Want to come?
I'd love to, but I don't have a tent.
No problem. You can share ours; it sleeps four.

L343.text: The concert's sold out. Should we look for tickets online?
Those cost twice as much. Let's just watch it on TV.

L346.text: Can I switch to an aisle seat?
Let me check. Yes, 14C is open. It's in the middle of the plane.

L351.text: A table for four, please. We don't have a reservation.
Then it'll be a twenty-minute wait. Would you like to sit at the bar?
No, thanks. We'll wait for a table.

L352.text: Are you going to the class reunion?
Probably not. I don't know anyone there anymore.
That's the point! You can catch up with everybody.

L354.text: How long is the drive to the airport? My flight's at seven.
Forty minutes, but traffic is heavy at five. Leave by four thirty.

L355.text: Is the new Mexican restaurant expensive?
Not at all. Lunch is under ten dollars, and the tacos are excellent.

L358.text: Excuse me, is this the line for tickets?
No, ma'am, it's for people who already have them.
Oh. Then I'll try that window on the left.

L359.text: Do you have any vegetarian dishes?
We have vegetable pasta or bean soup. Would you like bread?
The soup, please, but no bread.

L360.text: I'm going to Chicago for the weekend.
Nice! What are you going to do there?
Visit my sister and see a baseball game.

L361.text: Can you help me pick a laptop? It's mostly for school and e-mail.
Then you don't need an expensive one.

L362.text: Did you get a good deal on your car?
Yes. The dealer took two thousand off, and they gave me credit for my old one.

L364.text: Is there a gas station nearby? My fuel light just came on.
There's one about two miles ahead. If the light only just came on, you'll be fine.

L366.text: The hotel pool is closed for cleaning.
Is there another pool near here?
The community center has one, about a ten-minute walk away.

L368.text: How do you like living in the city?
I like the restaurants, but I miss the country. Maybe I'll move back after I retire.

L369.text: Your package has arrived, but the box is crushed.
Then I'll open it here before I sign for it.
Go ahead. Just sign here afterward.

L370.text: Did you buy the tickets for the show?
Yes, but only balcony seats were left.
Balcony? I hope we can see well from up there.

L372.text: I'd like to rent a bike for the day.
That's twenty dollars, helmet included. We'll also keep your ID until you bring it back.

L374.text: Excuse me, I think you're in my seat, twenty-two B.
Oh, you're right. Mine's twenty-three B. Sorry!

L375.text: We should plan our vacation soon. How about the beach?
We went there last year. Let's look at hotels on the coast.

L379.text: I'd like to exchange three hundred dollars for euros, please.
That comes to about two hundred seventy euros.

L382.text: How far is the next town? Anything to see on the way?
Fifty miles. There's a beautiful lake about halfway.

L383.text: Can I get this in a larger size?
Not here, but I'll call our other store. It'll just take a few minutes.

L384.text: I can't choose between these phones. One has a better camera; the other has a bigger battery.
Which matters more to you, then?
The camera, definitely. I take photos every day.

L385.text: The restaurant gave us the wrong bill. It has three steaks, and we only ordered two.
Let's ask the waiter to fix it.

L386.text: Want to go to the farmers market on Saturday? It opens at eight.
That's early, but the bread is worth it.

L390.text: Did the mechanics ever get around to that jeep with the leaking radiator?
They ordered the part last week, but it's still on back order, so the jeep's not going anywhere.

L391.text: Can you help me move this weekend?
I'd like to, but my hands are tied.

L394.text: The barracks inspection got moved up to Wednesday.
Wednesday? I was counting on the weekend to get my wall locker squared away.

L395.text: Did you get the job at the hospital?
They haven't made up their minds yet.

L396.text: Do you want to go out for dinner?
I'm too beat to go anywhere.

L398.text: Could you pull my staff duty Friday night? I'll take yours on Sunday.
I'd like to help, but I already traded Friday with Sergeant Ortiz.

L399.text: Are we still doing the twelve-mile road march tomorrow?
Not if the heat index stays above ninety. The first sergeant said she'd make the call at zero five hundred.

L402.text: Do you know if the new printer in the orderly room works yet?
It works, all right, as long as you only need one page at a time.

L403.text: How did your night land navigation course go?
Let's just say I found every point, eventually, about an hour after the cutoff.

L404.text: It went in one ear and out the other.

L406.text: I've got a sick call appointment at zero seven thirty, but formation's at the same time.
Medical comes first. Just let your squad leader know before you head over.

L407.text: Why is the whole company already lined up outside? It's only six fifteen.
Somebody didn't get the word. First formation was pushed up half an hour.

L408.text: Have your travel orders for the course in Texas come through?
Not yet, and the class starts Monday. Without them, I can't even book a flight.

L410.text: Did you enjoy the trip to the mountains?
It was out of this world.

L412.text: The inspector general's team arrives Tuesday. How do our supply records look?
Honestly, I wouldn't want anyone looking at them before Thursday at the earliest.

L414.text: How do you feel about the new uniforms?
I can take them or leave them.

L416.text: Are you going to buy that car?
The price is way out of my league.

L417.text: Do you think Private Allen will pass the course?
He's got a good head on his shoulders.

L419.text: I had fire guard from two to four, and then I couldn't get back to sleep.

L421.text: The battery on my truck is dead again. Can you give me a jump?
Sure. Is this the third time this week?
Fourth. I'm starting to think it's not the battery at all.

L422.text: Do you like your new boss?
We get along like a house on fire.

L423.text: Is the colonel in a good mood today?
I'd stay out of her way if I were you.

L424.text: Did you hear the news about the base closing?
Yes, it came as a total shock.

L426.text: Why did the first sergeant cancel the Friday afternoon formation?
The battalion commander gave everyone a four-day weekend for winning the safety award.

L427.text: Did you buy the blue shirt or the white one?
I couldn't make up my mind, so I got both.

L432.text: Did the captain sign the leave forms I left on his desk?
He didn't even get to them. He was in meetings all afternoon.

L433.text: Does the clinic give flu shots on weekends?
Only on the first Saturday of the month, and that was last week.

L435.text: Do you think Major Grant will retire this year?

L436.text: It was a little too salty for my taste.

L437.text: Should we cancel the outdoor PT session? The forecast says thunderstorms.
Not till this evening. If we start at six sharp, we'll be done long before it hits.

L439.text: My orders say I report to Fort Carson on the fifteenth, but my household goods won't ship until the twentieth.
That happens all the time. You can stay in temporary lodging until your things arrive.

L445.text: The sergeant major found dust on top of my locker during the inspection.
You too? He must have checked every single room with a white glove.

L447.text: Who's taking the platoon at formation while Lieutenant Park is on leave?
Sergeant First Class Hale will fill in for her until she gets back next month.

L453.text: Did you find a parking space?
I had to circle the block five times.

L458.text: The doctor put me on light duty for two weeks because of my back.
Does that mean no field exercise next week?
Right. I'll be helping out in the supply room instead.

L460.text: Did you send the training schedule to the battalion yet?
It's ready to go, but the operations officer asked for one more change before it goes out.

L461.text: Why is Specialist Reed washing all the trucks by himself?
He forgot to turn in his dispatch paperwork last week, so the motor sergeant gave him extra duty.

L462.text: Is the awards formation still at the gym, or did they move it outside?
They kept it inside. With this wind, nobody wanted to chase hats across the field.

L464.text: Did our vehicles pass the safety inspection this morning?
All except two. One had a cracked windshield, and the other was missing a fire extinguisher.

L466.text: Did you see the game last night?
I wouldn't have missed it for anything.

L469.text: I could use someone to help me inventory the arms room after lunch.
Count me in. Anything beats sitting at my desk all afternoon.

L471.text: The radio says the wind chill will be twenty below tonight.
Then make sure the guards on the night shift rotate every hour instead of every two.

L472.text: Is your sister coming to the wedding?
She wouldn't miss it for the world.

L473.text: Did the new obstacle course go over well with the recruits?
Too well. Half of them finished so fast that the drill sergeants want to make it harder.

L475.text: Why did the clinic send you to the hospital downtown?
They don't have an MRI machine on post, and the specialist I need only works there on Thursdays.

L476.text: Can you proofread my evaluation report before I turn it in?
Sure, but it'll have to wait until after the inspection on Friday.

L477.text: Has finance paid you for your trip to the conference yet?
No, they sent my travel voucher back twice for missing receipts.

L479.text: Did Specialist Moore ever show up for his shift at the gate?
Forty minutes late, and the sergeant of the guard is writing him up.

L482.text: Did the new trainee make a good impression?
She was a breath of fresh air.

L483.text: Can you finish the job by Friday?
I'll do my best, but no promises.

L485.text: How did you do on the range?
I hit the bull's-eye every time.

L488.text: Do you want to see a movie or go bowling?
Either one is fine with me.

L490.text: The printer is out of paper again.
There's a new box in the supply closet.

L491.text: I can't read the small print on this form.

L492.text: I'd like to deposit this check, please.
Please sign the back of it first.

L493.text: Open wide and tell me where it hurts.
The lower tooth on the left.

L494.text: I've had a terrible headache all day.
Why don't you lie down for a while?

L496.text: My car won't start this morning.
Let me get the jumper cables from my trunk.

L497.text: I'd like two tickets for the seven o'clock show.
I'm sorry, only the nine o'clock show has seats left.

L499.text: The baby has a fever and won't stop crying.
I'll call the clinic and ask for an appointment.

L502.text: Your blood pressure is fine, but you need to lose some weight.

L503.text: We're out of milk and eggs.
I'll stop at the store on my way home.

L504.text: I'd like to mail this package to Texas.
Would you like it to go by express or regular mail?

L506.text: Do you have this shirt in a medium?
Let me check in the back.

L509.text: Check your weapon before you go to the firing line.

L510.text: Could you show me where the history books are?
They're on the third floor, next to the maps.

L511.text: We can put you on the next one at four.

L512.text: I can move you to a room on the other side of the hotel.

L513.text: I need to get a new ID card.
Go to the personnel office in Building Three.

L514.text: I'd like to sign out a laptop for the staff meeting tomorrow.
I can do that, but it has to be back on my desk by sixteen hundred.

L516.text: Ma'am, you were going fifty in a thirty zone.
I'm sorry, officer. I didn't see the sign.

L518.text: My son is having trouble with math.
The library has free tutoring on Tuesdays.

L520.text: Let's take a picture in front of the fountain.
Okay, I'll ask someone to take it for us.

L521.text: The lights in the barracks keep going off.
I'll put in a work order with the engineers.

L522.text: How would you like your hair cut?
Just a little shorter on the sides.

L523.text: I think I left my phone in the taxi.
Call the taxi company right away.

L524.text: The movie starts in ten minutes.
Then we'd better skip dinner and go straight there.

L525.text: Put the boxes in the corner, please.
Do you want them stacked or side by side?

L528.text: Is this the bus to the airport?
No, you want the blue one across the street.

L529.text: I've been coughing for a week.
Take this syrup twice a day and come back if it doesn't help.

L530.text: I'd like to open a savings account.
Please fill out this form and show me your ID.

L532.text: Oops, I left it in the truck. I'll go get it.

L533.text: I'm here for my eleven o'clock appointment with Doctor Shaw.
She's running about forty-five minutes behind, so have a seat and we'll call you.

L534.text: My suitcase didn't come off the plane.
Fill out this form, and we'll deliver it to your hotel.

L537.text: Remove your shoes and put your bag on the belt.
Do I need to take my laptop out too?

L539.text: We need someone to drive the van tomorrow.
I can do it if I can leave early on Friday.

L540.text: I'm going to the store. Do you need anything?
Could you get me some batteries?

L543.text: Okay, squad, we've got ten minutes to set up the radio and make contact with headquarters.
Ten minutes? Last time it took us almost half an hour just to find the right frequency.

L544.text: I'd like a large pepperoni pizza for delivery.
Can I have your address, please?

L549.text: The base is on heat category five, so all outdoor training is suspended.
Then let's move the first aid class into the classroom and do the hands-on part tomorrow morning.

L551.text: Sorry, I don't have that much in the register.

L552.text: The motor sergeant wants all drivers to do their vehicle checks before the convoy leaves.
That's going to be tight. We roll out at zero six hundred, and half the trucks are still covered in ice.

L553.text: I'd like a one-way ticket to Boston.
The next train leaves in twenty minutes.

L554.text: My shoulder hurts when I lift my arm.
Let's take an X-ray to see what's wrong.

L555.text: How much longer is this field exercise? I haven't had a hot meal in four days.
We pull out Thursday, so just two more days of these ready-to-eat meals.

L557.text: I need to change the dates on my temporary duty orders. Who handles that?
Personnel, but they'll want a memo from your commander explaining why.

L559.text: Excuse me, which way to the emergency room?
Follow the red line on the floor.

L561.text: Raise your right hand and repeat after me.
I, Private Jones, do solemnly swear...

L562.text: I'm going to the gym. Want to come?
Sure, just let me get my shoes.

L564.text: I can't find the keys to the truck.
Did you look in the motor pool office?

L565.text: Please put on this gown and wait for the doctor.

L566.text: The dental clinic just called. They want to move your cleaning from Friday to next Tuesday.
Tuesday's no good; I'm at the range all day. I'll call them back first thing in the morning.

L567.text: This printer prints only in black and white.
Use the color printer in the hall.

L568.text: I'd like a haircut and a shave.
Have a seat; I'll be right with you.

L569.text: We need more chairs for the meeting.
I'll bring some from the classroom next door.

L574.text: My essay is due tomorrow, and I haven't started.
You'd better get to work right now.

L575.text: I'd like to see the manager, please.
I'm the manager. How can I help you?

L576.text: Are we supposed to wear our reflective belts for the morning run?
Only when it's dark out, and in December that's pretty much the whole run.

L578.text: I need to send a fax to headquarters.
The fax machine is in the operations office.

L581.text: I want to learn to swim.
The pool offers lessons for adults on Wednesday nights.

L583.text: Does the shuttle leave at eight or eight thirty?
It used to leave at eight, but now it's eight thirty.

L584.text: How much do I owe you for lunch?
Your half comes to seven fifty.

L588.text: That movie was the best I've seen all year.
I'd have to agree with you.

L589.text: How many people showed up for the blood drive this morning?
Over sixty, which is twice what we got last spring.

L590.text: Is it cheaper to fly or to drive?
Driving costs about half as much.

L591.text: What time does the store close tonight?
Normally at nine, but tonight at six because of the holiday.

L592.text: I think we should take the highway.
The back roads would be faster at this hour.

L593.text: How long did the convoy take to get here?
Six hours, two more than usual.

L594.text: Did you buy the red car or the gray one?
Neither; I got a white one.

L596.text: Do you think the colonel will like the plan?
I doubt it; it's too expensive.

L598.text: How many people are in your unit?
About three hundred, but a third are deployed.

L599.text: I think the test is on Thursday.
Actually, it's been moved up to Tuesday.

L601.text: How far is it to the next town?
About thirty miles, or forty minutes.

L602.text: Should we order the large or the medium pizza?

L603.text: Is this your first time in Texas?
No, I was stationed here ten years ago.

L604.text: When do we get paid this month?
On the thirtieth, since the first is a Sunday.

L605.text: I don't think we need to bring jackets.
The forecast says it'll get cold tonight.

L608.text: Is the hospital on this side of the river?
No, it's just across the bridge.

L610.text: It left on time but landed an hour late.

L612.text: I'm sure Sergeant Ray will win the competition.
Don't count your chickens before they hatch.

L613.text: How many copies should I make?
Make one for each of the twenty students, plus two extra.

L616.text: Should we leave at six or seven?
Six; traffic gets bad after six thirty.

L617.text: How much did the tickets cost?
Twenty each, but I had a coupon for five dollars off.

L618.text: I think the meeting was a waste of time.

L619.text: When do the new recruits arrive?
The first group on Monday and the second on Wednesday.

L620.text: How many rooms does the new barracks have?
Sixty, with two soldiers in each.

L622.text: Is the new clerk faster than the one who left?
Faster, sure, but I end up fixing half of what she types.

L623.text: How long have you been waiting?
Since a quarter to nine. It's almost ten now.

L630.text: Is it going to rain tomorrow?
Only in the morning; the afternoon will be clear.

L631.text: Where did you put the keys, on the desk or in the drawer?
In the drawer, under the papers.

L632.text: I'll pay for dinner this time.
No, it's my treat; you paid last time.

L633.text: How many people signed up for the trip?
Thirty, but there are only twenty-five seats on the bus.

L634.text: Do you like your new job better than the old one?
The pay is better, but the hours are longer.

L641.text: Do you want to sit in the front or the back?
As close to the front as possible.

L643.text: Normally forty, but today it's twenty-five percent off.

L644.text: Do you agree with the new policy?
In principle, yes, but not the details.

L646.text: When do you have to sign in at your new unit?
No later than the first of June, but I'm driving, so I'm leaving a week early.

L648.text: Is Lieutenant Harris in her office?
She just left for lunch; she'll be back at one.

L649.text: Which is faster, the bus or the subway?
The subway, by about fifteen minutes.

L650.text: How did the dining facility do on its health inspection?
Not as well as last year, though nothing serious enough to close it.

L651.text: How many soldiers were missing from morning formation?
Three, but two of them were at the clinic.
So we really only have one we can't account for.

L652.text: I think we should cancel the picnic.
Let's wait and see what the weather does.

L653.text: Is it far to the gate?
It's farther than it looks; about two miles.

L654.text: Have we got enough volunteers for the post cleanup on Saturday?
We need twelve, and so far I've got seven names on the list.

L655.text: Do you want to meet at noon or one?
Twelve thirty would be better for me.

L656.text: Do you think the store will have my size?
They usually do, but call first to be sure.

L657.text: How long is the drive to Fort Lee?
Three hours without stops, four with lunch.

L660.text: Should I call the clinic or just go in?
Call first; they take appointments only.

L661.text: Is the road to the training area open after last night's snow?
The main gate road is plowed, but the back road won't be cleared until this afternoon.

L662.text: How much does the uniform cost?
Ninety dollars, but you get an allowance of sixty.

L663.text: He was there, but he was ten minutes late.

L665.text: How long will the repairs take?
Two days for the parts and one day to install them.

L667.text: How many cups of coffee do you drink a day?
Two in the morning and one after lunch.

L669.text: When did you last see Sergeant Moss?
Around three, heading to the motor pool.

L670.text: Did the new desks for the office ever arrive?
They came Monday, but they're too wide to fit through the door, so they're sitting in the hallway.

L671.text: How late did you stay at the office last night?
Late enough that the cleaning crew had come and gone, and they don't start until ten.

L672.text: Do you think the bridge will be finished this year?

L673.text: My friend is sitting there, but she'll be back soon.

L674.text: How much did you pay for the car?
Less than I expected; the dealer gave me a discount.

L675.text: I just found out my flight home was canceled.

L676.text: Why didn't you come to the gym this morning?
I pulled a muscle in my back yesterday.

L677.text: What's the problem with your car?
It makes a loud noise when I brake.

L679.text: How did your room look during the first sergeant's walk-through?
She didn't say a word, which for her is practically a compliment.

L680.text: Why are you taking the bus today?
My car is in the shop for repairs.

L681.text: You're in a good mood. What happened?
I finally got my slot for airborne school. I've been on the waiting list since March.

L684.text: Why didn't you answer my e-mail?
It went into my junk folder by mistake.

L686.text: I fell off a ladder while painting the house.

L689.text: Why is the water off in the barracks?
The engineers are fixing a broken pipe.

L692.text: Why did Sergeant Ford get promoted early?
He scored first in his class at the leadership course.

L694.text: Why are you wearing civilian clothes on a duty day?
I'm out-processing today. My last formation with this unit was yesterday.

L700.text: What's the matter with the radio?
There's a lot of static; I can't hear anything.

L703.text: Why are you studying so late?
I have a test at eight tomorrow morning.

L705.text: What's the matter? You look pale.
I think I ate something bad at lunch.

L706.text: Why do you want to change jobs?
I'd like a chance to travel more.

L707.text: Why hasn't the plane taken off?
They're waiting for a passenger who checked in late.

L711.text: Why did you move your desk?
The sun was in my eyes all afternoon.

L713.text: Why can't you come to the party?
I promised to help my sister move.

L718.text: Why do you look so pleased?
My daughter got into the college she wanted.

L721.text: Why are you wearing a coat? It's warm.
The air conditioning in my office is freezing.

L723.text: Why don't you want to go to the beach?
I burn easily in the sun.

L724.text: Why is Corporal Lane so quiet today?
She didn't get the assignment she wanted.

L726.text: Why did you leave the party so early?
I had a headache, and the music was too loud.

L727.text: I got caught in the rain on the way here.

L728.text: How come the trucks are still here?
The drivers are waiting for their orders.

L729.text: Why do you want a transfer?
My wife got a job in another state.

L730.text: What's the matter with the coffee?
Someone forgot to add the coffee; it's just hot water.

L732.text: Why did you give up the piano?
I just never had time to practice.

L734.text: Why can't we use the conference room?
The general is having a meeting there.

L737.text: Why did you choose this school?
It has the best engineering program in the state.

L738.text: How come nobody's picking up the phone in the personnel office?
Most of the section went to the range, and the rest called in sick.

L739.text: Why did your squad fail the convoy exercise?
Our lead vehicle took a wrong turn, so we reached the checkpoint forty minutes late.

L740.text: Why haven't you finished the report?
I'm still waiting for the numbers from finance.

L745.text: Why aren't you taking the shuttle bus to the airport?
It leaves at four in the morning, and my flight isn't until after lunch.

L747.text: Why do you need a new uniform?
I've gained weight since the last one.

L750.text: Why is the motor pool closed this afternoon?
The whole maintenance platoon is at a safety briefing until sixteen thirty.

L751.text: Why do you always sit in the back?
I like to leave quickly when class ends.

L753.text: Why did you come back early from leave?
My unit was called up for an emergency.

L754.text: Why are there so many police cars outside?
There was a robbery at the bank.

L755.text: Why are you learning to cook?
My wife is going to be away for six months.

L758.text: Why is everyone wearing their dress uniforms today?
There's a change of command ceremony at ten, and the whole battalion has to be there.

L759.text: Why do you seem so relaxed?
I just got back from a week at the beach.

L760.text: Why don't you just take some aspirin for that headache?
The doctor told me not to mix it with the medicine I'm already on.

L761.text: Why was the parachute jump canceled this morning?
The aircraft had a mechanical problem, and the backup plane was already booked by another unit.

L762.text: Why are you still in uniform? Your shift ended an hour ago.
My relief got held up, so I'm staying on until he gets here.

L763.text: Why is the private standing outside the office?
He's waiting to see the first sergeant.

L764.text: Why is your car making that noise?
The muffler has a hole in it.

L765.text: Switch to the backup and call the motor pool.

L766.text: Ma'am, may I have Friday off?
Only if Corporal Tate can cover your shift.

L767.text: Has anyone signed for the new radios?
The supply sergeant signed for them this morning.

L770.text: Did the trainees finish the obstacle course?
All except one, who hurt his ankle.

L773.text: I need a vehicle for the trip to the port.
You'll have to fill out a dispatch form first.

L775.text: Should I wear my helmet to the range?
Helmets and vests are required at all times.

L776.text: The trucks are low on fuel.
The fuel point opens at six; we'll fill up then.

L779.text: I can't log in to the computer.
Your password probably expired; call the help desk.

L780.text: Is the convoy ready to move?
We're waiting for the last truck to be loaded.

L784.text: Can I use the conference room this afternoon?
It's reserved until three; after that it's free.

L785.text: Did the parts for the truck arrive?
They're on back order; maybe next week.

L786.text: Why are you still here? It's after five.
I have to finish the inventory before I go.

L788.text: How did the night exercise go?
We got lost twice, but we found the target.

L789.text: Do I need to bring my own sleeping bag?
No, the unit will issue one.

L790.text: Have you heard whether you were selected for the leadership course?
The list comes out Friday, but my first sergeant hinted that I shouldn't make any other plans.

L791.text: The copier on the second floor is broken.
Use the one in the operations office.

L792.text: How many hours did you fly this month?

L793.text: Has anyone seen the key to the conference room? The meeting starts in five minutes.
Try the front desk. Whoever used the room last was supposed to drop it off there.

L795.text: Who's responsible for the vehicle that came back with a dent in the door?
Whoever signed it out last, and according to the dispatch log, that was Corporal Evans.

L796.text: The jackets did, but the pants were too long.

L797.text: Are you working the holiday weekend?
Saturday and Sunday, yes, but I get Monday and Tuesday off to make up for it.

L798.text: Can you give the new soldier a tour of the base?
I'll show him around after lunch.

L799.text: Has the post put out a weather warning for tonight?
A freezing rain advisory, starting at nine. They're asking people to stay off the roads unless it's mission essential.

L800.text: Did everyone pass the fitness test?
Everyone except two, who will retest next week.

L802.text: Report it to security and get a temporary pass.

L803.text: Are we going to make the deadline?
Only if we work through the weekend.

L804.text: Did everyone make it through the swim test?
Everyone but Private Ford. He was doing fine until a cramp hit him on the last lap.

L808.text: When does the next class start?
In two weeks, on the first of the month.

L809.text: Who has the duty roster for next month?
Sergeant Lopez made it, but the first sergeant hasn't approved it yet, so it could still change.

L810.text: Can I take the jeep to the airfield?
Take the van; the jeep's in the shop.

L811.text: How long does it take to process a leave request?

L812.text: Are the soldiers back from the field?
The first group is; the second comes tonight.

L813.text: Did you get your gear laid out for the equipment inspection?
I'm only missing my canteen. I must have left it in the truck after the road march.

L817.text: We need more sandbags for the wall.
I'll send a detail to fill another hundred.

L819.text: The new printer is faster than the old one.
And it uses less ink, too.

L822.text: Can you lend me your compass?
I need it for the land navigation course.

L823.text: How many questions did you miss on the test?

L824.text: Where should I put my gear?
In the locker at the end of your bunk.

L825.text: When will my new ID card be ready?
They're printed same day, but the system's been down since Tuesday, so it could be a while.

L826.text: This map is out of date.
Get a new one from the operations office.

L828.text: Is the gym open twenty-four hours?
Only for active-duty soldiers with an access card.

L829.text: Did the general like the demonstration?
He said it was the best he'd ever seen.

L833.text: Did the weather delay the jump?
Yes, the winds were too strong this morning.

L836.text: A civilian contractor from the company that makes the radios.

L839.text: How often do we have to do those accountability formations?
Twice a day for now, until the investigation into the missing equipment is over.

L841.text: Where did you learn to fly helicopters?
At Fort Rucker, about ten years ago.

L844.text: Is the dining facility serving breakfast on Saturday?
Brunch only, from nine to one.

L845.text: Did you get the new computer passwords for the section?
I got everyone's except the lieutenant's. His account is locked until the help desk resets it.

L846.text: When do you get the cast off your wrist?
Not for another three weeks, and even then only if the bone has healed properly.

L848.text: Should I report to the clinic in uniform?
Yes, and bring your medical records.

L852.text: Who's running the driver training for the new soldiers?
Sergeant Cole was supposed to, but he's on leave, so you're it.

L853.text: Has the bus to the airport left?
The next one leaves at the top of the hour.

L854.text: Is it true the base pool is closing?
Only for two weeks, for repairs.

L855.text: Why is the major here so early?
He wants to review the plan before the general arrives.

L856.text: Can we use the gym for the ceremony?
Only if the auditorium isn't available.

L859.text: Do you want to go to the lake on Sunday?
Only if it's warm enough to swim.

L860.text: How was your son's first day at school?
He cried when I left, but he was fine by lunch.

L861.text: Can you pick up the kids at three?
I have a meeting until four. Can your mother do it?

L862.text: This briefing is excellent. Did you put all of these slides together yourself?
Most of them, but Sergeant Ward did the maps, and those took the longest.

L864.text: It's on sale for thirty-five, down from fifty.

L865.text: Did you remember to feed the cat?
I fed her before I left for work.

L866.text: There's a repair shop in the mall that fixes them in an hour.

L869.text: I'd like to get my hair colored.
We have an opening on Thursday at two.

L870.text: Are you going to the wedding?
I wouldn't miss it; the bride is my best friend.

L871.text: Do you want to exchange it for a smaller size?

L873.text: Where do you want to put the new sofa?
Against the wall, facing the window.

L875.text: The clinic gave me antibiotics, but I'm already feeling fine after two days.
Don't stop taking them, though. You're supposed to finish the whole bottle, even if you feel better.

L876.text: Did you buy everything on the list?
Everything except the bread; they were sold out.

L877.text: How long is the drive to your parents' house?
Two hours if traffic is light.

L879.text: He came, but he needs a part, so he'll be back tomorrow.

L880.text: How do you like the new neighbors?
They're friendly, but their dog barks a lot.

L884.text: The children are making a lot of noise.
They're excited about the trip tomorrow.

L887.text: Do I have to fill up the tank before I return the truck to the motor pool?
Only if it's below half. Otherwise the dispatcher won't care either way.

L888.text: The music was great, but our seats were terrible.

L889.text: When is the battalion run this week?
Friday at six thirty, unless the colonel's flight gets in late. Then it's Monday.

L890.text: I think this milk has gone bad.
Pour it out and open the new carton.

L891.text: It's almost ten years old, but it runs well.

L893.text: The new soldiers still haven't been issued their cold-weather gear.
Supply promised it by Wednesday, so we'll hold the winter training until Thursday.

L895.text: Do you want to watch the game at our house?
Thanks, but I've got tickets to see it live.

L897.text: How much do I owe you for the tickets?
Nothing; they were free from work.

L899.text: Is it supposed to clear up before the cookout this afternoon?
The forecast says the rain should stop by noon, but the ground will still be soggy.

L900.text: My flight is at six a.m.
Then you'd better leave the house by four.

L901.text: What did the safety inspector think of the new loading dock?
She liked the layout, but she wants railings on both sides before anyone uses it.
Great. That'll push the opening back another week.

L906.text: Do you know a good dentist?
Dr. Kim is great, and she's near your office.

L907.text: Turn off the water and call the repair service.

L909.text: Give me five more minutes to finish my makeup.

L910.text: I want to buy a bike for my daughter.
How old is she? We have different sizes.

L912.text: Can you watch the kids while I go to the store?

L913.text: How much did the vacation cost?
More than we planned, but it was worth it.

L914.text: I'm taking the new soldiers on a hike up Bald Hill this afternoon.
You'd better be back before three. The lightning usually starts rolling in by mid-afternoon this time of year.

L916.text: My mother is coming to stay for a month.
Then we'll need to clean the guest room.

L917.text: The colonel finally approved our training plan this morning.
It's about time. Now we can finally put in the ammunition request before Friday's deadline.

L918.text: Can I get this in blue?
Blue is sold out, but we have green and black.

L919.text: How long does the cake need to cool?
At least an hour before you frost it.

L921.text: Our flight is delayed two hours.
Let's get something to eat while we wait.

L923.text: Where are you going on vacation?
We haven't decided between the mountains and the beach.

L925.text: How many bedrooms do you need?
Three, one for each of the kids and one for us.

L926.text: The motor pool says there are no vans left for our trip to the training center.
Then let's rent one. It takes some extra paperwork, but it's better than canceling.

L928.text: How much is a coffee and a bagel?

L931.text: My daughter got the lead in the school play.

L933.text: What time does the parade start?
Ten, but we should get there early to find a spot.

L935.text: Want to take turns driving on the trip down to Texas? It's about ten hours.
Sure, but I'll take the second half, once the sun goes down. I always get drowsy after lunch.

L939.text: The shoe store is having a sale this weekend.

L940.text: How long have you lived in this town?
All my life, except for four years in college.

L943.text: How's the instructor course going so far?
Harder than I expected. Teaching is a lot different from just knowing the material.

L945.text: How long will the oil change take?
About thirty minutes. You can wait inside.

L946.text: Should we paint the room white or yellow?
Yellow will make it look warmer.

L950.text: This memo is way too long. The colonel won't read past the first page.
Then put the key points in a short summary at the top.

L953.text: I left my sunglasses at the restaurant.
Call them; they'll hold them for you.

L955.text: Attention, all passengers on Flight 482 to Denver. The departure gate has changed from Gate 12 to Gate 21. Boarding will begin in fifteen minutes. Please proceed to Gate 21 now.

L956.text: Good morning, everyone. Today's physical training will be a four-mile run instead of the usual three. We'll start at the north gate and finish at the gym. Bring water, because it's going to be hot.

L957.text: Hi, this is Dr. Patel's office calling for Sarah Lee. We need to change your appointment from Tuesday to Thursday at the same time, ten o'clock. Please call us back to confirm.

L958.text: Shoppers, the store will close in fifteen minutes. Please bring your final purchases to the registers at the front. Thank you for shopping with us, and have a good evening.

L959.text: Listen up. Tomorrow's convoy will leave at oh five hundred, not oh six hundred. All vehicles must be fueled and inspected by twenty-one hundred tonight. Drivers will meet at the motor pool at oh four thirty.

L960.text: Welcome to the base library. We're open from nine to nine on weekdays and from noon to five on weekends. You can borrow up to five books for three weeks. Please return them to the drop box by the front door.

L961.text: This is a weather alert for the county. A severe thunderstorm is expected this afternoon, with strong winds and hail. Residents should stay indoors and avoid driving until the storm passes, probably around six this evening.

L962.text: Hello, Mike, it's Jenny. I'm running about twenty minutes late because of traffic on the bridge. Please start the meeting without me, and I'll catch up when I get there. Sorry about this.

L963.text: Attention, please. The eleven fifteen bus to Atlanta has been canceled due to mechanical problems. Passengers may take the twelve thirty bus at no extra charge or receive a full refund at the ticket window.

L964.text: All personnel, the fire alarm test will take place today at fourteen hundred. When you hear the alarm, there is no need to leave the building. This is only a test of the system.

L965.text: Thank you for calling the base clinic. If this is an emergency, hang up and dial 911. To make an appointment, press one. For pharmacy information, press two. To speak to a nurse, press three.

L966.text: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome aboard. Our flight time to Chicago will be two hours and ten minutes. We expect some light turbulence, so please keep your seat belts fastened when you're seated.

L967.text: Soldiers, the range is closed today because of high winds. Your qualification has been moved to Thursday at the same time. Make sure your weapons are cleaned and ready by Wednesday evening.

L968.text: This is a reminder that the swimming pool will be closed all next week for repairs. It will reopen on Monday the fifteenth. During this time, the pool at the community center is available to all members.

L969.text: Hi, this is Tom from the car dealership. Your car is ready for pickup. The total for the service is two hundred and fifteen dollars. We're open until six today and from nine to noon tomorrow.

L971.text: Everyone, the new parking rules start Monday. Lot A is for officers only. Enlisted personnel will park in Lots B and C. Visitors must park in the visitor lot near the main gate.

L972.text: Good evening and welcome to the Grand Theater. Tonight's performance will last about two hours, with a fifteen-minute intermission. Please turn off your cell phones. Photography is not allowed during the show.

L973.text: This is your captain speaking. We are beginning our descent into Seattle. The weather there is cloudy, with a temperature of fifty-two degrees. We will be on the ground in about twenty minutes.

L974.text: Hi, it's your mother. I'll be arriving at the airport on Friday at three in the afternoon, on Delta flight 210. Please don't be late; you know I hate waiting. See you soon.

L975.text: All new soldiers must report to the education center tomorrow at oh eight hundred for in-processing. Bring your orders, your ID card, and your medical records. The process will take most of the day.

L976.text: Attention, shoppers. For the next hour, all frozen foods are twenty percent off. This offer is good only until three o'clock, so hurry to aisle twelve and take advantage of these savings.

L977.text: Good afternoon. I'm calling from the bank about your credit card. We noticed some unusual purchases in another state. Please call us back at the number on the back of your card as soon as possible.

L978.text: The base shuttle will follow a new schedule starting next week. Buses will run every fifteen minutes during rush hour and every thirty minutes at other times. The last bus will leave at eleven p.m.

L979.text: Welcome to the museum. Our guided tour begins in ten minutes at the main entrance. It lasts about one hour and covers the history of aviation. Audio guides are also available at the front desk.

L981.text: Hi, Lisa, this is Carlos from work. The team lunch has moved from Thursday to Friday at noon, still at the Italian restaurant on Fourth Street. Let me know if you can still come.

L982.text: Train passengers, please note that the train to Boston is running thirty minutes late due to a signal problem. We now expect it to arrive at four forty-five. We apologize for the inconvenience.

L983.text: Platoon, tomorrow we will practice land navigation. Each team will receive a map, a compass, and five points to find. The team that finds all five points fastest will get the afternoon off.

L984.text: This is a recorded message from the city water department. Water service on Oak Street will be shut off tomorrow from eight a.m. to two p.m. for pipe repairs. Please store water before that time.

L986.text: Attention, all drivers. The east gate will be closed for construction from Monday to Friday. Please use the main gate or the west gate during this time. Expect delays during rush hour.

L990.text: Hi, this is Karen from the travel agency. I found you a cheaper flight to Miami that leaves at six a.m. instead of ten. It saves you eighty dollars. Should I book it? Please call me back today.

L991.text: All soldiers going on leave this weekend must attend a safety briefing on Friday at fifteen hundred in the auditorium. The briefing will cover driving safety and weather conditions. Attendance will be taken.

L992.text: Welcome to City Zoo. The elephant show begins at eleven and two near the main pond. Feeding the animals is not allowed. The zoo closes at five, and the last entry is at four.

L993.text: Attention, passengers. Due to heavy fog, all flights are delayed by at least one hour. Please check the departure boards for updates. Free coffee is available at the information desk.

L994.text: Students, the library will extend its hours during exam week. It will be open from seven a.m. to midnight every day. Study rooms can be reserved at the front desk for up to two hours.

L996.text: All units, a training exercise will be held on the airfield tonight from twenty hundred to midnight. You may hear helicopters and explosions. There is no danger to the public.

L998.text: This is the school nurse. Your son has a fever of one hundred and one and needs to go home. Please pick him up at the front office as soon as you can.

L999.text: Good evening. Here is the weather. Tonight will be clear and cold, with a low of twenty-eight degrees. Tomorrow will be sunny, with a high of forty-five. Snow is possible on Saturday.

L1000.text: Attention, please. The lost and found has a black backpack found in the gym this morning. It contains a laptop. The owner can claim it at the front office with an ID.

L1002.text: Hello, this is the hotel front desk. Your room is ready for early check-in. Breakfast is served until ten in the dining room on the first floor. Enjoy your stay.

L1004.text: Welcome aboard the city tour bus. Our first stop will be the Capitol Building, where we'll spend thirty minutes. Then we'll visit the war memorial and end at the river park around noon.

L1005.text: This is a public service message. Next Saturday is free health check day at the community center. Nurses will check blood pressure and blood sugar from nine to three. No appointment is needed.

L1006.text: Hi, it's Amy. I can't make it to dinner tonight; my daughter is sick. Can we try for next week instead? I'm free on Tuesday and Wednesday. Let me know.

L1007.text: Passengers, the next station is Central Square. This train will not stop at Elm Street because of construction. Passengers for Elm Street should get off at Central Square and take the shuttle bus.

L1008.text: The base theater is showing two movies this weekend: a comedy on Friday and an action movie on Saturday. Both start at seven. Tickets are four dollars for adults and two for children.

L1010.text: Good morning, students. Remember that the science fair is next Friday. All projects must be set up in the gym by eight a.m. Judges will visit each project between nine and noon.

L1012.text: Hello, this is Officer Grant from base housing. Your new quarters will be ready on the twentieth. You can pick up the keys at the housing office after one p.m. that day.

L1014.text: Everyone, please remember that the office will close at noon on Friday for the holiday weekend. Make sure all reports are submitted by Thursday. Have a safe and happy holiday.

L1015.text: This is a message for residents of Building Six. The elevator will be out of service on Tuesday for maintenance. Please use the stairs. If you need help carrying anything, call the front desk.

L1016.text: Welcome to Basic Training. For the next ten weeks, you will learn discipline, teamwork, and basic combat skills. Your drill sergeants will be with you every day. Listen carefully and follow orders.

L1017.text: Shoppers, a child named Tommy is looking for his parents. He is wearing a red jacket and is waiting at the customer service desk. Will his parents please come to the desk?

L1018.text: The Grand Canyon is about two hundred and seventy-seven miles long and up to eighteen miles wide. It was formed over millions of years by the Colorado River cutting through rock. Today, more than five million people visit it every year.

L1019.text: Sleep is very important for good health. Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep each night. People who do not sleep enough are more likely to have accidents and to get sick.

L1020.text: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. The first flight lasted only twelve seconds and covered about one hundred twenty feet.

L1021.text: Honeybees are important to farmers because they carry pollen from flower to flower. This helps plants produce fruit and seeds. Without bees, many of the foods we eat would become rare and expensive.
