L1022.text: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States. It was completed in 1886 and stands on an island in New York Harbor. It has become a symbol of freedom around the world.

L1023.text: Drinking enough water is especially important in hot weather. When you sweat, your body loses water and salt. If you do not replace them, you can become dizzy and weak. Soldiers in the field should drink water regularly, even if they are not thirsty.

L1024.text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth. It covers about one third of the planet's surface. Its deepest point, the Mariana Trench, is nearly seven miles deep.

L1025.text: The Internet began as a military research project in the late 1960s. At first, it connected only a few universities and government offices. It became popular with the public in the 1990s, when the World Wide Web made it easy to use.

L1026.text: Regular exercise has many benefits. It strengthens the heart, helps control weight, and improves mood. Experts recommend at least thirty minutes of moderate exercise, such as fast walking, five days a week.

L1027.text: Alaska is the largest state in the United States, more than twice the size of Texas. However, it has one of the smallest populations. Much of the state is covered by mountains, forests, and ice.

L1028.text: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth president of the United States. He led the country during the Civil War and helped end slavery. He was killed in 1865, just days after the war ended.

L1029.text: The human heart beats about one hundred thousand times a day. It pumps blood through the body, carrying oxygen to every organ. Regular exercise and a healthy diet help keep the heart strong.

L1030.text: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, is the highest mountain in the world. It is about twenty-nine thousand feet tall. The first people to reach the top were Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, in 1953.

L1031.text: Many accidents at home happen in the kitchen. To stay safe, turn pot handles toward the back of the stove, keep knives out of children's reach, and never leave cooking food unattended.

L1032.text: The Mississippi River is one of the longest rivers in North America. It flows about two thousand three hundred miles, from Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico. For centuries, it has been an important route for trade.

L1033.text: The Moon has no air and no water. Its surface is covered with dust and craters. Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon between 1969 and 1972, during the Apollo missions.

L1034.text: Washing your hands is one of the best ways to prevent illness. Use soap and warm water, and wash for at least twenty seconds. This removes germs that can cause colds and the flu.

L1035.text: George Washington was the first president of the United States. Before that, he was the commander of the army during the War of Independence. The capital city, Washington, D.C., is named after him.

L1036.text: Deserts receive less than ten inches of rain a year. Although they are often very hot during the day, they can be very cold at night because there are few clouds to hold the heat.

L1037.text: Smoking damages almost every organ in the body. It is a major cause of heart disease and lung cancer. People who stop smoking, even after many years, quickly improve their health.

L1038.text: The Great Lakes are five large lakes on the border between the United States and Canada. Together, they hold about one fifth of all the fresh water on the Earth's surface.

L1039.text: Thomas Edison is famous for developing the first practical electric light bulb in 1879. He also worked on the phonograph and motion pictures. During his life, he received more than one thousand patents.

L1040.text: A healthy breakfast gives you energy for the morning. Good choices include whole grains, fruit, and eggs or yogurt. People who skip breakfast are often hungrier later and eat more unhealthy snacks.

L1045.text: Earthquakes happen when large pieces of the Earth's crust move suddenly. California has many earthquakes because it sits on the edge of two of these pieces. Most earthquakes are small, but some cause great damage.

L1046.text: The first transcontinental railroad in the United States was completed in 1869. It connected the east and west coasts and reduced the trip across the country from months to about a week.

L1047.text: Stress can affect your body as well as your mind. It can cause headaches, trouble sleeping, and high blood pressure. Exercise, enough sleep, and talking with friends can help reduce stress.

L1048.text: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they are excellent swimmers. They use their wings like flippers to move quickly through the water. Most penguins live in the Southern Hemisphere.

L1049.text: The Pentagon, near Washington, D.C., is the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense. It is one of the largest office buildings in the world. It was completed in 1943, during World War Two.

L1051.text: The Sun is a star. It is about ninety-three million miles from the Earth. Its light takes about eight minutes to reach us. Without the Sun's energy, there would be no life on Earth.

L1052.text: Many people believe that eating carrots improves your eyesight. Carrots contain vitamin A, which is important for healthy eyes. However, eating extra carrots will not make normal eyes see better.

L1053.text: The Civil War in the United States lasted from 1861 to 1865. It was fought between the northern and southern states. More Americans died in this war than in any other war in the nation's history.

L1054.text: Recycling saves energy and natural resources. For example, making a new can from recycled aluminum uses much less energy than making one from raw materials. Paper, glass, and plastic can also be recycled.

L1056.text: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco opened in 1937. At the time, it was the longest suspension bridge in the world. Its famous orange color helps ships see it in the fog.

L1058.text: The Amazon rainforest in South America is the largest tropical rainforest in the world. It is home to millions of kinds of plants and animals. It also produces a large part of the world's oxygen.

L1059.text: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Today, the Summer and Winter Games are each held every four years, two years apart. Athletes from over two hundred countries take part.

L1060.text: Sunburn is caused by the sun's ultraviolet rays. It can happen even on cloudy days. To protect your skin, use sunscreen, wear a hat, and avoid the strongest sun between ten and four.

L1061.text: Benjamin Franklin was a writer, scientist, and diplomat. He is famous for his experiments with electricity, including flying a kite in a thunderstorm. He also helped write the Declaration of Independence.

L1063.text: Good posture is important when you work at a desk. Keep your feet flat on the floor, your back straight, and the computer screen at eye level. Take a short break every hour to stretch.

L1064.text: The Liberty Bell is a famous symbol of American independence. It is kept in Philadelphia. The bell has a large crack and has not been rung for more than a hundred years.

L1065.text: Snakes are cold-blooded animals. This means their body temperature changes with the temperature around them. That is why snakes often lie in the sun in the morning to warm up.

L1067.text: The Erie Canal opened in 1825 and connected the Great Lakes to the Hudson River and New York City. It made shipping goods much cheaper and helped New York become the country's largest city.

L1069.text: Dolphins are mammals, not fish. They breathe air through a hole on the top of their heads. They are very intelligent and communicate with each other using clicks and whistles.

L1070.text: The White House has been the home of every American president since John Adams in 1800. It has one hundred thirty-two rooms and is open to visitors who book tours in advance.

L1071.text: Getting a flu shot every year is the best way to avoid the flu. The flu virus changes each year, so last year's shot may not protect you. Shots are usually given in the fall.

L1072.text: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth. Almost all of it is covered by ice, which in some places is three miles thick. No people live there permanently, but scientists work there in research stations.

L1073.text: Seat belts save thousands of lives every year. In a crash, a seat belt keeps you from being thrown from the vehicle. On base, everyone in a vehicle must wear a seat belt at all times.

L1075.text: The Earth's atmosphere protects us from the Sun's harmful rays and keeps the planet warm. It is made mostly of nitrogen and oxygen. Without it, life on Earth would not be possible.

L1076.text: Reading to young children helps them learn language. Experts suggest reading together for at least fifteen minutes a day. Children who are read to often learn to read more easily at school.

I did, but the mechanic says the front ones are wearing unevenly, so the wheels need to be aligned.

L2388.text: Could I check out this book for the weekend?
Sorry, it's a reference book. You can use it here, though, or make copies of the pages you need.

L2389.text: Hello, may I speak to Mr. Grant, please?
I'm afraid you have the wrong number. This is a dental office, not a law firm.

L2390.text: I've decided to take guitar lessons. Do you think I'm too old to start?
Not at all. My uncle learned to play at sixty, and now he performs at weddings.

L2391.text: This pasta is delicious. Did you make the sauce yourself?
I wish I could take the credit, but it came out of a jar.

L2392.text: Is the apartment on Elm Street still available?
It is, but the owner won't allow pets, and I know you have a dog.

L2393.text: How's your daughter enjoying her first year at college?
She loves her classes, but she calls home every night, so I think she's a little homesick.

L2394.text: These boots are on sale for forty dollars. Should I get them?
Only if they fit. Remember, you can't return anything that's marked down.

L2395.text: Why are all these cars slowing down?
There's a police officer up ahead checking speeds. You'd better watch how fast you're going.

L2396.text: Why was I charged thirty-five dollars on my account this month?
Your balance fell below five hundred, and that's the minimum required to avoid a monthly fee.

L2397.text: Did you get any good pictures at the lake?
Hardly any. I forgot to charge the camera battery, and it died after ten minutes.

L2398.text: Can you put my blue sweater in the dryer with the towels?
I wouldn't. The label says to dry it flat, or it'll shrink.

L2399.text: Do you want to study together for the chemistry final?
I'd like to, but I work until nine every night this week. How about Saturday morning?

L2400.text: Has the landlord done anything about the noise from upstairs?
He's talked to the neighbors twice, but they still play music past midnight.

L2401.text: I need proof that this letter was delivered. Is there a way to do that?
Send it certified. The person has to sign for it, and you'll get a receipt online.

L2402.text: I've been trying to reach you all afternoon. Is your phone off?
Sorry, it was charging in the car. I didn't see your messages until I got home.

L2403.text: Are you going to run in the ten-K on Saturday?
I signed up, but with this sore ankle I'll probably just watch from the sidelines.

L2404.text: The bill comes to sixty dollars. How much should we leave for a tip?
The service was great, so let's leave twelve. That's twenty percent.

L2405.text: The ATM kept my card and won't give it back.
That happens when the PIN is entered wrong too many times. The bank opens at nine, and they can give it back then.

L2406.text: Is it okay to park here for a few minutes while I run into the pharmacy?
Not unless you want a ticket. That space is for disabled drivers only.

L2407.text: Did you remember to pick up eggs and milk on your way home?
I got the milk, but the eggs completely slipped my mind.

L2408.text: Are your parents still living in that big house in the country?
No, they sold it last spring. Now they've got a small place near my sister so they can help with the grandkids.

L2409.text: When are the movers supposed to get here?
Between eight and noon, but they called to say they're running about two hours behind.

L2410.text: Have you decided whether to take the history class or the biology one?
I'm leaning toward biology. The history class meets at seven in the morning, and I'm no early bird.

L2411.text: My driver's license expires next week. Can I renew it online?
Not this time. You need a new photo, so you'll have to go in person.

L2412.text: Your tomatoes look great this year. What's your secret?
No secret, really. I just water them early every morning before it gets hot.

L2413.text: Your hair looks different. Did you go to a new barber?
Same barber, but he was out sick, so his son cut it instead.

L2414.text: Do you know a faster way to the stadium? The highway's backed up for miles.
Take the next exit and follow River Road. It's longer, but it'll save you time.

L2415.text: How did your final exam go?
Better than I expected. I thought I'd be lucky to pass, but I got a B.

L2416.text: I've been on hold with the cable company for forty minutes.
Why don't you hang up and try their online chat? It's usually much quicker.

L2417.text: Is your brother coming for Thanksgiving this year?
He'd planned to, but his flight got canceled, so he's spending it with his in-laws instead.

L2418.text: Are you still going to the gym every morning?
I used to, but since I got a bike, I ride to work instead and get my exercise that way.

L2419.text: Do you sell stamps here, or do I have to go to the post office?
We do. They come in books of twenty, and you can pay for them at any register.

L2420.text: The kitchen faucet has been dripping all week. Should I call someone?
Don't bother. It's probably just a worn washer; I can replace it myself this weekend.

L2421.text: Should I call ahead and reserve a table at Rosa's for Friday?
You'd better. Last time we went without a reservation, we waited over an hour.

L2422.text: Did the bank approve your car loan?
They did, but not until my father agreed to co-sign for me.

L2423.text: I'd like to return this jacket. I don't have the receipt, though.
In that case, I can only give you store credit, not cash.

L2424.text: Did you see the game last night? I fell asleep at halftime.
You didn't miss much. Our team was behind by twenty points and never caught up.

L2425.text: Can I get a large coffee with milk, no sugar?
Sure. Is that for here or to go?
To go, please. I'm already late for class.

L2426.text: Could I borrow your ladder? I need to clean out the gutters.
Sure, but my son has it right now. He should bring it back by tomorrow.

L2427.text: I'm thinking about joining the book club at the library. Is it any good?
The people are friendly, but they read a novel a week, which is a lot if you work full-time.

L2428.text: Someone backed into me in the grocery store parking lot and drove off without leaving a note.

L2429.text: Can your mother watch the kids on Saturday night?
She'd be glad to, as long as we bring them over before six. She goes to bed early.

L2430.text: Have you started your research paper yet? It's due a week from Monday.
Started it? I handed it in yesterday. I wanted it out of the way before my trip.

L2431.text: Is it true your rent is going up next month?
By a hundred dollars. I'm thinking of finding a roommate to split the cost.

L2432.text: Did anyone call while I was out?
Your dentist's office did. They want you to call back to move Thursday's appointment.

L2433.text: Why didn't you just order the lamp online? It's cheaper.
I thought about it, but the shipping was almost as much as the lamp itself.

L2434.text: When did you last have the oil changed in this car?
To be honest, I can't remember. It's been at least a year, maybe longer.

L2435.text: Do you want to play tennis after work tomorrow?
I'd love to, but I won't be off until seven, and the courts close at eight.

L2436.text: I'm going to Japan next month. Should I exchange my money here or at the airport?
Do it here. The airport rates are terrible, and they charge a fee on top of that.

L2437.text: Did you remember to feed the dog before you left?
I filled his bowl, but I didn't have time to take him for a walk.

L2438.text: I moved two weeks ago, but my mail is still going to my old address.
Did you fill out a change-of-address form? It can take up to ten days to start working.

L2439.text: Your Spanish has really improved. Have you been taking classes?
No, but I've been practicing with a coworker from Mexico during lunch every day.

L2440.text: Did you catch anything at the lake this morning?
Not a thing. But it was so peaceful out there that I didn't really care.

L2441.text: How do you get to work now that your car's been sold?
A neighbor drives me in, and I pay her for half the gas.

L2442.text: Does the soup of the day have any nuts in it? My son is allergic.
I'm not sure. Let me ask the chef before you order it.

L2443.text: What are you getting your parents for their fortieth anniversary?
My sister and I are chipping in to send them on a cruise.

L2444.text: You look exhausted. Didn't you sleep well?
Not really. The neighbor's car alarm kept going off until about three a.m.

L2445.text: Does this dress come in a smaller size?
Not in blue, I'm afraid. We've got your size in black, though, if you'd like to try it on.

L2446.text: Is everyone in your group doing their share of the project?
Everyone except Tom. He hasn't shown up to a single meeting, so the rest of us have been covering for him.

L2447.text: I can't log in to my bank account online. It keeps saying my password is wrong.
Click on 'Forgot password,' and they'll send a code to your phone so you can reset it.

L2448.text: Did you and Kevin decide on the house on Maple Avenue?
We loved it, but it was way over our budget, so we're still looking.

L2449.text: Hello? Jim? You keep cutting out. I only heard every other word.
Sorry, I'm in an elevator. Let me call you back in two minutes.

L2450.text: Is there a gas station near here? The light on my dashboard just came on.
There's one about two miles ahead, right after the bridge. You should make it.

L2451.text: Is Danny still taking swimming lessons at the community pool?
He was, but he's switched to soccer. He says it's more fun to play with his friends.

L2452.text: Do you know when the trash gets picked up on this street?
Tuesday mornings. But next week it's Wednesday because of the holiday on Monday.

L2453.text: How long is the wait for a table for four?
About forty-five minutes, but if you don't mind sitting at the counter, I can seat you right now.

L2454.text: Who won the basketball game between the officers and the sergeants?
The sergeants, but only by a single point, and that was in overtime.

L2455.text: There was a note on the door saying the mail carrier tried to deliver a package.
That means you'll have to pick it up at the post office, and bring your ID with you.

L2456.text: I heard your sister just had a baby. Boy or girl?
Twins, actually! One of each, so now I have a niece and a nephew.

L2457.text: Did you build that bookshelf yourself? It looks like it came from a store.
Thanks! I took a woodworking class last spring, and this is my first real project.

L2458.text: Would you like to buy an extended warranty for the TV? It's only thirty dollars.
No, thanks. It already comes with two years of coverage from the manufacturer.

L2459.text: Why are you taking the long way home?
Main Street's been closed since Monday for repairs, and it won't reopen until the end of the month.

L2460.text: Can I pick up my suits today? The ticket says they'll be ready Thursday.
Let me check. Yes, you're in luck. They finished them early this morning.

L2461.text: Have you registered for next semester's classes yet?
Not yet. I can't sign up until I pay a parking fine I got last fall.

L2462.text: Do you take credit cards, or should I go find an ATM?
Cards are fine, but there's a ten-dollar minimum. Your total is only seven fifty.

L2463.text: Our heating bill was almost double last month's.
No wonder. Somebody left the upstairs window open all weekend while we were away.

L2464.text: I tried to leave you a message yesterday, but your voicemail was full.
Oh, sorry about that. I never check it. Just send me a text next time.

L2465.text: Do you think I should pay off the furniture now or make monthly payments?

L2466.text: Did you ever hear back from the landlord about the broken window?

L2467.text: How often do your kids get to see their grandparents?

L2468.text: Excuse me, do you have these boots in a wider size?

L2469.text: Do you think watching American TV shows really helps your listening?

L2470.text: Are there any of those chocolate cookies left, or did the kids finish them?

L2471.text: Have you met the family that just moved in next door?

L2472.text: That new steak place was way too expensive for what we got, wasn't it?

L2473.text: Are you going to watch the soccer final at home or at the club?

L2474.text: Do you mind if I take this call? It's my daughter's school.

L2475.text: How do you manage to save money with three kids at home?

L2476.text: I'm thinking about buying the extended warranty on this laptop. Is it worth the money?

L2477.text: The final exam covers everything since the first week of class, doesn't it?

L2478.text: I'm afraid you've dialed the wrong number. Nobody named Kevin lives here.

L2479.text: Do you know whether family members can use the base pool on weekends?

L2480.text: Didn't you say you were allergic to peanuts? There are some in this salad.

L2481.text: How far in advance do we need to book the inspection before moving out of quarters?

L2482.text: Who's going to feed your cat while you're away on leave next month?

L2483.text: I need to send money to my parents back home. What's the cheapest way to do it?

L2484.text: Aren't you going to try out for the basketball team this season?

L2485.text: You couldn't lend me a pen for the test, could you? Mine just ran out of ink.

L2487.text: Hi, this is Tony from the gym. Your membership expires at the end of the month. If you renew this week, you'll get one month free. Stop by the front desk anytime.

L2490.text: Good morning, passengers. Due to track work, this train will run express from Grand Street to Park Avenue. Passengers for stations in between should take the shuttle bus at Grand Street.

L2492.text: The chaplain's office is open every weekday morning, and by appointment in the afternoon.

L2493.text: Only three of the eight trucks passed the safety inspection this morning.

L2494.text: The new dining hall can seat twice as many soldiers as the old one, which held two hundred.

L2495.text: The colonel said that leave requests for December must be turned in by November fifteenth.

L2498.text: What time do the gates close at night?

L2499.text: Has your paycheck been deposited yet? Mine usually shows up on Friday.
Mine too, but with Friday's holiday, it won't go through until Monday.

L2500.text: That used car looks like a great deal. Are you going to buy it?
Not until my mechanic takes a look at it. A low price can hide a lot of problems.

L2501.text: I'm having trouble with these math problems. Could you go over them with me?
I'd be glad to, but math was never my strong point. You might be better off asking Lisa.

L2503.text: This coupon says two for one on cereal. Can I use it here?
You could have yesterday. It expired at midnight, I'm afraid.

L2504.text: Are you still going camping this weekend?
We were, but the forecast calls for storms, so we've put it off until next month.

L2505.text: Is the training room free this afternoon?
The captain booked it until three. After that, it's yours.
Perfect, I only need an hour.

L2506.text: What do I need for the sergeant's course next year?
A recommendation from your platoon leader and a passing score on your last fitness test.

L2507.text: Formation has been moved up to zero six fifteen tomorrow, so don't count on having breakfast before PT.

L2508.text: If your room doesn't pass Friday's inspection, you'll lose your weekend pass and the first sergeant will check it again Saturday morning.

L2509.text: Staff duty can't be swapped without the sergeant major's approval, and he won't sign anything after sixteen hundred.

L2510.text: The change of command ceremony is in dress uniform, but the rehearsal on Wednesday is in the regular duty uniform.

L2511.text: Anyone pulling guard tonight is excused from the morning run, but they still have to make the noon formation.

L2512.text: Specialist Ortiz made sergeant before anyone else in his group because his board score was the highest in the battalion.

L2513.text: We used to have mail call every afternoon, but now the mail room only hands out packages on Tuesdays and Fridays.

L2514.text: Sergeant Kim isn't going on leave after all; his flight was canceled, so he'll be running the range tomorrow.

L2515.text: Weapons must be cleaned and turned in to the arms room before anyone is released for the long weekend.

L2516.text: Since the gym will be closed for repairs all week, PT will be held on the track behind the motor pool instead.

L2517.text: Specialist Grant is filling in for the supply sergeant until Monday, so take your hand receipts to him.

L2518.text: The barracks quiet hours start at twenty-two hundred on weeknights, but on Fridays and Saturdays they begin an hour later.

L2519.text: Hardly anyone showed up for the blood drive this morning, so the unit has decided to extend it through Thursday.

L2520.text: Remember, we don't salute indoors except when formally reporting to an officer, so don't salute the captain in the hallway.

L2521.text: The organization day picnic won't be at the lake after all; another unit reserved it first, so we're using the ball field.

L2522.text: Leave requests for the holidays must reach the orderly room no later than the fifteenth, or they won't be considered.

L2523.text: Your boots look fine, Private, but that haircut doesn't meet regulations; get it fixed before tomorrow's formation.

L2524.text: Unless the weather clears by noon, the awards ceremony will move from the parade field into the gym.

L2525.text: Every soldier signing out on leave must leave a phone number with the charge of quarters so they can be reached anytime.

L2526.text: The new first sergeant is stricter than the last one, but at least he explains the reasons behind his rules.

L2527.text: Guard mount is at seventeen thirty sharp; if you show up without your post orders, you'll be sent back to get them.

L2528.text: I'd rather do fire watch from midnight to two than get up at four for the last shift.

L2529.text: Because of the inspector general's visit, all offices will stay open through lunch on Thursday instead of closing at noon.

L2530.text: The colonel wants the entire battalion in formation by zero seven forty-five, fifteen minutes before she arrives.

L2531.text: Soldiers living off post no longer need to attend the evening accountability formation, as long as they check in by phone.

L2532.text: The motor sergeant won't release any vehicle for the trip until its driver has completed the safety briefing.

L2533.text: If you lose your ID card, report it to the military police before you go to get a replacement.

L2534.text: The barracks fire drill went well, except that it took the third floor nearly twice as long to get out as everyone else.

L2535.text: Make sure your name tape is sewn on straight; at the last inspection, three soldiers were marked down for crooked ones.

L2536.text: Corporal Diaz has been put in charge of the detail, so check with her, not me, before you leave the area.

L2537.text: The regulation says you may wear civilian clothes in the dining facility, but not shorts or sleeveless shirts.

L2538.text: The platoon won't be released for lunch until the sergeant has checked every room, so keep cleaning while you wait.

L2539.text: This weekend's duty roster was posted late because two soldiers had to be replaced at the last minute.

L2540.text: Anyone driving on post must stay under twenty-five miles an hour, and in housing areas the limit drops to fifteen.

L2541.text: Captain Ross asked me to remind you that the range brief has been pushed back to after lunch.

L2542.text: Now that Mike has been promoted to sergeant, he's moving out of his shared room into a private one on the second floor.

L2543.text: The inspection team found everything in order except the fire extinguishers, which hadn't been checked since March.

L2544.text: We'll march to the ceremony site in formation, but buses will bring everyone back afterward.

L2545.text: Sergeant Lee would have passed the fitness test if he hadn't slipped during the two-mile run.

L2546.text: Don't bother ironing your uniform for tomorrow; the inspection has been called off because of the general's visit.

L2547.text: Visitors without a base pass can only enter through the main gate, since the north gate is for ID card holders only.

L2548.text: Promotions will be announced at the end of the month, but the ceremony itself won't take place until after the holidays.

L2549.text: When retreat sounds at seventeen hundred, drivers on post must pull over and wait until the music ends before moving on.

L2550.text: I can cover your duty Saturday as long as you take my Sunday shift in return.

L2551.text: Any soldier caught using a cell phone in formation will have it taken away until the end of the duty day.

L2552.text: Our platoon came in second in the barracks competition, only a few points behind Alpha Company's third platoon.

L2553.text: We need two volunteers to set up chairs for the retirement ceremony, and whoever helps gets the afternoon off.

L2554.text: Everyone is to report to the company area in civilian clothes at eighteen hundred for the unit's holiday dinner.

L2555.text: The lieutenant wasn't happy that only half the platoon had their reflective belts on during this morning's run.

L2556.text: Tell the new privates that sergeants aren't called sir; that word is only used for officers.

L2557.text: Because the dining facility is short on cooks this week, breakfast will be served half an hour later than usual.

L2558.text: Sergeant Vega was supposed to be the range safety officer, but since he's sick, I'll be taking over.

L2559.text: The battalion run is mandatory for everyone, unless you have a medical profile signed by a doctor.

L2560.text: We'd better wash the trucks before Thursday's motor pool inspection; last time the sergeant major failed us for mud alone.

L2561.text: The first sergeant has an open-door policy, but she'd rather you talk to your squad leader first.

L2562.text: Because the colonel is inspecting personally, the platoon sergeant wants our rooms ready by zero eight hundred, an hour earlier than planned.

L2563.text: Specialist Moore can't attend the class because he's on a field exercise until the twentieth.

L2564.text: Remember that the uniform changes to long sleeves on the first of November, regardless of the weather.

L2565.text: Sergeant Park will be taking over the second squad while Sergeant Allen is at the leadership course.

L2566.text: Soldiers who haven't qualified on their weapons this year won't be allowed to deploy, so the range is open again Saturday.

L2567.text: Sick call starts at zero six thirty, and anyone who reports after zero seven thirty will have to wait for the afternoon session.

L2568.text: Before you sew on your new rank, wait until the promotion orders are published; wearing it early is against regulations.

L2569.text: Barracks visitors must sign in at the CQ desk and leave by twenty-two hundred on weeknights.

L2570.text: The washing machines on the second floor are out of order, so use the ones in the next building until they're repaired.

L2571.text: Take your cap off when you walk into a building, but don't forget to put it back on before you step outside.

L2572.text: If you get an alert call during the night, pass the message to the next person on the roster before you get dressed.

L2573.text: The hail and farewell is Friday at the community club; spouses are welcome, but children should stay home this time.

L2574.text: The weight room used to stay open all night, but under the new policy it closes at twenty-three hundred.

L2575.text: Put your gear on the bunk in the same order as the packing list, so the inspector can check it faster.

L2576.text: Stay on your post until the sergeant of the guard comes to relieve you, even if your shift is supposed to be over.

L2577.text: Specialists aren't noncommissioned officers, so even though Specialist Hall has more time in service, Corporal Reyes is in charge of the team.

L2578.text: The Soldier of the Month board meets Tuesday, and candidates should expect questions on regulations, military history, and first aid.

L2579.text: The unit photo will be taken right after formation on Monday, so make sure your uniform is clean and your boots are shined.

L2580.text: Hot plates and coffee makers aren't allowed in barracks rooms, so do your cooking in the day room kitchen.

L2581.text: Soldiers on a weekend pass must stay within two hundred fifty miles of post unless the commander approves a longer trip.

L2582.text: Starting next month, duty hours will begin at zero six hundred instead of seven because of the summer heat.

L2583.text: Before anyone goes to the field, the arms room will inventory every sensitive item, including night vision devices and radios.

L2584.text: Private Nolan was late to formation twice this week, so he'll be on extra duty in the dining facility all weekend.

L2585.text: Monday is a federal holiday, and the commander has also given us the Friday before it off.

L2586.text: To register a car on post, bring your license, registration, and proof of insurance to the visitor center.

L2587.text: The commander's parking spaces are marked in red, and anyone else who parks there will get a ticket from the MPs.

L2588.text: Commander's call has been rescheduled for Thursday at fifteen hundred, and attendance is mandatory for everyone except those on guard.

L2589.text: The dental clinic says a third of our company is overdue for an exam, and they won't be cleared for the overseas exercise.

L2590.text: Every soldier must finish the online equal opportunity course by the end of the quarter, or their promotions will be delayed.

L2591.text: We need six soldiers to clear snow tomorrow, and they'll be chosen from those who didn't have duty last weekend.

L2592.text: Police call is at zero seven hundred; walk the whole company area in a line and pick up any trash you see.

L2593.text: The buses for the field exercise leave at zero four hundred, so I'd pack your rucksack tonight rather than in the morning.

L2594.text: Headphones aren't allowed while running on post roads, but you can wear them on the indoor track or the treadmills.

L2595.text: Sergeant Brooks is retiring after twenty-two years, and the platoon is collecting money for a gift; give whatever you can to Specialist Webb.

L2596.text: The flag detail needs two more soldiers; it only takes fifteen minutes each morning, and it counts toward your volunteer hours.

L2597.text: Pets aren't allowed in the barracks, not even fish tanks, but soldiers in family housing may keep up to two animals.

L2598.text: The PT test has been postponed for a week because the track is being resurfaced, so you've got extra time to train.

L2599.text: Since the staff duty runner may not leave the desk, he'll need someone to bring his dinner from the dining facility.

L2600.text: Sergeant First Class Dunn outranks Staff Sergeant Wells, so he'll lead the convoy, and Wells will ride in the last vehicle.

L2601.text: The shot clinic will keep operating in building nine until the end of the month, when it moves to building forty-two.

L2602.text: Requests to change rooms go through your platoon sergeant first, and the housing office won't accept them without his signature.

L2603.text: The battalion staff meeting usually runs about an hour, but with three new officers to introduce, plan on staying until noon.

L2604.text: When you take over CQ, read the logbook from the last shift first, since it lists anything that still needs attention.

L2605.text: Everyone has to have their protective mask fitted before Tuesday's training, and the supply room is doing fittings only in the mornings.

L2606.text: After your temporary duty, you have five working days to turn in your travel voucher, or the payment will be delayed.

L2607.text: If my bag weighs more than fifty pounds, the airline will charge me an extra seventy-five dollars, so I'm repacking it tonight.

L2608.text: The shuttle to the terminal normally runs every fifteen minutes, but on weekends you might wait twice that long.

L2609.text: I didn't realize my license had expired until the rental agent asked to see it, so my husband had to drive.

L2610.text: Before you take the truck out of the motor pool, check the oil and tire pressure and sign the dispatch log.

L2611.text: Since you're in uniform, the gate agent says you can board with the first group instead of waiting for zone four.

L2612.text: The airline says my suitcase was put on a plane to Denver by mistake and should be delivered to my hotel tomorrow.

L2613.text: Take the second exit at the traffic circle, and if you reach the fire station, you've gone too far.

L2614.text: Our household goods shipment won't arrive in Germany for another six weeks, so we're renting furniture until then.

L2615.text: We could save six dollars by avoiding the toll road, but the free route adds about forty minutes to the trip.

L2616.text: Pack your carry-on so that the laptop comes out easily; security will ask you to put it in a separate bin.

L2617.text: I'd rather pay a little extra for an aisle seat than sit by the window for a nine-hour flight.

L2618.text: The mechanic said the brakes can wait another month, but the battery needs to be replaced before winter.

L2619.text: Packages sent to an APO address need a customs form, and lithium batteries can't be mailed there at all.

L2620.text: Traffic on the interstate was so heavy that I got off at the next exit and took the old county road.

L2621.text: The rental company charges drivers under twenty-five an extra fee, so my son can't afford to rent a car for the trip.

L2622.text: Unless the fog lifts by noon, all flights out of here will be held on the ground.

L2623.text: The post office closes at five, but the self-service kiosk in the lobby is open around the clock.

L2624.text: The GPS keeps telling me to turn onto a road that's been closed for repairs since last spring.

L2625.text: If you're flying space-available, bring enough money for a hotel, because you could be stuck at the terminal for days.

L2626.text: I've passed that sign a hundred times, but I never noticed the speed limit drops to twenty-five near the school.

L2627.text: The bus driver won't make change, so have the exact fare ready or buy a pass at the station.

L2628.text: Your vehicle registration expires at the end of the month, and you can't renew it until the car passes inspection.

L2629.text: We would have caught the earlier ferry if the line at the car rental counter hadn't been so long.

L2632.text: This envelope needs extra postage because it's thicker than a quarter of an inch, even though it's light.

L2633.text: Once you cross the bridge, stay in the right lane; the left two lanes go straight onto the interstate.

L2634.text: Hardly anyone rides the six o'clock train, so you can usually find a seat even without a reservation.

L2635.text: Our convoy will stop every two hours so drivers can rest, and nobody passes the lead vehicle for any reason.

L2636.text: Five of us from the unit share rides to work, and each person drives one day a week.

L2637.text: Passengers continuing on to Honolulu should stay on board; everyone else must take their belongings with them.

L2638.text: The last time I drove through the mountains, chains were required, so I'm not going without them this time.

L2639.text: Your ticket is good for any train until midnight, but you have to stamp it in the machine before you board.

L2640.text: The oil light came on halfway home, so I pulled over and called the motor pool instead of driving any farther.

L2641.text: Mail for soldiers in the field goes out only on Tuesdays and Fridays, so letters dropped off Saturday won't leave until Tuesday.

L2642.text: I always ask for a printed map at the rental counter, since my phone often loses its signal in the countryside.

L2643.text: The agent moved me to first class because my original seat was broken, and she didn't charge me a cent.

L2644.text: Trucks over ten tons have to pull into the weigh station, but pickups and cars can keep going.

L2645.text: I would have mailed the package by regular post, but it has to be there by Friday, so I'm paying for overnight delivery.

L2646.text: Don't bother looking for the bus stop on Main Street; they moved it around the corner while the road is being repaved.

L2647.text: The flight crew just announced we're expecting some rough air over the mountains, so keep your seat belt fastened.

L2648.text: We'll take the coastal road going down and the interstate coming back, since we'll be in a hurry then.

L2650.text: There's a recall on this model because the airbags may not open, so the dealer will replace them for free.

L2651.text: Instead of waiting for the shuttle, I walked to the terminal, and I still got there before it did.

L2652.text: When you come out of the subway, the embassy is the tall gray building directly across the street from the exit.

L2653.text: Your duffel bag has to go through the X-ray machine, but you can keep your boots on in this line.

L2654.text: I filled up the tank before returning the car, but they still charged me because the gauge wasn't quite on full.

L2655.text: Seats on the bus to the air show are free, but you have to sign up at the front desk by Wednesday.

L2656.text: Not until we reached the gate did I remember that my passport was still in the glove compartment.

L2657.text: The ten-forty to Baltimore will depart from track six instead of track two, and it's running about ten minutes behind.

L2658.text: Keep the receipt for the certified letter; it's the only proof that the landlord received our notice on time.

L2659.text: I asked for directions at the gas station, and the clerk drew me a map on the back of a receipt.

L2660.text: We're third in line for takeoff, so it should be another ten minutes or so before we're in the air.

L2661.text: The car needs new wiper blades and a headlight bulb, but neither job should take more than fifteen minutes.

L2662.text: Our flight leaves at six a.m. and check-in starts at four, so I'm just going to stay up all night.

L2663.text: The package was supposed to arrive Monday, but the tracking number shows it's still sitting in a warehouse in Ohio.

L2664.text: On a two-lane road, cars in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing.

L2665.text: The airport is only twelve miles away, but you should allow an hour, since the road out there is always backed up.

L2666.text: This truck burns more fuel than it should, so I'm going to have the mechanic check the air filter first.

L2667.text: If you miss the last bus, a taxi back to base costs about forty dollars, so keep an eye on the time.

L2668.text: Visitor parking is free for the first two hours; after that, it's three dollars an hour, up to a maximum of fifteen.

L2669.text: Rather than renting a car in the city, we took the train and rented one when we got to the countryside.

L2670.text: Customs officials will want to see receipts for anything you bought overseas that's worth more than eight hundred dollars.

L2671.text: My father learned to drive on a stick shift, and he still won't buy a car with an automatic transmission.

L2672.text: Our flight was delayed so long that the crew went over their working hours, and a new crew had to be called in.

L2673.text: The clerk said that without a return address, a package that can't be delivered just ends up in a warehouse.

L2674.text: I'd planned to fly, but by the time I booked, the fares had doubled, so I'm driving the eight hours instead.

L2675.text: The tow truck driver said it would be at least ninety minutes, so we started walking to the gas station two miles back.

L2676.text: Military members can check two bags for free on most airlines when they're traveling on orders.

L2677.text: On this map, one inch equals one mile, so the trail from the camp to the lake is about four miles.

L2678.text: The gas station off base charges twenty cents more per gallon than the one on base, so I always wait to fill up.

L2679.text: Your train ticket includes a seat reservation, so you'll need to sit in car eleven, seat forty-two, not just anywhere.

L2680.text: We wanted to visit the castle, but the last tour bus had already left, so we spent the afternoon in town instead.

L2681.text: These new tires should last fifty thousand miles, as long as you have them rotated every six thousand.

L2682.text: Before we drive into the training area, everyone should mark the rally point on their maps in case we get separated.

L2683.text: Packages over seventy pounds can't go through the post office, so we're shipping the big boxes with a freight company.

L2684.text: Returning the rental car in a different state adds a one-way charge of a hundred and fifty dollars.

L2685.text: The airline let me change my flight for free, but I had to pay the difference in price, which was sixty dollars.

L2686.text: The traffic light at Fifth and Elm has been stuck on red for an hour, and police are directing cars through by hand.

L2687.text: I'll drop you off at departures, park the car in the long-term lot, and meet you at the check-in counter.

L2688.text: Anyone caught speeding on post loses driving privileges for thirty days, no matter how many miles over the limit.

L2689.text: Bicycles are allowed on the commuter train except during rush hour, so I ride to work early and take the train home late.

L2690.text: We'll have to land in Shannon to refuel, so the trip will take about two hours longer than a direct flight.

L2691.text: The cheapest way to send these books home is media mail, but it can take up to two weeks.

L2692.text: The road to the range washes out every time it rains hard, so we'll go in by the north trail tomorrow.

L2693.text: My connecting flight was canceled, so the airline put me on a bus for the last two hundred miles.

L2694.text: Lieutenant Ross can't sign for the vehicle because her military license doesn't cover anything heavier than a pickup.

L2695.text: The highway department closes this pass every November and doesn't reopen it until the snow melts in May.

L2696.text: Leave the keys in the drop box if you return the car after hours, and someone will inspect it in the morning.

L2697.text: The train was so crowded that we stood all the way to the coast, and I'm still sore from it.

L2698.text: You can't drive through the gate without a base sticker, so visitors have to get a pass at the visitor center first.

L2699.text: I tried to buy a ticket at the machine, but it wouldn't take my card, so I paid the conductor on the train.

L2700.text: My mechanic says that grinding noise means the front brake pads are worn out, and I shouldn't drive far until they're replaced.

L2701.text: If you're going downtown, the express bus is quicker, but it doesn't stop at the hospital, so take the number nine.

L2702.text: The bridge has a weight limit of ten tons, so the fuel trucks will have to cross at the dam instead.

L2703.text: I was halfway to the airport before I realized I'd left my phone charger in the hotel room, but I didn't turn back.

L2704.text: Everyone on the trip should be at the bus by oh-seven-thirty; it leaves at oh-seven-forty-five, with or without you.

L2705.text: Our new car gets forty miles per gallon on the highway, which is almost double what our old one got.

L2706.text: Your package will arrive faster if you pay for priority, but regular ground shipping is fine for a birthday that's a month away.

L2707.text: Sick call starts at zero six thirty, but if you're not signed in by seven fifteen, you'll have to come back tomorrow.

L2708.text: I used to run five miles every morning, but since I hurt my knee, I've been swimming laps at the base pool instead.

L2709.text: While the dining facility is closed for renovations next week, hot meals will be served out of the gym instead.

L2710.text: With the wind chill, it'll feel like ten below this morning, so the first sergeant has moved PT indoors.

L2711.text: Before you're allowed to use the power saw in the wood shop, Sergeant Hill has to train you and sign your card.

L2712.text: If someone's nose is bleeding, have them lean forward, not back, and pinch the soft part of the nose for ten minutes.

L2713.text: Our softball game against the medics got rained out, so it's been rescheduled for Thursday evening if the field dries out.

L2714.text: The pharmacy won't have my prescription ready until after lunch, so I'll pick it up on my way back from the range.

L2715.text: If you're on the early shift, the cooks can pack you a boxed lunch, but you have to request it by the night before.

L2716.text: Hurricane season doesn't officially end until November, so keep your emergency kit stocked even though it's been quiet lately.

L2717.text: When you back the truck out of the motor pool, use a ground guide; you can't see the pole behind you from the cab.

L2718.text: For a minor burn, hold it under cool running water for about ten minutes, and whatever you do, don't put ice on it.

L2719.text: I passed the fitness test, but just barely; my run time was only eight seconds under the maximum for my age group.

L2720.text: My flu shot is due, but the clinic's walk-in hours conflict with my shift, so I'll have to make an appointment.

L2721.text: Since they started the healthy menu, the dining facility has replaced the fryer with a grill, and there's a salad bar every day.

L2722.text: The forecast calls for freezing rain overnight, so expect icy roads and a two-hour delay for all nonessential personnel.

L2723.text: Before you pick up that box, bend your knees and keep your back straight; most lifting injuries come from bending at the waist.

L2724.text: If you think someone has heat exhaustion, get them into the shade, loosen their clothing, and have them sip cool water.

L2725.text: I'd rather run on the treadmill than outside this time of year; the trail gets dark by five, and it's muddy besides.

L2726.text: The dentist said my teeth look fine, but I'm overdue for a cleaning, so they've put me on the schedule for next month.

L2727.text: Head count at the dining facility is done by scanning ID cards, so bring yours whenever you come to eat.

L2728.text: It's supposed to hit a hundred and five tomorrow, so the training schedule has been flipped: we'll do the ruck march before dawn.

L2729.text: Fire extinguishers are checked monthly, and if the needle isn't in the green, report it to the building manager right away.

L2730.text: If a bee stings you, scrape the stinger out with a card instead of squeezing it with tweezers, which can push in more venom.

L2731.text: Coach says anyone who misses two practices in a row won't start in Saturday's game, no matter how good they are.

L2732.text: The doctor put me on a profile for my ankle: no running for three weeks, but upper-body exercises are fine.

L2733.text: If you have a food allergy, let the cooks know, because the same spoons are often used for several dishes.

L2734.text: We had our first frost last night, which is early for October; the garden club says to cover any plants you want to keep.

L2735.text: Hearing protection is required on the flight line at all times, even if you're only crossing it to get to the hangar.

L2736.text: If someone is choking but can still cough forcefully, encourage them to keep coughing rather than slapping them on the back.

L2737.text: I signed up for the base marathon, but with only six weeks to train, I'm going to switch to the half instead.

L2738.text: Check that your shot records are current before the deployment briefing; anyone missing a vaccine will get it at the clinic that afternoon.

L2739.text: The dining facility serves breakfast until eight, but on weekends brunch runs from nine to one, and there's no separate lunch.

L2740.text: Lightning was spotted within ten miles, so the range is closed; we'll wait thirty minutes after the last thunder before going back out.

L2741.text: Don't run the generator inside the tent, even for a few minutes; carbon monoxide has no smell, and it can build up fast.

L2742.text: For a sprained ankle, rest it, put ice on it for twenty minutes at a time, and keep it raised above your heart.

L2743.text: The pool is closed for cleaning until Wednesday, so this week's water survival training will be held at the high school instead.

L2744.text: I've had this cough for nearly three weeks now, so I'm finally going to sick call tomorrow instead of waiting it out.

L2745.text: The field kitchen ran out of hot chow before the last platoon got there, so they had to eat packaged rations.

L2746.text: It may be cold on the mountain, but snow reflects the sun's rays, so pack sunscreen and sunglasses for the ski trip.

L2747.text: When the fire alarm goes off, leave by the nearest stairwell, never the elevator, and meet your section in the north parking lot.

L2748.text: If you find someone who isn't breathing, call for help first, then start chest compressions: hard and fast in the center of the chest.

L2749.text: Hydrate the day before a long run, not just that morning; your body needs time to absorb what you drink.

L2750.text: The optometry clinic is booked solid this month, but if you call at seven sharp, they sometimes have same-day cancellations.

L2751.text: Starting Monday, the dining facility will stop serving dinner at six thirty, half an hour earlier than it does now.

L2752.text: Visibility is down to a quarter mile in this fog, so all convoys are on hold until it lifts, probably around ten.

L2753.text: If you're driving on post after dark, slow down near the housing area; kids are out trick-or-treating until eight tonight.

L2754.text: Don't move someone who's fallen from a height unless they're in danger; a neck or back injury could be made much worse.

L2755.text: I can't make the spin class at noon anymore, but the gym just added an evening session, so I'll go to that one.

L2756.text: You'd better wear your mouth guard during combatives; last month two soldiers chipped their teeth, and the dental clinic was swamped.

L2757.text: The dining facility is asking for volunteers to help with Thanksgiving dinner, and anyone who helps will get a day off in December.

L2758.text: Tornado sirens are tested at noon on the first Wednesday of each month, so if you hear them then, don't panic.

L2759.text: Reflective belts are required for anyone running on post roads before sunrise or after sunset, and the MPs are enforcing it.

L2760.text: If a tourniquet is needed, place it two to three inches above the wound, but never directly on a joint like the knee.

L2761.text: Our team lost the volleyball final, but considering we were missing two starters, I think we played pretty well.

L2762.text: If you're taking that cold medicine, don't drive; the label says it can make you drowsy for several hours.

L2763.text: We're out of fresh milk, and the supply truck doesn't come until Thursday, so it's powdered milk or juice until then.

L2764.text: The pollen count is at a record high today, so if you have allergies, keep your windows closed and shower after training outside.

L2765.text: Lock out and tag the power before working on that machine, so nobody can turn it on while your hands are inside.

L2766.text: If someone gets a chemical in their eye, flush it with water for at least fifteen minutes, then get them to the clinic.

L2767.text: The new climbing wall at the gym is open to everyone, but you can't use it until you've watched a short safety video.

L2768.text: My blood pressure was a bit high at my physical, so I'm supposed to eat less salt and get rechecked next month.

L2769.text: The salad bar closes fifteen minutes before the main line does, so if you want salad, don't come at the last minute.

L2770.text: The snow plows clear the main roads first, so if you live in family housing, expect your street to be done last.

L2771.text: Weapons must be cleared at the clearing barrel before entering the building; no exceptions, even if you're just picking something up.

L2772.text: Frostbitten fingers should be warmed slowly in warm, not hot, water, and you should never rub them to get the blood flowing.

L2773.text: Sign-ups for the intramural basketball league close Friday, and each unit can enter only one team, so talk to your first sergeant soon.

L2774.text: If you're feeling stressed or can't sleep, the behavioral health clinic sees walk-ins every weekday morning, no appointment needed.

L2775.text: They've started weighing the food we throw away at the dining facility, and the unit that wastes the least wins a pizza party.

L2776.text: Because of the extreme heat, a black flag is up, so all strenuous outdoor activity is canceled until further notice.

L2777.text: The ice on the lake looks solid, but it's still too thin to walk on, so the recreation office has posted warning signs.

L2778.text: If someone faints, lay them flat on their back and raise their legs about a foot, unless you suspect a head injury.

L2779.text: You're allowed one retake of the swim qualification, but if you fail the second time, you'll have to wait ninety days.

L2780.text: Since the clinic switched to online scheduling, you can book appointments at night, but you can't cancel less than a day ahead.

L2781.text: The cooks had to throw out the chicken because the cooler broke overnight, so tonight's main dish will be spaghetti.

L2782.text: We usually get our first snow by mid-November, but this year it didn't come until after New Year's.

L2783.text: Everyone riding in a tactical vehicle must wear a seat belt, and the vehicle commander is responsible for checking before it moves.

L2784.text: Keep pressing on the wound, and if blood soaks through the bandage, put another one on top instead of taking the first one off.

L2785.text: Stretching is best after your muscles are warm, so jog for five minutes first instead of stretching cold.

L2786.text: I was going to give blood today, but they turned me away because I'd just gotten back from a country with malaria.

L2787.text: Soldiers on meal cards eat for free, but family members and civilians have to pay at the register before going through the line.

L2788.text: It's been so dry this summer that the post has banned outdoor grilling except in the designated picnic areas.

L2789.text: Please don't prop open the stairwell doors; they're fire doors, and they're meant to keep smoke from spreading between floors.

L2790.text: If you suspect heat stroke, don't wait to see if it gets better; call nine-one-one and start cooling the person immediately.

L2791.text: If your shoes have more than four hundred miles on them, replace them; worn-out running shoes are a common cause of shin splints.

L2792.text: The clinic will be closed Monday for the holiday, so get any refills by Friday or use the hospital pharmacy.

L2793.text: I'd rather eat at the dining facility than cook in the barracks; the food's decent, it's free, and I don't have to wash dishes.

L2794.text: Our first sergeant says it's not the heat but the humidity that wears you out down here, so plan on drinking twice as much.

L2795.text: Never mix bleach with other cleaning products when you're cleaning the latrines; some combinations give off toxic gas.

L2796.text: If you think someone is having a stroke, note the time the symptoms started; the doctors will need to know that.

L2797.text: The obstacle course is off-limits until the engineers repair the rope bridge, so we'll run hill sprints this afternoon instead.

L2798.text: If you wake up with a fever, call the clinic instead of coming to work; the last thing we need is the office sick.

L2799.text: Because of the field exercise, breakfast will be served an hour early on Thursday, from five to six instead of six to seven.

L2800.text: The wind is gusting to forty miles an hour, so the parachute jump has been scrubbed, and they'll try again at first light tomorrow.

L2801.text: If you smell gas in your quarters, don't turn on any lights or switches; get out first and then call the fire department.

L2802.text: A first aid kit is useless if it's empty, so tell the supply sergeant whenever you take something out of it.

L2803.text: I was skeptical about yoga, but after a month of classes, my back pain is gone and I sleep better.

L2804.text: Before your hearing test, avoid the firing range for at least fourteen hours, or the results might not be accurate.

L2805.text: The cooks are trying a new menu this month, and they've put comment cards by the exit, so tell them what you think.

L2806.text: Daylight saving time ends this Sunday, so set your clocks back an hour, and don't be surprised when it's dark by five.

L2807.text: Our English class usually meets in Room one-twelve, but this week we'll be in the language lab because they're painting the walls.

L2808.text: I scored a sixty-eight on the practice test, and I need at least seventy-five to qualify for the advanced course.

L2809.text: Unless you hand in your homework before Thursday's class, Mr. Harris won't accept it at all, no matter what your excuse is.

L2810.text: Reading English newspapers was hard for me at first, but after a few months I hardly needed my dictionary anymore.

L2811.text: The listening lab stays open until nine on weeknights, closes at noon on Saturdays, and is closed all day Sunday.

L2812.text: Sergeant Lopez asked me to tutor two new students in grammar, so I'll be staying after class on Mondays and Wednesdays.

L2813.text: If I'd known the final exam would focus on vocabulary, I would have spent less time on verb tenses last week.

L2814.text: Our instructor won't let us use our phones in class, not even to look up a word in a translation app.

L2815.text: The placement test takes about two hours, so eat something beforehand, because you can't leave the room once it starts.

L2816.text: I've been watching American TV shows with English subtitles, and it's helped my listening more than any textbook has.

L2817.text: Class is canceled tomorrow because of the storm, but the instructor still expects your essays by email before midnight.

L2818.text: My roommate speaks English much better than I do, but he gets nervous and freezes whenever he has to give a presentation.

L2819.text: You may use a dictionary on the reading section, but not on the listening section, and phones must stay in your bag.

L2820.text: According to the TV news, the new recycling program won't start until May, so keep putting everything in the regular trash for now.

L2821.text: Students who are absent more than three times this term will have to repeat the course, regardless of their test scores.

L2822.text: Light travels much faster than sound, which is why you see lightning before you hear the thunder.

L2823.text: The new English instructor used to teach pilots in Texas, so her examples are mostly about aviation and radio calls.

L2824.text: The local paper says the new public library downtown won't open until next spring because of construction delays.

L2825.text: Make sure you read chapters four and five before Monday, since the quiz will cover both of them, not just chapter four.

L2826.text: Water boils at a lower temperature on a high mountain, so cooking pasta up there takes longer than at sea level.

L2827.text: The copier on the second floor has been out of order since Monday, so we've all been using the one in the lobby.

L2828.text: I'd rather finish this report tonight than come in early tomorrow, because the inspection team arrives at eight sharp.

L2829.text: I need someone to fill in for me at the front desk this afternoon, since my dental appointment is at two.

L2830.text: The supply room is locked after five, so if you need paper or toner, get it from Mrs. Chen before she leaves.

L2831.text: Mr. Grant was supposed to retire in June, but he agreed to stay on until they find someone to replace him.

L2832.text: Please don't print anything in color unless it's for the commander, because each color page costs ten times as much.

L2833.text: I've been on hold with the travel office for twenty minutes, and nobody has answered yet.

L2834.text: Everyone has to change their computer password every ninety days, and you can't reuse any of your last five.

L2835.text: Before you file these forms, make two copies: one goes to personnel and the other stays in our office.

L2836.text: Our office is moving to Building forty next month, so start packing anything you won't need in the next few weeks.

L2837.text: The new manager is strict about deadlines, but she's very fair, and she always explains why a task is important.

L2838.text: I sent the budget to the colonel this morning, but I accidentally attached last year's numbers instead of this year's.

L2839.text: Hardly anyone uses the fax machine anymore, so the office is getting rid of it at the end of the month.

L2840.text: Since the receptionist is out sick, I'll be answering the main phone line until she comes back on Thursday.

L2841.text: If the director doesn't sign the purchase request by Friday, we'll have to wait until next quarter to buy new desks.

L2842.text: I've filled out this leave form three times already, and personnel keeps sending it back because of small mistakes.

L2843.text: Our team works four ten-hour days, so we're off every Friday, but someone has to be on call by phone.

L2844.text: The meeting room projector keeps shutting off after ten minutes, so maintenance is sending someone to look at it.

L2845.text: I can't find the training schedule anywhere; it must have been deleted when the shared drive was cleaned up.

L2846.text: We're short two people this week, so nobody can take leave until the new clerks report for duty on the fifteenth.

L2847.text: My laptop has been running slowly ever since the update, so I'm going to have the help desk take a look at it.

L2848.text: Always save your work every few minutes, because this old computer sometimes freezes without any warning.

L2856.text: Solar panels still produce some electricity on cloudy days, but far less than they do in bright sunshine.

L2857.text: The software license expires at the end of the month, and the office hasn't decided yet whether to renew it.

L2858.text: I'd rather type my reports than write them by hand, since spell check catches most of my mistakes.

L2859.text: Don't plug your personal flash drive into a government computer; it's against the rules and could spread a virus.

L2861.text: I accidentally deleted the file, but luckily I found it in the recycle bin and restored it.

L2863.text: The new laptops won't arrive until March, so the old ones will have to last another three months.

L2864.text: Every time I try to open the attachment, I get an error message, so could you send it again as a PDF?

L2865.text: Bees are very important to farmers, because many fruits and vegetables can't grow without the pollen they carry.

L2866.text: The technician said my hard drive is nearly full, and that's probably why my computer takes so long to start.

L2867.text: My phone battery dies by noon these days, so I carry a charger with me everywhere I go.

L2868.text: I tried calling you three times last night, but it kept going straight to voicemail.

L2869.text: The Wi-Fi in the barracks is so slow in the evenings that I usually wait until early morning to download anything.

L2870.text: You can't bring cell phones into this building, so leave yours in the locker at the entrance.

L2871.text: I'm moving overseas next month, so I'm canceling my phone plan and switching to an international one.

L2872.text: The video call kept freezing, so we finally turned off our cameras and just talked.

L2873.text: If you'd like to speak to an operator, press zero, or stay on the line and someone will be with you shortly.

L2874.text: I don't have much signal out here at the range, so text me instead of calling if it's urgent.

L2875.text: I bought a cheaper phone online, but it took three weeks to arrive and the screen was cracked.

L2876.text: The newspaper says gas prices should drop next month, now that the refinery near the coast is running again.

L2877.text: Remember that anything you post online can be seen by strangers, so never share your location during a deployment.

L2878.text: My daughter calls me every Sunday, but because of the time difference, it's already Monday morning where I am.

L2879.text: Turn your phones to silent before the ceremony starts, and please don't take pictures until it's over.

L2880.text: The internet bill went up again this month, so I'm thinking about switching to a different provider.

L2881.text: Text messages are fine for quick questions, but for anything important, I'd rather you sent me an email.

L2882.text: I lost my phone at the gym yesterday, and luckily somebody turned it in at the front desk this morning.

L2883.text: Our base app sends alerts about road closures and weather delays, so you might want to download it before winter.

L2884.text: Please keep personal calls short during duty hours, because the phone in this office is for official business.

L2885.text: I hardly ever check my voicemail, so if you need me, send a text and I'll get back to you right away.

L2886.text: The online form keeps rejecting my address because it doesn't recognize the zip code for this base.

L2887.text: The staff meeting has been pushed back to three thirty because the commander's flight landed late.

L2888.text: The training plan was due Friday, but the sergeant major gave us until Tuesday because half the staff was in the field.

L2889.text: Let's keep this meeting short; we only have the conference room until ten, and another group needs it right after us.

L2890.text: I won't be able to make the planning meeting on Thursday, so I'll send Sergeant Ruiz to take notes for me.

L2891.text: We're running behind on the project, so unless we work this Saturday, we'll never finish by the end of the month.

L2892.text: The briefing slides are due to the colonel by noon tomorrow, and he expects them to be checked for spelling errors first.

L2893.text: Nobody took notes at yesterday's meeting, so now we can't agree on what was decided about the new duty roster.

L2894.text: If you have anything to add to the agenda, send it to me by Wednesday afternoon; after that, it'll have to wait.

L2895.text: The monthly report is usually due on the first, but since that's a holiday this time, turn it in the day before.

L2896.text: Our quarterly meeting used to last all morning, but the new director cut it down to forty-five minutes.

L2897.text: I've asked for an extension twice already, so I doubt the captain will give me more time on this assignment.

L2898.text: I thought the application for the leadership course was due next Friday, but it turns out it closed yesterday.

L2899.text: Please don't wait until the last minute to submit your evaluations; the system always slows down right before the deadline.

L2900.text: We'll postpone the safety meeting until next week, since most of the drivers are out on a convoy today.

L2901.text: The radio said the marathon downtown will close Main Street until two this afternoon, so take the side roads to the base.

L2902.text: Doctors recommend that adults sleep seven to nine hours a night, but many people regularly get less than six.

L2903.text: The new weather satellite was launched successfully this morning, and it should start sending pictures back within a few weeks.

L2904.text: Metal expands when it gets hot, so engineers leave small gaps in bridges and railroad tracks.

L2905.text: According to the news, the museum downtown will be free for military families every Saturday this summer.

L2906.text: Phone batteries drain faster in very cold weather, so keep your phone in an inside pocket when you're outdoors in winter.

L2907.text: The jacket was forty dollars off, but the sale ended before I reached the register, so I left it there.

L2908.text: My paycheck usually posts on the first, but because of the holiday it won't show up in my account until Tuesday.

L2909.text: The landlord said he'd fix the leaking faucet this week, but I'd rather call a plumber myself than wait another month.

L2910.text: My brother and I used to fight all the time as kids, but now we talk on the phone almost every day.

L2911.text: We usually host Thanksgiving, but this year my sister has volunteered, so all we have to bring is dessert.

L2912.text: The steak was a little overcooked, but the service was so friendly that I left a bigger tip than usual.

L2913.text: Since I added my son to my car insurance, my monthly payment has gone up by almost a hundred dollars.

L2914.text: We'd planned to adopt a puppy this spring, but our apartment doesn't allow dogs over twenty pounds, so we're getting a cat.

L2915.text: Our new neighbors seem nice enough, though they've parked in our driveway twice this week without asking.

L2916.text: I'd have bought the TV online, but the store matched the website's price, so I picked it up on my way home.

L2917.text: If you use an ATM that isn't part of your bank's network, you'll probably be charged a fee by both banks.

L2918.text: The heater in the basement hardly works anymore, so we're replacing it before the cold weather sets in.

L2919.text: I haven't seen my college roommate in ten years, so when she called to say she was in town, I canceled my plans.

L2920.text: My parents' anniversary party is on the fourteenth, the day after I get back from training, so I can make it.

L2921.text: This recipe calls for fresh basil, but dried will do if you use about a third as much.

L2922.text: The dealer offered me less for my old truck than I expected, so I'm going to try selling it myself.

L2923.text: Whoever watches my dog this weekend should know that he won't eat unless someone stays in the room with him.

L2924.text: The people next door are moving out on Saturday, and they've asked if we'd like their lawn mower for free.

L2925.text: Clearance items can't be returned for a refund, but you can exchange them for another size within thirty days with a receipt.

L2926.text: I'd rather not carry cash when I travel, so I usually let my bank know where I'm going and use my card.

L2927.text: We were supposed to move into the new apartment on the first, but the painters won't be done until the tenth.

L2928.text: My daughter wants to borrow the car for prom night, but I told her she has to be home no later than midnight.

L2929.text: I'm not flying home for the holidays this year because ticket prices nearly doubled, so I'll visit my family in February instead.

L2930.text: We waited forty-five minutes for a table, and by the time we ordered, the kitchen had run out of the special.

L2931.text: My insurance will cover the repairs, but I have to pay the first five hundred dollars before they pay anything.

L2932.text: The vet said our dog is a few pounds overweight, so no more table scraps and twice as many walks.

L2933.text: The neighbor's dog barks every time we open the back door, but he's never once tried to come over the fence.

L2934.text: The price tag says nineteen ninety-nine, but there's an extra twenty percent off at the register this weekend.

L2935.text: I've been putting fifty dollars into savings every payday, and I've finally saved enough for a down payment on a car.

L2936.text: The roofer says the leak isn't serious yet, but if we put off fixing it until spring, the ceiling could be damaged.

L2937.text: My grandmother turns ninety next month, and the whole family is flying in to surprise her, even my cousins from Alaska.

L2938.text: The fireworks were supposed to start at nine, but they were pushed back an hour because of the thunderstorm.

L2939.text: Don't open the oven door while the cake is baking, or it'll sink in the middle no matter how long you leave it.

L2940.text: The used car looks great, but I won't buy it until my mechanic has had a chance to look under the hood.

L2941.text: My cat used to sleep all day, but since we brought home the new kitten, she's been much more active.

L2942.text: Mrs. Lopez across the street has offered to keep an eye on our house while we're on vacation.

L2943.text: I meant to get groceries after work, but the store closes at eight on Sundays, and I didn't leave the office until eight-thirty.

L2944.text: Somebody used my card number at a gas station in another state, so the bank froze my account and is sending a new card.

L2945.text: The apartment is smaller than our last one, but the rent's lower and I can walk to work, so it's worth it.

L2946.text: My best friend is getting married in June, and since his brother can't make it, I'm filling in as best man.

L2947.text: I was going to buy the blender today, but the clerk said it goes on sale next week, so I'm holding off.

L2948.text: These boots are sixty dollars a pair, but if you buy a second pair, it's half price.

L2949.text: The coupon I brought had expired the day before, but the cashier was kind enough to accept it anyway.

L2950.text: Shipping is free on orders over fifty dollars, and since my total was forty-five, I tossed in a pack of batteries.

L2951.text: The salesman kept pushing the extended warranty, but the laptop already comes with two years of coverage, so I said no.

L2952.text: The store had run out of the advertised printer, so they gave me a rain check for the sale price.

L2953.text: The large box of cereal costs only a dollar more than the small one, but it holds twice as much.

L2954.text: The credit union pays almost twice the interest my bank does on savings, so I'm moving my money over there.

L2955.text: I didn't realize my rent check had already cleared, so when I paid for groceries, my account was overdrawn.

L2956.text: You can deposit a check just by taking a picture of it with the bank's app, so there's no need to stand in line.

L2957.text: I lent my cousin three hundred dollars back in March, and so far she's paid back only a third of it.

L2958.text: My wife and I opened a joint account, so either one of us can pay the bills without checking with the other.

L2959.text: Since my husband's hours were cut, we've had to cancel cable and eat out a lot less to make ends meet.

L2960.text: Our lease is up in May, and if the rent goes up again, we'll look for a place closer to the base.

L2961.text: The bank won't approve my son's car loan unless someone with good credit agrees to sign for it with him.

L2962.text: We got three estimates for the new fence, and even the cheapest one was fifteen hundred dollars more than we'd budgeted.
