L2963.text: The landlord kept part of our security deposit because of the holes we'd left in the walls from hanging pictures.

L2964.text: The house was a real bargain, but it's a fixer-upper, so we'll be spending most weekends on repairs for a while.

L2965.text: Whenever I run the microwave and the hair dryer at the same time, the power in the kitchen goes out.

L2966.text: The plumber charges double on weekends, so unless the drip gets worse, we'll wait and call him on Monday.

L2967.text: There's a draft coming in around the bedroom window, so our heating bill has been higher than usual this winter.

L2968.text: My oldest friend is moving overseas next month, so a few of us are throwing him a going-away party on Friday.

L2969.text: My sister asked me to babysit on Saturday, but I'd already promised to help a friend move, so I turned her down.

L2970.text: I almost skipped my twenty-year class reunion, but I'm glad I went, because I got back in touch with old friends.

L2971.text: We give our son ten dollars a week, but he only gets it if he finishes his chores.

L2972.text: My father finally retired after thirty years at the plant, and now he can't sit still for more than an hour.

L2973.text: My in-laws are staying with us for two weeks, so we're giving them our bedroom and sleeping on the couch ourselves.

L2974.text: We're having a cookout on the Fourth, so if you're free, come by any time after two and bring the kids.

L2975.text: We bought six bags of candy for Halloween, but because of the rain, only a handful of kids came to the door.

L2976.text: I usually wait until the last minute to buy Christmas presents, but this year I finished in October to beat the crowds.

L2977.text: Every January I promise myself I'll go to the gym, but by February I've usually given up.

L2978.text: My niece graduates from high school on Saturday, and the whole family is chipping in to buy her a laptop for college.

L2979.text: If we leave right after work on Wednesday, we'll get stuck in holiday traffic, so let's head out early Thursday morning instead.

L2980.text: We'd planned a surprise party for my wife's birthday, but my son mentioned it at dinner, so now she knows all about it.

L2981.text: When the check came, my boss insisted on picking up the tab, so the rest of us just covered the tip.

L2982.text: That new Italian place doesn't take reservations, so if we want a table on Friday night, we'd better get there before six.

L2983.text: Could you ask the chef whether the sauce has peanuts in it? My daughter's allergic, and even a little can make her sick.

L2984.text: The turkey needs about four hours in the oven, so if we want to eat at six, it has to go in by two.

L2985.text: The portions there are so huge that I always end up taking half my dinner home for lunch the next day.

L2986.text: I tried baking bread from scratch for the first time, but it came out of the oven as hard as a rock.

L2987.text: Leasing would mean lower monthly payments, but since I drive so many miles for work, buying makes more sense for me.

L2988.text: My wife does most of the cooking during the week, but on weekends I take over the kitchen so she gets a break.

L2989.text: The dealer offered zero percent financing, but only if I paid two thousand dollars up front.

L2990.text: The other driver ran a red light and hit me, so his insurance company is paying for all my repairs.

L2991.text: The sticker price was twenty-four thousand, but after some bargaining, the salesman knocked off fifteen hundred.

L2992.text: My insurance company takes ten percent off if I complete a safe-driving class, so I signed up for one this weekend.

L2993.text: The hybrid costs about three thousand more than the regular model, but I'll save that much on gas within two years.

L2994.text: My car will be in the shop for a week, and luckily my policy covers a rental while it's being fixed.

L2995.text: Our cat kept scratching the couch until we bought her a scratching post, and now she leaves the furniture alone.

L2996.text: The kennel charges thirty-five dollars a night, so it's cheaper to pay my nephew to stay with our dog.

L2997.text: Adopting a dog from the shelter costs a hundred dollars, but that includes shots and a microchip, so it's a good deal.

L2998.text: I forgot to feed my son's goldfish while he was at camp, but luckily they can go a few days without food.

L2999.text: The neighbors upstairs had a party until three in the morning, and I had to be at work by seven.

L3000.text: Our puppy used to chew everything in sight, but after six weeks of obedience classes, he's a different dog.

L3001.text: Every time it snows, my son shovels the walk for the elderly couple next door, and he won't take a dime for it.

L3002.text: Our neighbor borrowed my ladder back in April, and I still haven't gotten it back, so I'll have to go ask for it.

L3003.text: When the new family moved in across the street, we brought over a plate of cookies to introduce ourselves.

L3004.text: A branch from our neighbor's oak tree fell on our garage roof, and we're not sure whose insurance should pay for it.

L3005.text: The homeowners association fined us fifty dollars because we left our trash cans out by the curb for two days.

L3006.text: The neighbors are having a yard sale this Saturday, so expect cars parked up and down our street all morning.

L3007.text: The convoy left the depot at zero six hundred and needs about four and a half hours to reach the range.

L3008.text: We ordered sixty cases of water for the exercise, but only forty-five arrived, so supply is sending the rest tomorrow.

L3009.text: The running shoes were marked ninety dollars, but the store gave me ten percent off for showing my military ID.

L3010.text: Our team was behind by six points at halftime, but we outscored them by ten in the second half.

L3011.text: Unless the fuel truck gets here by fourteen hundred, we won't have enough diesel to run the generators through the night.

L3012.text: The second shipment of tents weighs twice as much as the first, which came to eight hundred pounds.

L3013.text: I'd planned to call it a day at five, but the inventory count still doesn't match, so I'm staying until it does.

L3014.text: If we march at four kilometers an hour, we should cover the twelve kilometers to the range by zero nine hundred.

L3015.text: Batteries are buy two, get one free this week, and each pack costs four dollars, so I picked up nine packs.

L3016.text: We were supposed to finish loading the trailers by noon, but with three drivers out sick, we're running way behind schedule.

L3017.text: The PX doesn't open until ten on Sundays, so if you need boot polish for Sunday's nine o'clock formation, buy it today.

L3018.text: Our soccer team has won eight of its twelve games this season, twice as many as the team won all last year.

L3019.text: Hardly any of the new radios passed inspection; only three out of the twenty we received work properly.

L3020.text: I'll take over the night shift at the warehouse provided that someone covers my morning shift on Friday.

L3021.text: The bus to the range leaves every forty minutes starting at six fifteen, and I just missed the seven thirty-five.

L3022.text: The new boots cost more than the old model did, but they last nearly twice as long, so we save money in the end.

L3023.text: Order one water can for every four soldiers in the platoon, plus two extras; there are thirty-six of us.

L3024.text: The scoreboard says we lost, three to two, but the referee didn't count our last goal because time had already run out.

L3025.text: Recruits must finish the obstacle course in under nine minutes; Jones did it in eight minutes forty seconds, and Smith took forty seconds longer.

L3026.text: The store had sold out of the large tarps, so I bought two medium ones instead; together they cover the same area.

L3027.text: The flight with our spare parts was supposed to land at eleven hundred, but it's been delayed three and a half hours.

L3028.text: I drove the forty miles to the depot in under an hour, but coming back in heavy traffic took nearly two.

L3029.text: Our softball team scored more runs in the last inning than in the first eight combined, and we still lost by one.

L3030.text: Every vehicle gets an oil change after three thousand miles, and this truck has gone twenty-eight hundred since its last one.

L3031.text: These cots are on sale for thirty-five dollars each, but if you buy five or more, they drop to thirty.

L3032.text: The company ran the two-mile course in an average of fifteen minutes, a full minute faster than last month.

L3033.text: No one may sign out a rifle from the arms room unless their name is on the range roster for that day.

L3034.text: The warehouse used to ship orders within two days, but since we've been short-handed, it's taking closer to five.

L3035.text: I won't start packing the trucks until the lieutenant confirms the departure time, which should be after lunch.

L3036.text: Our basketball team needs to win four of its last five games just to make the playoffs, and we've already lost one.

L3037.text: Each case of rations holds twelve meals, and we need two meals a day for thirty soldiers over a four-day exercise.

L3038.text: The commissary is closed on Mondays; otherwise it's open nine to seven, except Sundays, when it closes at five.

L3039.text: My platoon finished the ruck march in second place, just three minutes behind first and well ahead of the other five platoons.

L3040.text: If you return the tent within thirty days, you get your money back; after that, it's store credit only, up to ninety days.

L3041.text: The new fuel cans hold five gallons, a gallon more than the old ones, and we're issuing two per vehicle.

L3042.text: We're not as far behind schedule as I thought; only two of the eight containers are still waiting to be unloaded.

L3043.text: The marathon started at seven, and my husband crossed the finish line at ten forty-five, twenty minutes faster than last year.

L3044.text: The supply sergeant says we can have either the new sleeping bags or the extra blankets, but not both, so I chose the bags.

L3045.text: Parts ordered before noon ship the same day, but anything ordered after that won't go out until the following morning.

L3046.text: We have a hundred and eighty kilometers left to the port, and the convoy averages sixty an hour, so dinner will be late.

L3047.text: I paid forty-eight dollars for this rain jacket at the PX, which was twenty percent off the original price.

L3048.text: The lieutenant said we'd stay in the field until the generator is fixed, and the mechanic can't come for at least two days.

L3049.text: Our volleyball team beat the engineers twice this season, but we've never won against the medics in three tries.

L3050.text: As soon as the last pallet is on the truck, call the dispatcher; she won't send a driver until she hears from you.

L3051.text: We lost the first softball game seven to two, but in the rematch we turned it around and won by the same margin.

L3052.text: I need to be at the airfield by fifteen hundred, and it's a forty-minute drive, so I'll leave no later than fourteen fifteen.

L3053.text: The hardware store charges three dollars a foot for that rope, and I need fifty feet, but I only have a hundred dollars.

L3054.text: No sooner had we set up the tents than the order came to pack up and move to a new location.

L3055.text: Of the hundred and twenty soldiers in the company, a quarter are on leave, and another ten are away at training courses.

L3056.text: The coach will let you skip Thursday's practice provided that you show up an hour early on Friday.

L3057.text: Last month we issued a third as many pairs of cold-weather boots as gloves, and we gave out three hundred pairs of gloves.

L3058.text: The game started at seven, and since our bus didn't leave until six forty for the fifty-minute ride, we missed the kickoff.

L3059.text: The range was set for Tuesday, but the ammunition truck broke down, so everything has been pushed back two days.

L3060.text: These batteries last about eight hours in normal weather, but in the cold they lose almost half their life.

L3061.text: Everything in the store is twenty-five percent off today, and members get an extra ten dollars off any purchase over fifty.

L3062.text: I've been on the phone with three suppliers, and not one of them can deliver the sandbags before the end of the month.

L3063.text: The trail is twelve miles round trip, and we hike about three miles an hour; we'll stop for lunch at the halfway point.

L3064.text: We can't load the ship until customs clears the cargo, and they don't work weekends, so it'll be Monday at the earliest.

L3065.text: Our unit ran out of drinking water on the second day, so next time we'll bring one and a half times as much.

L3066.text: Ten of us signed up for the ski trip, but the van only holds eight, so two people will have to drive themselves.

L3067.text: The quartermaster is so short-handed this week that uniform exchanges will be done only on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

L3068.text: My goal is to run three miles in under twenty-four minutes, and I did the first two in seven and eight minutes.

L3069.text: The warehouse holds four hundred pallets and is three-quarters full, but a shipment of a hundred and fifty arrives tomorrow.

L3070.text: Neither the forklift nor the pallet jack is working, so we'll have to unload these crates by hand.

L3071.text: My brother's team was in first place until the last game, when they lost and dropped two spots in the standings.

L3072.text: The fuel point is open from zero six hundred to eighteen hundred, but it shuts down for an hour at noon.

L3073.text: I'd rather pay the extra twenty dollars for next-day shipping than wait a week, since the exercise starts Monday.

L3074.text: The machine gun team scored thirty-eight hits out of fifty targets, two more than they needed to qualify.

L3075.text: Hardly anyone bought the new energy bars at the PX, so they've been marked down from three dollars to a dollar fifty.

L3076.text: Before we can leave the field, every weapon has to be cleaned, and nobody gets on the bus until the armorer checks it.

L3077.text: This laundry detergent costs twelve dollars for a hundred loads, while that one is eight dollars for fifty.

L3078.text: The new recruits arrive on the fifth, but their training won't start until ten days later, once their gear is issued.

L3079.text: We'd planned to work until eight, but since the parts never came, the sergeant had us call it a day at four.

L3080.text: Our convoy averaged fifty kilometers an hour on the highway, but only half that speed once we hit the mountain roads.

L3081.text: If the rain doesn't let up by morning, the soccer final will be played Sunday instead, unless the field is still flooded.

L3082.text: We received two hundred helmets, but forty were the wrong size, and we've sent those back to the supplier.

L3083.text: The commissary sells eggs for three dollars a dozen, but the farm stand outside the gate sells them for two fifty.

L3084.text: Yesterday's ammunition count was off by eighty rounds, but today's is off by only a quarter of that, so we're getting closer.

L3085.text: The parade starts at ten, the band must be in position forty-five minutes earlier, and the bus ride takes half an hour.

L3086.text: We have enough rations for four days, but if the exercise is extended, we'll have to cut back to two meals a day.

L3087.text: Our hockey team has played twelve games this season, winning seven and tying two, which puts us third in the league.

L3088.text: The first sergeant wants the motor pool cleaned before anyone leaves, and at this rate, we'll be here past dark.

L3089.text: This store charges five dollars for delivery, but it's free on orders of eighty dollars or more, and my cart comes to seventy-two.

L3090.text: The general's visit was moved up from Friday to Wednesday, so we have two fewer days to get the warehouse ready.

L3091.text: Gas was three dollars a gallon last week, but it's gone up twenty cents, and my truck's tank holds fifteen gallons.

L3092.text: We didn't get the replacement parts until Thursday, and by then the truck had missed the convoy, which left on Tuesday.

L3093.text: There are five of us on the relay team, each runner covers four hundred meters, and our best time is just under seven minutes.

L3094.text: I had hoped to get the tires for under four hundred dollars, but the cheapest set was four fifty, plus fifty for installation.

L3095.text: You'll get your new uniforms as soon as the order arrives, which won't be until the end of the month at the earliest.

L3096.text: Our rifle team placed fourth out of twelve, which is better than last year, when we didn't even make the top half.

L3097.text: It's twenty-two miles to the training site, and the shuttle averages forty-four miles an hour, so it's a short ride.

L3098.text: The supply clerk will no longer accept handwritten requests; from now on, everything has to go through the online system.

L3099.text: If we finish loading by sixteen hundred, we can make the six o'clock ferry; otherwise, the next one isn't until nine.

L3100.text: I'd have bought the tent if it were on sale, but at two hundred dollars, it's way more than I want to spend.

L3101.text: The forecast says the storm will hit around fifteen hundred, so let's have the trucks unloaded at least an hour before that.

L3102.text: Our team lost by a goal on Saturday, but since the other team played an ineligible player, we were awarded the win.

L3103.text: Each truck can carry six pallets, and we have thirty-two to move, so we'll need a sixth truck for the leftovers.

L3104.text: Admission to the base football game is four dollars, but children under twelve and anyone in uniform get in free.

L3105.text: We usually inventory the supply room once a quarter, but after last month's missing items, the captain wants it done every month.

L3106.text: The last bus to base leaves the mall at nine forty-five, and the stop is a fifteen-minute walk from the theater.

L3107.text: Do you know if the bus to the range leaves from the gym or the battalion parking lot?

L3108.text: How come you didn't qualify? You were hitting everything during practice yesterday.

L3109.text: Would you mind taking my place in the tower so I can grab some water?

L3110.text: Isn't it a little early to be zeroing our rifles if we don't qualify until spring?

L3111.text: Why are the targets on lane six still up? I thought the range was cold.

L3112.text: We're out of earplugs at this end of the firing line. Could you bring a box over?

L3113.text: You picked up your brass before leaving the firing point, didn't you?

L3114.text: Do you know whether we're allowed to bring our own scopes to the qualification range?

L3115.text: If this fog doesn't lift soon, will they still run the morning qualification?

L3116.text: Which relay are you in? I want to make sure we're not firing at the same time.

L3117.text: How come the first sergeant moved PT to the afternoon this week?

L3118.text: Did you pass the push-up event, or do you have to retest next month?

L3119.text: Would you mind holding my feet for the sit-ups? My partner hasn't shown up.

L3120.text: I can't believe they want us to do a six-mile run the day after the road march.

L3121.text: Do you know whether the gym is open early enough for us to work out before formation?

L3122.text: How long has your shoulder kept you out of PT?

L3123.text: Wasn't Sergeant Moore supposed to lead PT this morning? Where is he?

L3124.text: What time do you need to beat for the two-mile run in your age group?

L3125.text: Why don't we run the hill route today instead of going around the track again?

L3126.text: Are we still doing PT outside, or did they move it into the gym because of the ice?

L3127.text: Do you happen to know who's doing the inspection, the platoon sergeant or the commander?

L3128.text: How come my wall locker failed? Everything was hung up exactly the way they showed us.

L3129.text: The inspector's coming through in ten minutes, and your bed still isn't made.

L3130.text: Did the inspectors say anything about the oil leak under the second truck?

L3131.text: Would you mind looking over my uniform before I go in front of the promotion board?

L3132.text: Why does the first sergeant always find dust on top of the door frames?

L3133.text: Has anyone told you when the motor pool inspection is, or is it a surprise?

L3134.text: You've got a thread hanging off your sleeve. Want me to cut it off?

L3135.text: Didn't the team that inspected our arms room find a few problems with the paperwork?

L3136.text: How did your room do on the fire safety inspection last night?

L3137.text: Can we wear our fleece jackets in formation yet, or is it too early in the season?

L3138.text: Supply ran out of my boot size. What am I supposed to wear to the field?

L3139.text: How come your helmet cover is a different color from everyone else's?

L3140.text: Would you mind signing for the GPS units while I load the water cans?

L3141.text: Is it okay to wear civilian clothes to the dining facility on weekends?

L3142.text: My sleeping bag zipper broke on the last trip. Where do I get it fixed?

L3143.text: Do you know if we're supposed to sew rank on the new jackets, or pin it?

L3144.text: Whose rucksack is this? It's been sitting by the door since yesterday.

L3145.text: Do we have enough cold-weather gear for everyone, or should I order more?

L3146.text: How long should it take to get my new uniforms if I order them today?

L3147.text: Do you know why nobody at the gate is answering on channel four?

L3148.text: Can you read me now, or is there still a lot of static on your end?

L3149.text: Who's supposed to be on the radio tonight while the lieutenant is at the briefing?

L3150.text: Isn't it about time we changed the batteries in these handsets?

L3151.text: What's the call sign for the medical team? I don't want to get it wrong.

L3152.text: How come we have to keep radio silence until we reach the checkpoint?

L3153.text: Would you mind doing the radio checks this morning? My voice is almost gone.

L3154.text: The radio in truck three keeps cutting out. Should I take it to the repair shop?

L3155.text: Did anyone copy the grid coordinates the patrol sent a minute ago?

L3156.text: You keep holding the talk button down, so nobody else can get on the net.

L3157.text: Do you know who's relieving you at the gate at midnight?

L3158.text: What should I do if someone shows up without an ID card?

L3159.text: Aren't you supposed to keep a log of every vehicle that comes through the gate?

L3160.text: How long is each shift on guard this weekend, two hours or four?

L3161.text: I can't stay awake on these night shifts at the gate. What do you do?

L3162.text: The sergeant of the guard said we can't use our phones on post, right?

L3163.text: Would you mind trading guard shifts with me on Friday? My parents are visiting.

L3164.text: How come there are two guards at the back gate tonight instead of one?

L3165.text: Did you remember to sign the guard roster before you went on post?

L3166.text: You look exhausted. Weren't you on guard duty all last night?

L3167.text: Do you know if the safety briefing before the long weekend is mandatory for everyone?

L3168.text: Where's the operations briefing being held, since the conference room is being painted?

L3169.text: Why did the commander's briefing go on for so long this morning?

L3170.text: I missed the convoy briefing. Is there anyone who can fill me in?

L3171.text: Are we supposed to bring anything to tomorrow's briefing, or do we just show up?

L3172.text: Could you put the slides for the weather briefing on the shared drive tonight?

L3173.text: You're giving the brief to the colonel tomorrow, aren't you? Are you nervous?

L3174.text: How come they're holding the morning briefing outside when it's this cold?

L3175.text: Did the briefing say what time the buses leave for the training area?

L3176.text: I think the captain's briefing has been canceled, but I'm not totally sure.

L3177.text: Do you know yet whether your unit is deploying in the spring or the fall?

L3178.text: How are you going to stay in touch with your family while you're overseas?

L3179.text: Isn't it hard to leave your kids for nine months at a time?

L3180.text: Have you finished packing your gear, or do you need a hand with anything?

L3181.text: When is the advance party supposed to fly out, before or after the holidays?

L3182.text: Did you get all your shots before deploying, or do you still need some?

L3183.text: Do you know how many bags we're allowed to bring on the flight over?

L3184.text: Who's going to take care of your car while you're deployed?

L3185.text: You must be glad to be home after such a long deployment.

L3186.text: How come your deployment got extended? I thought you were coming back in May.

L3187.text: Has your leave request been approved yet, or is it still on the first sergeant's desk?

L3188.text: Are you planning to use up your leave before you change units, or sell it back?

L3189.text: Would you mind signing my leave form before you go to lunch?

L3190.text: Do you know if I can take leave during the holidays if I'm on the duty roster?

L3191.text: Why did your leave get denied? You put it in two months ago.

L3192.text: If I take leave next week, who's going to cover my shift in the motor pool?

L3193.text: Is it true that you have to be back from leave a day before the field exercise?

L3194.text: Are you going home on leave, or are you just staying around here?

L3195.text: Can I still get emergency leave if my father is in the hospital?

L3196.text: Do you think the captain would approve a three-day pass for my wedding anniversary?

L3197.text: Do you know whether the post office on base is open on Saturday mornings?

L3198.text: My ID card expires next week. Do I need an appointment to renew it?

L3199.text: Why can't I log on to my computer this morning? Did they change something overnight?

L3200.text: Wasn't the staff meeting supposed to start at ten? Nobody's here yet.

L3201.text: How come my paycheck was smaller this month? I didn't change anything.

L3202.text: Do you know how long the waiting list is for family housing on post?

L3203.text: I have a dental appointment at two. Would you mind covering the phones until I get back?

L3204.text: Where do I turn in these leave forms once the commander has signed them?

L3205.text: Your phone's been ringing all morning. Aren't you going to answer it?

L3206.text: This package has to reach Germany by Friday. What's the fastest way to send it?

L3207.text: I left my ID card in the computer at work. Can I still get through the gate?

L3208.text: Can you take notes at the budget meeting? I have to be at the hospital.

L3209.text: Is it true the finance office won't cash personal checks anymore?

L3210.text: The heater in my quarters has been broken for a week. Who should I call?

L3211.text: I'm afraid I can't make our appointment on Thursday. Could we do Monday instead?

L3212.text: Do you happen to know who's in charge of fixing the printers in this building?

L3213.text: Are we allowed to mail batteries overseas, or will they send the box back?

L3214.text: They told me at the ID card office that the system is down again.

L3215.text: Should I bring printed copies of the slides, or will everyone see them on the screen?

L3216.text: I filed my travel claim a month ago. Shouldn't I have been paid by now?

L3217.text: You haven't seen a blue folder with my name on it lying around, have you?

L3218.text: Do you think we could move the training schedule review up to this afternoon?

L3219.text: Would you mind showing me how to attach a file to this e-mail?

L3220.text: Isn't it a little early to start packing? Your move isn't until next month.

L3221.text: How much would it cost to send these photos to my parents in Texas?

L3222.text: My wife's dependent ID was stolen. What does she need to bring to replace it?

L3223.text: Who's going to run the meeting while the colonel is on leave?

L3224.text: Do you know if we get paid early when payday falls on a holiday?

L3225.text: Can you remind me what time I'm supposed to pick up the general at the airport?

L3226.text: My laptop keeps shutting down in the middle of my work. Any idea what's wrong?

L3227.text: We're thinking about living off post. Does housing help you find an apartment?

L3228.text: I got a notice saying they tried to deliver a package. Where do I pick it up?

L3229.text: Wouldn't it be quicker to make an appointment than to stand in line all morning?

L3230.text: I'm going to be about ten minutes late for the meeting. Could you let them know?

L3231.text: Do I really have to fill out this whole form just to borrow a projector?

L3232.text: Where would I go to set up an allotment so part of my pay goes to my mother?

L3233.text: This phone won't hold a charge for more than a couple of hours. Is it the battery?

L3234.text: I thought you swapped shifts with Sergeant Long. How come you're here so early?

L3235.text: Excuse me, is this the right office for getting a copy of my orders?

L3236.text: Have you noticed how slow the internet has been since they moved our offices?

L3237.text: We're moving to Fort Bliss next month. How do I get our mail forwarded?

L3238.text: My wife changed her last name when we married. Does she need a new ID?

L3239.text: I typed my PIN wrong three times and now I'm locked out. What do I do?

L3240.text: I opened an account at a new bank. How do I change my direct deposit?

L3241.text: Are we allowed to have a dog in base housing, or is that against the rules?

L3242.text: Did you remember to reserve the conference room for Wednesday's planning meeting?

L3243.text: The clinic called to move my physical to Tuesday, but I've got a range day then.

L3244.text: Do you know where I can get this power of attorney notarized on post?

L3245.text: I tried calling Sergeant Wong, but his voicemail is full. Do you know another way to reach him?

L3246.text: Can you help me read this pay statement? I can't tell what these deductions are.

L3247.text: When is the housing inspector coming? I want the place spotless before I clear quarters.

L3248.text: Who's supposed to send out the minutes from yesterday's meeting? I haven't seen them.

L3249.text: Our son turns ten next month. Does he need his own ID card now?

L3250.text: Did you finish the online security training? It's due by the end of the week.

L3251.text: My package arrived with the box torn open. Should I complain to the post office?

L3252.text: Is block leave still starting on the twentieth, or did they change the dates again?

L3253.text: Is there any chance I could turn in the inventory report on Monday instead of today?

L3254.text: Our household goods won't arrive for six weeks. Does housing lend out furniture in the meantime?

L3255.text: Is it all right to use my work phone for personal calls once in a while?

L3256.text: We lost the connection with the other base again. Should we just finish this by phone?

L3257.text: I lost the key to my post office box. Will they make me pay for a new one?

L3258.text: The card reader won't read my ID anymore. Do you think the chip is damaged?

L3259.text: I keep getting messages that my inbox is full. How do I clear some space?

L3260.text: Is it a good idea to take advance pay for my move, or will I regret it later?

L3261.text: The smoke detector in our hallway keeps beeping every few minutes. Is it broken?

L3262.text: Is the safety briefing this afternoon mandatory, or can I skip it if I'm busy?

L3263.text: Do you know if the nine o'clock call is nine our time or their time?

L3264.text: The colonel's out until Friday. Is there anyone else who can sign this request?

L3265.text: I cracked the screen on my phone this morning. Can it be repaired on post?

L3266.text: Do I have to fill out a customs form to mail a package to an APO address?

L3267.text: I was promoted two months ago, but my pay still hasn't gone up. Is that normal?

L3268.text: Are utilities included in the rent for on-post housing, or do we pay separately?

L3269.text: My computer wants to restart for an update. Can I put it off until after lunch?

L3270.text: Who's giving the briefing to the general tomorrow, you or Captain Ruiz?

L3271.text: My parents are visiting next week. Where do they get passes to come on base?

L3272.text: I need a haircut before the ceremony Friday. Do they take appointments at the barbershop?

L3273.text: They sent my form back because it was an old version. Where's the new one?

L3274.text: Will the per diem for the conference cover meals, or just the hotel?

L3275.text: Wouldn't it be safer to send those documents certified, so someone has to sign for them?

L3276.text: I just got an e-mail asking for my password. That's not from our IT people, is it?

L3277.text: What should I do with these old personnel files? Can they go in the regular trash?

L3278.text: Is Friday's meeting still on? I heard the major might be called away.

L3279.text: Do you happen to know the password for the guest Wi-Fi in this building?

L3280.text: If I reenlist this year, will I get the whole bonus at once or in payments?

L3281.text: The neighbors upstairs play loud music every night. Is there anything housing can do?

L3282.text: The line at the post office is out the door. Is there a stamp machine somewhere?

L3283.text: I hate the picture on my new ID card. Can I ask them to take another one?

L3284.text: My car inspection is due this month. Do I need an appointment, or can I just show up?

L3285.text: Do you know when we're supposed to get our tax forms for this year?

L3286.text: Has anyone sent out the agenda for tomorrow, or are we just going to wing it?

L3287.text: Do you know whether the shuttle to the terminal still runs after midnight?

L3288.text: How come you rented such a small car for a five-hour drive?

L3289.text: Would you mind keeping an eye on my bags while I check the departure board?

L3290.text: The forecast says snow in the pass tonight. Shouldn't we wait until morning to drive?

L3291.text: Excuse me, is this the right line for passengers connecting to international flights?

L3292.text: Did you remember to pack the adapters, or will we have to buy some there?

L3293.text: Isn't the hotel supposed to have a shuttle from the airport?

L3294.text: Do you happen to know how long it takes to drive to the coast from here?

L3295.text: Our flight's been canceled. Should we try to rebook or just rent a car?

L3296.text: Do you think I'll need a visa, or is my military ID enough?

L3297.text: Could you tell me which bus goes downtown? This map is really confusing.

L3298.text: You've driven on the left side of the road before, haven't you?

L3299.text: I can't find my passport anywhere. You didn't pack it in your bag, did you?

L3300.text: Why is traffic so heavy on the highway this afternoon?

L3301.text: Would you rather take the night train or fly out early tomorrow morning?

L3302.text: Is there a gas station between here and the airport, do you know?

L3303.text: The hotel lost our reservation. Do you want to look for another place?

L3304.text: How come the train hasn't left yet? It was supposed to depart at nine.

L3305.text: Can you give me directions to the post exchange? I'm new here.

L3306.text: We'd better leave early tomorrow, don't you think? The bridge will be jammed.

L3307.text: Do you know if they'll let me carry this camera bag onto the plane?

L3308.text: I missed my connection in Chicago. What are my options at this point?

L3309.text: How far is the nearest rest area? I've been driving for four hours.

L3310.text: Wasn't our gate changed? The screen says B twelve, but the ticket says C four.

L3311.text: Would you mind turning the air conditioning down? I'm freezing back here.

L3312.text: You booked a room with two beds, not one, didn't you?

L3313.text: Is it true that the coastal highway is closed because of the flooding?

L3314.text: Excuse me, which platform does the express to the city leave from?

L3315.text: How come you're taking the bus? I thought your car was fixed.

L3316.text: Should I bring a heavy coat, or will it be warm where we're going?

L3317.text: Have you heard whether our flight is delayed because of the storm?

L3318.text: Let me help you with that suitcase. It looks heavier than you are.

L3319.text: Do you mind if we stop for coffee before we get on the interstate?

L3320.text: Why don't we take a taxi instead of waiting for the hotel van?

L3321.text: I heard the rental company charges extra if we return the car late. Is that right?

L3322.text: Did they say how long the road would be closed for repairs?

L3323.text: Wouldn't it be cheaper to fly than to take the train across the country?

L3324.text: Could you remind me what time we have to check out of the hotel?

L3325.text: Is this seat taken, or can I put my bag here?

L3326.text: Didn't you say the hotel was within walking distance of the station?

L3327.text: Do you know whether we need exact change for the city bus?

L3328.text: I'm not sure I can find the hotel without GPS. Can you give me some landmarks?

L3329.text: How long have you been waiting for your luggage to come out?

L3330.text: Are you sure we're going the right way? We've passed that sign twice.

L3331.text: Can you believe they want forty dollars to check a second bag?

L3332.text: Would it be possible to get a room on a lower floor?

L3333.text: Why do we have to go through security again? We never left the airport.

L3334.text: Isn't it a little early to leave for the airport? The flight isn't until four.

L3335.text: Would you like me to drive for a while so you can rest?

L3336.text: Have they started boarding yet, or do we still have time to grab a bite?

L3337.text: Do you know where I can exchange dollars for local currency around here?

L3338.text: You look exhausted. Didn't you get any sleep on the overnight flight?

L3339.text: Are we allowed to park here, or is this space reserved for buses?

L3340.text: Which would you prefer, the scenic route along the river or the faster highway?

L3341.text: Do you have your boarding pass on your phone, or did you print it out?

L3342.text: How come the bus didn't stop? We were standing right at the sign.

L3343.text: How long do you think the line at the border crossing will be this morning?

L3344.text: Would you mind checking whether the hotel has a gym before we book?

L3345.text: I left my sunglasses in the rental car. Is it too late to get them back?

L3346.text: Could you tell me whether this train stops at the airport?

L3347.text: Doesn't the speed limit drop to forty-five once you get into town?

L3348.text: Who's picking us up when we land, your brother or a taxi?

L3349.text: The rental agent says all the compact cars are gone. Do you mind a van?

L3350.text: Is it true you have to show your passport to check into hotels there?

L3351.text: What time do you think we should set off to beat the rush hour?

L3352.text: You did call the airline about your seat assignment, didn't you?

L3353.text: The road ahead looks icy. Do you want me to slow down a bit?

L3354.text: Do you know if the hotel offers free breakfast, or is it extra?

L3355.text: Did you notice the tire pressure light come on when we got off the highway?

L3356.text: How come they moved our seats? We booked them months ago.

L3357.text: Shall I call ahead and tell the hotel we'll be arriving late?

L3358.text: Which line should I get in if I've already checked in online?

L3359.text: Could you look up whether there's construction on the road to the base?

L3360.text: I've never traveled abroad before. What's the first thing I should do?

L3361.text: There's an accident up ahead. Is there another way to get to the stadium?

L3362.text: My suitcase is over the weight limit. What would you take out?

L3363.text: Don't you think it's a bit risky to drive through the mountains in this fog?

L3364.text: Do you know whether the trains are running on a holiday schedule today?

L3365.text: I'm afraid I've locked the keys in the rental car. What should we do?

L3366.text: Excuse me, are there any direct flights to Dallas, or do they all stop somewhere?

L3367.text: We've been sitting at this light forever. Do you think it's broken?

L3368.text: Will the hotel let us check in early if our room is ready?

L3369.text: Did you hear the announcement? I think they said our gate was changed.

L3370.text: How long would it take to walk to the museum from our hotel?

L3371.text: You remembered to fill up the tank before returning the car, right?

L3372.text: Why don't you put your liquids in a clear bag before we reach security?

L3373.text: How come your bag came out first? We checked them in at the same time.

L3374.text: Would you rather sit by the window or on the aisle for this flight?

L3375.text: Is it going to be a problem if our train arrives after the last bus?

L3376.text: Have you ever stayed at the hotel near the base gate? Is it any good?

L3377.text: Do you know whether your parents are still planning to visit us this summer?

L3378.text: How come the grocery bill is so high? We only bought a few things.

L3379.text: You're not still going to play soccer this afternoon with that sprained wrist, are you?

L3380.text: Would you mind if we sat out on the patio instead of near the kitchen?

L3381.text: The new neighbors' dog barked all night again. Shouldn't somebody say something to them?

L3382.text: We're having a few people over for the Fourth of July. Can you and your husband make it?

L3383.text: Is it true the commissary gives you a discount if you bring your own bags?

L3384.text: Has anybody figured out why the kitchen sink keeps backing up?

L3385.text: How about going bowling with us Friday night, unless you've got other plans?

L3386.text: Excuse me, I ordered my steak well done, but this one is still pink inside.

L3387.text: Didn't you say your old roommate from basic training was coming to town this week?

L3388.text: Do you think it's too late to send out invitations for Saturday's birthday party?

L3389.text: Wouldn't it be cheaper to buy the TV online instead of at the mall?

L3390.text: Would you rather I picked the kids up from school, or are you going to?

L3391.text: Should we leave a bigger tip? The waiter was really helpful with the kids.

L3392.text: I'm going to be away for two weeks. Could you water my plants while I'm gone?

L3393.text: Do you know if the base pool is open to family members on weekends?

L3394.text: My in-laws have invited us for New Year's, but I'd rather stay home this year.

L3395.text: These boots are too tight. Can I exchange them, or do I need the receipt?

L3396.text: Mom called while you were out. She wants to know whether we're coming for dinner Sunday.

L3397.text: Isn't this the place your sister said had the best seafood in town?

L3398.text: I'm a little short this week. Could you lend me twenty dollars until payday?

L3399.text: Would you mind turning the game down a little? I'm trying to read.

L3400.text: Have you met the couple who just moved into the house across the street?

L3401.text: Are we supposed to bring a gift to the office holiday party, or just food?

L3402.text: Why don't we paint the living room ourselves instead of hiring someone?

L3403.text: Could we get the check, please? We have to be at the theater by eight.

L3404.text: How did you manage to get tickets to the playoff game? They sold out in minutes.

L3405.text: You paid sixty dollars for that shirt? Wasn't it on sale last week?

L3406.text: You and Karen used to be close. How come you two don't talk anymore?

L3407.text: My son wants a dog, but I'm not sure he's old enough to take care of one.

L3408.text: Thanks for the invitation, but do you mind if I bring my cousin along?

L3409.text: This soup is cold. Would you mind asking the waiter to warm it up?

L3410.text: Do you know whether the bank charges a fee for using another bank's ATM?

L3411.text: Are you still taking guitar lessons, or did you give them up?

L3412.text: Somebody keeps parking in front of our driveway. Do you know whose car that is?

L3413.text: What are you doing for Labor Day? We're thinking of having a barbecue.

L3414.text: Honey, have you seen my reading glasses? I thought I left them on the kitchen table.

L3415.text: Do they take reservations here, or do we just have to wait in line?

L3416.text: That jacket looks great on you. Why don't you go ahead and buy it?

L3417.text: You run every morning. Wouldn't you like to sign up for the base marathon?

L3418.text: I'm moving apartments on Saturday. Any chance you could give me a hand?

L3419.text: I'm making lasagna tonight. Is there anything you don't eat?

L3420.text: Are your parents coming here for the holidays, or are you flying home this year?

L3421.text: Have you noticed that gas prices went up again? It's almost four dollars a gallon.

L3422.text: The baby finally fell asleep. Can you keep the TV down for a while?

L3423.text: Is the hiking trail by the lake open again, or is it still closed from the storm?

L3424.text: Would you mind feeding my cat this weekend? I'm going camping with my brother.

L3425.text: We've been waiting forty minutes for our food. Is there a problem in the kitchen?

L3426.text: I didn't get an invitation to Mike's wedding. Do you think he forgot about me?

L3427.text: How come you didn't tell me your sister had her baby last week?

L3428.text: Excuse me, do these batteries come in a bigger pack, or is this the largest?

L3429.text: Didn't the coach say practice would be moved indoors if it rained?

L3430.text: Are you going to finish your fries, or can I have a couple?

L3431.text: Tom and Lisa are moving back to Texas, aren't they?

L3432.text: Would you like to come to my daughter's graduation party next Saturday afternoon?

L3433.text: Would it make more sense to open a savings account here or at the credit union?

L3434.text: Do you think we should get the furnace checked before winter comes?

L3435.text: Is the fish fresh today, or would you recommend something else?

L3436.text: I've been meaning to ask you: where did you learn to play chess so well?

L3437.text: Our neighbor's tree fell onto our fence last night. Who's supposed to pay for it?

L3438.text: If I pay cash, is there any chance you could knock a few dollars off?

L3439.text: Is your brother still living with your parents, or did he finally get his own place?

L3440.text: Has the base planned anything for Veterans Day, or is it just a day off?

L3441.text: Let's try that new Thai place tonight, unless you're not in the mood for spicy food.

L3442.text: I heard you and Sarah are getting together for lunch. Mind if I join you?

L3443.text: Which do you enjoy more, watching football on TV or going to the stadium?

L3444.text: I can't find the remote anywhere. Did one of the kids take it to their room?

L3445.text: These prices seem really high. Isn't there a discount for military families?

L3446.text: Can I get the dressing on the side? I'm trying to cut back on calories.

L3447.text: We're having a small get-together for Mom's sixtieth. Could you help me with the decorations?

L3448.text: You haven't seen Jim lately, have you? He hasn't answered any of my calls.

L3449.text: Is it worth fishing off the pier, or do you really need a boat out here?

L3450.text: Do you want to split a dessert? I'm too full to eat a whole one.

L3451.text: The PX closes at six on Sundays, doesn't it? I still need a birthday card.

L3452.text: Shouldn't we start saving now if we want to send the kids to college?

L3453.text: Would you like to join us for Thanksgiving dinner, since your family is so far away?

L3454.text: Could you pick up our mail and newspapers while we're at the beach next week?

L3455.text: How come you quit the softball team? I thought you loved playing.

L3456.text: Your phone bill is a hundred dollars? Have you thought about switching to a cheaper plan?

L3457.text: Is it all right if we bring our own birthday cake, or is there a charge?

L3458.text: My mother-in-law is staying with us for a month. Can you believe it?

L3459.text: I'm having a garage sale Saturday. Do you know anyone who might want an old couch?

L3460.text: Did you remember to send your grandmother a card for her birthday, or did it slip your mind?

L3461.text: Would you rather go to the movies or just stay in and play cards tonight?

L3462.text: Excuse me, but I think there's a mistake. We didn't order the onion rings.

L3463.text: Do you think I should buy a new car or keep fixing the old one?

L3464.text: Didn't you and Rachel go to high school together back in Ohio?

L3465.text: I'm going to mow our lawn anyway. Want me to do yours while I'm at it?

L3466.text: How much did you end up paying for the new refrigerator, if you don't mind my asking?

L3467.text: Do you know whether Sergeant Ortiz is still teaching the night grammar course this term?

L3468.text: How come you didn't get your flu shot when the clinic had walk-in hours?

L3469.text: Did anyone call while I was at the dentist? I'm expecting to hear from the housing office.

L3470.text: It's supposed to clear up by the afternoon, isn't it? I'd hate to cancel the barbecue.

L3471.text: Would you mind restarting the projector? The screen went blank right in the middle of my slides.

L3472.text: Do you happen to know if we can leave early once we finish the listening part?

L3473.text: We're getting a group together for bowling on Friday night. Do you want in?

L3474.text: I tried calling you three times last night. Was your phone turned off?

L3475.text: Did the doctor give you anything for that cough, or just tell you to rest?

L3476.text: How did you manage to raise your ECL score so much in only two months?

L3477.text: You're coming to Captain Reyes's farewell party on Saturday, aren't you?

L3478.text: My laptop keeps freezing whenever I open more than two programs. Any idea what's wrong?

L3479.text: Why are they keeping us inside for PT this morning? It's not even raining.

L3480.text: Do you want to study together for the vocabulary quiz, or do you prefer working alone?

L3481.text: If my supervisor calls while I'm at lunch, could you tell him I'll call back by one?

L3482.text: Would you rather I drove you to the clinic, or can you manage on your own?

L3483.text: I heard the oral interview counts for half of the final grade. Is that true?

L3484.text: Haven't you met my wife? She's been wanting to meet everyone in the platoon.

L3485.text: Who should I call about the Wi-Fi? It's been down in the barracks since Monday.

L3486.text: How come you're taking the evening class instead of the one in the morning?

L3487.text: Do you know if Mr. Haskins will let us retake the reading quiz we missed on Monday?

L3488.text: I've had this headache since Tuesday. Do you think I should go to sick call tomorrow?

L3489.text: Could you text me the restaurant's address? I don't have anything to write with.

L3490.text: They're calling for thunderstorms all weekend. Do you still want to go camping at the lake?

L3491.text: Aren't we supposed to bring a pencil to the placement test, or do they provide them?

L3492.text: The classroom printer keeps jamming. Should I call the help desk or fix it myself?

L3493.text: A few of us are going to the movies after class. Would you like to join us?

L3494.text: Do you know if the clinic opens on Saturdays, or is the ER my only option?

L3495.text: I left you a voice mail this morning. Did you get a chance to listen to it?

L3496.text: It's ninety-five degrees out there. Are they still going to make us run at fourteen hundred?

L3497.text: How long do we get for the listening section? I always run out of time.

L3498.text: I can't open the attachment you sent. Could you send it again in a different format?

L3499.text: You haven't been to one of our game nights yet, have you?

L3500.text: The pharmacy said my prescription won't be ready until tomorrow. Can I get it filled anywhere else?

L3501.text: I can't make sense of my notes from today's lecture. Can I borrow yours?

L3502.text: My screen goes black every few minutes. Is there a setting I can change?

L3503.text: My ECL is next Thursday, and my listening still isn't great. What would you do?

L3504.text: Should I bring an umbrella to the ceremony, or is it going to stay dry?

L3505.text: Would you mind calling the eye doctor for me? I need to cancel tomorrow's appointment.

L3506.text: How come you left the party so early on Saturday? Everyone was asking about you.

L3507.text: Is the essay for Ms. Lane's class due on Friday, or did she give us more time?

L3508.text: I'm supposed to fast before my blood test. Does that mean I can't drink water either?

L3509.text: I accidentally deleted the file with all my homework. Is there any way to get it back?

L3510.text: Did Sergeant Kim say what he wanted when he called, or should I just call him back?

L3511.text: The roads are supposed to be icy tomorrow morning. Are you still driving to the airport?

L3512.text: Did they tell you your score right away, or do you have to wait for the results?

L3513.text: My sister's in town this weekend. Do you mind if she comes along to the picnic?

L3514.text: I'm thinking about dropping the math course. It's taking up all my free time.

L3515.text: Did the doctor say how long you have to stay off that ankle?

L3516.text: I keep getting calls from a number I don't recognize. Should I answer them?

L3517.text: My headset isn't working, and the listening lab starts in five minutes. What should I do?

L3518.text: Do you think it'll warm up enough for us to play golf on Sunday?

L3519.text: I heard they're changing the format of the ECL next year. Do you know anything about it?

L3520.text: We're throwing a surprise party for Jenna. Can you keep it a secret?

L3521.text: Could you help me with these vocabulary flashcards, or are you too busy right now?

L3522.text: You look pale. Wouldn't it be better to go home and lie down?

L3523.text: The line's breaking up. Can you hear me, or should I call you back on a landline?

L3524.text: My phone's been running really slow since the last update. Has yours been doing that too?

L3525.text: Isn't it unusual to have this much fog in August?

L3526.text: You passed the oral proficiency interview on your first try, didn't you?

L3527.text: Thanks for inviting me, but would it be all right if I came a little late?

L3528.text: Do you know where I can find a quiet place to study? The barracks are too noisy.

L3529.text: The nurse says I need to come back in two weeks. Can I schedule that online?

L3530.text: Did you write down the name of the woman who called about the car for sale?

L3531.text: I forgot my password again. Who do I ask to get it reset?

L3532.text: How come they canceled the flight training? It looks perfectly clear outside.

L3533.text: Do you happen to know where the test results will be posted?

L3534.text: I'm thinking of joining the base choir. Do you think I'd fit in?

L3535.text: Our instructor wants us to work in pairs for the project. Do you have a partner yet?

L3536.text: Do I need a referral to see a specialist, or can I make the appointment myself?

L3537.text: Can I leave a message for Lieutenant Park? She's not answering her phone.

L3538.text: My e-mail has been sending messages to people I don't know. What's going on?

L3539.text: Did you hear whether they're closing the base tomorrow because of the snowstorm?

L3540.text: Would it help if I quizzed you on the reading passages before your test?

L3541.text: I'm having a few friends over to watch the game. Want to stop by?

L3542.text: Don't you think the teacher went over the new grammar a little too fast today?

L3543.text: I twisted my knee playing soccer. Should I put ice on it or heat?

L3544.text: I've been on hold with the finance office for twenty minutes. Should I just hang up?

L3545.text: Do you know if the new software will work on our old computers?

L3546.text: It's been raining for a week. Do you think the river will flood?

L3547.text: Is it true they won't let us use dictionaries during the writing test?

L3548.text: I'm new on base and don't know anyone yet. Any suggestions for meeting people?

L3549.text: Have you finished the reading for tomorrow, or are you as far behind as I am?

L3550.text: I need a physical before I can go to airborne school. Do I need an appointment?

L3551.text: I texted you twice about Saturday but never heard back. Is everything okay?

L3552.text: Could you show me how to print on both sides of the page?

L3553.text: We were going to go hiking, but did you see how windy it is out there?

L3554.text: How come you're taking the ECL again? I thought you already had a passing score.

L3555.text: Are you going to Tom's housewarming on Friday, or are you on duty?

L3556.text: The medic said I should take these pills with food. Does that mean before or after eating?

L3557.text: Can I sign out the van for the trip to the airfield this afternoon?
Not with that license. It expired on Friday, and the dispatcher won't budge on that.

L3558.text: The armorer wouldn't hand me my rifle this morning. Apparently my weapon card was never updated after I changed platoons.
Then you'd better see the supply sergeant before the range bus leaves at ten.

L3559.text: Should I bother packing my wet-weather gear? The forecast for the training area looks clear all week.
I wouldn't leave it behind. Last time they said the same thing, and we were soaked by the second night.

L3560.text: Anything I need to know before I take over staff duty?
Just that the fire alarm in Building Twelve went off twice for no reason. Facilities promised to send someone first thing tomorrow.

L3561.text: Are we still forming up on the parade field at seven?
Not in this downpour. The first sergeant moved it into the motor pool bays, same time.

L3562.text: My promotion board is Thursday, and I still haven't memorized the soldier's creed.
You've got three days. Say it out loud every time you walk to the dining facility, and you'll have it down cold.

L3563.text: I was hoping to start the leadership course in May, but they won't take me without a current fitness test.
Eight months ago. It only counts for six.

L3564.text: My orders for Germany finally came in. I report in sixty days.
Then don't wait on the no-fee passport. Those can take six weeks or more, especially for family members.

L3565.text: There's a puddle under the truck I just parked. Should I write it up as a leak?
Touch it first. If it's clear and has no smell, it's just water from the air conditioner.

L3566.text: Why is everyone still waiting outside the arms room? It's already past six.
Sergeant Kemp has the keys, but it takes two people to open it, and the other one's stuck at the gate.

L3567.text: I promised my kids I'd be home Friday. Is the field exercise still ending Thursday night?
It was, until the brigade tacked on two more days of night training. Now we won't be back before Saturday evening.

L3568.text: Private Wells signed out on a pass Saturday morning, but he never signed back in last night.
Did you try his cell phone before calling it in to the first sergeant?
Three times. It goes straight to voicemail.

L3569.text: The promotion list came out this morning, and my name isn't on it, even though I made the cutoff score.
It could be a data problem. Ask the personnel office to check whether your latest points were entered.

L3570.text: Can I just skip the online part of the course? I'll be at the schoolhouse in person in March anyway.
Afraid not. They won't even let you sign in at the front desk without the certificate showing you finished it.

L3571.text: Personnel amended my orders. I now report to Fort Bliss on the third instead of the twentieth.
That's more than two weeks earlier. Does that cut into your leave?

L3572.text: I thought tomorrow's formation was in PT uniform.
It was, but the commander wants everyone in the duty uniform for the photo. Make sure your patches are on straight.

L3573.text: Why did Sergeant Hughes chew you out in the motor pool?
I backed the truck out without a ground guide. Nothing happened, but he said that's how people get hurt.

L3574.text: Are you finally done with your rifle? We started cleaning at fourteen hundred.
Not even close. The armorer sent it back twice for carbon in the bolt. At this rate I'll be here until dinner.

L3575.text: Can I use my flashlight to read the map, or is that against the rules tonight?
Only with the red lens, and keep it under your poncho. We don't want to give away our position.

L3576.text: Has staff duty heard anything about the snow? The roads by the housing area are pure ice.
Post just announced a two-hour delay, so first formation's at nine, not seven.

L3577.text: Who's going to pin on your new rank at the ceremony Friday?
My wife, if she can get off work. Otherwise, my old drill sergeant offered to do the honors.

L3578.text: I heard Specialist Tran didn't graduate with the rest of her class.
She hurt her wrist the week before the final exam, so they're letting her finish with the next class instead of starting over.

L3579.text: Did you ask branch to push your report date back to summer?
I did, so my son can finish the school year here. They approved it, but only until the first of July.

L3580.text: You missed first formation. What happened?
The power went out overnight, and my alarm clock never went off. I've already explained it to my squad leader.

L3581.text: The van we signed out is overdue for service. The sticker says it was due at twelve thousand miles.
Then park it. If it breaks down on the highway, guess who'll have to explain why we took it.

L3582.text: Why is the arms room closed all day? I wanted to turn in my night vision goggles.
It's the monthly inventory. They count every serial number, so nothing goes in or out until they're done.

L3583.text: How are your feet after yesterday's road march?
Covered in blisters. The medic says I can still train, as long as I change my socks twice a day.

L3584.text: A civilian at the barracks door says he's here to visit his brother. It's almost midnight.
Visiting hours ended at ten. Take his name and phone number, and tell him to come back tomorrow.

L3585.text: My promotion was effective the first of last month, but my pay still hasn't changed.
Don't worry. Once finance catches up, you'll get the difference for both months in one payment.

L3586.text: Congratulations on graduating! Is it true you made the commandant's list?
I did, by half a point. Honestly, I didn't think I had a chance until the last exam.

L3587.text: I need a copy of my orders for the housing office, but I deleted the email.
No problem. Personnel can reprint them, but bring your ID. They won't hand them to anyone else.

L3588.text: Are you nervous about getting your medal in front of the whole battalion?
Not about the medal. I'm more worried I'll salute with the wrong hand when the colonel walks up.

L3589.text: We need to top off the tanks before the convoy leaves Sunday morning.
Better do it today, then. The fuel point's closed on weekends, and nobody's going to open it for us.

L3590.text: My shots are all hitting low and to the left.
Then your sight's probably off. Adjust it a few clicks and fire another group before you shoot for record.

L3591.text: Our platoon is playing the enemy during next week's exercise.
Lucky you. The opposing force usually gets more sleep and hot food, while everyone else hikes all night.

L3592.text: The battalion commander called the duty desk at two a.m., and nobody answered.
Specialist Dunn. He says he was doing rounds, but nothing in the log backs that up.

L3593.text: I'm only twelve points short for promotion to sergeant. Any ideas?
Knock out a couple of online correspondence courses. Each one's worth a few points, and you can do them at night.

L3594.text: Did you get into the Korean course at the language school?
Not this cycle. My aptitude score was two points under the minimum, but I can retake the test in six months.

L3595.text: The movers said our household goods are over the weight limit for your rank.
About eight hundred pounds. Either we pay the difference or we have a garage sale.

L3596.text: Any chance we'll get released early before the long weekend?
If the safety briefing goes quickly and the barracks pass the walk-through, the commander said we could be gone by noon.

L3597.text: Dispatch won't release the Humvee to me. The front left tire is reading twenty pounds low.
The air compressor in bay three is working again. Fill it up, have the mechanic sign off, and try again.

L3598.text: The serial number on this rifle doesn't match the one on my hand receipt.
Don't sign anything yet. Let me pull the property book; someone may have swapped weapons during the last turn-in.

L3599.text: How did land navigation go? You were out there a long time.
I walked right past my second point in the dark. If I hadn't counted my paces, I'd still be looking for it.

L3600.text: My shift on staff duty ended an hour ago, and Sergeant Ortiz still hasn't shown up to relieve me.
Don't leave the desk. Call the staff duty officer and let him track Ortiz down.

L3601.text: Personnel sent my promotion packet back again. This time it's missing the commander's signature.
He's on leave until the fifteenth, but the executive officer can sign for him. I'd catch her before lunch.

L3602.text: Why did the tower call a cease-fire? We'd only fired two rounds.
A deer wandered onto lane six. Nobody shoots until range control says it's clear.

L3603.text: I've got guard from two to four tonight. Would you switch with me? I'm wiped out after that march.
Sure, as long as you take my midnight shift on Thursday. I'm on an early convoy Friday.

L3604.text: I'm supposed to finish clearing post today, but the library won't sign my checklist.
You probably still have a book checked out. Return it or pay for it, and they'll initial the form.

L3605.text: I count twenty-eight in formation, but the roster shows thirty. Who's missing?
Garcia's at the dental clinic, and Lee is on leave. They're both on the board in the orderly room.

L3606.text: Do I really have to sit through the whole combat lifesaver course again? I took it two years ago.
Your certification ran out last month. If you'd renewed it in time, you'd only need the one-day refresher.

L3607.text: When will my truck be off the deadline report? It's been sitting in the bay for three weeks.
The mechanics are ready to go, but the fuel pump is still on back order. Could be another month.

L3608.text: The water truck won't reach us until tomorrow afternoon. How much do you have left?
Two canteens and half a bladder. If we go easy and stay in the shade, we should be all right.

L3609.text: Airborne school just called. Someone dropped out, and they can take me Monday if I can get there.
That's awfully short notice. Will your section chief let you go with the inspection coming up?

L3610.text: Sensitive items check came up one compass short. We're not leaving until it turns up.
Check Private Diaz's cargo pocket. He was using one on the land nav course and never gave it back.

L3611.text: Why did all those cars pull over a minute ago? There's no accident.
It's five o'clock. When the bugle plays for the flag coming down, everyone on post stops and pays respect.

L3612.text: I made the list for staff sergeant, but my enlistment ends in eight months.
Then you'll have to extend or reenlist before they'll pin it on. Have you talked to the career counselor?

L3613.text: My English score was eighty-two. Is that enough for the aviation course?
Not quite. They want eighty-five, but the language school can get you there in about six weeks.

L3614.text: We just got back from the field. Can't the trucks be washed tomorrow?
Not if you want to turn them in. The wash rack is booked solid after today, so it's tonight or next week.

L3615.text: A specialist wants the key to the supply room. He says he left his wallet in there.
Is he on the key access roster? If not, he'll have to wait for the supply sergeant at six.

L3616.text: Why is everyone sitting in the trucks? We still have two lanes to run.
Lightning was spotted eight miles out. We can't go back out until thirty minutes after the last strike.

L3617.text: My orders for the conference in Denver don't authorize a rental car. How am I supposed to get around?
The hotel runs a free shuttle to the training center, and you can claim taxis for anything official.

L3618.text: This is the third rehearsal for the change of command. Do we really need another one in this heat?
The new colonel's family is flying in, and the general will be here. Nobody wants it to look sloppy.

L3619.text: With Sergeant Pruitt on leave for three weeks, who's running the squad?
You are. The platoon sergeant said it'll look good at your next board, so don't let it slide.

L3620.text: I left the keys in the Humvee while I grabbed lunch. Is that a big deal on post?
Around here it is. If staff duty finds an unsecured vehicle, the whole section pays for it.

L3621.text: A few of us are reviewing for the final in the classroom tonight. Want to join?
I wish I could, but I'm on charge of quarters until midnight. Save me a copy of your notes, though.

L3622.text: Did Sergeant Boyd really weigh everyone's ruck before we stepped off?
Every single one. Mine was three pounds light, so he made me carry two extra cans of water.

L3623.text: Third floor is complaining about loud music in room three-twelve again. It's after eleven.
Go knock and ask them to turn it down. If they argue, log it and I'll deal with it tomorrow.

L3624.text: Transportation won't schedule my movers. I told them I'm leaving for Fort Riley in July.
They don't go by what you tell them. Until the actual orders are published, they can't do a thing.

L3625.text: The generator for the command post won't start. I think the battery's dead.
Grab the slave cable off the wrecker and jump it from the truck. Just don't let it run out of fuel this time.

L3626.text: How did your practice class go at the instructor course?
My material was fine, but I ran twelve minutes over. The evaluator said if it happens again, I'll be dropped.

L3627.text: Is the arms room open Monday? I need to draw my pistol for the escort mission.
Monday's a federal holiday, so it's closed unless you get the commander's approval ahead of time. I'd put in the request today.

L3628.text: My night vision goggles keep flickering. Do you have any spare batteries?
Fresh out. Supply only issued one pack per squad, and we burned through ours on the first night.

L3629.text: The first sergeant asked me to carry the guidon at the ceremony. Isn't that usually a corporal's job?
Usually. But he picks whoever looks sharpest at inspection, and your uniform was the best in the company.

L3630.text: Could you look over my uniform before the board? I want to make sure everything's right.
Your ribbons are in the wrong order, and your name tag's a quarter inch too low. Otherwise, you look great.

L3631.text: The packing list for the mountain course says ski boots are optional. Should I bring my own?
If yours fit well, definitely. The ones they issue there are worn out, and blisters will end your course fast.

L3632.text: My orders were changed. Instead of Hawaii, I'm going to Fairbanks, Alaska.
Well, you can forget the beach. You'd better start shopping for a serious winter coat.

L3633.text: On my last round I found the back door of the barracks propped open with a rock.
Somebody probably got tired of using the main entrance. Secure it, write down the time, and check it again next round.

L3634.text: Is chow coming out to the field tonight, or is it MREs again?
The mess truck got stuck in the mud on the range road, so it's MREs. Maybe tomorrow, if it doesn't rain.

L3635.text: My sergeant orders say effective the first. Can I go ahead and put the new rank on today?
Not until it's pinned on at the ceremony. The captain is strict about that, and it's only four days.

L3636.text: The environmental inspector is coming through the motor pool after lunch.
Then get drip pans under every vehicle that's leaking, and clear those empty oil cans out of the bay. That's what they write us up for.

L3637.text: I got back from temporary duty last week. Is there a deadline for turning in my travel voucher?
Five working days. You're already past it, so attach a memo explaining the delay or finance may kick it back.

L3638.text: Do we really have to put the camouflage nets back up? We're moving again at dawn.
The evaluators fly the drone over every few hours. If they spot our trucks, the whole company gets marked down.

L3639.text: Did you get accepted to the signals intelligence course?
Conditionally. They'll hold my seat, but if my clearance isn't approved by the start date, it goes to the next person on the list.

L3640.text: I passed the written test for the five-ton. When can I start driving it on missions?
Not until you log ten hours behind the wheel with an instructor. Then there's the road test.

L3641.text: Why was everyone already in formation when I got here? It's only six-fifteen.
Didn't you see the email? The first sergeant moved it up to six for the run with the battalion.

L3642.text: I qualified during the day, but I missed night fire because of sick call. Do I have to shoot the whole thing over?
Only the night part. Sign up for the make-up range on the twentieth.

L3643.text: Half the stakes for the big tent are missing, and the wind is picking up.
Tie the corners off to the trucks for now. Supply's bringing more stakes out with the evening run.

L3644.text: I'm applying for the warrant officer program. Do you think the colonel would write me a letter of recommendation?
He might, but he barely knows you. Your company commander's letter would carry more weight.

L3645.text: I failed the radio operations test this morning. Does that mean I'm out of the course?
Not yet. Everyone gets one retest, usually on Friday. Fail that, though, and you'll be recycled.

L3646.text: Has anyone from the new unit contacted you about your move to Italy?
My sponsor emailed last week. She's already found me a temporary room and will meet me at the airport.

L3647.text: The temperature gauge on my truck shot into the red on the way back from the range.
Don't open the radiator cap while it's hot. Let it sit for half an hour, then top off the coolant.

L3648.text: A Red Cross message just came in for Private Hale. His father's in the hospital.
Wake his squad leader first, then the commander. They'll want to tell him in person, not over the phone.

L3649.text: I can't raise battalion on the radio. Did they change frequencies again?
At midnight, like the schedule said. The new one's on the card taped inside the vehicle door.

L3650.text: The barracks internet is too slow for my online course. Where else can I work on it?
The education center has a computer lab, but it closes at four, so you'd have to use your lunch hour.

L3651.text: My evaluation report is due to personnel Friday, and my rater still hasn't written his part.
He's at the field site until Thursday. Email him the draft tonight so he can sign it the moment he gets back.

L3652.text: Where do I fall in? I'm new to the company, and nobody's told me which platoon I'm in.
Stand at the end of second platoon for now. The first sergeant assigns new arrivals after formation.

L3653.text: The printer on the second floor keeps eating my pages. Do you know who handles that?
Don't bother calling the help desk. Sergeant Diaz fixes it faster than they ever answer the phone.

L3654.text: I turned in my leave form two weeks ago, and I still haven't heard anything.
That's odd. The commander signed a whole stack yesterday. Check with the orderly room before you buy any tickets.

L3655.text: My ID card expires on the thirtieth. Can I just walk in at the ID office?
You can try, but the wait is usually three or four hours. Most people book online.

L3656.text: My housing allowance wasn't on this month's pay. Finance says it's because my lease never reached them.
Bring a copy to them today, and they'll probably pay you back on the next check.

L3657.text: Is the training meeting still at fourteen hundred?
They pushed it back an hour because the colonel's flight was late. Same room, though.

L3658.text: I typed my password wrong three times, and now the system won't let me in at all.
Join the club. IT is resetting accounts at the front desk, but the line's out the door.

L3659.text: Captain Reyes's office. She's in a briefing until eleven. May I take a message?
Yes, please tell her the housing office called. Her quarters will be ready a week earlier than planned.

L3660.text: Can I file my travel voucher without the hotel receipt? I think I threw it away.
Not unless you want to wait months. Call the hotel; they can usually email you a copy.

L3661.text: Can you take the minutes at Thursday's staff meeting? Tanya's on leave.
I'd be glad to, if it weren't for the range qualification I've got that whole morning.

L3662.text: Excuse me, I need forty copies of this map, in color if possible.
Color's down until the technician comes. I can run them in black and white, or you can come back tomorrow.

L3663.text: I opened a new bank account. How long does it take to switch my direct deposit?
If you update it online before the fifteenth, it should take effect on the next payday. Otherwise, it'll be the one after.

L3664.text: The heater in our quarters has been broken since Monday. I've called housing twice.
Then put it in writing this time. They don't act on phone calls unless it's an emergency.

L3665.text: I've been trying to get an appointment with the career counselor, but he's booked solid through the end of the month.
He holds open hours every Friday afternoon. You don't need to sign up for those.

L3666.text: Why is your computer showing that blue screen? Did it crash?
No, it's just installing updates. It started on its own, and it says it'll take another forty minutes.

L3667.text: I was hoping to take leave the week of the twelfth. Is that going to be a problem?
That's when the inspection team arrives. I wouldn't count on anyone getting time off then.

L3668.text: I've been transferred three times, and every office tells me to call someone else.
I'm sorry about that, sir. Give me your number, and I'll have the right person get back to you within the hour.

L3669.text: Personnel sent my reenlistment packet back. Apparently I signed in the wrong block.
That happens all the time. Just initial the change and have your supervisor sign next to it.

L3670.text: The projector in the conference room won't turn on, and the briefing starts in ten minutes.
Let's not waste time on it. We'll pass out paper copies of the slides instead.

L3671.text: Finance just told me I was overpaid four hundred dollars last spring, and they want it back.
Ask them to spread it out over a few months. Otherwise they'll take it all from one paycheck.

L3672.text: I lost my ID card at the gym. Can I get a new one today?
Not without a memo from your unit saying it's lost. Get that first, then come back.

L3673.text: We're out of printer paper again, and the supply closet is locked.
