Staff Sergeant Lee has the only key, and she's at lunch until one. Borrow a ream from personnel down the hall.

L3674.text: I'm here for my nine o'clock appointment with the legal office.
I've got you down for nine o'clock tomorrow, Sergeant. But if you don't mind waiting, someone may cancel.

L3675.text: All my files on the shared drive are gone. Did someone delete them?
Relax. IT moved everything to the new server last night. Your folders should be under the new drive letter.

L3676.text: Did you get the extra pay for being away from your family during the deployment?
Not a cent. Nobody told me I had to apply for it. I'm filling out the form now.

L3677.text: I tried calling Major Hill all morning, but his voicemail is full.
He's at a conference in Denver all week. You'd have better luck sending him an email.

L3678.text: How long is the waiting list for a three-bedroom house on post?
About six months right now. If you'd take a two-bedroom, you could probably move in by next month.

L3679.text: Does Tuesday morning work for the budget review?
Tuesday's no good; I'm at the dentist. Any time Wednesday, though, I'm free.

L3680.text: Here's my request for a change of station. I filled it out last night.
I'm afraid this is last year's version of the form. We can't accept it anymore, but the new one's almost the same.

L3681.text: My son just turned ten. Does he need his own ID card now?
He does. Bring his birth certificate, and you'll both need to come in, since you have to sign for him.

L3682.text: I got my new laptop this morning, but I can't do anything with it.
That's because your account hasn't been created yet. It usually takes IT two or three days after you sign the user agreement.

L3683.text: My father's in the hospital back home. How fast can I get emergency leave?
Usually the same day, once the Red Cross message comes in. Have your family contact them right away.

L3684.text: I'm stuck behind a convoy at the main gate. Can you start the meeting without me?
Sure. We'll cover the schedule first and save the budget items until you get here.

L3685.text: Why is my paycheck smaller this month? I didn't change anything.
Did you sign up for the extra life insurance last month? The premium comes out of every check.

L3686.text: I'm clearing my quarters on Friday. Do I have to clean the carpets myself?
You can, but if they don't pass inspection, you'll be charged. Most people just pay the contractor.

L3687.text: I keep dialing the extension for the motor pool, but I get a fax machine.
Their numbers changed when they moved buildings. The new list is posted on the bulletin board by the elevator.

L3688.text: Where can I get this power of attorney notarized before I deploy?
The legal office does it for free, but only on Tuesday and Thursday mornings. Bring your ID.

L3689.text: Did I miss anything important at the safety meeting?
Not really. It was mostly the same slides as last quarter. The only new thing is that reflective belts are required after dark.

L3690.text: My email keeps bouncing back. I'm trying to send the training videos to the battalion.
The files are too big for email. Put them on the shared drive and send them the link instead.

L3691.text: My husband's ID expired yesterday, and the gate guard wouldn't let him in.
He'll have to get a day pass at the visitor center until he renews it. Make sure he brings his driver's license.

L3692.text: Can I get an advance on my travel pay before the move? I'm short on cash.
You can get up to eighty percent ahead of time, but you'll have to pay back anything you don't actually spend.

L3693.text: I sent my report to the printer ten minutes ago, but nothing's come out.
Check which printer you picked. Half the office has been printing to the one in the colonel's office by mistake.

L3694.text: Do I need an appointment to register my car on post?
Not anymore. But don't go on a Monday. That's when everyone who arrived over the weekend shows up.

L3695.text: Four hours, and we could have finished in one if people hadn't kept repeating each other.

L3696.text: According to my pay statement, I only have six days of leave left. I thought I had sixteen.
Did you count the ten days you took over Christmas? They might not have been charged until this month.

L3697.text: Personnel has had me on hold for twenty minutes. I'm about to give up.
Hang up and walk over there. It's only two buildings down, and you'll be done before they pick up.

L3698.text: When are the evaluation reports due to the battalion?
The deadline was the first, but they gave us an extension until the fifteenth because of the field exercise.

L3699.text: Are you still living in the barracks?
Not since my promotion. I share an apartment in town with two guys from my section now.

L3700.text: My account got suspended. Something about an expired training certificate.
You missed the annual security course. Take it online tonight, and they'll turn your access back on tomorrow.

L3701.text: Is it true we're getting a four-day weekend for the holiday?
Only if the inspection goes well on Thursday. Otherwise it's the usual three days.

L3702.text: There's another group in the conference room. I booked it for ten.
So did they, apparently. The scheduling system must have let both of us reserve it. Let's use my office.

L3703.text: When will my reenlistment bonus show up? I signed the contract in March.
Half comes within sixty days of signing. The rest is paid in equal parts every year until your contract ends.

L3704.text: My computer won't accept my ID card PIN anymore. I've been locked out since yesterday.
Only the ID card office can reset that. They take walk-ins until three, so you'd better hurry.

L3705.text: Sorry, sir, you're breaking up. Could you repeat the last part?
I'm driving through the hills, so I'll lose you again. Just text me the time of the meeting.

L3706.text: How many signatures do I still need to clear post?
Just the library and the housing office. But housing won't sign until your final inspection, and that's not until Wednesday.

L3707.text: Can you show me how to scan this to my email? I've never used this copier before.
I would, but I'm late for formation. Ask Private Ortiz; she set the machine up.

L3708.text: Will housing let us keep a large dog in our quarters?
Two pets are allowed, but certain breeds aren't. Bring his vet records, and they'll tell you right away.

L3709.text: Headquarters can see us, but they can't hear a thing.
Somebody muted the microphone on the table again. Hand it here and I'll switch it on.

L3710.text: The fifteenth is a Sunday this month. Does that mean we don't get paid until Monday?
Just the opposite. When payday lands on a weekend, the money comes on the Friday before.

L3711.text: My leave was approved, right? I gave the paper form to the clerk last week.
We switched to the online system on the first. Paper forms aren't even being looked at anymore.

L3712.text: I need an official passport for my assignment in Japan. How long does it take?
Six to eight weeks, so don't put it off. You can't apply until you have your orders in hand, though.

L3713.text: My screen froze again in the middle of the report. That's the third time today.
When was the last time you actually shut it down? Most of these machines run for weeks without a restart.

L3714.text: I pinned on sergeant two months ago, and I'm still getting paid as a corporal.
The paperwork must be stuck somewhere. When it catches up, you'll get the difference for both months.

L3715.text: Do I really have to sit through the newcomers' briefing? I've been stationed here before.
Everyone does, I'm afraid. A lot has changed since then, including the gate hours.

L3716.text: I'm signing for my quarters today. Can my wife pick up the keys tomorrow if I'm in the field?
Only if you give her a special power of attorney. Otherwise, the keys have to be signed for by you.

L3717.text: Is Sergeant First Class Kim around? I need to talk to him about the range schedule.
He just stepped out, but he should be back in fifteen minutes. Want me to have him call you?

L3718.text: Personnel rejected my form again. I double-checked every block.
Did you sign it in blue ink? They only take black. I learned that the hard way.

L3719.text: I got an email saying my pay account will be closed unless I send my password. Should I answer it?
Absolutely not. Forward it to the security office and delete it.

L3720.text: Who's giving the logistics brief tomorrow, now that Captain Shaw is gone?
Lieutenant Price was supposed to, but she's sick. So it looks like you're it, unless you can find someone else.

L3721.text: When do we get the clothing allowance? My boots are falling apart.
Once a year, on the anniversary of the month you came in. For you, that's not until August.

L3722.text: They retook my ID photo three times. I blinked in every one.
Well, at least you won't have to look at a bad picture for the next four years.

L3723.text: I've got forty days of leave saved up, and I'm getting out in May. What happens to them?
You can take them before you leave or sell them back. Most people sell them, since they're paid in cash.

L3724.text: The printer says the black cartridge is empty, but I just replaced it on Monday.
Did you pull off the plastic tape? It won't print at all if that's still on.

L3725.text: I have to cancel my appointment at the education center. Something came up at work.
Call them right now, then. If you just don't show up, they'll make you wait a month for another slot.

L3726.text: Are your slides ready for the commander's meeting at one?
Almost. I'm just waiting on the numbers from supply. If they don't come in, I'll brief that part from memory.

L3727.text: The landlord wants a twelve-month lease, but I might get orders in the spring.
Ask him to add a military clause. Then you can break the lease without a penalty if you're reassigned.

L3728.text: I want part of my pay to go straight to my mother every month. Is that possible?
Sure, you can set up an allotment. Just keep in mind it takes a full pay period to start.

L3729.text: I called the housing office at five-fifteen, and nobody picked up.
They close at four-thirty. After that, the calls go to a recording with the emergency number.

L3730.text: Should I turn in Specialist Ward's award packet now or after the holiday?
Now. If it isn't on the colonel's desk by Friday, it won't be approved before Ward transfers out.

L3731.text: Can I finish this report from home tonight?
Only if you've got a government laptop. Personal computers can't connect to our network.

L3732.text: Do I need to bring anything to the quarterly training brief?
Your training calendar, and a printed copy of the range requests. The commander doesn't want laptops in the room.

L3733.text: Do we get per diem if the meals are provided during the course?
Only a small amount for incidentals. Since the government is already feeding you, they won't pay for meals twice.

L3734.text: What should I bring to my in-processing appointment at finance?
Your orders, your bank information, and every receipt from the move. If you forget something, you'll just have to come back.

L3735.text: Why can't I send any emails this afternoon?
Your mailbox is probably full again. Delete some of those old attachments, and it should start working.

L3736.text: My leave got denied because two other people in my section are already off that week.
Could you swap with one of them? Sometimes people are willing to trade if you ask nicely.

L3737.text: My parents are flying in next week. Can they get on post with me?
They'll need passes. If you register them at the visitor center ahead of time, it only takes a few minutes when they arrive.

L3738.text: Do I have to set up the electric bill myself when I move into post housing?
No, utilities are included. But if you go over the monthly baseline, you'll get a bill for the extra.

L3739.text: Could you send me the notes from yesterday's meeting? I had to leave halfway through.
They're already in your inbox. I sent them to everyone on the distribution list this morning.

L3740.text: I still haven't received my tax form in the mail. Should I call finance?
They stopped mailing those a few years ago. You can download it from the pay website whenever you want.

L3741.text: What's the number for the conference call with the training center?
It's in the calendar invite. But they've changed it twice this week, so make sure you've got the latest one.

L3742.text: This security clearance form wants every address I've lived at for ten years. I've moved fourteen times.
Welcome to military life. Start with your old orders; they'll have most of your duty stations on them.

L3743.text: Hey, the spreadsheet you sent won't open on my computer.
You must have the older version of the program. I'll save it in a different format and resend it.

L3744.text: I'd like to see the commander about my transfer request. Do I need an appointment?
Not on Thursdays. That's his open-door afternoon, but you'd better tell your first sergeant first.

L3745.text: My family's been in the guest lodging for two weeks. Can we stay longer while we look for a house?
Only if housing gives you a letter saying nothing's available. Otherwise, you'll be paying out of your own pocket.

L3746.text: I've been waiting on the video call for ten minutes, and nobody else has joined.
The invite was in Eastern time. It doesn't start for another hour here.

L3747.text: Now that I'm married and living off post, will they stop taking money out for the dining hall?
They should, but only after you turn in your meal card. Until then, the deduction continues.

L3748.text: A man just called asking for Sergeant Bell's home address. He said he's an old friend.
You didn't give it to him, did you? We never release that kind of information over the phone.

L3749.text: The airline's offering a three-hundred-dollar voucher to anyone who'll take the later flight. Interested?
Normally I'd jump at it, but my sponsor is picking me up at the airport tonight.

L3750.text: Our flight from Denver landed forty minutes late, so we missed the connection to Norfolk.
The agent already rebooked us on the first one out tomorrow, and the airline's covering a hotel.

L3751.text: Did you catch that announcement? They just moved our flight from B twelve to C forty.
Then forget the coffee. C forty is at the far end of the other concourse.

L3752.text: Excuse me, will this bag fit in the overhead bin?
It's a bit over the size limit, sir. We'll tag it here, and it'll be waiting for you on the jet bridge when you land.

L3753.text: My phone just died, and my boarding pass is on it. You don't have a charger, do you?
Not on me, but the agent at the counter can print you a paper one in a minute.

L3754.text: Any chance of getting on the space-available flight to Ramstein tonight?
There are eight seats, but you're number twenty on the list, so I wouldn't count on it.

L3755.text: Should I list the sausages from my aunt on the customs form?
Definitely. If you declare them, the worst that happens is they take them away. If you don't, you could be fined.

L3756.text: You look exhausted. Didn't you get back from Germany two days ago?
I did, but my body still thinks it's three in the morning when we're standing in formation.

L3757.text: I booked the red-eye to save a little money. It gets in at five forty-five.
Fine, but don't plan on driving straight to the office. You'll be useless after a night like that.

L3758.text: They canceled the eleven o'clock flight. Something about the crew running out of duty hours.
Well, at least it's not mechanical. Maybe they can find a fresh crew by this afternoon.

L3759.text: The gate agent says I've been upgraded to first class, and I didn't even ask.
That's what all those business trips get you. Enjoy the extra legroom.

L3760.text: Where should I pick you up on Thursday, at the curb outside baggage claim?
Just wait in the cell phone lot. I'll text you once I have my bags, and then you can swing by.

L3761.text: I can move you to a window seat if you'd like, sir.
Thanks, but with my bad knee, I'd rather be where I can stretch my leg into the aisle.

L3762.text: Our flight's not until ten fifteen. Do we really need to leave the house at six?
Have you seen the security lines on a holiday weekend? I'm not taking any chances.

L3763.text: My passport expires in March. That's fine for a trip in January, right?
Not for that country. They want at least six months left on it when you arrive.

L3764.text: If the meeting runs past nine, we'll miss the last train back to base.
Then let's agree now: we split a cab, and nobody keeps checking the clock.

L3765.text: Does the number seven bus still stop in front of the library?
Not this month. With the road work on Main, it's been moved two blocks over, to Elm.

L3766.text: I only need a one-way ticket to Philadelphia, but it costs more than a round trip.
That happens all the time. Buy the round trip and just don't use the return half.

L3767.text: Does the shuttle to the medical clinic run on Saturdays?
Only on weekdays, every twenty minutes. On weekends, you'd have to call the duty driver.

L3768.text: Excuse me, would you mind taking your call somewhere else? This is the quiet car.
Oh, I'm so sorry. I didn't see the sign. I'll step out between the cars.

L3769.text: Is this the train for Riverside? I need to get off at Fourth Street.
It goes to Riverside, but it's the express. It doesn't stop until the end of the line, so wait for the local.

L3770.text: The overnight bus to Atlanta is only forty dollars. The flight is almost two hundred.
Sure, but you'd lose a whole night's sleep, and you report at seven the next morning.

L3771.text: How do I get to the stadium from here on the subway?
Take the red line two stops, then change to the green line at Central. It's the third stop after that.

L3772.text: I'm spending almost three dollars a day on bus fare just getting to work and back.
Why don't you get a monthly pass? It's sixty dollars, and you can ride as much as you want.

L3773.text: The board says our train's delayed because of a signal problem. Any idea how long?
Last time it took over an hour. I'd grab a sandwich if I were you.

L3774.text: Did you book a sleeper for the trip to Chicago?
They were sold out, so it's a regular seat for eighteen hours. I'm bringing a neck pillow.

L3775.text: I only have a twenty. Will the driver be able to break it?
No, drivers don't carry cash. You need exact change or a fare card from the machine at the stop.

L3776.text: Do I have to fill up the rental before I bring it back tomorrow?
You don't have to, but if they fill it for you, it's almost nine dollars a gallon.

L3777.text: The rental clerk keeps pushing the extra insurance. Should I take it?
Not when you're on official orders. The government rate already covers damage, so you'd be paying twice.

L3778.text: Why is my rental total so much higher than the price I saw online?
There's a daily fee for drivers under twenty-five. You only turned twenty-four in May, didn't you?

L3779.text: We've got a flat, and there's no spare in the trunk of this rental.
Figures. Let me find the roadside assistance number. It's usually on the key tag.

L3780.text: Should I take the toll road to the airport? I don't have any cash on me.
The rental has a transponder on the windshield, so the tolls just go on your bill.

L3781.text: You might want to ease off the gas. The limit drops to thirty-five through this town, and they're strict about it.
Thanks. I'd hate to get a ticket my first week here.

L3782.text: The GPS lost its signal about ten miles back, and none of these roads have signs.
Pull over at that general store. Somebody in there will know the way to the lake.

L3783.text: They're out of compact cars, so they're giving me a full-size SUV for the same price.
Nice, but with gas prices what they are, that free upgrade won't be cheap to drive.

L3784.text: The short-term garage is full. Every level says Lot Full.
Then head to the economy lot. The shuttle from there only takes ten minutes, and we've got time.

L3785.text: Are you driving to the training conference in Norfolk on Monday?
I was planning to, but Sergeant Diaz offered me a ride, so my car's staying home.

L3786.text: When you rent a car in England next month, remember they drive on the left.
Don't worry. I'm taking trains everywhere. I'm not about to learn that on vacation.

L3787.text: Will my state driver's license be enough to drive in Korea once I get there?
Not by itself. You'll also have to pass a short written test on base before they'll give you a local permit.

L3788.text: The low fuel light just came on. How far is the next exit?
About thirty miles, according to that sign. We usually get around forty after the light comes on, but I wouldn't push it.

L3789.text: The radio says chains are required on the pass above four thousand feet.
We don't have any, so either we buy a set in town or we take the long way through the valley.

L3790.text: This rental's making a grinding noise every time I hit the brakes.
Don't drive it another mile. Take it back to the counter and have them give you a different one.

L3791.text: Officer, is there any way through to Highway Nine? This road's blocked off.
There's been a rockslide. You'll have to go back to the bridge and follow the orange detour signs.

L3792.text: I'm new on base. Can you tell me how to get to the commissary?
Sure. Go past the gas station, take the second left, and it's the big building across from the gym.

L3793.text: My parents are flying in Saturday. Can they just drive onto the base with me?
Not without passes. Stop at the visitor center by the main gate first, and bring their IDs.

L3794.text: Weren't we supposed to turn at that last light?
Oh no, you're right. I was so busy talking I didn't even notice. Let's turn around at the next driveway.

L3795.text: I'm looking for building twenty-two fifteen, but the numbers around here seem to jump all over the place.
They do. Twenty-two fifteen is actually behind twenty-one ten. Go around back by the loading dock.

L3796.text: Should I call a cab to get to the conference center?
Save your money. It's just across the river, and you could walk there before a cab even showed up.

L3797.text: How will I recognize your street? All the houses out there look the same.
Look for the water tower. We're the first right after it, the house with the blue truck in front.

L3798.text: My phone says the hotel is right here, but this is an empty parking lot.
Your map must be out of date. The hotel moved downtown last year. I'll call for the new address.

L3799.text: I'll be getting back late from the airport. Is the back gate open after ten?
No, it closes at nine. After that, the main gate is the only way in.

L3800.text: The elevator in the parking garage is out of order again.
Great. And we're on the sixth level with four suitcases.

L3801.text: Billeting's full the week of my course. Where am I supposed to stay?
They'll give you a statement of non-availability, so you can book a hotel off base and still get reimbursed.

L3802.text: My flight doesn't land until ten tonight. Will you still hold my room?
Only if you guarantee it with a credit card. Otherwise, it's released at six.

L3803.text: We're a little early. Is our room ready yet?
Not quite, ma'am. Check-in is at three, but I can keep your luggage behind the desk while you have lunch.

L3804.text: Our room's right above the hotel bar, and the music didn't stop until two.
I'm terribly sorry, sir. Let me move you to the top floor, and tonight's on us.

L3805.text: Our flight isn't until seven. Any chance we could check out later than eleven?
I can give you until one at no charge. After that, it's half the nightly rate.

L3806.text: My key card isn't working. The light just keeps flashing red.
It was probably sitting next to your phone. Hand it over, and I'll reprogram it for you.

L3807.text: Does the hotel shuttle run to the airport early in the morning?
Starting at four thirty, every half hour. Just sign up at the desk the night before.

L3808.text: The only hotel near the course charges a hundred and forty a night, and my lodging allowance is only one twenty.
Then either you cover the difference yourself, or you look a little farther out.

L3809.text: Could I get a wake-up call at four fifteen, please?
Certainly. The breakfast room won't be open that early, so I'll have a breakfast bag waiting for you at the desk.

L3810.text: Do you allow dogs? We're moving across the country and have two with us.
We take pets up to forty pounds, with a twenty-five-dollar fee per night for each one.

L3811.text: I turned in my travel voucher, but finance sent it back to me.
Let me guess. You gave them the credit card slip instead of the hotel's itemized bill.

L3812.text: My bag didn't come off the carousel, and I've got a meeting first thing tomorrow.
Fill out this claim form. Most delayed bags turn up on the next flight, and we'll deliver it to your hotel tonight.

L3813.text: Your suitcase is fifty-six pounds, sir. Anything over fifty is a hundred-dollar fee.
Hang on. Let me move a few things into my backpack.

L3814.text: One of the wheels on my suitcase snapped off. I'll deal with it once I get to the hotel.
I wouldn't. Most airlines won't accept a damage claim after you've left the airport.

L3815.text: These aren't my clothes! This bag looks exactly like mine, but it's someone else's.
Then yours may still be going around the carousel, unless somebody else grabbed it by mistake, too.

L3816.text: Why did you tie that bright orange ribbon on your suitcase handle?
Half the bags on every flight are black. This way I can spot mine from across the room.

L3817.text: My orders say I'm allowed two checked bags. Does the airline charge for them?
Not when you're traveling on orders. Show them at the counter, and they'll waive the fees.

L3818.text: They took my sunscreen at security. It was a brand-new bottle!
Was it bigger than three point four ounces? Anything larger has to go in your checked bag.

L3819.text: The movers are coming to pack us out on the fifteenth, right?
That was the plan, but they called this morning. It's been pushed back to the twenty-second because of the holiday.

L3820.text: The estimate came back at fourteen thousand pounds, and my allowance is only twelve thousand.
Then it's time for a yard sale. Otherwise, the extra weight comes out of your own pocket.

L3821.text: Our quarters at the new base won't be ready for three weeks.
Temporary lodging is fine, but the allowance only covers ten days. You'll pay for the rest.

L3822.text: Has anyone from the new unit contacted you about your arrival?
Yes, my sponsor emailed. She's meeting me at the airport and has already reserved a room for me.

L3823.text: How long is the wait for on-base housing for a family of four?
Six to nine months, last I heard. Most people rent in town and move on when their name comes up.

L3824.text: I'm thinking about doing the move myself with a rented truck. Is it worth it?
If you've got the time and a strong back, yes. The government pays you what the movers would have cost.

L3825.text: Do I need to hand-carry the kids' school records, or will the old school send them?
Bring copies yourself. Mailed records get lost, and the new school won't enroll them without proof.

L3826.text: I've got eleven offices on my in-processing checklist. Think I can knock it out in a day?
Not a chance. Half of them close at noon, and finance alone can take all morning.

L3827.text: Is there anything special we need to do to bring our cat to Japan?
Start now. She'll need a microchip, two rabies shots, and a blood test, and the whole process takes months.

L3828.text: Should I ship my car to Italy or sell it before I go?
Your car's eleven years old. Once you pay to have it inspected and registered over there, you're better off selling.

L3829.text: We don't leave until August. Do I really have to book the movers this early?
Summer's the busiest season. If you wait until July, you'll get whatever date is left, if there's any at all.

L3830.text: The movers scratched our dining table pretty badly. Is it even worth filing a claim?
Absolutely. But there's a deadline of seventy-five days to report it, so don't put it off.

L3831.text: I'm dropping my car off at the shipping center tomorrow. I'll fill up the tank on the way.
Don't. They won't accept it with more than a quarter tank of gas.

L3832.text: If I ship my car next week, when will it get to Hawaii?
Figure five to six weeks. Most people rent something or buy a cheap one to get around until it shows up.

L3833.text: Can I pack some boxes in the trunk when I ship my car? It's going overseas anyway.
Nope. Everything has to come out except the spare and the jack, or they'll turn you away.

L3834.text: We've got two cars. Will the government ship both of them to Germany?
Just one. If you want the second one over there, you'll be paying for it yourself.

L3835.text: We've been sitting at the gate for forty minutes. What's the holdup?
The captain says we're waiting our turn to be de-iced. There's a long line of planes ahead of us.

L3836.text: Have they ordered an evacuation for the base yet?
Not yet, but they're saying it could come by noon. I'd load the car now so we don't get stuck in traffic.

L3837.text: Why are we landing in Richmond? This flight was supposed to go to Norfolk.
Fog. The pilot said you can barely see anything there, so they'll either bus us down or wait for it to lift.

L3838.text: The interstate's closed from here to Denver because of the snow.
Then there's no point sitting in the lobby. Let's ask the front desk to keep us one more night.

L3839.text: The app says our flight is on time, but there's nobody at the gate.
There's a ground stop because of lightning. Nothing takes off until the storm passes, whatever your app says.

L3840.text: Can I take the underpass on Grant Street to get to the gym?
Not after last night's rain. It's under two feet of water. Go up Fifth and cross at the light instead.

L3841.text: Is the base opening late this morning because of the ice?
Two hours, according to the hotline. Essential personnel still report on time, though, and that includes you.

L3842.text: Is the ferry to the island still running this afternoon?
They canceled the two o'clock because of high winds, and the four o'clock doesn't look any better.

L3843.text: Sir, the captain has turned on the seat belt sign. I'll need you to return to your seat.
Can't it wait two minutes? There's a line for the restroom, and I'm next.

L3844.text: I'm going to be about an hour late returning the rental. Will they charge me for another day?
There's a twenty-nine-minute grace period. After that, it's an hourly rate, up to the price of a full day.

L3845.text: I need to go on sick call tomorrow. Do you know what time they start seeing people?
Sign-in closes at zero seven thirty, so if you show up after formation, you're out of luck.

L3846.text: My dental appointment got moved up to Thursday morning. That's the day of our ruck march, isn't it?
It is, but a dental exam takes priority. Just let the platoon sergeant know ahead of time.

L3847.text: How did your fitness test go? You were worried about the two-mile run.
I beat my old time by almost a minute, but my push-ups were way down. I must have pulled something in my shoulder.

L3848.text: I got to the dining facility at one fifteen, and the doors were already locked.
On weekends they switch to brunch hours. You should have gone before twelve thirty.

L3849.text: They're calling for thunderstorms after three. Should we still hold the softball game at four?
Let's play it by ear. If there's any lightning, we'll clear the field and wait it out.

L3850.text: I'm heading out for a run. It's already getting dark, though.
Then grab your reflective belt. Drivers on Perimeter Road can hardly see runners after sunset.

L3851.text: Have you gotten your flu shot yet? The deadline for our unit is the end of the month.
Not yet. I'd rather wait until the walk-in clinic isn't so packed. The line was huge last week.

L3852.text: Is the gym on the north side open twenty-four hours now?
Only with your ID card at the side door. The front desk isn't staffed after ten, so the pool is off-limits.

L3853.text: I dropped off my prescription at the pharmacy an hour ago. Is it ready yet?
Let me check. It looks like we're waiting on your doctor to approve the dose. Could you come back after lunch?

L3854.text: This place is packed. Should we put our name on the list or try the diner across the street?
The hostess said forty-five minutes. I'm starving, so I'm not waiting that long.

L3855.text: It's supposed to hit a hundred and two this afternoon. Are we still doing the obstacle course?
Not until tomorrow at first light. The heat index is already in the danger zone, and it's only going to climb.

L3856.text: I'm just changing one light bulb in the warehouse. Do I really need someone to hold the ladder?
Every time. The last guy who skipped that ended up with a broken wrist.

L3857.text: You look exhausted. Didn't you get any sleep after your shift?
Barely. The construction next to my barracks started at six, and I'd only gotten in at four.

L3858.text: The dentist says I need my wisdom teeth out. Will I be on quarters afterward?
Usually for a day or two. You'll want soft food for a while, so stock up on soup and yogurt.

L3859.text: Are you playing in the intramural basketball game tonight?
I wish. I sprained my ankle on Monday, and the doctor told me to stay off the court for two weeks.

L3860.text: Do I have to pay at the dining facility now that I've moved off post?
Yes. Once you start drawing a food allowance, your meal card stops working, so bring cash or a card.

L3861.text: The roads are icy this morning. Is the post on a delayed reporting schedule?
Two-hour delay for non-essential personnel. Since you work at the fire station, though, you're expected at the normal time.

L3862.text: The fire alarm's going off again. It's probably just another drill, right?
Maybe, but we still walk out to the parking lot and wait for the all clear. No exceptions.

L3863.text: Your eyes are all red. Are you coming down with something?
No, it's just allergies. The pollen count is sky-high this week, and I left my medicine at home.

L3864.text: Did the clinic call you back about your blood test?
They did. Everything came back normal, but they want me to cut down on salt and come back in six months.

L3865.text: I signed up for the water survival test on Friday. Any advice?
Practice treading water in uniform. It's a lot harder than in a swimsuit, and that's where most people fail.

L3866.text: I'm allergic to peanuts. Is there any way to know what's in the food at the dining facility?
Ask the shift leader. They keep the recipe cards behind the counter, and every ingredient is listed.

L3867.text: Do you still want to go to the lake on Saturday? It's supposed to rain all weekend.
Only in the morning, according to the radio. We could leave after lunch and still get a few hours in.

L3868.text: Do I really need earplugs for the range? I'm only going to fire twenty rounds.
Twenty is plenty to damage your hearing. And Range Control won't let you on the firing line without them.

L3869.text: I've had a headache all afternoon, and I feel kind of dizzy.
How much water have you had today? With all that time outside, I'd bet you're dehydrated.

L3870.text: I've been calling the appointment line since seven, and it just keeps ringing.
Everybody calls first thing in the morning. Try the online portal; you can usually book a slot in a couple of minutes.

L3871.text: Lunch is on me today. You covered it last time.
If you insist. But let me at least leave the tip.

L3872.text: Is the morning flight to the training site still on? I can barely see across the road.
It's on hold until the fog lifts. Operations will make the call at ten.

L3873.text: Why did the sergeant stop the truck before it backed out of the motor pool?
Nobody was ground guiding it. You never back up a military vehicle without someone outside watching.

L3874.text: How's your knee? Are you back to running yet?
Not quite. Physical therapy has me on the bike and in the pool for another month before I can hit the road.

L3875.text: My orders to Korea came through. Do I need any shots before I go?
Probably a few. Take your shot record to immunizations; they'll compare it with the requirements for that region.

L3876.text: I've only got ten minutes before the bus leaves. Is there time to eat?
Not a sit-down meal, but the DFAC has a grab-and-go line by the side entrance. You can eat on the bus.

L3877.text: The wind is really picking up. Will that affect our qualification scores?
It could at the longer targets. Watch the flags along the range and adjust your aim a little into the wind.

L3878.text: This floor cleaner isn't working very well. Want me to mix in some bleach?
Absolutely not. Those two together can give off toxic fumes. Just scrub harder.

L3879.text: I keep getting headaches when I read. Do you think I need glasses?
Could be. The optometry clinic takes walk-ins on Tuesday mornings, so you won't need an appointment.

L3880.text: Are you running the base ten-K on Saturday?
I signed up, but I haven't trained much. I'll probably jog the first half and walk the rest.

L3881.text: Excuse me, I ordered my steak well done, but this is still pink in the middle.
I'm so sorry about that. I'll have the kitchen put it back on the grill, and your dessert is on the house.

L3882.text: I haven't been sleeping well since I got back from deployment. Is that normal?
It's pretty common. But if it keeps up, talk to someone at behavioral health. They see this all the time.

L3883.text: The sirens just went off. Is it a tornado warning or just a test?
Tests are only on the first Wednesday at noon, so this is real. Get to the basement now.

L3884.text: It's freezing in this office. Can I plug my space heater into that power strip?
Better not. Heaters draw too much power for a strip like that. Use the wall outlet instead.

L3885.text: My mouth will be numb for a few more hours, and I was planning to grab a burger on the way home.
I'd hold off. You could bite your cheek and not notice until the feeling comes back.

L3886.text: Personnel says I can't start the leadership course next month. Something about my medical readiness being red.
That usually means your annual health assessment is overdue. Book it today, and you should be cleared in time.

L3887.text: I rolled my ankle on the stairs. Should I put heat on it?
Not right away. Ice it and keep it up on a pillow for the first day or two. Heat can make the swelling worse.

L3888.text: Doc put me on a temporary profile for my back. Does that mean I'm off PT completely?
Not at all. You'll just do whatever the profile allows, like walking or the stationary bike, while everyone else runs.

L3889.text: I took some nighttime cold medicine by mistake at lunch, and I'm supposed to drive to the airport at three.
I wouldn't. That stuff knocks me out for hours. I'll take you myself.

L3890.text: I'm giving blood at the drive this afternoon. I skipped breakfast, so I figured I'd just go on an empty stomach.
Bad idea. People who haven't eaten are the ones who get lightheaded. Have a real lunch first.

L3891.text: They're dilating my eyes at the optometry appointment tomorrow. Is that a big deal?
Not really, but everything will be blurry and bright for a few hours. Bring sunglasses and have somebody else do the driving.

L3892.text: My tooth has been killing me since last night, but the dental clinic's next opening is three weeks out.
With pain like that, go to dental sick call in the morning. They'll see you the same day.

L3893.text: Wow, your neck is bright red. Were you at the beach all weekend?
Just the pool, and only for an hour. I fell asleep on the lounge chair and forgot to put sunscreen back on after swimming.

L3894.text: I completely forgot about my physical therapy appointment this morning. Is that going to be a problem?
It might. Miss too many and they can drop you. Next time, call a day ahead if you can't make it.

L3895.text: We just got back from three days in the woods. I'm dying for a hot shower.
Good, and while you're at it, check yourself for ticks, especially behind the knees and along your hairline.

L3896.text: I just got new boots. Think I can wear them on the twelve-mile march Saturday?
Only if you want blisters the size of quarters. Wear your old pair, and break the new ones in around the barracks first.

L3897.text: I've been throwing up since midnight. Should I still come in for the inventory today?
Absolutely not. The last thing we need is the whole section catching it. Stay home, keep drinking fluids, and I'll cover for you.

L3898.text: My yearly hearing test is set for the afternoon of our range day. That shouldn't matter, should it?
Actually, it might. Your ears need a break from loud noise before the test, or the results won't be accurate.

L3899.text: My daughter's fever went up again tonight, and the clinic is closed until Monday.
Call the nurse advice line. They're available around the clock and can tell you whether she needs the emergency room.

L3900.text: I tried lifting after work yesterday, but I waited twenty minutes just to use a bench.
Five o'clock is rush hour there. Try lunchtime, or five in the morning; you'll have the place to yourself.

L3901.text: The six a.m. spin class is full again. I've been on the waiting list all week.
Just show up anyway. Any bikes that aren't claimed by five past six go to whoever's standing at the door.

L3902.text: Our soccer team is short a goalie for the tournament. You played in high school, didn't you?
Years ago, and I was a defender. But if you're really stuck, I'll give it a shot.

L3903.text: I pulled my hamstring sprinting during PT this morning. I can barely walk.
Did you warm up first? I see people go straight from the car to all-out sprints, and that's asking for trouble.

L3904.text: I want to swim some laps tonight. Is the indoor pool open?
It's open, but from six to eight it's family swim, so the lanes come out. You'd be better off going after eight.

L3905.text: The bowling alley is starting a Thursday night league. Want to be on my team?
I'd love to, but I've got night classes on Thursdays until December. Ask me again in the spring.

L3906.text: I'd like a workout plan, but personal trainers downtown charge a fortune.
Have you asked at the fitness center on post? They have trainers on staff, and the sessions don't cost a thing.

L3907.text: Let's hit the climbing wall at the rec center after lunch.
Didn't you see the sign? It's shut down until the safety inspector signs off on the new ropes.

L3908.text: My shins have been aching after every run this month.
How old are your running shoes? Once they've got a few hundred miles on them, the cushioning is gone, and your legs take the beating.

L3909.text: Did you get us a tee time for Sunday?
Seven fifteen. I know it's early, but by noon the course will be like an oven, and it fills up fast anyway.

L3910.text: I'm going to carry fifty pounds on every training ruck, starting tomorrow.
I'd build up to it, a few pounds a week. Jumping straight to that is how people get stress fractures.

L3911.text: Is it true the senior leaders serve the food at the Thanksgiving meal in the dining facility?
Every year. The commander and the first sergeant even dress up in their best uniforms to do it.

L3912.text: Excuse me, could we get separate checks? There are six of us.
I'm sorry, for parties of six or more we can only do one bill. But you're welcome to split it among yourselves.

L3913.text: The pizza driver just called. She says the gate guards won't let her onto post.
That's normal without a pass. Somebody will have to walk out to the visitor center and meet her.

L3914.text: Where's everybody going for lunch? The dining facility is practically empty.
It's Friday. The taco truck parks outside headquarters, and the line's usually around the building by eleven thirty.

L3915.text: I called the steakhouse about a table for eight on Saturday. The earliest they have is nine thirty.
That's way past the kids' bedtime. Let's see if they can fit us in on Sunday instead.

L3916.text: Are we stuck with MREs the whole time we're in the field this week?
Only for lunch. The cooks are bringing out hot chow every evening, as long as the trucks can get through the mud.

L3917.text: Somebody left the leftover chicken on the counter all night. Is it still okay to eat?
I wouldn't risk it. Cooked meat that's been sitting out that long can make you seriously sick. Toss it.

L3918.text: My new roommate doesn't eat meat. Will she find anything at the dining facility besides salad?
Plenty. There's always a meatless main dish on the line, and the short-order grill makes veggie burgers if you ask.

L3919.text: That coffee line is out the door. We'll never make the eight o'clock briefing.
Watch this. I'll order on the app, and it'll be waiting on the pickup counter before we even get inside.

L3920.text: The bill came to a hundred and forty dollars. How much should we leave for the tip?
Look at the bottom. They've already added eighteen percent because we're a big group, so we're all set.

L3921.text: I've got KP on Saturday. What does that even involve?
Mostly washing pots and mopping in the dining facility. Bring a change of socks; your feet will be soaked by noon.

L3922.text: I went back to the buffet four times. I don't think I can move.
Your eyes were bigger than your stomach again. Next time, take small portions and wait a few minutes before going back.

L3923.text: The forecast says it might drop below freezing at the campsite Saturday night. Should we still go?
Sure, as long as we pack the cold-weather sleeping bags and a few extra layers. A little frost never hurt anyone.

L3924.text: The hurricane's supposed to make landfall Thursday. Do you think they'll evacuate the base?
Hard to say yet. Either way, fill your gas tank tonight and pick up water before the stores run out.

L3925.text: Why is nobody in the water? It's a perfect beach day.
See the red flags by the lifeguard stand? Rip currents. They can pull even strong swimmers out, so swimming's off for today.

L3926.text: I want to hike the ridge trail tomorrow. Did it survive all that rain?
The lower half washed out in a mudslide. Rangers have it closed, but the lake loop's open and just as pretty.

L3927.text: I'm taking the kids fishing at the pond behind the commissary. Do I need anything besides poles and bait?
You'll need a fishing permit from the outdoor recreation office. Kids are usually free, but adults get checked.

L3928.text: Let's hold the section barbecue at the park pavilion on Saturday. We can just show up, right?
Not on a weekend. You have to reserve it through the rec office, and they book up weeks ahead.

L3929.text: This fog is so thick. Should I turn on my high beams so I can see better?
That actually makes it worse; the light just bounces back at you. Stick with your low beams and slow down.

L3930.text: My windshield's covered in ice, and I'm already late. Can I just pour hot water on it?
Don't. The sudden temperature change can crack the glass. Start the engine, run the defroster, and use a scraper.

L3931.text: It's pouring. Is the change of command ceremony still on the parade field at ten?
They moved it inside to the gym, but the time didn't change. Seating will be tight, so get there early.

L3932.text: It's eight degrees with the wind chill. Are we still doing PT outside this morning?
We are, but warm caps and gloves are authorized. Layer up, and you'll be fine once you get moving.

L3933.text: Why did the lifeguard blow the whistle? It isn't even raining.
She saw lightning off to the west. Everyone has to stay out of the water until thirty minutes after the last strike.

L3934.text: Why did the MP stop you this morning? You were only jogging.
I had my earbuds in. Apparently they're not allowed while running on post roads because you can't hear traffic coming.

L3935.text: The smoke detector in my hallway keeps chirping every minute. There's no smoke anywhere.
That chirp usually means the battery is low. Swap it out tonight; don't just pull the battery and forget about it.

L3936.text: These boxes of copier paper weigh a ton. I'll just carry two at a time to save trips.
And wreck your back? Use the hand truck in the supply room. It's there for a reason.

L3937.text: I took them off for a second. They keep fogging up.
There are anti-fog wipes in the cabinet. Use one, but they go back on before you touch that grinder.

L3938.text: It's so cold that I warm up my truck in the garage every morning with the door shut.
Stop doing that. The fumes build up fast, and you can't smell them. Open the door first.

L3939.text: I just got off a twelve-hour night shift, and my sister's expecting me for lunch. It's a four-hour drive.
Get a few hours of sleep first. She'd rather you show up late than not at all.

L3940.text: I'm almost out of water, but that stream looks really clean. I'll just fill my bottle there.
Not without treating it first. Clear water can still carry bacteria. I've got purification tablets in my pack.

L3941.text: Are you taking the kids to the base pool this afternoon like you promised?
I was planning to, but have you looked outside? Those clouds are getting darker by the minute.

L3942.text: That jacket looks great on you. Are you going to buy it?
At two hundred dollars? Not unless it goes on sale. I'll keep an eye on it.

L3943.text: I'd like to deposit this check, but I left my account number at home.
No problem, ma'am. If you have a photo ID, I can look it up for you.

L3944.text: The kitchen faucet has been dripping all week. Should I call the housing office?
You could, but they'll take ages. My brother fixed ours in ten minutes with a new washer.

L3945.text: Somebody backed into my car in the commissary parking lot and just drove away.
That's awful. Did anyone get the license plate? Without it, your insurance might not cover the whole thing.

L3946.text: Our new neighbors' dog barked half the night again. I'm about to go over there and complain.
I'd give them a few days. They just moved in, and the poor thing is probably scared.

L3947.text: We're having a few people over for Thanksgiving. Would you and your wife like to join us?
We'd love that. My in-laws were supposed to visit, but their flight got canceled, so we're free.

L3948.text: Honey, did you remember to sign Emma's permission slip for the field trip?
Oh no, it's still on the refrigerator. Can you drop it off at the school on your way to work?

L3949.text: Didn't you say you were saving up for a new TV? I saw one at the PX for four hundred dollars.
I was, but then the transmission went out on my truck. So much for that plan.

L3950.text: The bank charged me a thirty-five dollar fee. Apparently my account went below zero last week.
Didn't you sign up for overdraft protection? I thought it would move money over from savings automatically.

L3951.text: How's the apartment hunt going? Did you look at that place near the main gate?
I did. The rent's reasonable, but the walls are so thin I could hear the neighbors' TV from the bedroom.

L3952.text: My car insurance is going up again, even though I haven't had a single accident.
Have you shopped around? When I compared rates last spring, I ended up saving almost three hundred a year.

L3953.text: Excuse me, I think some of your mail got delivered to my box by mistake.
Thanks so much. I've been waiting for a package slip all week. I was starting to wonder what happened.

L3954.text: Are you coming to the unit's Fourth of July cookout? Everyone's bringing a side dish.
I wish I could, but I'm driving to my sister's that weekend. Maybe next year.

L3955.text: Could you watch the baby for an hour? I have a dentist appointment at three.
I'm supposed to meet Dave at the gym at two thirty, but I can always call and push it back.

L3956.text: I'd like to return these boots. They're a size too small.
I can exchange them for you, but since you don't have the receipt, I can't give you cash back.

L3957.text: Is the bank on base open on Saturdays? I need to get a cashier's check for my landlord.
Only until noon, and the line is usually out the door by ten. I'd get there early.

L3958.text: Did the maintenance guy ever come to look at your air conditioner?
He came, took one look, and said he'd have to order a part. So I'm sleeping with a fan for now.

L3959.text: Your check engine light has been on for weeks. Aren't you going to get it looked at?
I keep meaning to, but the car runs fine. I'll take it in after payday.

L3960.text: The people next door are throwing a party tonight. Should we ask them to keep it down?
Let's not. They invited us, remember? It would look strange to complain about a party we skipped.

L3961.text: Are you flying home for Christmas this year?
I looked at ticket prices and nearly fell out of my chair. I think I'll drive, even if it takes two days.

L3962.text: My mother-in-law is staying with us for a month. Any advice?
Give her something to do. When my mom visited, she reorganized my whole kitchen, and honestly, I didn't mind one bit.

L3963.text: I'm thinking about getting one of those warehouse club memberships. Is it worth the sixty dollars?
Only if you have the space. We bought forty rolls of paper towels, and they're still in our hallway.

L3964.text: I'm trying to transfer money to my parents overseas. Do you know how long it takes?
Through the bank, usually three to five business days. But watch out, the exchange fees can really add up.

L3965.text: Our landlord said he'd paint the living room before we moved in, but it's still the same ugly green.
Did you get that promise in writing? If not, I'm afraid it's your word against his.

L3966.text: I'm thinking of buying a used car from a guy in my unit. He wants six thousand for it.
Before you hand over any cash, have a mechanic check it out. You don't want to buy someone else's problems.

L3967.text: Have you met the couple who moved into the corner house? They seem really friendly.
Friendly, sure. They've borrowed my ladder, my lawn mower, and my drill, and I haven't seen any of them since.

L3968.text: Jessica invited us to her wedding in June. Can you get leave that week?
I already put in for it, but my commander hasn't signed off yet. Don't book the hotel just yet.

L3969.text: Tommy says he wants a puppy for his birthday. What do you think?
He also wanted a hamster last year, and guess who ended up cleaning the cage?

L3970.text: I can't believe how much I spent on groceries this month. It was almost six hundred dollars.
That's what happens when you go shopping hungry. Try making a list and sticking to it.

L3971.text: I just got a text saying my debit card was used in another state. I've never even been there.
Don't reply to that text. Call the number on the back of your card and ask them directly.

L3972.text: I heard you're moving off base. Are you going to rent or buy?
With orders coming in two years, buying doesn't make much sense. But my husband keeps looking at houses online anyway.

L3973.text: A rock hit my windshield on the highway, and now there's a crack across the whole thing.
Check your policy. A lot of insurance plans cover glass with no deductible, so it might not cost you anything.

L3974.text: The guy upstairs is moving furniture again at midnight. This is the third time this week.
Have you actually talked to him about it? He might not realize how much noise carries.

L3975.text: What are you doing for New Year's Eve? A few of us are going downtown to watch the fireworks.
Thanks, but crowds aren't my thing. I'll probably just watch them on TV and be asleep by twelve thirty.

L3976.text: Did the kids finish their homework before they went outside to play?
They told me they did, but I found Sarah's math worksheet under the couch, completely blank.

L3977.text: This coffee maker was on sale for forty dollars last week, and now it's back up to sixty.
Ask the manager. Some stores will honor a sale price if it ended only a few days ago.

L3978.text: We're finally applying for a home loan. Is there anything we should do first?
Pull your credit report and fix any mistakes. My husband found an old phone bill on his that wasn't even his.

L3979.text: The toilet upstairs keeps running all night. Can you take a look at it this weekend?
I'd be happy to, but remember what happened when I tried to fix the sink last year? Maybe we should call a plumber.

L3980.text: I need to get my car registered in this state. Do I have to go to the DMV in person?
Not anymore. Most of it can be done online now, though you'll still need to get it inspected first.

L3981.text: Mrs. Lopez next door is going to be in the hospital for a week. Should we do something?
I could mow her lawn on Saturday, and maybe you could bring her mail in every afternoon.

L3982.text: We're having a housewarming party on Saturday. Can you make it?
Saturday's my daughter's soccer tournament, but if it ends early, we'll swing by for a bit.

L3983.text: Your son is getting so tall. How old is he now?
He'll be thirteen in March, and he eats more than I do. Our grocery bill has nearly doubled.

L3984.text: Should I pay for this laptop with my credit card or use the store's payment plan?
Read the fine print first. Those plans look cheap until you see the interest rate after six months.

L3985.text: I need to open a checking account for my daughter. She just started her first job.
If she's under eighteen, you'll have to come in with her and sign as a joint owner.

L3986.text: The housing office says there's a six-month waiting list for a three-bedroom on base.
Six months? Then you'd better start looking off base. You can't keep living out of a hotel.

L3987.text: I'm driving to Texas next week. Do you think my old tires will make it?
I saw them yesterday. Honestly, I wouldn't take them to the grocery store, let alone across three states.

L3988.text: Someone's car has been parked in front of our driveway since this morning.
I think it belongs to the Parkers' guests. Why don't you knock on their door before calling for a tow truck?

L3989.text: Are you decorating for Halloween this year? Your yard was the best on the street.
Don't remind me. It took me a week to set up and two weeks to take down. This year it's just a pumpkin.

L3990.text: Where's the remote? I've looked everywhere in the living room.
Did you check the baby's toy box? Last time we found your car keys in there.

L3991.text: Would you like to buy the extended warranty for this washing machine? It's only eighty-nine dollars for three years.
The machine itself only costs three hundred. I think I'll take my chances.

L3992.text: I went to cash my paycheck at the bank, but they said they'd hold the funds for three days.
That happens with large checks sometimes. Next time, have it deposited directly, and you won't have to wait.

L3993.text: There's water coming through the ceiling in the bathroom. I think it's from the apartment above us.
Turn off the main valve just in case, and I'll go upstairs to see if anyone's home.

L3994.text: My daughter just got her driver's license. How much will it cost to add her to our insurance?
Quite a bit, but if she keeps a B average in school, a lot of companies give a good-student discount.

L3995.text: The new family across the street has four kids. It's going to get noisy around here.
Maybe, but it'll be nice for our boys to have someone to play with besides each other.

L3996.text: My sister's getting married in Hawaii, and the whole family is invited.
Lucky you! But a wedding in Hawaii must cost guests a fortune. Are you actually going?

L3997.text: I'm exhausted. The baby woke up four times last night.
Why don't you take a nap this afternoon? I'll handle dinner and bath time tonight.

L3998.text: I ordered a sofa online three weeks ago, and it still hasn't shipped.
That's why I'd rather buy furniture in a store. At least you can sit on it and take it home the same day.

L3999.text: The ATM kept my card and didn't give me any money. What should I do?
If it happened at a branch, go inside right away. If it's after hours, call the bank's twenty-four-hour line.

L4000.text: Is it true you're breaking your lease early? Won't that cost you?
Normally, yes, but military orders let you out of it without a penalty. I just need to give thirty days' notice.

L4001.text: Did you get your car back from the body shop?
Yesterday, finally. They matched the paint so well you can't even tell where the dent was.

L4002.text: Our neighbor's tree hangs over our fence, and the leaves are everywhere. Can I just cut the branches?
Maybe, but I'd talk to him first. You don't want to start a war over a few leaves.

L4003.text: My parents want us to spend Christmas with them, but your parents asked first.
Why don't we do Christmas Eve at mine and Christmas Day at yours? They only live an hour apart.

L4004.text: Did you tell your dad we're selling the old family car?
Not yet. He taught me to drive in that car, so I'm waiting for the right moment.

L4005.text: I can't decide between the cheaper vacuum and the one that's twice the price.
My dad always says, 'Buy cheap, buy twice.' Ours broke after six months.

L4006.text: My bank keeps charging me a monthly fee because my balance drops below five hundred dollars.
The credit union on base doesn't have a minimum balance. I switched last year and haven't paid a fee since.

L4007.text: I finally found a house to rent, but the owner wants first and last month's rent plus a deposit.
Ouch. That's three months' worth of money up front. Can you swing it?

L4008.text: My car battery died again this morning. That's the second time this month.
If it's a new battery, the problem could be your alternator. Have a mechanic test the whole charging system.

L4009.text: I'm going out of town for two weeks. Would you mind keeping an eye on my house?
Not at all. I'll check on it every evening when I walk the dog. Just leave me a spare key.

L4010.text: Thanks for inviting us to the barbecue. What can we bring?
Just yourselves. Well, actually, if you have extra folding chairs, we could use a few.

L4011.text: You promised you'd fix the fence this weekend, and now you're going fishing?
The fish are biting today, and the fence will still be there tomorrow. I'll do it Sunday, I swear.

L4012.text: Do you know if the commissary is open on Mondays?
It's closed Mondays, and the line on Sunday is a nightmare. I usually go Tuesday morning when it's empty.

L4013.text: I want to start saving for my son's college. Is a regular savings account good enough?
It's safe, but the interest is next to nothing. You might look into an education savings plan instead.

L4014.text: The heater in our bedroom stopped working last night. It was freezing.
I put in a work order this morning. They said someone would come by between eight and noon tomorrow.

L4015.text: Did you report that little fender bender to your insurance company?
I thought about it, but the damage was only three hundred dollars, and my deductible is five hundred.

L4016.text: Did you hear? The Johnsons are selling their house. The sign went up this morning.
Really? They just redid their kitchen. I wonder if he got orders.

L4017.text: We're doing a gift exchange at the office party. The limit is twenty dollars.
Twenty? Last year Mike brought a fifty-dollar gift card, and everyone else looked cheap.

L4018.text: Mom called. She's wondering if we can host the family reunion this summer.
In this little house? We'd have people sleeping in the bathtub. Maybe we could rent a cabin instead.

L4019.text: I just found two charges for the same dinner on my credit card statement.
That happens. Call the card company and dispute the second charge. They'll usually take it off while they look into it.

L4020.text: I'd like to withdraw two thousand dollars in cash, please.
Certainly. For amounts over one thousand, though, I'll need to see a photo ID and get a manager's approval.

L4021.text: The neighbor's kids keep riding their bikes across our lawn. The grass is completely worn down.
Want me to put a few rocks along the edge? That usually sends a message without anybody having to say a word.

L4022.text: These shoes were half off, so I bought three pairs.
Half off three pairs is still a pair and a half at full price. Did you really need three?

L4023.text: Why is there a hold on my account? I paid off my credit card last month.
Let me take a look. Ah, it's not the credit card. It looks like a check you deposited bounced.

L4024.text: We're supposed to move out Friday, and the carpet still has that big stain from the dog.
If we don't get it cleaned, they'll take it out of our deposit. I'll call a carpet cleaner today.

L4025.text: I'm selling my car before I PCS overseas. How much do you think I can get for it?
Check the value online first. Dealers usually offer much less, so you might do better selling it yourself.

L4026.text: The bank turned down my application for a car loan. They said my credit history was too short.
That's common for young people. Having someone with good credit co-sign might help you qualify.

L4027.text: The guy next door keeps leaving his trash cans at the curb for days.
It drives me crazy too. But he's been working double shifts since his wife had surgery, so I just roll them in for him.

L4028.text: The cashier gave me change for a twenty, but I paid with a fifty.
Go back right now before she closes her register. Once she counts the drawer, it's much harder to prove.

L4029.text: Did you remember to pick up Lily from daycare? They close at six.
Oh no, I thought it was your turn today. It's five fifty. I can make it if I leave right now.

L4030.text: Did you see that the Garcias painted their house bright purple?
Hard to miss. I'm not sure the homeowners' association is going to be thrilled about it.

L4031.text: We're throwing a surprise party for Dad's sixtieth. Can you keep him busy Saturday afternoon?
Leave it to me. I'll ask him to help me pick out a new grill. That'll take hours.

L4032.text: There's a strange smell in the hallway, kind of like rotten eggs.
That could be a gas leak. Get everyone outside and call the gas company from the yard, not from in here.

L4033.text: I found the same printer online for thirty dollars less than you paid.
Did it include shipping? Because by the time I paid that, it would have cost me more.

L4034.text: I let my friend borrow my car, and he got into an accident. Whose insurance pays?
In most states, the insurance follows the car, not the driver. So yours would probably pay first.

L4035.text: Our neighbor's smoke alarm has been beeping all day. I don't think anyone's home.
It's probably just a low battery. That chirp happens every minute until somebody changes it.

L4036.text: Did you get the invitation to Captain Reed's retirement ceremony?
I did. It says RSVP by the tenth, and I still don't know if I'll be back from training by then.

L4037.text: I heard the language lab is closed for repairs until Monday. Where are you going to practice your listening?
My roommate has the same audio files on his laptop, so I'll borrow it tonight.

L4038.text: My phone keeps dying by lunchtime, even though I charge it every single night.
No wonder. You've got about thirty apps running in the background.

L4039.text: Let's grab dinner after the briefing tomorrow. And put your wallet away; it's on me this time.
Deal, but I'm choosing the place. Last time you picked, we waited an hour for a table.

L4040.text: I've been teaching myself guitar from online videos, but my fingers still hurt after ten minutes.
That makes two of us. I gave up on the violin after a month for the same reason.

L4041.text: How did you learn so many new words before the vocabulary exam?
I put flashcards on my phone and went through them every time I was standing in line somewhere.

L4042.text: Are you still up for bowling tonight? The lanes are reserved for seven.
I've been a little under the weather since this morning. Could you ask Sergeant Ortiz to take my spot?

L4043.text: The computer in the classroom says it needs to restart for an update. Should I do that now?
Not with class starting in five minutes. That thing takes forever. Wait until lunch.

L4044.text: We're having a few people over on Saturday to see our new apartment. Can you make it?
I wouldn't miss it. What should I bring?
Just yourself. My wife has been cooking for two days.

L4045.text: These sunrise photos are amazing. Do you use some kind of special camera?
Just my phone. The trick is getting up at four thirty and waiting for the right light.

L4046.text: I understand almost everything the instructor says, but when I have to speak, my mind goes blank.
Try chatting with the American students at the gym. Practice makes it a lot easier.

L4047.text: I figured out a way to get through all twelve chapters before the final.
I'm all ears. At the rate I'm going, I'll be lucky to finish eight.

L4048.text: I typed my password wrong three times, and now the system won't let me in.
Same thing happened to me. The help desk can reset it, but only if you call before sixteen hundred.

L4049.text: It's almost midnight, and I have PT at zero six hundred. I think I'm going to call it a night.
Already? The band hasn't even played its last set. Well, drive safely.

L4050.text: Did you finish the novel for book club? I couldn't put it down.
I'm only halfway through, so don't tell me how it ends.

L4051.text: My instructor keeps telling me I pronounce "ship" and "sheep" exactly the same way.
Record yourself reading the word list, then compare it with the audio. That helped me with my "th" sound.

L4052.text: I dropped my phone in the parking lot, and now the screen looks like a spider web.
Does it still work? If it does, the PX can replace the glass for about sixty dollars.

L4053.text: A few of us are going to the jazz festival downtown on Sunday. Want to join us?
Jazz isn't really my cup of tea, but thanks for asking. Have a good time.

L4054.text: We need a fourth player for game night on Friday. Are you in?
Count me in, as long as we don't play the one that took five hours last time.

L4055.text: Our study group meets in the library at nineteen hundred. You should come.
I tried that once. We talked about everything except the lesson. I get more done alone.

L4056.text: How do you keep in touch with your family back home? International calls must cost a fortune.
We video chat every weekend. It doesn't cost a thing as long as you have Wi-Fi.

L4057.text: Why does the printer keep saying it's out of paper when the tray is completely full?
Beats me. Ask the guy from IT; he's in the office next door until fifteen hundred.

L4058.text: How'd you do on the grammar test? You looked worried when you came out.
I was sure I'd failed, but I ended up with an eighty-eight. I guess I worry too much.

L4059.text: Remember, the party for Captain Lee is a surprise. Don't say a word to him.
My lips are sealed. What time should we all be at the dayroom?

L4060.text: Your bread smells great. When did you start baking?
Last winter, when I was snowed in for a week with nothing to do. Now I can't stop.

L4061.text: My laptop crashed last night, and my whole presentation was on it.
Didn't you save a copy online? If not, the computer lab might be able to recover the files.

L4062.text: I'm stuck in traffic outside the gate. Go ahead and start the movie without me.
We'll wait. The previews take twenty minutes anyway, so you'll probably make it.

L4063.text: Is the essay for Mr. Grant still due on Thursday?
He pushed it back to next Tuesday, since half the class had range duty this week.

L4064.text: Are you going to sign up for the scuba course? The deadline is tomorrow.
I'm still on the fence. It's two hundred dollars, and I'm not a strong swimmer.

L4065.text: The GPS told me to turn left into a field, so I stopped and asked at a gas station.
Those maps can be out of date out here. That's why I keep a paper one in the glove box.

L4066.text: They put me in the intermediate class, but I think the material is too easy for me.
Talk to the course director. If you score high on the first two quizzes, they might move you up.

L4067.text: Did you send back the reply card for Tom's wedding? It's due Friday.
Oops. It's still on my desk under a pile of mail. I'll drop it in the mailbox on my way to work.

L4068.text: I tried to get tickets for the country music concert, but they sold out in ten minutes.
Don't give up yet. People often resell theirs online the week before the show.

L4069.text: How was the land navigation written test? Everyone says it's a nightmare.
Honestly, it was a piece of cake, as long as you've done the practice questions.

L4070.text: My phone bill was twice the usual amount this month, and I don't know why.
Did you stream videos while you were on leave? Without Wi-Fi, that eats up your data fast.

L4071.text: Is it okay if I bring my cousin to your barbecue? She's visiting this weekend.
Of course. The more the merrier. Just let me know if she's a vegetarian.

L4072.text: Are you still taking that online history course at night?
I dropped it. After twelve hours on duty, I couldn't keep my eyes open during the lectures.

L4073.text: Your tomatoes are huge this year. What's your secret?
No secret. I just moved the garden to the other side of the house, where it gets sun all afternoon.

L4074.text: I studied the wrong chapter for today's quiz. I thought we were still on chapter six.
No wonder you looked confused. We finished six last week.

L4075.text: Since I got this watch that counts my steps, I've been taking the stairs instead of the elevator.
Same here. Funny how a number on your wrist can change your habits.

L4076.text: It's been ages since we talked. Let's catch up over coffee sometime this week.
I'd like that. I'm free any morning except Wednesday, when I have a dental appointment.

L4077.text: Do you know if the education center library stays open late during exam week?
Normally it closes at eighteen hundred, but this week they're keeping it open until midnight.

L4078.text: Did you get my text about tonight? You never answered.
My phone's been on silent since the briefing. Let me check... Oh, I'd love to come.

L4079.text: We're grilling steaks at my place tonight. Want to come over around six?
Can I take a rain check? I promised to help my brother move this evening.

L4080.text: I want to fly my new drone over the parade field this weekend.
Better check with the base safety office first. They don't allow drones near the airfield without permission.

L4081.text: I watch American movies with English subtitles to improve my listening. Is that cheating?
Not at all. Just try turning them off the second time you watch.

L4082.text: My phone won't take any more pictures. It says the memory is full.
Move your old photos to your computer and delete the apps you never use. That should free up plenty of space.

L4083.text: Are you going to Sergeant Diaz's farewell lunch? He leaves for Germany next week.
I'll be on a field exercise, unfortunately. Could you sign the card for me?

L4084.text: Want to shoot some pool after dinner?
I'd love to, but I really need to hit the books. My final is the day after tomorrow.

L4085.text: I signed up for an evening painting class at the community center. It starts next month.
Good for you. I've seen your sketches, and you've got real talent.

L4086.text: Do you remember a Lieutenant Parker from the language school? She says she knows you.
The name rings a bell, but I can't picture her face. Was she in the Spanish course?

L4087.text: The tracking says my package was delivered, but there's nothing at my door.
Check the mailroom. On this base, they hold anything that doesn't fit in the mailbox.

L4088.text: I missed three days of class with the flu. I'm afraid I've fallen way behind.
Don't panic. I'll lend you my notes, and we can go over the hard parts on Saturday.

L4089.text: I'm making lasagna for the potluck. Is that okay with everyone?
Sounds great, but Kim doesn't eat meat. Maybe make a small pan without it.

L4090.text: I started a new video game at nine and didn't look at the clock until three in the morning.

L4091.text: I'm thinking of getting the newest tablet for my English classes.
Those cost an arm and a leg. Last year's model does the same things for half the price.

L4092.text: I'm going to stay up all night and review everything before the final.
Bad idea. You'll remember more if you get a good night's sleep and look over your notes at breakfast.

L4093.text: My son spends four hours a day on his tablet, and I don't know what to do.
We set a rule at our house: no screens until homework and chores are done. It works.

L4094.text: A bunch of us are driving to the beach on Saturday. There's room in the car if you want to come.
I'll come if we're back by six. I'm on duty that night.

L4095.text: I've practiced Spanish on my phone app for two hundred days in a row.
Impressive! I usually give up on those things after a week.

L4096.text: The test starts at zero eight hundred, and I just got off the bus at seven fifty-five.
You're cutting it close. Run! The room's on the third floor.

L4097.text: My essay came back covered in red ink. I thought it was pretty good.
Don't take it personally. Mr. Hale marks up everything, even the best papers in the class.

L4098.text: Is the Wi-Fi in the barracks working for you? Mine keeps cutting out.
It's terrible after twenty-one hundred, when everyone gets back and starts streaming.

L4099.text: Thanks for having us over. Everything smells wonderful.
I'm glad you could make it. Plates are on the counter, so help yourselves.

L4100.text: I'd like to join the chess club, but I barely know how the pieces move.
Don't worry. Tuesday nights are for beginners, and the members are happy to teach you the ropes.

L4101.text: Why didn't anyone tell me our class moved to Room two-ten?
It was in the group email yesterday. You must not be on the list. That's why you're out of the loop.

L4102.text: Math was never my strong point, and now I need it for the electronics course.
The education center offers free tutoring on weekday evenings. Lots of people in my unit go.

L4103.text: Can I borrow your charger? My phone's at three percent, and I'm expecting a call from my mom.
Sure, but it won't fit your phone. Ask Sam. He has the same model as you.

L4104.text: My daughter's birthday party is on Saturday afternoon. Would your kids like to come?
They'd be thrilled. What does she like? I don't want to bring something she already has.

L4105.text: The hiking club is doing the mountain trail on Sunday. It's about twelve miles round trip.
Twelve miles? Count me out. My knees haven't been the same since the last road march.

L4106.text: The bookstore wants ninety dollars for the new edition of our grammar book.
The instructor said the old edition is fine. You can find used copies for around fifteen.

L4107.text: So are you and your family going to Hawaii for the holidays?
It's still up in the air. It depends on whether my leave gets approved.

L4108.text: Can you hear me? I've been talking for two minutes, and nobody's responding.
We can see you, but there's no sound. Check the little microphone icon at the bottom of your screen.

L4109.text: Have you met the couple who moved in next door? They seem friendly.
