Only to wave hello. Maybe we should invite them over for coffee this weekend.

L4110.text: Did you really build that bookshelf yourself? It looks like it came from a store.
I took the woodworking class at the hobby shop on base. They let you use all the tools for free.

L4111.text: Before my presentation, my American roommate told me to break a leg. Was that some kind of threat?
Ha! No, it's just a way of wishing someone good luck before they perform.

L4112.text: I read every sentence twice, so it takes me forever to finish an article.
Try reading the whole thing once quickly just to get the main idea. Then go back for the details.

L4113.text: I meant to text my boss "See you at the meeting," but autocorrect changed it to something silly.
That's why I always reread my messages before hitting send. It's saved me more than once.

L4114.text: Thanks for covering my shift on Friday so I could go to my sister's graduation. I owe you one.
Don't mention it. You can return the favor when my parents visit next month.

L4115.text: I've always wanted to learn the piano, but I'm forty-two. Isn't it too late?
My uncle started at sixty, and now he gives little concerts at the library.

L4116.text: I tried to register for the evening English class, but it's already full.
Put your name on the waiting list. Someone always drops out during the first week.

L4117.text: Every time I log in to my email, it sends a code to my phone. It's so annoying.
It's a pain, but it stops strangers from getting into your account even if they learn your password.

L4118.text: Why is Rivera smiling so much today?
He found out he passed the language exam with the highest score in his group. He's on cloud nine.

L4119.text: Who's organizing the bowling trip? The group chat has two hundred messages and still no plan.
Nobody, apparently. I'll make a quick poll for the date, and we'll go from there.

L4120.text: Are we still going camping this weekend? The forecast says heavy rain on Saturday.
Let's push it back a week. Sleeping in a wet tent isn't my idea of fun.

L4121.text: How did you learn the whole phonetic alphabet so fast? Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, and all the rest?
I made up a silly story using all twenty-six words. Once I had the story, the list stuck.

L4122.text: My laptop takes ten minutes just to start up. I think it's on its last legs.
How old is it? If it's more than six or seven years, it's probably time to replace it.

L4123.text: We're going to try that new karaoke place Friday night. You've got a great voice, so come with us!
Thanks, but I'll pass. Singing in front of strangers makes me nervous.

L4124.text: The new instructor talks so fast that I miss half of what he says.
Ask him to slow down. He told us on the first day that he doesn't mind.

L4125.text: My grandfather left me his coin collection. Some of the coins are over a hundred years old.
Have an expert look at them before you sell any. A few could be worth a lot.

L4126.text: I lost every photo from my deployment when my phone was stolen.
That's awful. I learned the hard way too. Now everything I shoot gets saved to the cloud automatically.

L4127.text: Wasn't the speaking test supposed to be this afternoon?
It was, but two of the examiners are sick, so they've moved half of us to tomorrow morning.

L4128.text: What should I wear to the unit ball? I've never been to one.
Your dress uniform. And be ready for a long night; they usually go past midnight.

L4129.text: I finally bought a smartphone, but I can't even figure out how to answer a call.
Bring it over after dinner. I'll walk you through the basics in fifteen minutes.

L4130.text: My neighbor's band practices in his garage every evening until ten. I can't even hear my own TV.
Have you talked to him? He might not realize how far the sound carries.

L4131.text: The base theater needs volunteers to run the lights for the spring show. Interested?
Maybe. Let me sleep on it and get back to you tomorrow.

L4132.text: Is our printer working again? I need forty copies of the slides for the ten o'clock brief.
It's still jammed until the technician comes after lunch. Try the S-3 shop down the hall, but ask Sergeant Kim first.
Got it. I'll go find her right now.

L4133.text: Can you open the shared drive? I keep getting an access denied error, and my report for the major is due at noon.
No. They reset everyone's passwords last night, and the permissions didn't carry over. Ask the help desk for a priority ticket.
Good idea. I'll call them right now.

L4134.text: Are we really moving to Building twelve next week? Nobody's told me anything.
The memo came out yesterday. Everything has to be boxed up by Thursday afternoon.
Thursday? I have a training meeting all day Wednesday, so I only get one morning.

L4135.text: We're down to our last toner cartridge. Did you send in the supply request?
Not yet. I filled it out, but the supply officer has to sign it, and he's on leave until the fifteenth.
Captain Ruiz can sign for him. Take it to her now.

L4136.text: Captain Hale is at the range all day. Should I forward his calls to your desk?
Please don't. I'm in the budget meeting from nine to three. Send them to Sergeant Diaz to take messages.

L4137.text: Has my leave form been approved yet? My bus leaves Saturday morning, and I can't buy the ticket without approval.
Not yet. The first sergeant has been out sick since Tuesday. I'll ask the sergeant major to approve it this afternoon.
Thanks. I'll buy the ticket as soon as it's signed.

L4138.text: Sergeant Brooks, my evaluation is due at battalion on the thirtieth, but my rater is TDY in Texas until the fifth.
Then e-mail it to her. She can sign it digitally. Battalion won't take it late without a memo from the commander.
Good. I'll do that this afternoon.

L4139.text: Who's picking up the unit mail today? Specialist Ward usually does, but he's on sick call.
I can go, but I'm not on the access list for the mail room.
The clerk won't give you anything without that. I'll add your name and call ahead.

L4140.text: Ms. Grant, payroll says your timecard for last week never came in.
I submitted it Friday, so the system must not have saved it. I'll redo it now.
Good. If it isn't in by fourteen hundred today, your paycheck will be two weeks late.

L4141.text: Did you hear? The range is closed Thursday because of lightning. Qualification isn't canceled, just moved to Saturday, zero six hundred.
Saturday? I was supposed to drive my family to the airport that morning.
Oh no. Can you work something out?

L4142.text: The land navigation course is fogged in, and the safety officer won't let us start before ten. That leaves only five hours of daylight.
That's not enough time for the full course. Let's skip the last three points and do those next week.
Good call. I'll tell the other teams.

L4143.text: The CPR class on the twelfth is full, and my certification runs out on the twenty-eighth. The next class isn't until the third.
Talk to the instructor anyway. People often drop out at the last minute, and she keeps a waiting list.
Really? I'll call her this afternoon.

L4144.text: We got only half the ammunition we requested for next week's qualification. The rest won't come until next quarter.
That isn't enough for sixty soldiers. Let's put those whose qualification expires first at the top of the list.
Okay. I'll sort the list by expiration date.

L4145.text: My Spanish class meets Thursday evenings, but I'm on the duty roster every Thursday this month, and nobody will trade.
Ask the first sergeant. If the class is on your training plan, he's supposed to work around it.
Good point. I'll talk to him tomorrow.

L4146.text: Is the fitness test still on the twentieth? I've been training for that date.
No, they moved it to the thirteenth because the battalion has a field exercise the following week.
A week earlier? I wanted more time to cut my run time.

L4147.text: How many drivers do we have for the convoy training next month?
Twelve, but four have licenses expiring before then. To renew, they need the driver's course at the motor pool. It's two weeks, starting Monday.
Then sign all four up today. We can't run the convoy with only eight.

L4148.text: The pool on base is closed until November. Where will we do the swim qualification?
The training officer arranged it at the community college in town. Be at headquarters for the bus at zero seven hundred, and bring a towel.
Understood. I'll tell the rest of the squad.

L4149.text: The first aid instructor called in sick. Should we cancel this afternoon's class?
I'd rather not. Half the platoon still needs it before we deploy.
Sergeant Lopez used to be a medic. Maybe she could fill in.

L4150.text: They bumped our driving simulator time on Wednesday for a general's visit. The other slots are Friday after sixteen hundred or next Tuesday morning.
Half the section leaves early on Fridays. Take the Tuesday slot.

L4151.text: Battalion wants our November training schedule by Friday.
Already? We haven't even finished October. Why so early?
It's the new rule. Everything is locked in six weeks ahead so they can request ranges and buses.

L4152.text: If we add a night convoy, we'll need five hundred more gallons of fuel. And the drivers need rest before the next morning.
Then let's move the morning start time to ten. I'll put in the fuel request today.

L4153.text: This report says you still haven't finished three of your online training courses.
I know, ma'am. The website kept crashing whenever I reached the final test.
That's no excuse after two months. The computers in the learning center work fine.

L4154.text: Before Tuesday's gas chamber training, everyone's masks must be checked at the CBRN office in Building four, from eight to eleven.
Then I'll send my section over at eight sharp. The line gets long by nine.
Good. It's first come, first served.

L4155.text: Has the packing list for the field exercise come out yet?
It's on the board by the orderly room. It's the same as last time, except everyone needs cold-weather gear.
Makes sense. It's supposed to freeze at night.

L4156.text: My radio receives fine, but nobody can hear me when I transmit. I've already tried two fresh batteries.
Then it's probably the antenna. Check that it's screwed in tight.
Okay, I'll check. If that fails, I'll turn it in to commo.

L4157.text: Sergeant, truck fourteen won't start. I've tried three times.
It's the cold. That battery's weak. File a work order, but for now jump it from truck twelve. We roll out in twenty minutes.
Yes, Sergeant. I'll grab the cables.

L4158.text: The projector in the conference room just went dark. The bulb burned out, and supply doesn't have a spare yet.
The colonel's briefing starts in fifteen minutes. Bring the big TV from the training room and hook up your laptop.
Okay, I'll set it up now.

L4159.text: There's a big puddle of oil under the generator behind the command post. It wasn't there yesterday.
Shut it down and switch to the backup. Then put sand on the spill and call maintenance.
Right away. Someone could slip on it.

L4160.text: This GPS says we're in the middle of the lake. The sticker says it was last updated in March of last year.
That's the problem. They should be updated every six months. Use the map and compass for now.
Okay. We'll update it when we're back.

L4161.text: I counted nine pairs of night vision goggles, but the hand receipt says ten.
Did you check the pair that went to the shop for repair?
Oh, I forgot. I'll look for the turn-in slip in the binder.

L4162.text: My laptop keeps shutting off, and it gets really hot underneath.
Is it sitting on that pile of papers? That blocks the air vents. Put it on something hard and flat.
I'll try that. If it still happens, I'll call the IT shop.

L4163.text: The forklift in the warehouse won't lift anything heavier than a few boxes.
The hydraulic fluid is low again, the third time this month. Topping it off won't help, since there must be a leak.
Then let's tag it out of service and call the contractor.

L4164.text: The air conditioner in the server room quit an hour ago. It's almost ninety degrees in there and climbing.
Bring in the portable fans from storage and leave the door open. I'll tell facilities it's an emergency.
Please hurry. If it gets much hotter, the servers will start shutting down.

L4165.text: Before we leave, did anyone check the tires? The rear left one looks soft, maybe from a nail.
I did yesterday, but let's not risk a forty-mile trip. I'll put on the spare.
Good idea. I'll get the jack.

L4166.text: The copier is out of order again. What happened this time?
A paper jam, and the repairman can't come until Thursday.
Thursday? I have to copy the training packets for tomorrow!

L4167.text: The body armor they issued me is a size too big. Supply says they're out of smalls until next month.
Ask if another company has any to spare. I don't want you going to the field in gear that doesn't fit.
Good idea. I'll ask around today.

L4168.text: We tested the tent heaters this morning, and two of the six won't light. The parts take ten days, but we need them working by Friday.
Borrow two from Bravo Company. They don't go to the field until next month.
Good idea. I'll go ask them.

L4169.text: Is the staff meeting still Tuesday at nine?
No, the major has a dental appointment Tuesday, so it's Wednesday, same time.
But I'll be at the range then. I'll send Sergeant Kelly to take notes.

L4170.text: Rivera, could you swap staff duty with me? I'm on Saturday, but my brother's getting married that day.
Sorry, I already have Sunday, and I can't work two days in a row. Ask Tanaka. He wants weekdays off next month.

L4171.text: Tomorrow's formation is at zero six fifteen, not six thirty. The brigade commander wants to speak before the run.
Thanks. Half my squad doesn't check their phones in the morning, so I'll tell them tonight.
Please do. We start on time.

L4172.text: Is the finance office open Monday or Tuesday? I need to fix a problem with my housing allowance.
Monday's a federal holiday. Tuesday it's open, but everyone who missed Monday will be there, so go before it opens.

L4173.text: We're short six guards, so starting next week everyone at the gates works twelve-hour shifts instead of eight.
Twelve hours in this heat is rough. At least make sure they get water breaks.
Every hour, I promise. It's the only way to cover all three gates.

L4174.text: Ma'am, the colonel's flight from Germany is delayed. He won't land until eighteen hundred.
Then move the sixteen hundred brief to eight tomorrow morning. But tell the staff the slides are still due today.
Understood. I'll have them on your desk tonight.

L4175.text: Sergeant, my dental appointment Thursday morning conflicts with the range roster. I waited almost two months for it.
Then keep it. I'll move you to the afternoon relay, but be back here by thirteen hundred.
Thank you, Sergeant. I will be.

L4176.text: The bus to the training area leaves at zero five thirty instead of zero six hundred, because of road construction.
Then I can't eat breakfast at the dining facility. It doesn't open until five thirty.
True. Better grab something from the vending machines tonight.

L4177.text: The change of command rehearsal is Thursday at fourteen hundred on the parade field. Duty uniform for that, dress uniform for Saturday's ceremony.
Then my dress uniform has to go to the cleaners tomorrow.
Better drop it off early, then.

L4178.text: I'm due at Fort Carson on the fifth, but I still don't have my orders.
They're written. They just need the colonel's signature, and I'll walk them to his office this afternoon.
Good. But I can't buy a plane ticket until I have them, and prices go up every day.

L4179.text: Finance sent back my travel voucher because the hotel receipt is missing. I think I threw it away.
Call the hotel. They can usually e-mail a copy. Without it, finance won't pay you for the room.
I'll call them right after lunch.

L4180.text: My orders for the Denver conference don't authorize a rental car. How do I get from the airport to the hotel?
Take the shuttle or a taxi and keep the receipt. You'll be paid back, just not for a car all week.

L4181.text: My government travel card was declined at the hotel last night, and I've spent only about eight hundred of my five-thousand-dollar limit.
Then it was probably deactivated because you hadn't used it in months. Call the number on the back.

L4182.text: The airline canceled my Tuesday flight, so I won't get to Germany until Thursday.
Your orders say Wednesday, so you need an amendment from the S-1 office. Bring the airline's notice to show it wasn't your fault.

L4183.text: You've been picked for the exercise in Japan in March. Is your official passport current?
I think so, but it expires next summer.
That could be a problem. Many countries want at least six months left on it when you arrive.

L4184.text: Bad news. The inspection team needs us here until the eighteenth, so our temporary duty is extended a week.
Another week? I promised my kids I'd be home for my daughter's birthday on Saturday.
I'm sorry. Maybe you can celebrate next weekend instead.

L4185.text: The lodging on post is completely full for my school next month. What should I do?
Call them back and ask for a non-availability number. Without that proof, finance won't pay for a hotel off post.
I see. I'll call them right now.

L4186.text: Finance returned my travel voucher again. It still needs Major Chen's signature, but she's on leave.
Then it's not your fault. Her deputy can sign while she's gone.
Good. I'll take it to him now.

L4187.text: When do you have to report to your new unit?
By the twentieth, but I'll go around the fifteenth to find an apartment. They'll pay for a hotel for up to ten days.

L4188.text: How did your room do on the inspection this morning?
The first sergeant found dust on top of my wall locker. If it isn't clean by seventeen hundred, I lose my weekend pass.
Wow. Who even looks up there?

L4189.text: I can't dispatch this truck. The fire extinguisher tag expired last month.
Can't we just swap in one from another vehicle?
Only if it's current. Check the trucks in row B; they were just inspected.

L4190.text: During the arms room inventory, one rifle's serial number didn't match the list. Two digits were reversed, so it's probably a typo.
Don't fix it yourself. Write it up and let the commander decide. That's the regulation.
Understood. I'll write it up now.

L4191.text: The Inspector General's team arrives on the ninth. Are our training records up to date?
Mostly, but seven soldiers missed their annual safety briefing. I can hold a make-up session on Monday.
Please do. We want everyone current by then.

L4192.text: The inspector wrote us up because three extension cords in the break room were plugged into each other to reach the microwave.
That is a fire hazard. Let's have an electrician put an outlet on that wall.
Good idea. Then we can get rid of the cords.

L4193.text: Specialist Moore, your name tape is coming loose. We have an in-ranks inspection at thirteen hundred.
Sorry, Sergeant. I haven't had time to sew it. Where can I get it fixed fast?
The alterations shop by the PX takes half an hour. Go at lunch.

L4194.text: The health inspector visits the dining facility tomorrow. How are the walk-in coolers?
One is reading forty-five degrees. It's supposed to be under forty-one.
Move everything into the other cooler tonight and put in an emergency work order.

L4195.text: The brigade supply team checks hand receipts next week. Is everything in your section signed for?
Everything except the new printers. They came in after the last update.
Get the supply sergeant to add them before Monday. Anything not on a hand receipt counts as a finding.

L4196.text: The fire marshal inspects the building at ten. Is anything going to be a problem?
Just the boxes of manuals at the back exit. There's room in the second-floor storage closet, so some privates will carry them up.
Good. Exits can never be blocked.

L4197.text: Sergeant, these paint cans in the hazardous materials locker have no labels. The environmental office will pick them up if we fill out a form.
They came from the old building, and nobody knows what's inside. Request a pickup. I'd rather not fail the inspection.
Yes, Sergeant. I'll fill out the form.

L4198.text: Sergeant Wells is on emergency leave, so who's taking notes at the training meeting this afternoon?
I can, until I leave for a medical appointment at fifteen thirty. Corporal Hughes can finish. I'll ask him now.
Good. The meeting usually goes until four, so that works.

L4199.text: I reserved the conference room for ten, but some contractors are in there. They say they booked it too.
The scheduling system must have made a mistake. The library's small meeting room is usually free in the morning. Want me to check?
Please. The deputy commander is in my meeting.

L4200.text: We've lost the video connection with headquarters again, the third time in twenty minutes. The audio still works, though.
Then turn off the video and keep going by voice. We have to finish before Washington closes for the day.

L4201.text: That meeting ran three hours, and I missed lunch. The dining facility closed at thirteen hundred.
The snack bar at the bowling center serves food until five. Want to walk over before the next meeting?

L4202.text: The logistics meeting is in an hour, and I still haven't seen an agenda.
I sent it last night. Did you check your junk mail folder?
There it is! Your e-mails have ended up in there before.

L4203.text: The barracks contractor wants to meet every Monday at seven thirty. I asked for later, but their crews start at eight.
Seven thirty is during PT, but fine. I'll work out on my own on Monday evenings.
Good. I'll let the manager know.

L4204.text: My slides are due at fifteen hundred, and I'm still waiting on the motor pool's maintenance numbers. Their clerk promised them this morning.
Don't wait. Call the motor sergeant directly. He knows those numbers off the top of his head.
Good idea. I'll call him now.

L4205.text: They want one of us at the exercise planning conference in Georgia in May, but my son graduates from high school that week.
Then I'll go. Send me the registration link, and I'll start my travel request.

L4206.text: The boots I ordered through supply finally came, but they're a size nine. I asked for a ten.
Was that their mistake or yours?
Theirs. I have a copy of my request right here.

L4207.text: I need cots out of the supply room for visitors arriving at noon, but Sergeant Burke is on leave. Who has the keys?
The executive officer has the spare set, but he's in meetings all morning. I'll text him.
Thanks. They'll need somewhere to sleep.

L4208.text: The pump parts for the generator are back-ordered for six weeks. Could we use the part from the one waiting to be turned in?
Do it, but document it. We can't go to the field in three weeks without power.
Understood. I'll write it up today.

L4209.text: Can we just throw out the twenty old computers in the storage room? Nobody uses them.
No, they're government property. List the serial numbers, and the property office will schedule a pickup in a couple of weeks.
All right. I'll start writing them down today.

L4210.text: When is the cold-weather gear being issued? My guys are freezing on morning runs.
Next Tuesday, nine to three, by platoon. First platoon is at nine, and yours is third, so around one o'clock.

L4211.text: We're almost out of printer paper, and I can't order any more.
Why not? Is it a delivery problem?
No, this year's budget is used up. New money doesn't come until October first.

L4212.text: Forty people will be at the range for eight hours tomorrow. Is thirty cases of water enough?
Make it forty. It's supposed to hit ninety-five, and I'd rather bring some back than run out.
Forty it is. I'll pick them up.

L4213.text: We use so many radio batteries that I'm ordering them every week.
Have you thought about rechargeable ones? They cost more at first, but they last for years.
We'd need chargers and a place to keep them.

L4214.text: I'm leaving the section Friday, so I have to sign over the forty items on my hand receipt to you.
Let's count them together Wednesday morning. If anything's missing, we'll still have two days to find it.

L4215.text: How many meals did you order for the field exercise?
Three a day for four days, for fifty soldiers. That's six hundred meals.
But they added a fifth day at the end. You'd better call the food service office.

L4216.text: The barracks are out of mops and cleaner again. We use more with all the new soldiers, so let's double the monthly order.
That would fill up our storage space. Let's order every two weeks instead.
All right, that works for me.

L4217.text: This truck is two thousand miles past its scheduled service.
I know. We kept meaning to bring it in, but it was always out on a mission.
It's not going anywhere else until it gets an oil change and a full check.

L4218.text: The roof over bay three is leaking again, and public works still hasn't acted on my work order from two weeks ago.
Move the vehicles to bay one and put a bucket under the leak. I'll call them myself. A captain's voice might get things moving.
Yes, ma'am. I'll move them now.

L4219.text: The lock on the arms room's outer door is sticking. I had to jiggle the key for five minutes this morning.
Call the locksmith on post and mark it urgent. Until it's fixed, we'll post a guard outside the door.
Good. If it breaks, nobody gets in or out.

L4220.text: Our helicopter flight to the training area is canceled. They found a crack in a blade during the inspection.
Then we'll have to drive. It's four hours by road, so we should leave by noon to get there before dark.
Okay. I'll tell the others to be ready.

L4221.text: The elevator's out again, and the new filing cabinets are coming at two. They're going to the fourth floor.
Not by hand. They weigh almost two hundred pounds each. Maintenance says the elevator works again Thursday night, so ask them to come Friday.
Good idea. I'll call them now.

L4222.text: The barracks heat hasn't worked since Sunday, and the soldiers are sleeping in their jackets. The technician never showed up.
That's not acceptable. I'll see the housing manager in person this afternoon.
Good. I'll get space heaters from supply.

L4223.text: Monday morning is vehicle maintenance, and every driver must check his own vehicle.
Even the new drivers? Most of them have never done it.
Especially them. Pair each one with an experienced driver, and go through the checklist together.

L4224.text: The mechanic says the van's brake pads are almost gone. He can replace them today if we get it there before noon.
Then take it over now. We need it to pick up the visitors tomorrow, and I'll find someone to cover your desk.

L4225.text: The paint shop's fumes are coming into our office through the air vents.
I smell it too, and some people have headaches. Should we use the empty classroom across the street?
Yes, let's move there until they finish painting.

L4226.text: I'm doing the tool room inventory, and the large torque wrench isn't here.
Check the sign-out sheet. Someone may have taken it to the flight line.
Garcia took it yesterday afternoon and never signed it back in. I'll call him.

L4227.text: There was no hot water in the women's barracks this morning, and there's water on the boiler room floor.
That sounds like a broken tank. I'll call public works, and I'll ask if the gym showers can stay open late.
Good idea. They had cold showers today.

L4228.text: Two sinks in the second-floor latrine are clogged again. The plumber said last time that the pipes are old and need replacing.
Then request new pipes this time, not just another repair. Otherwise we'll be calling him every month.
Good point. I'll fill out the work order now.

L4229.text: A rock cracked the staff car's windshield on the highway. The repair shop can't replace it until Friday.
And we can't drive it on base like that. I'll reserve a motor pool vehicle for the colonel's trip Wednesday.
Good. The military police would stop us for sure.

L4230.text: A contractor is coming at nine to fix the network. Does he need an escort?
If he has no base ID, yes. He'll get a visitor badge, but someone must stay with him the whole time.
I have a meeting at ten, so I'll ask Specialist Park to cover.

L4231.text: Starting next month, the office opens at seven instead of seven thirty, and we leave at sixteen hundred.
That works for me. I'll finally be able to pick up my kids from school.
Good. The commander wants us to match the headquarters overseas.

L4232.text: I finally booked the Pine Lake cabin for the Fourth of July weekend. It was the last one.
Great! Did you check the cancellation policy? Let's not tell the kids until I'm sure about my work schedule.
I did. We can cancel two weeks before and get everything back, minus a fee.

L4233.text: The kitchen faucet is dripping again, and now there's water under the sink. The landlord says his plumber can't come until Thursday.
Thursday? Then we'd better close the valve under the sink tonight and get our water from the bathroom until then.
Okay. I'll put some towels down for tonight.

L4234.text: How's the ankle you twisted playing basketball? Will you be able to make the hiking trip next month?
It's still swollen, but the x-ray showed no break. The doctor says ten days off it, so I should be fine by then.

L4235.text: I tried to book Marco's for our anniversary. Saturday's full, and Friday has only a nine fifteen table. That's late.
I'd rather eat late at a place we love than early somewhere we don't. Let's take it.

L4236.text: The check engine light came on this morning, but the car seems to drive fine.
Don't ignore it. Mine was just a loose gas cap, but the auto parts store on Elm Street will read the code for free.
Okay, I'll stop by on my way home.

L4237.text: You look worried. Is it your online history class?
Yes. My final paper is due Sunday, but we're in the field all week. I'll email my instructor tonight, with a copy of my orders.
Smart. Mine gave me an extra week when I deployed.

L4238.text: Look at my bank statement. The gas station charged me twice for the same fill-up on Tuesday, and the manager won't help.
Then call the number on the back of your card. The bank will dispute the extra charge.
Good idea. I'll call them now.

L4239.text: Are we still having the family picnic at the park on Saturday?
Thunderstorms are forecast, so the committee is moving it to the gym on base. Same day, same time.
That's fine. I'll tell the other families.

L4240.text: My parents are coming for two weeks, but they can't climb stairs well anymore, so the upstairs guest room won't work.
Then our son can move up there, and they can have his room on the first floor.
He'll complain, but it's only two weeks. I'll talk to him tonight.

L4241.text: Our softball team needs one more player, or we'll forfeit our games. We practice Tuesday evenings. Interested?
I haven't played since high school. I'd probably just slow you down.
Nobody on the team is very good. We mostly play for fun.
In that case, count me in.

L4242.text: Excuse me, I drive a delivery truck, and my allergies have been terrible this week. What do you recommend?
This one works well, but it can make you sleepy, so take this other one instead. It won't make you drowsy.

L4243.text: Are you taking Highway Ten to the airport tomorrow? They're repaving it, and my husband needed an hour to go eight miles.
Then I'll leave at six instead of seven. My flight isn't until nine forty, but I'd rather wait at the gate than in traffic.
Smart. Good luck with your trip.

L4244.text: Want to study together for the chemistry exam? I still don't get chapter seven.
Sure. Kevin, Ana and I have a room at the library Wednesday night until eleven. There's space for one more.
I've got a shift at the restaurant until nine, but I'll come over right after.

L4245.text: Our lease renewal came. The rent is going up seventy-five dollars a month, unless we sign for two years.
Two years? I might get orders next summer. What if we have to leave early?
The letter says military families can break the lease with thirty days' notice.
Then the longer one makes more sense.

L4246.text: With the hurricane coming, the county ordered everyone near the coast to evacuate. We're ten miles inland. Should we stay?
I'd rather not take the chance. Let's go to my brother's place in Atlanta until the storm passes.
All right. I'll help you pack the car.

L4247.text: I'd like to return this jacket. I've never worn it, and the tags are still on.
It's been forty-two days, and refunds are only allowed within thirty. But I can give you a gift card for the full amount.
Well, I guess that's better than nothing.

L4248.text: How did your checkup go? Did the doctor give you any pills?
Not yet. My cholesterol is normal, but my blood pressure is high, so first she wants me to cut back on salt and walk daily.
That sounds like a good start.

L4249.text: My flight from Denver landed late, and I missed my connection to Boston. Is there anything tonight?
The eight o'clock is full, so the next seat is at seven ten tomorrow morning. Since the delay was our fault, here's a hotel voucher.
Tomorrow morning? Well, at least I'll get some sleep.

L4250.text: I'm training for the city marathon, and my shins have hurt all week. I went from thirty to forty miles a week this month.
That sounds like shin splints. You increased too fast. Cut back for a couple of weeks and get new shoes.

L4251.text: Where should we take Priya for her birthday? She doesn't eat meat.
How about the steakhouse on Main? They have a big salad bar.
That's not much of a dinner for her. The Indian place near the mall has lots of vegetarian dishes.

L4252.text: Do you hear that banging? It's the furnace again. It started when the weather turned cold.
When did you last change the filter? A dirty one makes it work too hard.
The filter? I didn't even know it had one.

L4253.text: The babysitter has the flu and can't watch the kids tomorrow. Could your mother take them?
She's visiting my aunt until Sunday. I'll move my ten o'clock dentist appointment and stay home with them.
Are you sure? You've already rescheduled it twice, and I can't miss my training.

L4254.text: I got a speeding ticket this morning. The fine is a hundred and fifty dollars, but I'm more worried that my insurance will go up.
Ask the court about a driving safety course. If you take it, the ticket never goes on your record.
Good idea. I'll call them today.

L4255.text: Have you picked a major yet? Registration closes Friday.
I'm stuck between nursing and business. Nursing has better job security.
Maybe, but you faint at the sight of blood. Remember when Jake cut his hand?

L4256.text: They're saying eight to twelve inches of snow tonight, and schools are already closed tomorrow.
Then I'll get milk and bread before it starts. Can you find the snow shovel? It's probably behind the bikes in the garage.
Sure. But the store's going to be packed.

L4257.text: I'm thinking about buying this laptop for my classes. It's nine hundred dollars.
Can you wait two weeks? The store has a big sale before school starts. My cousin saved almost two hundred last year.
My classes don't start for a month, so I can wait.

L4258.text: I'm having my wisdom teeth out Friday morning. They'll put me to sleep, so I can't drive myself home.
I'm off on Fridays. I'll take you there and wait.

L4259.text: How's your guitar going? You've been learning from free videos for three months, right?
Yes, but I keep making the same mistakes, and nobody tells me what I'm doing wrong.
My neighbor teaches guitar for twenty-five dollars a half-hour. I'll text you her number.

L4260.text: Want to try that new Mexican place on Fourth Street for lunch? We only have forty-five minutes.
I've heard it's slow. Lisa waited forty minutes for her food there. Let's just grab something from the food truck outside.
Good idea. The meeting starts at one.

L4261.text: Are you going to exchange money before your trip to Japan?
I'm planning to change five hundred dollars at the airport.
Don't. Airport rates are terrible. Just take cash out of a machine when you land.

L4262.text: I heard a branch came through your roof in the storm. Has the insurance company been out yet?
Not until Monday, and the bedroom ceiling is leaking. Could I borrow your big plastic tarp this afternoon to keep the rain out?
Of course. I'll bring my ladder over after lunch.

L4263.text: I have a flat tire on the interstate, and I'd change it, but my spare is flat too.
Are you somewhere safe? Call the roadside assistance number on your insurance card. If they can't come within an hour, call me back.
I'm on the shoulder with my flashers on. I'll call them now.

L4264.text: Emma turns eight next month. Should we have her party at home again?
Twenty kids at home last year nearly drove me crazy. Let's try the bowling alley. They do the food, the cake, and the cleanup.
Okay, if the price is reasonable. But let's keep it to twelve kids this time.

L4265.text: Have you gotten your flu shot yet?
Not yet. I keep meaning to make an appointment, but I never get around to it.
You don't need one. The clinic takes walk-ins Tuesdays and Thursdays, one to four. I was out in fifteen minutes.

L4266.text: Excuse me, I ordered my steak medium rare, but this one is cooked all the way through.
I'm so sorry, sir. The kitchen will make you a new one in fifteen minutes, and your dessert tonight is on the house.
Fifteen minutes? My wife is almost finished eating.

L4267.text: Are you still fishing at the reservoir this weekend? Did you get a license? Wardens are checking everyone.
I had no idea I needed one! We're going out on my brother-in-law's boat Saturday. Where do I get it?
Online, in five minutes. It's twenty dollars, much cheaper than a two-hundred-dollar fine.

L4268.text: My professor returned my research paper with a disappointing grade. She liked my ideas, but my sources weren't cited properly.
Try the writing center in the library. It's free for students, but make an appointment soon, before finals.
Thanks, I'll book one online today.

L4269.text: We spent almost nine hundred dollars on groceries, mostly diapers. The warehouse store charges sixty dollars a year, but diapers are a third cheaper.
Then we'd earn back that sixty in a couple of months. Let's join this weekend.

L4270.text: Hi, I'm in room four twelve. The ice machine outside my door ran all night, and I have a big meeting tomorrow.
I'm sorry, sir. I can move you to a quiet room on the sixth floor, away from the elevators. New keys will be ready.
Perfect. I really need some sleep.

L4271.text: It's supposed to hit a hundred and three Saturday. If we still do the canyon hike, let's start at sunrise instead of ten.
That means getting up at four thirty, but you're right. I don't want to cancel after weeks of planning.
Good. And let's bring twice as much water as usual.

L4272.text: Jason keeps asking for a phone. What if he earns one? Three months of good grades and chores, and he gets a basic phone.
He's only eleven, but all right, if it's just for calls and texts.
Agreed. No games and no social media at first.

L4273.text: How's your back? Is the therapy helping? Are you back at the gym?
It helps a lot, but no weights yet. The therapist says another month of stretching, or I could end up back where I started.

L4274.text: Gas to the base costs me almost a hundred dollars a week. You live near Oak Hill, right? Want to carpool?
Sure, I'm two streets from the shopping center. But I drop my son at day care at seven.
That's fine. We'll alternate weeks and both save half.

L4275.text: I've used a phone app to learn Spanish for six months, and I read pretty well now.
Impressive! Can you actually hold a conversation?
Not really. When someone talks to me, I freeze. The app never makes me speak.

L4276.text: I picked up a takeout order under Garcia, but the fried rice wasn't in the bag. I live twenty minutes away.
I'm sorry. I'll refund the eight fifty to your card now, and mention this call next time for ten percent off.

L4277.text: What do you think of the living room? I finished painting it last night.
It looks nice, but I can still see the old dark green in a few spots.
I noticed that this morning in the daylight. One coat wasn't enough, so I'll buy another gallon.

L4278.text: I'm going to the post office tomorrow to apply for the kids' passports. Can you give me their birth certificates?
They're in the safe. Both parents must be there, or one signs a form. I'll take the afternoon off and go with you.
Good thing I asked. I'd have wasted the morning.

L4279.text: The oil change sticker on your windshield says March, and you've driven to Florida and back since then.
March? It's already September! I'll take it to the shop by the gate Saturday morning.

L4280.text: I joined the new climbing gym. Want to come Saturday? Beginners stay on the low walls unless they take a safety class.
I've never climbed, but I don't want to stay on the low walls. Sign me up for the class.
Great. It's an hour long and costs fifteen dollars.

L4281.text: The refrigerator is eleven hundred dollars, and the salesman wants us to add a five-year warranty for two hundred more.
It already has a one-year warranty, and I read these models hardly ever break down. I'd rather keep that money in savings.
All right. We'll take the refrigerator by itself, then.

L4282.text: Have you looked outside? The fog is so thick I can't see the end of the driveway.
The radio says the bridge is closed until it lifts, probably around ten.
Ten? I have a dental appointment across the river at nine thirty!

L4283.text: My brothers and I want to send Mom and Dad on a cruise for her seventieth in May.
Great idea, but what will it cost? Money's tight for us with the car payment.
About three thousand, split evenly among the three of us. My brother Tom offered to pay more, but I'd feel bad.

L4284.text: I had my eyes checked this morning. They've changed quite a bit since last year.
That explains the headaches you've been getting after work. When do you get new glasses?
In ten days. Until then, the doctor says to rest my eyes from the screen every hour.

L4285.text: How did you do on the statistics quiz?
Not well, a fifty-five. I haven't gone to her office hours because she has over two hundred students.
That's what they're for. Hardly anyone goes, so you'd practically have her to yourself.

L4286.text: Does the chocolate cake have any nuts in it? My daughter is allergic.
The cake itself doesn't, but it's made in the same kitchen as our pecan pie, so I can't promise there's no contact.
Then we'd better not risk it. Do you have anything else?

L4287.text: Should we just buy the theme park tickets at the gate? There are five of us.
No way. They're ninety-five dollars each there, but only seventy-nine online if you order a day ahead.
That's a big difference. Let's order them tonight.

L4288.text: Where should we park for the concert? Last time we drove around for half an hour. What about the Second Avenue garage?
It's twenty dollars, but I'd pay that to avoid the stress. The meters are free after six, but spots are hard to find.

L4289.text: Did you get tickets for Saturday's game against Navy? If not, come watch it at our place.
No. They sold out in ten minutes, and resale sites want three hundred a seat. I'd love to come.
Great. Mike's putting it on the big screen, and he'll be grilling burgers.

L4290.text: We were offered a house on base, three bedrooms with a yard. I could walk to work instead of sitting in traffic for an hour.
Sounds perfect. Is there any downside?
My wife says the kitchen is small, and the house is older than our apartment.

L4291.text: Tommy says his ear doesn't hurt anymore. Can I stop the medicine? It's been four days, and the bottle says ten.
No, keep going until the bottle is empty. If you stop early, the infection can come back.

L4292.text: Because of the ice, everyone who isn't essential reports two hours late today, but the roads still haven't been salted.
Then don't drive. The shuttle bus at the corner runs every twenty minutes, and those drivers are used to this weather.
Good idea. I'll walk to the corner.

L4293.text: I found an almost new leather couch online for two hundred dollars, but it won't fit in my car.
My brother has a pickup truck. If he's free Saturday, we could go get it together.
Perfect. The seller wants it picked up by Sunday anyway. I'll pay for his gas.

L4294.text: The kids want to adopt that big brown dog from the shelter. They've promised to walk him.
They promised that about the hamster too, and guess who cleaned its cage. I can't walk a dog with my hospital hours.
Fair point. Let's have them walk the neighbor's dog for two weeks first.

L4295.text: I heard you had an accident on the way home. Are you all right?
I'm fine. Someone backed into my bumper at the grocery store. She gave me her number and insurance, and admitted it was her fault.
Good. Take pictures of the dent too, in case she changes her story later.

L4296.text: I need two recommendation letters for the scholarship. My calculus professor said yes, and I'm thinking of asking my old basketball coach for the other.
I'd ask your physics teacher instead. The committee will care more about your academic work than your basketball games.
Good point. I'll ask him tomorrow.

L4297.text: A table for four, please. The kids are already starving.
It'll be forty-five minutes. But I can seat two of you at the counter now and the other two in ten minutes.
Splitting up isn't ideal, but it beats waiting. We'll do that.

L4298.text: Honey, come down to the basement! There's water all over the floor.
Oh no. Is it the water heater?
No, a hose on the back of the washing machine split. I've turned off the water, but the carpet is soaked.

L4299.text: Are you flying to your parents' place for Thanksgiving?
No. The airline wants a hundred and twenty-five dollars each way to put my dog in a crate. I'm checking the train.
Good. Dogs under twenty pounds can ride next to you, and yours is only fifteen.

L4300.text: My tomato plants are tall but hardly produce any tomatoes, and I water them daily. They're on the north side of the house.
That's your problem. They need at least six hours of direct sun. Next spring, plant them by the garage, where it's sunny.

L4301.text: You look exhausted. Still having trouble sleeping?
Yeah. I'm in bed by eleven but awake until three. I drink coffee after lunch and watch my phone in bed.
Try cutting out afternoon coffee and leaving your phone in the kitchen. If that doesn't help, see a doctor.

L4302.text: Ryan's science project is due Monday, and he's barely started. I might just build the volcano for him this weekend.
Don't. The teacher will be able to tell, and he won't learn anything. Buy the materials and let him do the work.
You're right. It's his project, not mine.

L4303.text: My books for this semester came to almost four hundred dollars. Have you bought yours yet?
I rent mine now, for about a third of the price. Have you ever opened a textbook again after a class ended?
Honestly, no. They're all sitting in boxes in my closet.

L4304.text: Should I get all-season or snow tires? I drive twenty-five miles to the base every day, over the mountain.
Snow tires. All-season ones are fine for town, but not for a mountain road in January.
That makes sense. I'll order them today.

L4305.text: I've decided to learn golf. My husband plays every Sunday, and I'm tired of staying home alone.
Good for you. The club's private lessons are expensive, but the city course has cheap group lessons on Saturday mornings.
That sounds much more reasonable. Do you have their number?

L4306.text: Your sister's wedding is outdoors on Saturday, right? With a seventy percent chance of rain, can't they use the barn?
It's booked for another event. But my uncle is bringing a big party tent on Friday night.
That's a relief. At least the guests will stay dry.

L4307.text: My suitcase never came out at carousel six, and my hotel is an hour from here.
Your bag missed its connection in Atlanta. It arrives at eight tonight, and we'll deliver it to your hotel free of charge.
Thank you. My clothes for tomorrow's meeting are in that bag.

L4308.text: The movers quoted two thousand dollars to pack and move everything across town.
We could rent a truck for two hundred, but that means carrying the piano ourselves. What if we hire them only for the heavy pieces?
My back can't take that, so I'll call them about the heavy pieces.

L4309.text: I cut my hand pretty badly. Should we go to the emergency room for stitches?
Let's try the urgent care clinic. On a Saturday the emergency room could mean a four-hour wait, and our insurance charges more there.
Okay, but if it's too deep for them, we're going straight to the hospital.

L4310.text: Have you seen this phone bill? It's three hundred forty dollars, and it's usually around sixty.
That must be from our Canada trip. Did you turn off your data while we were there?
I thought I did, but I guess I used the maps all the way to Montreal.

L4311.text: The youth soccer league needs a coach for Lily's team. Practices start in two weeks.
Don't look at me. I know nothing about soccer. I've only ever played baseball.
They don't need an expert. It's one practice a week, plus games on Saturday mornings.

L4312.text: Our marketing presentation is Thursday, and Derek still hasn't sent his slides. I've texted him three times since Sunday.
Tell the professor now, not after the presentation. And just in case, start working on his section yourself.
I guess extra work is better than failing with him.

L4313.text: The check is a hundred and eighty for the six of us. Should we split it evenly, or ask for separate checks?
Neither. I only had soup, and it's a busy night. Let's not make more work for the server. I'll pay my share in cash.
Fair enough. Don't forget the tip.

L4314.text: The registration sticker on my license plate expired last month. Can I just renew it online?
Yes, but your car has to pass the state safety inspection first. The garage on Fifth Street does them without an appointment.
Good. The gate guards are checking stickers now, so I'll go at lunch tomorrow.

L4315.text: The sirens just went off. Is that a tornado warning or the monthly test?
It's not the first Wednesday, so it isn't a test. Get the kids into the hall closet, away from the windows.
Okay. I'll grab the flashlight and the radio.

L4316.text: Your mom called. She fell in her kitchen last night. She's okay, but she sounded scared.
That's the second fall this year. She's too proud to move in with us, but she might accept help a few hours a day.
Then let's look into home care this weekend and talk to her together.

L4317.text: Our car isn't ready. They can upgrade us to a minivan for free, or we wait two hours for a compact.
A minivan will be a nightmare to park in the old city, but I won't waste two hours of our vacation.
Then let's take the van and use the public garages.

L4318.text: The dog next door barked again today. My wife says it went from nine until almost five.
I hear it on my days off too. The owners probably have no idea, since it's quiet whenever they're home.
True. I don't want a fight, though. They just moved in.

L4319.text: I need a refill on my asthma inhaler. I'm leaving the country Saturday for two weeks.
Your insurance won't cover a refill until next Thursday. You can call them for a vacation override, or pay about forty dollars today.
I'll try the phone call first. Forty dollars is forty dollars.

L4320.text: I joined the woodworking shop on base. It's fifteen dollars a month, and I'm making a bookcase for the kids' room.
That's a bargain. Can you use all their tools?
Not the big saws. I need a one-evening safety course first, and the next one isn't until the end of the month.

L4321.text: I placed into basic algebra, not college algebra. Now I need an extra class that doesn't even count toward my degree.
You can retake the placement test once. My roommate did practice tests online for two weeks and jumped a whole level.
Really? Then that's my plan before registration closes.

L4322.text: I booked the Italian restaurant's private room for Sergeant Miller's retirement dinner. It's free if we spend fifteen hundred dollars.
Easy. The family-style dinner is seventy dollars a person, so with twenty-two people we'll be over the minimum.
Good. I wasn't sure we'd reach it with so few guests.

L4323.text: Tyler wants to take his driving test next week. The test is all in town, so he should pass, right?
He's fine on quiet streets, but he panics when merging. Soon he'll be on the interstate every day to get to work.
True. Maybe he needs another month of practice with you.

L4324.text: Because of the drought, the city says even-numbered houses can water only Tuesdays and Saturdays, and odd ones Wednesdays and Sundays.
We're forty-three, so that's us on Wednesdays and Sundays. Our sprinkler's set for noon every day, though.
Reset it. Watering's allowed only before eight in the morning or after seven at night.

L4325.text: Maddie wants to stay out until midnight Friday for a birthday party at the Johnsons'. Karen will be home.
Her curfew is ten thirty. But all right, if I'm at the door at twelve to drive her home. She's not walking that late.
Okay, I'll tell her. She'll be thrilled.

L4326.text: I found a used pickup online, ninety thousand miles for only six thousand dollars. I'm seeing it Saturday, and he wants cash.
That sounds almost too good. Before you pay, ask if a mechanic can check it. If he says no, walk away.

L4327.text: I'd like to camp at Yellowstone in July, but everything is booked months ahead. Maybe I'll just get a motel.
My cousin got a campsite last summer by checking the website every morning. People cancel all the time.
Then I'll check before work every day.

L4328.text: We leave for Kenya in three weeks. Do we need any shots?
A few. One works best if you get it at least a month before traveling.
A month? Then we're already too late for that one.

L4329.text: Why did the bank take twelve dollars out of my checking account? I didn't buy anything.
That's a monthly service fee. You're charged whenever your balance drops below five hundred dollars. The basic account is free with direct deposit.
My paycheck already goes in directly, so I'll switch today.

L4330.text: My doctor thinks yoga might help my lower back. Honestly, I can't picture myself doing it with all those flexible people.
I felt the same way. Now I go three times a week, and half the beginners' class is retired. Come once.
Okay, one class. But no promises.

L4331.text: Are we still taking the boat out on the lake tomorrow? The kids can't wait.
The forecast says winds of twenty-five miles an hour, gusting to forty. That's too rough for our boat. How about the aquarium?
Good idea. I'll tell the kids the boat trip is just postponed.

L4332.text: Good afternoon, Bravo Company. The change of command ceremony is this Friday at ten hundred on the parade field, but the full rehearsal will be held on Thursday at fifteen hundred, and attendance is mandatory. Wear the same uniform you will wear on Friday so the first sergeant can check it. If it rains on Thursday, we'll rehearse inside the gym. The reception after the ceremony is open to families.

L4333.text: Attention, all personnel. Starting Monday, the Main Street dining facility will close for about three weeks while the kitchen floor is replaced. During that time, breakfast and dinner will be served at the Riverside dining facility next to the fitness center. Lunch will not be served there; instead, a food truck will park outside Building Twelve from eleven to one. Soldiers on meal cards may use either location at no charge.

L4334.text: Shooters, listen carefully before we go hot. Anyone on this line who sees an unsafe act may call 'cease fire.' When you hear that command, take your finger off the trigger, put your weapon on safe, and keep it pointed downrange. Do not turn around to see what happened, and do not move until a range safety officer tells you to. Firing will start again only on the tower's command.

L4335.text: Good morning. The heat category flag outside headquarters is now black, the highest level. Until it drops, all outdoor training is suspended except for mission-essential tasks. Anyone who must work outside will follow a cycle of ten minutes of work and fifty minutes of rest, and drink at least one quart of water every hour. Leaders, check your soldiers often for headaches, dizziness, or confusion. The flag will be updated every hour.

L4336.text: All right, drivers, here's the plan for tomorrow's road march. We'll line up at the motor pool at zero five thirty and roll out at zero six hundred. The fuel truck will travel last, right behind the maintenance vehicle, so nobody gets left without help. If you lose sight of the vehicle ahead of you, don't speed up to catch it. Pull over at the next checkpoint and wait there for the trail vehicle to collect you.

L4337.text: Attention on the range. Lightning has been detected eight miles from our location. Under our policy, the range goes cold whenever lightning is within ten miles. Clear your weapons, leave them on the firing points, and move to the buses in the parking area. Stay inside the buses, not under the trees. We will wait thirty minutes after the last strike before anyone returns to the line.

L4338.text: Before we head out to the training area, a reminder about the cold. Temperatures tonight will fall to about ten degrees, and with the wind it will feel much colder. Bring at least two extra pairs of socks and change them whenever your feet get wet or sweaty. Every two hours, team leaders will check their soldiers' fingers, toes, and faces. Report any numbness right away; frostbite is much easier to treat when it's caught early.

L4339.text: Listen up, everyone. The medics found ticks on three soldiers after yesterday's field problem. Before you go back into the woods, tuck your pants into your boots and spray repellent on your uniform, not on your skin. When you come back in, check yourself and your buddy, especially behind the knees and along the waistband. If you find a tick, don't pull it off with your fingers. Go to the aid station, and the medics will remove it properly.

L4340.text: Good morning, and thank you for calling the visitor control center. Our hours are six a.m. to six p.m. on weekdays and eight to four on weekends. All visitors age eighteen and older need a valid photo ID and must pass a background check, which can take up to twenty minutes. If your guest arrives after hours, you'll have to meet them at the main gate and sign them in yourself. For more information, please stay on the line.

L4341.text: Hello, this is Ms. Harmon at the education center with a reminder for everyone planning to take college classes this spring. Tuition assistance requests must be submitted online at least seven days before your class begins, and your supervisor has to approve them first. Requests that come in late cannot be paid, and you'll be responsible for the full cost. If you need help with the application, our counselors are available on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

L4342.text: Squad leaders, every hour on the hour, I want a sensitive items report over the radio. That means you physically lay eyes on every weapon, night vision device, and radio in your squad, and then call in the numbers. Don't report from memory. If anything is missing, freeze the area: nobody moves, nobody packs up, until we find it. Last month one company spent nine hours searching for a lost scope, so take this seriously.

L4343.text: This is a message from the network operations office. Some users have received an e-mail that looks like it comes from the finance office and asks them to update their bank information through a link. That e-mail is fake. Do not click the link or reply. Instead, use the report button at the top of your e-mail program. If you've already entered any information, call the help desk at extension forty-two fifty right away so we can lock your account.

L4344.text: Effective immediately, no vehicle leaves this motor pool without a valid dispatch. Before you pick up the keys, complete your before-operation checks and have the dispatcher sign the form. Dispatches are good for one day only, so if you keep a vehicle overnight, you'll need a new one in the morning. The dispatch office opens at zero six thirty. Any driver caught without a dispatch will lose driving privileges for thirty days.

L4345.text: Hello, families of the Second Battalion. Our next family readiness meeting will be held next Tuesday at six thirty p.m. in the community center ballroom. Since the unit leaves next month, representatives from the legal office and the finance office will be there to answer questions about powers of attorney and pay. Free child care will be provided at the youth center, but you must reserve a spot by Friday. Light refreshments will be served.

L4346.text: If you missed qualification last week because of leave or a medical appointment, your makeup date is next Wednesday. Transportation leaves from the battalion parking lot at zero six fifteen. Bring your weapon card, eye protection, and ear plugs; the range will not issue them. Soldiers who fail to qualify on the makeup day will be scheduled for remedial marksmanship training the following week, so get some practice on the simulator before then.

L4347.text: Hello, residents. This is the housing maintenance office with an update. Starting next month, routine repair requests, such as dripping faucets or broken cabinet doors, must be submitted through our new online portal instead of by phone. Our staff will contact you within three working days to schedule a visit. However, emergencies like a gas smell, a water leak, or no heat in winter should still be reported by phone, twenty-four hours a day. Please do not use the portal for these.

L4348.text: Tonight's land navigation course begins at nineteen thirty. Each of you will find four points in four hours, working alone. Use only the red lens on your flashlight, and keep it covered unless you are reading your map. The boundary is marked by the paved road on the east and the power lines on the west. If you get lost or hurt, stay where you are and blow your whistle three times. A safety vehicle will be patrolling the road all night.

L4349.text: Attention, shoppers. The commissary's spring case lot sale will take place this Friday and Saturday from nine a.m. to five p.m. in the parking lot behind the store. Items will be sold by the case only, so it's a great time to stock up on canned goods, paper towels, and bottled water. Because of the sale, that parking lot will be closed to regular customers, who should park at the bowling alley across the street. Shuttle carts will run between the two lots.

L4350.text: Before anyone leaves this range, we account for every round. Unused ammunition goes back to the ammo point, not into your pockets or your vehicle. Brass casings go into the buckets at each firing point. Next to the tower, there's an amnesty box. If you find a loose round in your gear, drop it in the box, and no questions will be asked. But if a round turns up during the vehicle search at the gate, the whole company will wait while we search everyone again.

L4351.text: Good morning. Due to icy roads, the installation is on a two-hour delayed reporting schedule today. Non-essential personnel should report at zero nine thirty instead of zero seven thirty. Mission-essential personnel, including gate guards, firefighters, and dining facility staff, must report at their normal time. The child development centers will open two hours late as well. Please drive slowly, leave plenty of space, and check the installation website or call the hotline for updates before you leave home.

L4352.text: Drivers and assistant drivers, listen up. Our convoy to Camp Ridley is about two hundred miles, so we'll make two rest halts. The first will be at the truck stop at mile marker eighty, where we'll also refuel. The second is a short halt on the shoulder, at about mile one forty, for ten minutes only. During halts, assistant drivers will check tires and fluids while drivers stay with their vehicles. Nobody walks away from the convoy without telling the convoy commander.

L4353.text: Hello, this is the troop medical clinic with a message for Charlie Company. According to our records, twelve of your soldiers are overdue for their annual health assessment, and they are now listed as not medically ready. That means they cannot go to the field next month until it's done. We're holding walk-in hours this Wednesday and Thursday from one to four. The assessment takes about forty-five minutes. Soldiers should bring their glasses and a list of any medicines they take.

L4354.text: Tomorrow's water survival training is at the indoor pool at zero seven hundred. You'll swim in your uniform and boots, so bring a dry set of clothes and a towel. The first event is a fifteen-meter swim, followed by a five-minute float. If you are not a strong swimmer, tell an instructor before you get in the water; you'll be placed in a separate lane near the side of the pool. Instructors will be in the water with you at all times.

L4355.text: Parents, please note that starting October first, the child development center will open at six a.m. and close at six p.m. That's thirty minutes earlier in the evening than before. If you arrive after closing time, a late fee of one dollar per minute will be charged, and three late pickups in one month may lead to the loss of your child's spot. If you know you'll be delayed, call the front desk and let us know who will pick up your child.

L4356.text: Listen up, third platoon. The fire marshal will inspect the barracks on Friday morning. Hot plates, candles, space heaters, and extension cords plugged into other extension cords are not allowed in your rooms. If you have any of these, take them home or put them in your car before Thursday night. Coffee makers and microwaves are fine as long as they're plugged directly into the wall. Any room that fails will be inspected again every week for a month.

L4357.text: Good morning, everyone. Before flight operations begin, we'll do a foreign object walk on the flight line at zero seven hundred. Line up shoulder to shoulder at the edge of the hangar and walk slowly toward the runway, looking down the whole time. Pick up anything that doesn't belong there: bolts, rocks, plastic, even small pieces of paper. A single loose bolt pulled into a jet engine can cause millions of dollars in damage. Put everything you find into the bags the supervisors will hand out.

L4358.text: Today you'll go through the vehicle rollover trainer. The crew compartment will turn on its side and then upside down, so secure everything loose before we start, including water bottles and phones. Keep your seat belt fastened until the vehicle stops moving completely. When it stops, the vehicle commander will call out, and each person will answer with a status. Then brace yourself with one hand, release the belt with the other, and exit through the nearest door.

L4359.text: This is the post office with a reminder about holiday mail. If you are sending packages from here to the United States, the deadline for regular service is November eighth. Priority mail must be dropped off by December second. Every package needs a customs form, which you can fill out online before you come in to save time. Remember that lithium batteries and anything flammable cannot be shipped. Our lines get very long on Saturdays, so if you can, come during the week.

L4360.text: Guard mount, listen up. Starting tonight, every ID card at all three gates will be scanned, not just checked by eye. Hold the card face up under the scanner until you hear the beep. A green light means the person may enter. A yellow light means the card is expiring soon, so let them in but remind them to renew it. A red light means stop: do not let the vehicle through, direct it to the visitor lane, and call the desk sergeant.

L4361.text: Attention, Alpha Company. Flu shots for the unit will be given next Tuesday at the battalion aid station, starting at zero eight hundred. Every soldier must receive the vaccine by the end of the month unless they have a medical exemption on file. If you already got your shot at a pharmacy off post, bring the receipt or the card to the aid station so we can update your record. Soldiers who are sick on Tuesday should come back on Thursday instead.

L4362.text: Good afternoon. The brigade run is this Friday morning. Formation is at zero six hundred on Patton Field, and we'll step off fifteen minutes later. The four-mile route follows Main Street, Lee Avenue, and the perimeter road, which will be closed to traffic from zero five thirty until zero seven thirty. Family members and pets may not join the formation, but they're welcome to cheer along the route. Soldiers on profile will meet at the finish line to hand out water.

L4363.text: Good morning, everyone. On Thursday at fourteen hundred, we'll hold a retirement ceremony for Command Sergeant Major Ellis, who has served for thirty-two years. The ceremony will be in the post theater rather than on the parade field because of the expected rain. The uniform for soldiers is the service uniform. After the ceremony, there will be a cake-cutting in the lobby. Seats in the first two rows are reserved for the Sergeant Major's family, so please sit behind them.

L4364.text: Here are the field sanitation rules for this exercise. Drink and cook only with water from the water buffalo or bottled water; never from the stream, even if it looks clean. Hand-washing stations are set up outside the latrines and next to the mess tent, and you'll wash your hands before every meal, no exceptions. Food waste goes in the sealed containers, not in open pits, so we don't attract animals. Anyone with diarrhea or vomiting reports to the medics immediately.

L4365.text: Attention, customers. The military clothing sales store will be closed Monday through Wednesday next week for its yearly inventory. If you need uniform items before then, we're open regular hours through Saturday. During the closure, name tapes and rank can still be ordered online and picked up when we reopen on Thursday. Soldiers who need items urgently for a deployment or a board appearance may contact the store manager, who will make special arrangements.

L4366.text: Attention, Headquarters Company. Protective mask fitting and inspection will be held in the chemical defense room, Building Two Twelve, on Monday and Tuesday. Bring your mask, carrier, and hood. If you wear glasses, you'll also need your mask inserts; if you don't have them, the eye clinic needs about three weeks to make them, so make an appointment today. Soldiers whose masks fail inspection will be issued new ones on the spot.

L4367.text: Good news, everyone. The installation tax center opens on February first in Building Nine, next to the legal office. Free tax preparation is available to service members, family members, and retirees. Appointments are required; walk-ins will only be accepted on Friday afternoons. Please bring your W-2 forms, social security cards for everyone listed on the return, and last year's tax return if you have it. Volunteers can also file your state return at no cost.

L4368.text: Before we load the trucks tomorrow, every rucksack will be laid out and checked against the packing list. Squad leaders will do the layout at zero six hundred in the company area. Your rucksack should weigh no more than fifty pounds; we'll have a scale there. Do not pack personal electronics other than a watch. If something on the list is missing, see the supply sergeant tonight, not tomorrow morning, because the supply room will be closed when we leave.

L4369.text: This is a weather warning for all units in the field. Winds of forty to fifty miles per hour are expected between midnight and six a.m. Tie down all tents and camouflage nets, and remove anything loose from the tops of vehicles. Do not sleep in tents that are near dead trees, which can fall in strong winds; move to the vehicles instead. Fire pits and stoves must be put out completely before ten p.m.

L4370.text: Drivers, this week's night driving training will be done with night vision goggles and blackout lights only. Before you go out, adjust and focus your goggles in the dark room at the motor pool; don't do it on the road. Remember that the goggles take away depth perception, so it's harder to judge distances. Keep your speed under fifteen miles per hour on the course, and leave at least twice the usual distance between vehicles.

L4371.text: If you lose your military ID card, here's what to do. First, report the loss to the military police; they will give you a signed memo. Next, have your unit print a verification letter. Take both documents and one other form of photo ID, such as a driver's license or passport, to the ID card office. Appointments are strongly recommended, because walk-in wait times can be over two hours. If you later find the old card, turn it in; don't keep using it.

L4372.text: Before the arms room will accept your weapon after the exercise, it has to pass inspection by your team leader and then by the armorer. That means no carbon, no sand, and a light coat of oil. The arms room will be open from thirteen hundred to nineteen hundred today. If your weapon is not turned in by nineteen hundred, you'll keep it under guard overnight with your squad. So start cleaning now and don't wait until the last minute.

L4373.text: This is a reminder from the training office. All annual online courses, including cyber awareness and information security, must be completed by the thirtieth of this month. As of today, the battalion is at sixty percent. Soldiers who have not finished will not be able to sign out on leave until their certificates are uploaded. If you don't have a computer at your work area, the learning center has open hours every evening until twenty-one hundred.

L4374.text: Before the aircraft arrive, here's how to load safely. Never approach a helicopter from the rear; the tail rotor is almost invisible when it's turning. Wait until the crew chief signals you, then move in from the front or side, where the pilot can see you. Carry your weapon pointed down and your antenna tied down. Hold onto your headgear, or better, take it off, because the rotor wash will blow away anything loose.

L4375.text: Attention, gym users. Starting Monday, the Lincoln Fitness Center will close for four months while the locker rooms and the indoor track are renovated. Weight equipment and treadmills will be moved to the old hangar on Airfield Road, which will be open from five a.m. to ten p.m. Showers will not be available there, so plan accordingly. Group exercise classes will continue at the youth center gym on their normal schedule.

L4376.text: Soldiers returning from temporary duty: you have five working days after you get back to turn in your travel voucher. Attach your orders, your lodging receipts, and receipts for any single expense over seventy-five dollars. Meals don't need receipts; they're paid at a daily rate. Submit everything through your unit's travel clerk, not directly to finance. If your voucher is late or incomplete, your payment could be delayed by a month or more.

L4377.text: This is range control with a flash flood warning for the training area. Heavy rain in the hills this afternoon may cause streams to rise quickly, even where it isn't raining. Low-water crossings on Tank Trail Four and Tank Trail Nine are closed until further notice. Do not try to drive through moving water; just six inches can knock a person down, and two feet can carry away most vehicles. Units should move their camps to higher ground before dark.

L4378.text: The next combat lifesaver course runs from the ninth through the thirteenth at the medical simulation center. Each squad must send at least one soldier, and we only have twelve seats, so squad leaders need to give me names by Wednesday. The first three days are classroom work; the last two are hands-on, outside, in all weather. Students who pass will be certified for three years. Anyone who already holds a current certificate should not be nominated.

L4379.text: Range control, all units. Before you occupy any range or training area, you must call us on the range radio net and get permission. Give your unit, the range number, the officer in charge, and the number of personnel. Report every hour with a communications check. If we don't hear from you for more than two hours, we'll close the range and send someone out to find you. When you're finished, call us again before you leave so we can clear the area.

L4380.text: Next Friday is our battalion's organization day, so there will be no regular duty after zero nine hundred. The day starts with a short ceremony honoring this year's award winners, followed by sports competitions between companies: volleyball, tug-of-war, and a relay race. Families are invited to join us for lunch at noon. Each company will bring two side dishes, and the battalion will provide the main course. First sergeants, send me your team rosters by Tuesday.

L4381.text: Attention, residents of Barracks Building Forty. Plumbers will be replacing a broken pipe tomorrow, so the water in the building will be turned off from eight a.m. until about three p.m. That means no showers, sinks, or toilets during those hours. Portable toilets will be placed in the parking lot, and you may shower at the gym across the street. Please fill a few bottles with drinking water tonight. We're sorry for the inconvenience.

L4382.text: Welcome to the rappel tower. Before anyone climbs, the instructors will check your harness, your gloves, and your helmet strap. You'll make your first rappel from the thirty-foot wall, and only after two good runs there will you move to the sixty-foot side. Your brake hand never leaves the rope. If you freeze or panic, the belay person at the bottom will pull the rope tight and stop you, so trust the system. Stay off the tower stairs unless you're next.

L4383.text: Hello, this is the passenger terminal. Service members on leave may sign up for space-available flights by e-mail or in person, up to sixty days in advance. Seats are given by category and by sign-up date, not by when you arrive at the terminal. Flights can be canceled or changed at the last minute, so have enough money for a commercial ticket and a hotel just in case. Remember, your leave starts when you sign up, not when you fly.

L4384.text: Here's the latest on road conditions. Because of freezing rain overnight, the installation is at road condition red. Tactical vehicles may not leave the motor pools for any reason except emergencies, and only with the battalion commander's approval. Privately owned vehicles may still be driven, but at no more than fifteen miles per hour. Today's convoy training is postponed until Thursday. Sand trucks are working on the main roads now; side streets will be done by noon.

L4385.text: Hello, this is the dental clinic. Annual dental exams for First Battalion are scheduled throughout next week. Your unit has a sign-up sheet, and each soldier must choose one time slot. Exams take about thirty minutes and include X-rays and a cleaning if needed.
