If you have a toothache or a broken tooth before then, don't wait; come to dental sick call any weekday between six thirty and seven thirty in the morning.

L4386.text: Sergeant promotion board candidates, your board is on the twenty-first at zero eight thirty in the battalion conference room. Uniform is the service uniform with all awards. Your records must be checked and signed by your first sergeant no later than the fourteenth. Each of you will answer questions from five board members, so study the guide and practice reporting in front of your squad leader. Mock boards will be held every Tuesday afternoon until then.

L4387.text: This is the environmental office. The base recycling center on Depot Road is now open Tuesday through Saturday, eight to four. Cardboard must be flattened, and glass, cans, and plastic should be rinsed before you drop them off. Units can bring large amounts of scrap metal, but they need to call ahead. Please do not leave anything outside the gate after hours; items left there are considered dumping, and the unit or person responsible will be fined.

L4388.text: Drivers, tomorrow we load our vehicles onto the train at the railhead. Your fuel tanks should be no more than three-quarters full, and every vehicle must have its mirrors folded and antennas tied down. You will drive onto the rail cars one at a time, following the ground guide's hand signals only. Once your vehicle is in place, set the parking brake, put it in neutral, and get off. The rail crew will handle the chains and tie-downs.

L4389.text: Attention, everyone. The forestry office will conduct a controlled burn in Training Areas Six and Seven on Wednesday, if winds are light. The burn is planned to reduce dry brush and lower the risk of wildfires later this summer. Smoke may be visible from housing areas and may drift across Range Road, so drivers should turn on their headlights and slow down. People with asthma should keep their windows closed. Please do not call the fire department to report this smoke.

L4390.text: Before you leave for the four-day weekend, a few rules. Anyone traveling more than two hundred and fifty miles from post needs an approved leave form, not just a pass. Get at least seven hours of sleep before any long drive, and stop every two hours. If you've been drinking, call a friend, a taxi, or your squad leader, any time of day or night. Formation is Tuesday at zero six thirty, and everyone will be there on time.

L4391.text: Good morning, and welcome to the testing center. Before we begin, please turn off your phones and smart watches and place them in the box at the front of the room; they will be returned to you when you leave. You may not leave the room once the listening section begins. If you need a restroom break, take it now. You will have seventy-five minutes in total. Raise your hand if your headset is not working, and a proctor will help you.

L4392.text: This morning we're running the obstacle course in teams of four. Before you start, the instructor will demonstrate each obstacle once; watch carefully because there won't be a second demonstration. You may skip only one obstacle, and you'll lose thirty seconds for it. If the bars or ropes are wet, you must wear gloves. Anyone who falls from more than five feet must stop and be checked by the medic, even if they say they feel fine.

L4393.text: This is the installation safety office. Because of two recent accidents involving runners, we're reminding everyone of the rules for physical training on roads. Run facing traffic, and wear a reflective belt from thirty minutes before sunset to thirty minutes after sunrise. Headphones and earbuds are not allowed while running on any road on post. Formations on roads must have road guards at the front and the rear. Military police will be enforcing these rules starting this week.

L4394.text: Here's the meal plan for the field exercise. Breakfast and dinner will be hot meals brought out by the mess team. Lunch will be a ready-to-eat meal, which you'll pick up from your platoon sergeant at morning formation. Don't eat your lunch early; you won't get another. Soldiers with food allergies, see the first sergeant today so the cooks can prepare something special. Trash goes back with the mess team, never into the woods.

L4395.text: Hello, this is the housing office calling about your move-out. Your final inspection is scheduled for the twelfth at ten a.m. Before then, please make sure all your belongings are removed, the carpets are vacuumed, and the oven and refrigerator are clean. If you'd rather not clean yourself, you can choose our cleaning service for a fee of two hundred dollars, but you must request it at least a week before the inspection. Keys will be collected at the end of the visit.

L4396.text: Attention, all personnel. Tomorrow between nine and eleven a.m., the installation will conduct a full-scale emergency exercise. You may hear sirens and see fire trucks and military police vehicles moving quickly around the main post area. Some gates may close for short periods. This is only a drill; however, if you are told to shelter in place, follow the instructions as if it were real. Please do not call emergency numbers about the exercise.

L4397.text: This is the installation operations center. A tornado warning is now in effect for the main post until four forty-five p.m. A tornado has been spotted twelve miles southwest of us, moving northeast. Take shelter now in a basement or an inside room on the lowest floor, away from windows. If you are in a vehicle or an open field, do not try to outrun it; get to a sturdy building or lie flat in a low area. Wait for the all-clear signal.

L4398.text: Before you pull into the fuel point, here are the rules. Turn off the engine, and nobody stays inside the vehicle while it's being fueled. Cell phones must be off and left in the cab. Touch the vehicle with your bare hand before you open the fuel cap to get rid of static electricity. If there's a spill, don't try to wash it away with water; use the spill kit next to each pump and tell the fuel handler immediately.

L4399.text: Welcome to Fort Lane. The newcomers' orientation is held every Monday at the community center from nine to two, and all soldiers arriving this month must attend with their spouses, if possible. You'll hear from housing, finance, the schools, and the medical clinic, and you'll get a free bus tour of the post. Lunch is provided. Child care is free during the orientation, but space is limited, so call the center by Thursday to reserve a spot.

L4400.text: Tonight is night fire. Once it gets dark, no white light is allowed anywhere on the range; red lens only, and only when you're behind the firing line. Your night vision devices must be mounted and checked before we start. Each firing order will have twenty minutes on the line. If your device fails during firing, put your weapon on safe, raise your hand, and wait; a safety will bring you a replacement. Don't get up and walk back yourself.

L4401.text: This is a public health notice for residents of the North Housing area. Because of low water pressure after a pipe break, a boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Do not drink tap water without boiling it for at least one minute first. Use boiled or bottled water for brushing teeth, making baby formula, and washing fruits and vegetables. Showering is safe, but don't let small children swallow the water. Free bottled water is available at the community center.

L4402.text: A reminder after yesterday's accident in the motor pool: every vehicle that moves inside the motor pool must have a ground guide walking in front, and when you back up, you'll use two, one at each rear corner. Drivers, if you lose sight of your ground guide, stop immediately. Ground guides, never walk backward, and never stand between two vehicles. At night, use a flashlight with a colored wand so the driver can see your signals.

L4403.text: Hi, this is Ms. Turner from Army Community Service. We're offering a free class on buying your first car next Wednesday at noon in Room Three. We'll talk about loans, interest rates, and how to avoid dealers who target young service members with high-cost financing. All junior enlisted soldiers are welcome, and attending counts toward your unit's financial readiness training. Bring your lunch; we'll provide drinks. To sign up, call us at extension five six two zero.

L4404.text: Welcome to the mountain training center. We're now at nine thousand feet, and the air here holds about thirty percent less oxygen than at sea level. For the first two days, there will be no heavy physical training, so your body can adjust. Drink more water than you think you need, avoid caffeine, and get plenty of sleep. Severe headache, confusion, or trouble breathing at rest are warning signs; report them right away, because they can become dangerous quickly.

L4405.text: Good morning. Smoke from wildfires to the west has made the air quality on post unhealthy today. All physical training will be done indoors or canceled, at the commander's discretion. Outdoor work should be kept as short as possible. If you have asthma or any heart or lung condition, stay inside and contact your supervisor about working from another location. The air quality index will be posted at noon, and we'll decide then about this afternoon's outdoor activities.

L4406.text: Candidates for the expert badge, the twelve-mile foot march starts Saturday at zero four hundred at the main gate. You'll have three hours to finish. Your rucksack must weigh at least thirty-five pounds without water, and it will be weighed both before you start and when you cross the finish line. If anything is removed along the way, you're out. Water points are at miles four and eight. Medics will follow in a vehicle behind the last candidate.

L4407.text: Attention, soldiers with orders to Japan or Korea. You and your family members will need no-fee official passports before you travel. Applications are taken at the passport office in Building Eighty, on Mondays and Wednesdays only. Bring your orders, birth certificates, and two passport photos, which the photo shop in the exchange can take for you. Processing takes six to eight weeks, so apply as soon as your orders arrive. Tourist passports cannot be used for this purpose.

L4408.text: For the flight next week, each soldier may check two duffel bags, and neither may weigh more than seventy pounds. Your carry-on is your assault pack, which must fit under the seat in front of you. Weapons will travel in the cabin with you, but no ammunition, lighters, or aerosol cans are allowed in any bag. Bags will be weighed and inspected at the company area on Monday at zero eight hundred, three days before we fly.

L4409.text: Snow is expected tonight, so here's a reminder about snow removal on post. Crews will clear the main roads, the hospital, and the gates first, and housing streets after that. To let the plows through, residents should park on the even-numbered side of the street on even dates and the odd side on odd dates. Cars that block plows may be towed. Residents are responsible for clearing the sidewalk in front of their own homes within twenty-four hours.

L4410.text: Listen up, second platoon. We have dining facility duty next week. Six soldiers per day will report to the kitchen at zero four thirty and work until the evening meal is cleaned up. The roster is posted on the board outside the platoon office. If you can't make your day because of an appointment, it's your job to find a replacement and tell me by Friday. Wear your physical training uniform; aprons and hair nets will be issued there.

L4411.text: Hello, this is the hospital pharmacy. To reduce waiting times, prescription refills are no longer picked up at the main pharmacy. Please order your refill by phone or online, then pick it up two working days later at the drive-through window behind the commissary. New prescriptions from your doctor will still be filled at the main pharmacy inside the hospital. The drive-through is open weekdays from eight to six. Please have your ID card ready when you reach the window.

L4412.text: Before you leave for the long weekend, update your phone number and address on the recall roster. On Saturday, the battalion will test the alert system without warning. When you receive the call or text, you'll have one hour to reply to your team leader. You do not need to come in unless you're told to. Last time it took more than four hours to reach everyone, which is not acceptable, so keep your phone on and nearby.

L4413.text: Hello, this is the transition center. Soldiers who plan to leave the service within the next year must attend our five-day employment workshop. Classes cover writing a résumé, practicing interviews, and using your education benefits. The workshop is offered twice a month, and seats fill quickly, so register at least ninety days before your separation date. Spouses are welcome to attend. Business attire is encouraged on the last day, when local employers will visit.

L4414.text: One change to the route for tomorrow's move. The bridge over Miller Creek on Route Seven has a new weight limit of twenty tons. Our trucks and smaller vehicles can cross it as usual, but the heavy equipment transporters must take the bypass on County Road Twelve, which adds about forty minutes. Those transporters will leave thirty minutes before the main body so that both groups reach the assembly area at about the same time.

L4415.text: Planning a weekend trip? Outdoor Recreation rents tents, sleeping bags, kayaks, and camping trailers at low prices. Equipment can be reserved up to thirty days ahead and is picked up on Friday afternoons. Weekend rentals must be returned by noon Monday, clean and dry. A late return costs one extra day's rental, and anything damaged or lost will be charged at full replacement cost. Boating rentals require a short safety class, offered every Thursday evening.

L4416.text: Welcome to the battalion. Each of you has been assigned a sponsor, a soldier from your new company who will help you during your first two weeks. Your sponsor will show you your barracks room, take you to in-processing appointments, and introduce you to your chain of command. If your sponsor hasn't contacted you by tonight, tell the staff duty officer at headquarters. Formation tomorrow is at zero six thirty, in physical training uniform.

L4417.text: The Armed Services Blood Program will hold a blood drive on Thursday from nine to three in the gym annex. Donors must weigh at least one hundred and ten pounds and feel well on the day of the drive. Please eat a good meal and drink plenty of water beforehand. If you got a tattoo in the last three months or traveled to certain countries, you may be asked to wait. The whole process takes about an hour, and donors get the rest of the day off.

L4418.text: Platoon sergeants, the storm knocked out power across post last night, and some phones are down. By ten hundred, I need a full accountability report: every soldier, by name, located and checked on, including those living off post. If you can't reach someone by phone, send two soldiers to their home. Report anyone injured or without power who needs a place to stay; the gym is open as a shelter with cots and hot food.

L4419.text: Attention, all units and personnel. Deer hunting season opens Saturday, and some training areas will be open to hunters with permits on weekends. Anyone walking, jogging, or bicycling in those areas should wear a bright orange vest or hat. Units training on weekends must check the hunting map at range control and avoid areas marked in red. During the season, never move quietly through the woods dressed in brown or gray; you could be mistaken for a deer.

L4420.text: Good evening, passengers booked on flight two eighteen to Denver. Because the aircraft scheduled for this flight needs a minor repair, we have arranged a replacement plane, which is parked at Gate twenty-four in the north concourse. Please gather your belongings and make your way there now; the walk takes about ten minutes. Boarding will begin at seven fifteen, roughly forty minutes later than planned. Passengers with connecting flights in Denver should speak with an agent at the new gate.

L4421.text: Attention, shoppers. For the next thirty minutes only, all winter coats and jackets in our outerwear department on the second floor are forty percent off the lowest marked price. This discount cannot be combined with coupons, and it does not apply to boots or gloves, which are already on clearance near the escalators. If you need a different size, ask any associate wearing a red vest, and they will check our stockroom for you. Thank you for shopping with us.

L4422.text: This is your seven forty traffic update. Drivers heading downtown on Highway Ten should expect long delays near the Pine Street exit, where a truck lost part of its load and the two right lanes are blocked. Crews say the cleanup could take another hour. If you can, use River Road instead; traffic there is moving well. The Oak Avenue bridge, which was closed yesterday for painting, has reopened in both directions. We'll have another update in fifteen minutes.

L4423.text: Hi, Daniel, this is Karen from Westside Auto calling about your car. We finished the brake job this morning, but while it was up on the lift, our mechanic noticed that your front tires are badly worn. We didn't replace them because we needed your approval first. The car is safe to drive for now, and you can pick it up anytime before six. If you'd like us to put on new tires, call me back by three so we can order them today.

L4424.text: Good morning, everyone. Before I hand out the final exam, a few reminders. You'll have ninety minutes. Phones must be switched off and left in your bags at the front of the room. You may use a calculator, but not the one on your phone. Write your answers in pen; anything written in pencil will not be graded. If you finish early, you may leave quietly, but nobody may leave during the last fifteen minutes. Good luck.

L4425.text: Welcome to the Hall of Flight. Before we begin, please note that flash photography is not permitted in this gallery, because bright light can damage the older fabric on some of the aircraft. Regular photos without a flash are fine. Our tour will last about forty-five minutes and will end in the gift shop on the lower level. If you'd like to sit inside a real cockpit, the line for that forms near the exit, and children under twelve must be with an adult.

L4426.text: Thank you for calling Lakeview Community Bank. To hear your account balance, press one. To report a lost or stolen card, press two; this line is open twenty-four hours a day. For questions about loans, press three. Please note that our branches will be closed on Monday for the holiday, but our cash machines will work as usual. To repeat these options, press nine, or stay on the line to speak with a representative.

L4427.text: Hi, I'm Nurse Patel from the community health clinic. With temperatures expected to reach the high nineties this week, I want to share a few tips. Drink water before you feel thirsty, because by then you're already low on fluids. Avoid heavy outdoor work between noon and four, when the sun is strongest. Watch for warning signs like dizziness, headache, or cool, damp skin. If someone shows these signs, move them to a shady place and give them water slowly.

L4428.text: Welcome to the Harbor View Hotel. Breakfast is served in the Garden Room from six thirty to ten on weekdays and until eleven on weekends. The pool on the roof is open until nine at night, but there is no lifeguard on duty, so children must be with an adult. If you need extra towels or pillows, dial zero for the front desk. Checkout time is noon; if you need to stay later, please ask at least one day in advance.

L4429.text: Ladies and gentlemen, this is the eight oh five express to Union Station. Because of track work, this train will not stop at Maple Grove or Fairview this morning. Passengers for those stations should get off at Hillcrest, the next stop, and take the free shuttle bus waiting outside the main entrance; it stops at both stations. Please remember that the quiet car is at the back of the train, and phone calls are not allowed there. Thank you for riding with us.

L4430.text: Good afternoon, shoppers. Riverside Mall will close early today, at six o'clock, so that crews can prepare the center for tomorrow's holiday sale. Most restaurants in the food court will also close at six, but the movie theater will stay open for its regular evening shows; theater guests should use the entrance on Elm Street after six. Tomorrow, the doors open at seven in the morning, two hours earlier than usual. We apologize for any inconvenience.

L4431.text: Hi, this is Linda, the building manager. I'm calling all residents on the third floor to let you know that the water will be shut off tomorrow from nine until about one while a plumber replaces a leaking pipe in the wall near the elevator. If you need water during that time, the laundry room in the basement won't be affected. Also, please move anything you keep in the hallway, because the plumber will need space to work. Thanks for your patience.

L4432.text: Good morning, this is Mike with your weekend weather. Today will start foggy, especially near the river, but the fog should lift by ten, leaving us with sunny skies and a high of seventy-two. Enjoy it, because a cold front arrives tonight. Expect heavy rain after midnight, and Sunday will be windy and much cooler, with highs only in the fifties. If you have outdoor plans this weekend, today is clearly the better day.

L4433.text: Thank you for calling Rosa's Kitchen. We're open for lunch Tuesday through Sunday from eleven thirty to two thirty, and for dinner every evening from five to ten. We accept reservations for groups of six or more; smaller parties are seated in the order they arrive. For takeout orders, please visit our website, since we no longer take orders by phone. To leave a message for the manager, please stay on the line.

L4434.text: Welcome to Introduction to Computer Skills. This course meets every Tuesday and Thursday evening for eight weeks. Each week, you'll complete a short practice assignment, which isn't graded but must be turned in before the next class. Your final grade comes from two projects, one due in week four and one in week eight. If you have to miss a class, email me beforehand, and I'll send you the notes. Don't worry if you've never used a computer before; we'll start with the basics.

L4435.text: Hello, this is Nurse Gloria Kim from Maple Family Clinic, following up on your visit this morning. The doctor has sent your antibiotic to the pharmacy. Please take one pill twice a day, with food, for ten days. Even if you feel better after three or four days, keep taking them until they're gone; stopping early can bring the infection back. If you get a rash or have trouble breathing, stop the medicine and call us right away.

L4436.text: Attention, travelers in the security line. To help things move faster, please remove laptops and large electronics from your bags and place them in a separate bin. Liquids must be in containers of three ounces or less, all inside one clear plastic bag. You do not need to remove your shoes if you are under twelve or over seventy-five. Finally, please keep your boarding pass and identification in your hand until you reach the officer.

L4437.text: Good evening, shoppers. Our pharmacy counter will close in fifteen minutes, at eight o'clock. If you're waiting for a prescription, please make sure you've given your name to the pharmacist. Any orders not picked up tonight will be ready tomorrow after nine. The rest of the store remains open until eleven. Also, don't forget that today is the last day to use your double-points coupon in the bakery and deli.

L4438.text: Good morning, and welcome to Cedar Falls State Park. I'm Ranger Tom, and I'll be leading today's two-mile hike to the falls. The trail is rocky in places, so watch your step, and please stay on the marked path to protect the plants. We'll stop halfway at a viewpoint for a short rest. You'll see a lot of wildlife, but feeding the animals is against park rules, even in small amounts. If you brought pets, they must stay on a leash.

L4439.text: Hello, this is Megan from the Greenfield Public Library. The book you requested, Mountains of the West, has arrived and is being held for you at the front desk. We can keep it for seven days, until next Friday. After that, it will go to the next person on the waiting list. Please bring your library card when you come in. Also, you currently have one overdue item, so please return it at the same time to avoid further fines.

L4440.text: Good morning, students. Because of the snowstorm expected this afternoon, school will dismiss two hours early today, at twelve fifteen. Buses will run on their normal routes, just earlier. All after-school activities, including basketball practice and the chess club, are canceled. Students who usually walk home but don't have a key should go to the main office to call a parent. Lunch will be served at the regular time.

L4441.text: Good evening, guests. We'd like to let you know that the elevator on the east side of the building is out of order and will be repaired tomorrow morning. In the meantime, please use the west elevator next to the gift shop. Guests who have difficulty with stairs and are staying on the east side may request a room change at the front desk at no extra cost. We're sorry for the trouble, and thank you for your understanding.

L4442.text: You have reached Valley Water and Power. If you are calling to report a power outage, press one. Please note that we are aware of the outage in the Brookside neighborhood, and crews expect power to be restored by four this afternoon. To pay your bill, press two. To start or stop service because you are moving, press three. Wait times are currently longer than usual, so you may want to visit our website for faster service.

L4443.text: Here's your afternoon traffic report. If you're heading to tonight's baseball game, give yourself extra time. The stadium parking lots are expected to fill up by six, and officials are encouraging fans to take the light rail instead. Trains will run every ten minutes until midnight. Meanwhile, on Interstate Five, the accident near Exit Twelve has been cleared, and traffic is back to normal. Have a safe drive home.

L4444.text: Okay, you've got a mild sprain, so here's what I'd like you to do at home. For the first two days, keep the ankle raised above the level of your heart whenever you can, and put ice on it for twenty minutes every few hours. Never put ice directly on your skin; wrap it in a thin towel. You can take a pain reliever if you need it. If the swelling hasn't gone down in a week, come back and see us.

L4445.text: May I have your attention, please. The four fifty train to Springfield, scheduled to leave from Track Three, will now depart from Track Seven. This train is running about ten minutes late because of a signal problem outside the station. The snack bar on Track Seven is closed today, but you can buy food and drinks in the main hall before boarding. Passengers with bicycles must board through the first car only.

L4446.text: Welcome to the City Art Museum audio guide. To hear about a painting, type the three-digit number on the small sign next to it and press the green button. To pause, press the red button. You can listen in any order you like. Please keep the volume low so you don't disturb other visitors. When you finish, return the device to the coat check on the first floor, where you'll get back the photo identification you left as a deposit.

L4447.text: Hey, Jessica, it's Amy. Listen, about dinner on Thursday. The Italian place we picked just called me. They've had a kitchen fire, nothing serious, but they're closed until next week. So I booked a table at that Thai restaurant on Fifth Street instead, same time, seven thirty. It's a little farther from your office, so if you'd rather I pick you up, just text me. Otherwise, I'll see you there.

L4448.text: Good evening, and welcome to the defensive driving course. Tonight's class runs about four hours, with a fifteen-minute break at the halfway point. To receive your certificate, which may lower your car insurance rates, you must attend the entire class and pass a short written quiz at the end. If you leave early, even for an emergency, you'll need to sign up again and repeat the full course. Restrooms are down the hall to your left.

L4449.text: Attention, shoppers. The maker of Sunny Fields peanut butter has recalled its sixteen-ounce jars because they may contain small pieces of plastic. If you bought this product in the past month, please don't eat it. Bring the jar, opened or not, to our customer service desk for a full refund; you don't need a receipt. Other sizes and other brands of peanut butter are not affected and remain safe to eat.

L4450.text: Welcome to Portland. Passengers arriving on flight five forty-two from Chicago, your bags will be delivered to carousel number four, not carousel two as shown on the screens. Oversized items such as strollers, golf clubs, and car seats will come out at the special baggage door at the end of the hall. If your luggage doesn't arrive within thirty minutes, please visit the baggage service office next to carousel one before leaving the airport.

L4451.text: This is a winter storm warning for the entire county, in effect from six tonight until noon tomorrow. Forecasters expect eight to twelve inches of snow, with strong winds making it hard to see on the roads. The county asks residents to stay off the roads unless travel is absolutely necessary. If you must drive, carry a blanket, water, and a charged phone. Several schools have already announced they'll open two hours late tomorrow.

L4452.text: Thank you for calling room service. Please note that our full menu is available until ten thirty. After that, and until six in the morning, we offer a smaller late-night menu with sandwiches, salads, and soups. All orders include a delivery charge of five dollars. If you have food allergies, please tell us when you order, and the chef will let you know which dishes are safe. Please hold, and the next available staff member will take your order.

L4453.text: Hello, this is the school nurse, Carol Benson, calling about your son, Lucas. He came to my office about twenty minutes ago complaining of a stomachache. He doesn't have a fever, and he's resting now, so I don't think it's serious. He'd like to stay for his afternoon classes, and that's fine with me, but I wanted you to know. If you'd prefer to take him home, just call the front office.

L4454.text: You have reached Riverside Medical Group. If this is a medical emergency, hang up and dial nine one one. To schedule, change, or cancel an appointment, press one. To request a prescription refill, press two; refills may take up to two business days. For billing questions, press three. Our office is closed for lunch from twelve to one, and calls during that hour will be returned the same afternoon.

L4455.text: Before we start, let me explain my policy on late work. Essays turned in up to two days late will lose ten percent of their grade. After that, I won't accept them at all, unless you have a note from a doctor or another serious reason. My office hours are Wednesdays from two to four, in Room three fifteen of the Language Building. If that time doesn't work for you, send me a message and we'll find another time.

L4456.text: Good afternoon, visitors. In fifteen minutes, our keepers will feed the sea lions at the outdoor pool next to the Ocean Cafe. It's a great show, and you'll learn how the animals are trained. Seats fill up quickly, so we recommend arriving early. Please note that the first three rows may get wet. Also, the penguin house is closed this afternoon for cleaning, but it will reopen tomorrow morning at nine.

L4457.text: Hi, this is Rachel Moore from the human resources office at Northwind Shipping, returning your call about the warehouse supervisor position. We'd like to invite you for an interview next Tuesday at ten in the morning. Please bring a copy of your driver's license and two references. The interview should take about an hour, and it will include a short tour of the warehouse, so wear comfortable shoes. Please call me back to confirm.

L4458.text: Attention, riders. This weekend, the Blue Line will not run between Central Station and Airport Station because of track repairs. Free shuttle buses will replace trains between those stops, so please allow an extra thirty minutes for your trip. Travelers going to the airport may want to take the Green Line to Harbor Station and transfer to the airport express bus, which is usually faster. Normal service returns Monday morning.

L4459.text: Good morning, shoppers, and welcome. Today only, our customer rewards members receive an extra fifteen percent off everything in the home department, including bedding, towels, and kitchen items. Not a member? Joining is free and takes just two minutes at any register. Please remember that the fitting rooms on the second floor are closed for remodeling; you can try on clothes in the fitting rooms on the third floor near the shoe department.

L4460.text: Good evening. Starting Monday, the state will begin a six-week repair project on the Lincoln Bridge. During the work, only one lane will be open in each direction, and trucks heavier than ten tons will be sent to the Washington Street Bridge. Work will take place mainly at night, from eight in the evening to five in the morning, so daytime delays should be small. Drivers should expect lower speed limits through the work area at all times.

L4461.text: Hi, I'm Nurse Angela from the children's health line. When your child needs medicine, always use the measuring cup or syringe that comes with it, not a kitchen spoon, because spoons vary in size. Check the label for the correct dose based on your child's weight, not age. Never give adult medicine to a child, even in a smaller amount. And if you're not sure, call us; we're here twenty-four hours a day.

L4462.text: Attention, museum visitors. The museum will close in thirty minutes. The special exhibit on ancient Egypt on the third floor stops admitting visitors in ten minutes, so if you haven't seen it, please go there now. The gift shop will remain open for fifteen minutes after the museum closes. Please remember to collect any items from the coat check. Tomorrow, the museum opens at ten, and admission is free all day for local residents.

L4463.text: Here are your keys, Mister Ford. You're in room eight twelve, on the eighth floor; the elevators are just behind me on the right. The wireless internet is free, and the password is printed on your key card holder. Breakfast is included and is served in the lobby restaurant. Since you're checking out early on Thursday, before breakfast starts, we can prepare a boxed breakfast for you if you call us the night before.

L4464.text: Welcome to the beginner swim program. Classes last thirty minutes and start right on the hour. Please have your children arrive ten minutes early, already in their swimsuits, because the locker rooms get crowded. You're welcome to watch from the seating area upstairs, but not from the pool deck, since it distracts the kids. If your child misses a class, we can't offer a makeup lesson, but you may switch to another time slot that week if there's space.

L4465.text: Good afternoon, passengers on flight three ninety to Atlanta. We are now ready to begin boarding. First, we invite passengers who need extra time, as well as families traveling with children under two. Next, we'll board groups one through five; please check your boarding pass for your group number. This flight is completely full, so space in the overhead bins will be limited. We're offering free checked baggage to anyone willing to check a carry-on bag here at the gate.

L4466.text: Hi, this is Steve from Quick Fix Heating and Cooling. I'm scheduled to come out tomorrow between one and three to look at your air conditioner. I just wanted to let you know that my morning job got canceled, so I could come earlier, around ten, if that works for you. If not, no problem; I'll keep the original time. Either way, please make sure someone over eighteen is home, and clear a path to the unit outside.

L4467.text: Welcome to our Saturday cooking class. Today we're making fresh pasta and two sauces. Please wash your hands at the sink by the door before you touch any food, and tie back long hair. Each station has its own knives and cutting boards, so please don't take tools from other stations. If you have any food allergies, let me know now, because one of the sauces contains nuts. At the end, you'll eat what you've made, so I hope you came hungry.

L4468.text: And now the beach forecast. Expect sunny skies this morning with a light breeze, but thunderstorms are likely to develop after two this afternoon. Lifeguards will clear the water at the first sound of thunder, and swimmers will have to wait thirty minutes after the last thunder before going back in. Water temperatures are around seventy-five degrees, and the risk of dangerous currents is low today.

L4469.text: Hi, welcome to the Blue Fern. I'm Emily, and I'll be taking care of you tonight. Our soup of the day is tomato basil, and our special is grilled salmon with rice and vegetables. Just so you know, the kitchen is running a bit behind because of a large party, so food may take about twenty-five minutes. If you're in a hurry, the salads and sandwiches come out much faster. Can I start you off with something to drink?

L4470.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to the planetarium. Today's show, Journey to the Planets, lasts about thirty-five minutes. Once the show begins, the doors will be locked, and late arrivals will not be admitted, so if you need to use the restroom, please do so now. The seats lean back, so you can see the whole dome above you. Food and drinks are not allowed inside, but bottled water is fine.

L4471.text: Thank you for calling Skyway Airlines. Due to the storm in the Northeast, we are experiencing very high call volume. If your flight has been canceled, you do not need to call; you have already been rebooked on the next available flight, and the details have been sent by email. To change a flight for any other reason, press one. To check the status of a flight, press two. For all other questions, please stay on the line.

L4472.text: Good morning, shoppers. This Saturday at ten, our garden center will hold a free workshop on planting a vegetable garden. You'll learn how to prepare the soil and which plants grow best in our area. Space is limited to twenty people, so please sign up at the customer service desk. Everyone who attends will receive a free packet of seeds and a coupon for ten percent off garden tools.

L4473.text: Hello, this is Julie Hart, your daughter Emma's fourth-grade teacher. I'm calling because we're going on a field trip to the science center next Friday, and I still haven't received Emma's signed permission form. I need it by Wednesday at the latest, or she'll have to stay at school with another class that day. The trip is free, but she should bring a packed lunch. Thanks, and feel free to call me if you have any questions.

L4474.text: Good morning, new students. A few quick notes about parking. Every car on campus needs a parking permit, which you can buy online or at the campus police office. Students living in the dorms may park only in Lot C, behind the stadium. Commuter students may use Lots A and B. Parking in faculty spaces, marked with blue lines, will get you a seventy-five dollar ticket, even on weekends.

L4475.text: Your blood test is scheduled for eight tomorrow morning, so here's how to prepare. Don't eat anything after ten tonight; the test measures your sugar and cholesterol, and food would change the results. You may drink plain water, and in fact it helps, because it makes your veins easier to find. Take your regular medicines unless your doctor told you otherwise. And bring a snack to eat right after the test.

L4476.text: Good evening, passengers. The dining car, located between cars four and six, is now open for dinner service. Seating is by reservation only; if you haven't reserved a time, please see the dining car attendant. The cafe car, at the front of the train, offers sandwiches and snacks without a reservation until eleven tonight. Sleeping car passengers, your meals are included in your ticket price.

L4477.text: Welcome to the Rose Garden. Our garden has more than four hundred kinds of roses, and right now, in early June, most of them are in full bloom. Please don't pick any flowers, but you're welcome to smell them. All the paths can be used by wheelchairs. About halfway through, we'll stop at the greenhouse, where it's very warm and humid, so you may want to leave your jacket with me before we go in.

L4478.text: Good morning, it's six fifteen. Dense fog is causing problems for early commuters, especially on the coastal highway, where drivers can see only about fifty yards ahead. Police are asking drivers to slow down and use their low-beam headlights, not high beams, which reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. The fog should burn off by nine. Flights at the regional airport are delayed by about an hour.

L4479.text: Good morning, and thank you for staying with us. Our free airport shuttle leaves from the front entrance every thirty minutes, on the hour and half hour, from five in the morning until eleven at night. The ride takes about twenty minutes. During busy times, the shuttle may fill up, so we suggest catching one at least two and a half hours before your flight. Please let the driver know which airline you're flying with.

L4480.text: Good evening, passengers waiting for flight one twenty to Phoenix. Unfortunately, the crew for this flight is arriving on a delayed plane, and our new departure time is ten forty-five. We know this is frustrating. To thank you for your patience, each passenger may pick up a fifteen-dollar meal voucher at the service desk across from Gate Nine. The vouchers can be used at any restaurant in this terminal. We'll give you another update at nine thirty.

L4481.text: Hello, shoppers. This Saturday from noon to four, Lakeside Mall will host its spring family day in the center court. Kids can meet characters from their favorite movies, get their faces painted, and enter a drawing to win a new bicycle. All activities are free, but children must be at least three years old to take part in face painting. Parking will be busy, so we recommend using the lower garage near the cinema entrance.

L4482.text: Hey, Marcus, it's Paul from next door. I hate to ask on such short notice, but my flight to Denver leaves tonight, and the person who was going to watch my dog just canceled. Could you feed him tomorrow morning and evening? The food is in the kitchen closet, and he gets one cup each time. I'll leave a key under the mat. I'll be back Sunday afternoon. Let me know either way, and thanks.

L4483.text: Good morning, and welcome to the English placement test. The test has three parts, listening, reading, and writing, and it takes about two hours in total. There is no passing or failing score; the results simply help us put you in the right class level. You'll find out your level by email within three days. Please don't use dictionaries or translation apps. If you have a problem with your headphones, raise your hand.

L4484.text: Hi, this is Nurse Brian with the twenty-four-hour advice line. Not sure whether to go to the emergency room or an urgent care center? Urgent care is usually faster and cheaper for minor problems like sprains, small cuts, or a sore throat. But for chest pain, trouble breathing, or a serious head injury, go straight to the emergency room or call nine one one. When in doubt, call us first, and we'll help you decide.

L4485.text: Attention, customers. Beginning next month, paper tickets will no longer be sold on board the train. Passengers who board without a ticket will be charged an extra five dollars. You can buy tickets at the machines on every platform or with our phone app. Monthly passes will still be accepted, and their prices will not change. Senior citizens and students can continue to receive half-price fares by showing a valid card.

L4486.text: All right, everyone, gather around. The skeleton in front of you is about sixty-six million years old and was discovered by a farmer in Montana in nineteen ninety. About eighty percent of the bones are real; the rest, mostly in the tail, are copies made of plaster. Please don't lean on the railing. In a moment, we'll head downstairs, where you can touch real fossils and watch scientists cleaning bones through a glass wall.

L4487.text: Hi, this is Lena calling from Harbor Grill to confirm your reservation for eight people this Saturday at seven. Because it's a large group, we'll seat you in our private room upstairs. Please note that for parties of eight or more, an eighteen percent service charge is added to the bill automatically. If any of your guests have special dietary needs, let us know ahead of time. Call us back if you need to make any changes.

L4488.text: Thank you for calling Clearline Internet. If your internet is not working, please try restarting your modem first: unplug it, wait thirty seconds, and plug it back in. This fixes most problems. If you're still having trouble, press one to speak with technical support. To ask about your bill, press two. To upgrade your service, press three. Please have your account number ready; you'll find it in the top right corner of your monthly statement.

L4489.text: This is your Tuesday weather update. It'll be another warm, breezy day with highs near eighty-five. Unfortunately for allergy sufferers, the pollen count is very high, mostly from oak and pine trees, and the wind is spreading it everywhere. If you have allergies, keep your windows closed and try to stay indoors in the early morning, when pollen levels peak. Some relief is on the way: steady rain on Thursday should clear much of it from the air.

L4490.text: Attention, shoppers. Beginning Monday, our store hours will change. We'll open at seven in the morning instead of six, and we'll close at ten at night instead of midnight. The pharmacy hours will stay the same. We're making this change so our staff can restock the shelves before opening. Also, starting next week, the self-checkout lanes will accept cash as well as cards. Thank you for shopping with us.

L4491.text: Hi, this is Tina from Parkside Furniture. Your new sofa is scheduled for delivery this Thursday. Our truck will arrive sometime between eight and noon, and the driver will call about thirty minutes ahead. Please measure your front door before then. The sofa is thirty-four inches deep, and if your doorway is narrower, we'll need to remove the legs, which takes a few extra minutes. There's no charge for taking away your old sofa.

L4492.text: Okay, class, before we start today's lab, listen up. Goggles must stay on the entire time, even when you're just cleaning up. Long hair should be tied back. Do not pour any chemicals down the sink; there's a labeled waste container on each table. If anything spills on your skin, rinse it under the safety shower right away and then tell me. Once you've finished, wash your hands before you leave.

L4493.text: Good morning, and welcome to Red Rock Canyon. Private cars are not allowed on the scenic road between April and October, so please use our free shuttle buses, which leave the visitor center every fifteen minutes. The last bus back from the canyon leaves at six. The longer trails have no water, so bring at least two quarts per person. And remember, temperatures at the bottom of the canyon can be fifteen degrees higher than here.

L4494.text: Good morning, guests. This is the front desk. Today between ten and eleven, we'll be testing the fire alarm system, so you may hear the alarm several times during that hour. Please do not leave the building during the test. However, if the alarm sounds outside that time, or if you see smoke, please leave immediately using the stairs, not the elevators. We apologize for the noise and thank you for your cooperation.

L4495.text: Welcome aboard the terminal train. This train stops at all gates in Terminals A through D. For international departures and customs, please stay on until the final stop, Terminal E. Hold on to the handrails, as the train starts and stops quickly. Please stand clear of the doors when they're closing; the next train will arrive in about two minutes. If you've left the secure area, you'll need to go through security again to return.

L4496.text: Good afternoon. With the long holiday weekend starting, traffic leaving the city is already heavy. Expect the worst delays between three and seven tonight on the northbound highway toward the lakes. If you can wait until after eight, your trip could be an hour shorter. There's no construction on the highway this weekend, but police will be out in large numbers watching for speeding and for drivers who aren't wearing seatbelts.

L4497.text: Good evening, book lovers. In just ten minutes, best-selling author Maria Lopez will read from her new mystery novel in the cafe area on the second floor. After the reading, she'll answer questions and sign copies. Please note that she will sign only books purchased in our store today, so keep your receipt with you. Copies are available at the front registers. Seating is first come, first served.

L4498.text: Hi, this is Jason from Peak Fitness. I'm calling because your membership expires at the end of this month. If you renew before the fifteenth, you'll get two extra months free on a one-year plan. If you'd prefer not to renew, you don't have to do anything; your membership will simply end. Also, please remember to empty your locker before your last day, or the contents will be donated.

L4499.text: If your child has a fever, here's what we recommend. Keep them home from school until they've been fever-free for a full twenty-four hours without medicine. Offer plenty of fluids, like water or soup, and let them rest. Dress them in light clothing; piling on blankets can actually raise their temperature. Call the doctor if the fever goes above one hundred and three or lasts more than three days.

L4500.text: Good morning, everyone. We are now approaching Hartford, where we'll stay for about twenty minutes while we change engines. You're welcome to step off the train to stretch your legs, but please stay on the platform and listen for the whistle; we will not wait for passengers who wander off. If Hartford is your final stop, please check around your seat and the overhead racks for your personal belongings.

L4501.text: Welcome to the Whitfield House, built in seventeen eighty-five. This home belonged to a ship captain and his family of nine. As we go through the rooms, please don't touch the furniture; most of it is original and very fragile. The staircase is narrow and steep, so anyone who'd rather not climb can wait in the kitchen, where a volunteer will show you how bread was baked at that time. The tour ends in the garden.

L4502.text: Thank you for calling Greenway Pharmacy's automatic refill line. Please enter your seven-digit prescription number, found on the label of your medicine bottle, followed by the pound key. To refill more than one prescription, press star after each number. Refills requested before two o'clock will usually be ready the same day after five. If your prescription has no refills left, we will contact your doctor for you.

L4503.text: Good evening. For guests interested in seeing the city, our concierge desk sells tickets for the hop-on, hop-off bus tour. The bus stops right outside the hotel at nine, eleven, one, and three. A ticket is good for twenty-four hours, so you can get off at any stop and catch a later bus. Tickets bought at the hotel are five dollars cheaper than on the bus. The tour takes two hours if you stay on the whole time.

L4504.text: Hi, everyone, and welcome to the computer lab orientation. To log in, use your student number and the password you created during registration. Each student gets one hundred free pages of printing per semester; after that, it's ten cents a page. Please save your work to your online storage account, not to the lab computers, because they erase everything every night. Food isn't allowed in here, but drinks with lids are okay.

L4505.text: This is a special weather update. Hurricane Ella is now expected to reach the coast late Thursday night. Residents of the beach communities should prepare to leave if an evacuation order is issued tomorrow. Now is the time to fill your car's gas tank, gather medicines and important papers, and plan where you'll go. Shelters will open at three local high schools, and pets are welcome at the Jefferson High shelter only.

L4506.text: Attention, shoppers. The store will be closing in fifteen minutes. Please bring your final selections to the front registers. Our garden center and the side entrance are already closed, so please exit through the main doors. If you're picking up an online order, the pickup counter near customer service will remain open until all orders are collected. We open again tomorrow at eight. Thank you, and have a good night.

L4631.text: Do you know whether the mechanics finished changing the oil in my truck, or should I come back?

L4632.text: Don't you think it's too early to plant tomatoes? We could still get a frost.

L4633.text: Would you mind showing me how to check the tire pressure before I take the van out?

L4634.text: Why don't you ever come to the base library? They have a great quiet room for studying.

L4635.text: My son's soccer team needs another coach. You played in college, didn't you?

L4636.text: This cough medicine says it may cause drowsiness. Do you think I can still drive to work?

L4637.text: I've been running every day, but I haven't lost a pound. What am I doing wrong?

L4638.text: The car makes a loud squeaking noise every time I brake. Should I be worried?

L4639.text: Do you happen to know if the language lab is open on Sundays, or only during the week?

L4640.text: How come you dropped your online college course? I thought you needed the credits.

L4641.text: Isn't it a bit risky to go hiking alone when the weather can change so fast?

L4642.text: I'm making chili for the unit potluck. Do you think it should be mild or spicy?

L4643.text: Excuse me, could you tell me whether this treadmill is reserved, or can I use it?

L4644.text: Didn't the weather service say this storm would miss us? It's pouring out there.

L4645.text: Would you rather take the written driving test first, or practice on the road a little more?

L4646.text: How long do you think we'll be out in the field this time, a week or longer?

L4647.text: I keep forgetting new vocabulary a day after I learn it. Do you have any tips?

L4648.text: Who's going to drive the water truck while Corporal Diaz is at the clinic?

L4649.text: The kitchen faucet's been dripping for days. Do you think we can fix it ourselves?

L4650.text: Is it worth paying extra for a gym with a pool, or is the base gym good enough?

L4651.text: Our team lost again. Do you think we need a new coach, or just more practice?

L4652.text: The lieutenant wants the map overlay finished tonight. Can you stay a little late to help?

L4653.text: I picked up my prescription, but the pills look different from last time. Is that normal?

L4654.text: With freezing rain coming tonight, should we park the trucks inside the hangar?

L4655.text: Would you mind proofreading my essay for the English course? It's due tomorrow morning.

L4656.text: Do you need a license to fish at the lake on post, or can anyone go?

L4657.text: The sergeant asked me to lead the next class on first aid. Any advice?

L4658.text: Whose turn is it to clean the bathroom? I did it the last two weeks.

L4659.text: Did you hear that they're going to start charging for parking at the base hospital?

L4660.text: Are you coming over to watch the game Sunday, or do you have duty?

L4772.text: I'm mailing these books to my brother in Spain. Will they get there before his birthday on the ninth?
Not by regular mail. If it has to be there by then, you'd better pay for express.

L4773.text: The babysitter just canceled, and we have dinner reservations at seven. Could your daughter watch the kids tonight?
She's got a big chemistry exam tomorrow, but let me ask. She might bring her books along.

L4774.text: The seller says the car has only forty thousand miles and has never been in an accident.
That may be true, but I wouldn't hand over a penny until a mechanic has looked at it.

L4775.text: These books were due back last Friday. Am I going to owe a fortune?
Not at all. The base library stopped charging late fees years ago. They just want the books returned.

L4776.text: I'm thinking of painting the living room dark blue this weekend.
In base housing? You'll have to paint it white again before you move out, or they'll take it out of your deposit.

L4777.text: That smoke detector has been chirping every minute since midnight.
It's just the battery running low.
Well, could you swap it out before you leave for work? I didn't sleep at all.

L4778.text: I'm taking my son fishing at the lake on Saturday. Do I need anything besides the poles?
You do if you're over sixteen. The game warden checks permits out there, and the fine isn't cheap.

L4779.text: My project partner hasn't answered a single message all week, and the presentation is Monday.
I'd let the instructor know now rather than wait. Otherwise you could both end up with the same low grade.

L4780.text: There's a charge on my card from a hotel in Miami. I haven't been to Florida in years.
Call the bank right now and have them cancel the card. Somebody must have gotten hold of your number.

L4781.text: Are you signing the twins up for swimming lessons at the base pool this summer?
I wanted to, but by the time I got through on the phone, every class was already full.

L4782.text: During my walk-through, I noticed the fire extinguisher tags on the second floor are all from last year.
Then they're past due for inspection. Put in a work order with the fire department before the inspectors catch it.

L4783.text: Last night's storm knocked the neighbor's tree onto our fence. Who's supposed to pay for that?
Usually your own insurance handles it, unless the tree was already dead and they ignored it.

L4784.text: I dropped my phone and cracked the screen. Luckily it's still under warranty.
Don't count on that. Most warranties only cover defects, not accidents.

L4785.text: My algebra class at the community college starts in two weeks. Can I still apply for tuition assistance?
Yes, but it has to be approved a week before the class begins, so don't put it off.

L4786.text: We need one more player for the Thursday night bowling league. Interested?
I'd love to, but I haven't bowled since high school. I'd probably bring the team average way down.

L4787.text: Our electric bill was almost three hundred dollars this month. That's twice what we usually pay.
Well, the air conditioner ran nonstop during that heat wave. I'm not surprised at all.

L4788.text: The visiting officers from Brazil arrive tomorrow. Do we have an interpreter lined up?
Sergeant Costa speaks Portuguese, but he's on leave until Friday. We may have to borrow someone from the language school.

L4789.text: Jake keeps asking me to teach him to drive, but every time he gets behind the wheel, I panic.
Why not sign him up for driving school? Besides, it might lower your insurance rate once he's licensed.

L4790.text: The concert sold out in ten minutes. Some guy online is selling two seats for four hundred dollars.
That's a lot more than they're worth, and half of those online sellers turn out to be scams.

L4791.text: I'm heading to the field for two weeks. Would you mind feeding my cat while I'm gone?
Not at all, but I'll be away the first weekend myself. Is there anyone who could cover those two days?

L4792.text: My car wouldn't start this morning. The engine just clicked a few times and died.
Sounds like the battery to me. It was ten below last night. I've got cables in my trunk if you want a jump.

L4793.text: The food drive was supposed to end Friday, but people keep bringing in cans.
Then let's leave the boxes in the lobby through next week. The shelter can always use more.

L4794.text: The auto shop can't take my car until next Thursday. The oil change is already five hundred miles overdue.
The hobby shop lets you do it yourself for a few dollars. I'll show you how; it takes twenty minutes.

L4795.text: Did you get your score from the reading test back? You looked worried when you came out.
I passed, but only by two points. I'll need to do much better on the listening part next month.

L4796.text: The inspector gave my room a failing grade, and I spent all night cleaning.
Did you remember the top of your wall locker? That's the first place Sergeant Diaz runs his finger.

L4797.text: The check came to eighty-four dollars. Should we split it four ways?
That hardly seems fair to Lisa. She only had a salad and water while we ordered steaks.

L4798.text: We just got orders here. How long does it take to get a toddler into the child development center?
The wait is usually about six months, so most new families use a home day-care provider until then.

L4799.text: My eyes have been itching ever since we started PT outside on the grass.
The pollen count's been sky-high all week. Ask the pharmacy for allergy drops; they don't need a prescription.

L4800.text: Why are all the recycling bins still out on the curb? Today's Tuesday.
Didn't you see the notice? Pickup moved to Wednesdays starting this month, so they'll be emptied tomorrow.

L4801.text: My physical therapist wants me doing these knee exercises three times a day, but they're so boring.
Boring or not, skip them and you'll be on crutches again. Try doing them while you watch the news.

L4802.text: I got a speeding ticket off post last night. Can I just pay it online and forget about it?
You can, but the points go on your license. Taking a defensive driving class might keep them off.

L4803.text: Ray's wedding invitation says to reply by the first. Are you going?
I'd hate to miss it, but it's the same weekend as my brother's graduation in Ohio. I'll send a gift.

L4804.text: Supply says the brake pads for our trucks are on back order until March.
March? We can't keep half the fleet off the road that long. Check whether the depot in Texas has any.

L4805.text: Tickets to the air and space museum are twenty-five dollars each. That's a hundred for the four of us.
Not with my ID. They let active-duty families in free from Memorial Day through Labor Day.

L4806.text: There are black spots on the bathroom ceiling again. I scrubbed them off just last month.
That's mold, and it'll keep coming back as long as that fan doesn't work. Call maintenance instead of scrubbing.

L4807.text: My CPR card expires next month. Do I have to take the whole eight-hour class again?
Not if you renew before it lapses. There's a short refresher course, but once it's expired, you start over.

L4808.text: I'm going to change my dollars into euros at the airport before my flight to Italy.
I wouldn't. The airport rates are terrible. You'll get a better deal just using an ATM once you land.

L4809.text: Something smells like it's burning. Did you leave the rice on the stove?
Oh no, I forgot all about it.
Well, I guess it's pizza again tonight.

L4810.text: Do we really have to show up for the graduation rehearsal at seven? I know where to stand.
The commandant made it mandatory. Last year two students who skipped it weren't allowed to march at all.

L4811.text: Somebody turned in a wallet at the front desk. There's no ID in it, just cash and a gym card.
The gym can look up whose card it is. I'll run it over there on my lunch break.

L4812.text: I just started putting three percent of my pay into the retirement plan.
Good start, but you should go to at least five. Below that, you're leaving the government's matching money on the table.

L4813.text: Emma's math homework is way over my head. They teach it so differently now.
The library on post has free tutors for kids on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. You might give that a try.

L4814.text: Do I have to clear the sidewalk in front of our quarters, or does the housing office handle that?
Residents are responsible within twenty-four hours of a snowfall. If someone slips on it, it's on you.

L4815.text: For the unit bake sale, I'm making three dozen brownies. What are you bringing?
Honestly, I can't bake to save my life. How about I run the cash box instead?

L4816.text: My browser crashed in the middle of the online quiz, and now it says I've used my only attempt.
Email the instructor a screenshot of that message right away. They usually reset it if you explain quickly.

L4817.text: I'm canceling my membership at the gym downtown. Why pay forty dollars a month when the base gym is free?
Read your contract first. A lot of those places charge a fee if you quit before the year's up.

L4818.text: I only parked in front of the PX for two minutes, and I came out to a ticket.
Was it the red curb by the entrance? That's a fire lane. Two minutes or two hours, it's the same fine.

L4819.text: I ordered contacts online using my old prescription, but the website won't accept it.
Contact prescriptions usually expire after a year. You'll need a new eye exam before anyone will sell you lenses.

L4820.text: This pallet weighs in at ten thousand two hundred pounds. Can we load it as is?
The limit for that position is ten thousand. Pull off a couple of the water cans and weigh it again.

L4821.text: I tried to book a table at Marco's for our anniversary on Saturday, but they're full.
What if we went Friday instead? I'm off that afternoon anyway, and it'd be less crowded.

L4822.text: Any chance you could help me move a couch on Saturday morning? It won't take long.
I've heard that before. Last time 'it won't take long' turned into six hours and three trips across town.

L4823.text: I'm visiting my parents in Poland next month. Will my phone work over there?
It'll work, but roaming charges can be brutal. Buying a local SIM card at the airport is usually much cheaper.

L4824.text: It's pouring. Are we still practicing with the colors on the parade field this afternoon?
We'll move into the gym. The flags can't get soaked, but the ceremony's Monday, so we can't skip practice either.

L4825.text: I was only at the beach for an hour, and look at my shoulders. They're bright red.
The sun's strongest around noon, even when it's cloudy. Next time, put on sunscreen before you leave the house.

L4826.text: This TV is three hundred dollars cheaper at the store across town.
Bring up their ad on your phone. We match any local competitor's price.
Great, that saves me a trip.

L4827.text: The pilots want to know if they can fly to the range this afternoon.
Visibility's fine now, but a line of storms is due by fifteen hundred. If they're going, they'd better leave before lunch.

L4828.text: The dealer offered me a loan at nine percent. That's not bad, is it?
My credit union gave me under six on mine. Get a quote from them before you sign anything.

L4829.text: The youth soccer league is desperate for coaches. Have you ever thought about it?
I'd be happy to help out at practices, but with my deployment in the spring, I can't commit to the whole season.

L4830.text: Derek asked to borrow two hundred dollars again. He still owes me from last time.
Then I'd tell him he can have it as soon as he pays back the first loan.

L4831.text: A one-day lift ticket at the resort is a hundred and twenty dollars. That's crazy.
Check with the recreation office on base. They sell discount tickets, sometimes for half price.

L4832.text: I was planning to hike Eagle Ridge on Sunday, but the trailhead's blocked off with a sign.
Because of fire danger, I bet. It hasn't rained in six weeks. They usually close the high trails until the fall.

L4833.text: For three days now, the shower water hasn't gotten more than lukewarm.
The water heater's probably on its last legs. It's fifteen years old. I'll get a plumber out here this week.

L4834.text: The tracking says my package was delivered at two, but there's nothing on my porch.
Did you check with the Hendersons? The driver always mixes up our houses.
Oh, right. Their numbers fell off last winter.

L4835.text: I've been studying Spanish for a year, but I freeze up whenever I actually have to talk to someone.
Books only get you so far. The education center has conversation groups on Wednesday evenings.

L4836.text: There's a little boy crying by the shoe section. He says he can't find his mom.
Stay with him, and I'll have the front desk make an announcement. Don't take him anywhere.

L4837.text: Gas is almost forty cents a gallon cheaper across the state line. Should we fill up there?
It's a thirty-mile drive each way. Whatever we'd save, we'd burn getting there.

L4838.text: Have you finished the project management course your supervisor recommended?
I finished every module yesterday, but the certificate still won't print. I've emailed the help desk twice.

L4839.text: Are families allowed at the dining facility for the Thanksgiving meal?
They are, but there's a small charge for guests. And get there early; last year the line went out the door.

L4840.text: We're collecting money for Ms. Park's farewell lunch. Everyone's putting in ten dollars.
I'm a little short until payday. Can I give you mine Friday?
Sure, as long as it's before the lunch on Monday.

L4841.text: The tire shop says there's a nail in my rear tire. They want to sell me a whole new set.
If it's in the tread, a patch usually costs about twenty dollars. Don't let them talk you into more.

L4842.text: I got a flat on my bike halfway to work and had to push it the last two miles.
So that's why you missed the eight o'clock meeting. The boss was asking where you were.

L4843.text: Our street is having a holiday lights contest. Should we put something up this year?
Sure, as long as it doesn't involve me on a ladder. Remember what happened to my wrist last December?

L4844.text: Private Lewis just bought a brand-new sports car. He's been in the Army four months.
At twenty-two percent interest, I'll bet. Someone should sit him down and go over a budget with him.

L4845.text: We're having a yard sale before we move. Do we need permission from housing?
Yes, they only allow them on the first Saturday of the month, and you have to register by Wednesday.

L4846.text: The hurricane's supposed to hit the coast Thursday night. Should we start stocking up?
I'd go today. By Wednesday the shelves will be empty of water and batteries.

L4847.text: I picked up my dress uniform from the cleaners, and two of the buttons are missing.
Take it back. They're supposed to replace anything they lose, and the ball is next Saturday.

L4848.text: Want to play tennis after work? I can reserve a court.
I'd better not. I've got a ton of laundry, and I haven't been grocery shopping in two weeks.

L4849.text: There's hydraulic fluid dripping under the left wing. Can the crew still make the ten o'clock launch?
Not until we find the leak and run a pressure check. Tell them to plan on noon at the earliest.

L4850.text: I gave up coffee on Monday, and I've had a pounding headache ever since.
That's normal when you quit cold turkey. Cutting back a little each day is usually easier.

L4851.text: The lamp I ordered online arrived in pieces. The box looked like someone had sat on it.
Take pictures of everything, the box too, before you throw anything out. They'll want proof for a refund.

L4852.text: The sign on the bridge says twenty tons. Our loaded truck is close to twenty-five.
Then we're not crossing here. Get on the radio and find out if the north route is open.

L4853.text: Our car insurance went up eighty dollars a month, and neither of us has had a ticket.
Rates went up for everyone in this state. Still, it wouldn't hurt to call around for other quotes.

L4854.text: Excuse me, I asked for a small coffee with milk, but this one's black and it's a large.
I'm so sorry. I'll make you a new one right away, and you can keep that one at no charge.

L4855.text: I need somewhere quiet to study for the language exam. The barracks are way too noisy.
The library has private study rooms, but you have to reserve one a day ahead.

L4856.text: The garage door's stuck halfway, and my car's inside. I've got to be at work in twenty minutes.
Take mine. I don't need it until this afternoon.
Thanks. I'll call someone about the door at lunch.

L4857.text: One of the international students in my class hardly says a word. I think he's homesick.
The school has a sponsor program. Local families invite students over for weekend dinners. I'll get you the number.

L4858.text: I listed the old dresser online for a hundred dollars, and a woman offered sixty.
We're moving in five days, and the movers won't take it anyway. I'd grab the sixty.

L4859.text: The blood drive is in the gym tomorrow. Are you giving this time?
They won't take me yet. I just got back from a country with malaria, and there's a three-month waiting period.

L4860.text: My brother got us tickets for the Army-Navy game, but they're in the very top row.
Who cares where we sit? I've wanted to see that game in person since I was a kid.

L4861.text: This cake recipe calls for buttermilk, and the commissary is closed. Got any ideas?
Just stir a spoonful of lemon juice into regular milk and let it sit for a few minutes. It works every time.

L4862.text: The parent-teacher conference is Tuesday at three, and I've got staff duty that day.
Ask if they'll do it over the phone. Mrs. Grant did that for us last year when you were in the field.

L4863.text: We finally paid off the credit card. Now we can start saving for a trip to Hawaii.
Let's build up an emergency fund first. If the car broke down tomorrow, we'd be right back in debt.

L4864.text: The taco truck's line goes all the way around the building.
And we only have half an hour for lunch. The sandwich place across the street never has more than two people waiting.
Fair enough. Tacos can wait until Friday.

L4865.text: I used the last of the bandages from the vehicle first aid kit at the range today.
Then restock it before you turn in the truck. The next driver won't know it's empty until it's too late.

L4866.text: The kids want to go to the zoo tomorrow, but it's supposed to be ninety-eight degrees.
Then let's get there when it opens at nine. Most of the animals hide in the shade by noon anyway.

L5000.text: My promotion board is next Thursday. I'm more nervous about the questions than my uniform.
Sergeant Diaz runs mock boards on Tuesday afternoons for anyone who asks. Just e-mail him by Friday.
I had no idea. I'll write to him today.

L5001.text: Weren't you supposed to be off at five? It's almost seven.
The armorer wouldn't take our rifles back. He found carbon in nearly every bolt, so the whole squad had to clean them again.
That's rough. Didn't your team leader check them first?

L5002.text: I'm sponsoring a new soldier from Korea. His flight lands at eleven forty Sunday night, after the shuttle to post stops running.
Then you're making a late-night airport run. And call the barracks manager so his room key is ready.
Good point. I don't want him sleeping on my couch.

L5003.text: Sergeant Okafor wants me on the color guard for the Veterans Day ceremony. Practice is at six every morning next week.
Every morning? Doesn't your college class start at seven?
It's online now, so that's fine. The real problem is that I've never carried a flag in my life.

L5004.text: I missed the passing score on the English test by three points again. Listening kills me, and I only read grammar books at night.
That's your problem. You need to train your ears, not your eyes. Try the language lab after duty.

L5005.text: The doctor gave me a temporary profile for my knee. No running or jumping for thirty days.
So you can skip morning PT?
Not exactly. I still have to show up and ride the stationary bike or swim while everyone else runs.

L5006.text: The commander wants an award for Specialist Chen before she leaves at the end of the month. When does the write-up need to be done?
The paperwork takes about three weeks to get signed. So yesterday would have been nice.

L5007.text: How was CQ last night? I heard your building's fire alarm went off.
At two a.m. Someone burned popcorn, and we all stood in the parking lot. Starting tonight, microwaves are only allowed in the day room.
Wow. That sounds like a long night.

L5008.text: My reenlistment window closes in March. The bonus is tempting, but I've always wanted to finish my degree full-time.
Could you do both? My husband reenlisted for a training job with regular hours and finished his degree at night.
I never thought of that. I'll ask the career counselor.

L5009.text: My husband deploys in two weeks, and they said packages can take a month to reach him. Is that true?
Sometimes. When I was overseas, letters took about ten days, but boxes took a lot longer.
Then I'd better mail his birthday present now, even though his birthday isn't until December.

L5010.text: This security clearance form wants every address since high school, and I've moved eight times. I threw out most of my old leases.
Ask your parents or check your old e-mails, but don't guess. A wrong address can drag the investigation out for months.
Right. I'll call my parents tonight.

L5011.text: Are they canceling tonight's jump? The wind is really picking up.
Not officially, but gusts are over twenty knots. The jumpmaster makes the final call at eighteen hundred. If not, we'll try Saturday morning.
So we might wait in the hangar for nothing.

L5012.text: I missed qualifying on the rifle range by two targets. I was hitting everything in practice!
Didn't they just replace your rifle? Every weapon has to be zeroed for its shooter. Talk to the range NCO.
Yes, on Monday. I went straight out to the range and never checked it.

L5013.text: Officers from Senegal visit Monday and Tuesday, and their interpreter just canceled. Does anyone here speak French?
Lieutenant Moreau grew up in Quebec, and her leave starts Wednesday. But her section chief won't release her without a written request.
Good. I'll have it on his desk this afternoon.

L5014.text: For the after-action review, what do you think went wrong yesterday?
The plan was fine. Second platoon never heard we moved the meeting point. Their sergeant was out, and nobody passed it on.
I did send it to their sergeant. Next time I'll send changes to two people.

L5015.text: The holiday meal at the other dining facility ends at three, but some of my soldiers are on guard until four.
Send me their names, and I'll have the cooks set plates aside for them.
Perfect. I'll send the list today.

L5016.text: Anything I should know before you head out? I heard the Charlie Company patrol was late.
