Yes, their radio battery died, so they called from a gas station. The duty officer wants a short report by morning, and you'll send it.
Got it. I'll write it up.

L5017.text: Are you ready for Friday's twelve-mile road march?
I hope so. My old boots have a hole, so I bought new ones and I'm wearing them.
Don't. I did that once, and by mile six my feet were bleeding. Break them in first.

L5018.text: Have you seen the forecast for tomorrow? A hundred and five by early afternoon.
Yes. The commander moved the obstacle course from one o'clock to seven in the morning, and the medics will be standing by.
Good. Last summer, two soldiers ended up at the clinic with heat exhaustion.

L5019.text: We still need someone to run the grill at organization day. Your volleyball tournament doesn't start until after lunch, does it?
True. I'll cook from eleven to one, but somebody else has to clean up. I can't be scrubbing grills at game time.
Deal. I'll find someone for that.

L5020.text: I typed my PIN wrong too many times, and my ID card is locked. Can I just walk in?
You can, but expect a two-hour wait. Book an appointment online from a coworker's computer, and you'll be in and out in ten minutes.

L5021.text: Every night. My new roommate snores like a chainsaw, and earplugs don't help. He says he'll see a doctor, but that could take weeks.
Then ask the barracks manager about an empty room. You can't do your job on two hours of sleep.

L5022.text: I got into the January leadership course, but there's a lot of writing, and I haven't written more than an e-mail in years.
The education center has a free workshop on Wednesday nights. The instructor will look over your drafts.
That's perfect. I'll sign up this week.

L5023.text: I can't find my ID card. The commissary checked the self-checkout and didn't find it, so maybe it fell out in the parking lot.
Then report it to your unit today, before you go for a new one. The ID office will want a statement saying it's lost.

L5024.text: They wouldn't let me give blood at the drive in the gym today. My iron was too low.
No surprise. You skip breakfast every day and hardly eat any meat.
That's what the nurse said. She told me to eat more beans and spinach and come back in a few weeks.

L5025.text: Are you still driving to your sister's for the long weekend?
I'm taking the train, because holiday traffic is a nightmare. It costs a little more, but with no parking fees it's about even.
Smart. You can even get some work done on the way.

L5026.text: Hi, I have a reservation under Kowalski for three nights, starting tonight.
I see it, but it's for next month. We're nearly full with the conference, but I can give you a suite for the regular price.
Next month? I must have clicked the wrong month. A suite would be great.

L5027.text: Let's take the mountain road to Colorado instead of the interstate. It adds three hours, so we should stay overnight by the lake.
I like that. We'd get there a day later, though, so I'll have to ask for another day of leave.

L5028.text: I'm hoping to catch a space-available military flight to Germany for my leave. Have you ever done that?
Twice. It's cheap, but don't count on it. Last time I waited three days and never got a seat.
Wow. Maybe I should buy a backup ticket.

L5029.text: Your suitcase is fifty-eight pounds, sir. Our limit is fifty, so there's a fee for the extra weight.
Can I just move some things, like my boots, into my backpack instead?
Sure, if it fits under the seat. Step aside and repack.

L5030.text: I got back from Korea yesterday, and I was wide awake at three this morning. I'd napped for four hours after I got home.
That nap is what keeps you on Korean time. Stay up until at least nine tonight and get outside in the sunlight.

L5031.text: The branches from the Hendersons' oak are hanging right over our garage roof.
I know. One good storm and we'll have a hole in the roof. I was going to rent a saw and cut them myself.
Talk to Mr. Henderson first. It's his tree, and he might pay to have it trimmed.

L5032.text: The power's been out since six. How long will the food in the freezer last?
Probably a day, if we keep the door shut. Every time you open it, the cold gets out. The power should be back by midnight.
Okay, I'll stop checking on it.

L5033.text: Our final housing inspection is on the twentieth, and the movers come on the eighteenth. Should we clean it ourselves or hire a company?
Hire one. It costs more, but if they miss anything, they come back for free.
Good point. I'll book them today.

L5034.text: Why is our trash still at the curb? It's Tuesday afternoon.
Didn't you see the notice? Because of Monday's holiday, everything is pushed back a day this week.
So it's tomorrow? Great, and now the raccoons have been through it.

L5035.text: The internet technician is coming Friday between eight and noon, and I'm taking Grandma to her eye appointment at ten.
I have a briefing at nine I can't miss. Let me see if I can move it to the afternoon.
Please try. Your mother wouldn't know what to tell the technician.

L5036.text: We move in five weeks, and the garage is still full. Let's have a yard sale. Not my weight bench, though.
Especially your weight bench. You haven't touched it since we moved here. Whatever doesn't sell goes to the thrift shop.
All right, all right. It goes in the sale.

L5037.text: I found mouse droppings in the garage again, right next to the dog food.
I set two traps last week, but they haven't caught anything.
Traps won't help if they keep getting in. There's a gap under the side door you could fit your hand through.

L5038.text: My hearing test shows some loss in my left ear. Last month on the machine gun range, I lost an earplug and kept firing.
That's how it starts. Get earplugs on a cord, so you can't drop them.
Good idea. I'll order some today.

L5039.text: The school won't let Ava start Monday without her shot records. I'm not opening thirty moving boxes to find them.
The clinic on post should have them in the computer. I'll stop by and get a printout on my way home.
Perfect. That's much easier than calling her old doctor.

L5040.text: I've saved three thousand dollars, enough for a down payment on a new car.
Don't you still owe money on your credit card? I'd pay that off first. The car can wait.
I owe about two thousand, and I only make the minimum payment. You may be right.

L5041.text: Are you paying someone to do your taxes this year? The tax center on post does them for free.
Really? The place downtown wanted two hundred dollars. Do I need an appointment?
No, they take walk-ins, but go soon. By April, the line goes out the door.

L5042.text: I just got a text from my bank saying my account's frozen. It wants me to click a link and enter my password.
Don't touch it. Banks never ask for passwords by text. Call the number on the back of your card instead.
Good idea. I'll report it while I'm at it.

L5043.text: Did Marcus ever pay you back the four hundred dollars? Are you going to say something to him?
Not yet. He keeps saying next payday. I don't want to ruin a ten-year friendship over money, but I won't lend him anything again.

L5044.text: Our car insurance went up two hundred dollars, and we haven't had a single accident. I just renew it every year.
Get quotes from other companies, and ask about putting your car and renter's insurance together. My sister saved a lot that way.
Maybe I'll do that this weekend.

L5045.text: I signed up for an online business class that starts Monday. Can I still get tuition assistance?
Did the education office approve it before you registered?
No. I didn't know that was required.

L5046.text: The study rooms are all booked until Friday. Could my group use the third floor tables tonight, or is that still the silent floor?
It's quiet during the day, but after eight it's open study, so you can talk.

L5047.text: How's your English listening coming along?
Better. I play news podcasts on my way to work, but the speakers talk so fast. I catch maybe half.
Slow them down in the app at first, then speed them up a little each week until they sound normal.

L5048.text: My application essay should be five hundred words, and mine's almost eight hundred. But I like all of it, especially the part about my grandfather.
Keep that part; it's the most personal. But the committee won't care about your two paragraphs on high school sports.

L5049.text: Tonight's accounting class is canceled because the instructor's car broke down. She'll make up both sessions Saturday morning, nine to one.
Again? I have duty Saturday until ten, so I'll show up late and borrow somebody's notes for the first hour.
Good plan. I can lend you mine.

L5050.text: I want to rent a kayak from outdoor recreation this weekend. Have you done it?
Yes. They won't give you a paddle until you take their safety class. Bring a towel, because you'll probably tip over in the practice.
Good to know. I'll take the class this Saturday.

L5051.text: Half the people from Saturday's potluck have been sick since Sunday. Did you feel all right?
I'm fine, but I didn't touch the chicken salad with the mayonnaise. It sat out in the sun for hours.
That's what everybody blames. I had some. Next time let's keep it in a cooler.

L5052.text: Two tickets for the seven o'clock show, please.
Sorry, sir, that show just sold out. The next one is at nine forty-five.
That's too late for us. Our babysitter can only stay until ten.

L5053.text: I signed us up for that cooking class at the community center. It's every Tuesday in March.
Every Tuesday? I thought it was a one-night thing. And I've got a night shift the second Tuesday.
It's four sessions, starting with knife skills. I'll ask the instructor if you can make one up.

L5054.text: Are you running the charity ten K on Saturday? It's really about raising money for the children's hospital, not a race.
That helps. I barely trained, so I was worried about my time. Now I'll just ask my coworkers for donations.
Perfect. Lots of people walk half of it anyway.

L5101.text: Hello, this is the base veterinary clinic calling for Sergeant Miller about your move to Germany. Your dog's rabies shot is still current, but the microchip we found is an older type that may not be readable overseas, so we recommend putting in a new one before your health certificate appointment. That appointment has to be close to your departure date, so please call us back to schedule both visits. We're open weekdays from eight to four, but we close for lunch from noon to one.

L5102.text: Jumpers, listen up. Ground winds at the drop zone are gusting to eighteen knots, which is above our limit, so this morning's jump is on weather hold. Stay in the hangar, keep your equipment together, and don't leave the building without telling your team leader. We'll check the winds again at ten thirty. If they haven't calmed down by noon, the jump will be canceled and moved to Thursday morning, with the same aircraft and the same jump order.

L5103.text: Hi, this is Coach Linda from the Tigers youth soccer team. Because of all the rain this week, the fields at the youth center are closed, so Saturday's game against the Hawks has been moved to the high school field on Elm Street. The start time is the same, nine a.m., but please have your kids there by eight thirty to warm up. Also, it's our turn to bring snacks, so if you signed up for this week, remember to bring enough for both teams. See you Saturday.

L5104.text: Good morning, crew. We'll be tied up in port from tomorrow at zero eight hundred until Sunday evening. Liberty begins once the ship has been cleared, probably around noon. Everyone going ashore must travel with at least one buddy and carry a liberty card. Liberty for junior sailors ends at midnight, and anyone who comes back late will lose liberty for the rest of the visit. The old market downtown is well worth seeing, but watch your wallets, because pickpockets work the crowds there.

L5105.text: Good afternoon, passengers waiting for the three fifteen ferry to Pine Island. Because of high winds and rough water in the channel, this crossing is delayed by at least one hour. Passengers with cars should stay in their lanes, but you may leave your vehicles briefly to use the restrooms and the snack bar in the terminal. If the crossing is canceled, your tickets will be good on any ferry tomorrow, and refunds are also available at the ticket window.

L5106.text: All right, operators, winter is coming early this year, so this week we're getting every vehicle ready for the cold. Check the antifreeze first; the mechanics will test it and top it off if needed. Next, make sure every truck has a working heater and an ice scraper. Tire chains will be issued next Monday, not this week, because supply is still waiting on the order. Finally, batteries lose power in the cold, so start each vehicle at least once every three days, even if it isn't being used.

L5107.text: Welcome to the language learning center. Before you start, here's how things work. The listening booths on the left are for headphone practice only, so please keep your voices down there. If you'd like to practice speaking, reserve one of the conversation rooms at the front desk; you can book up to two hours a week. Our tutors are available Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and no appointment is needed. Food and drinks are allowed only in the lounge, and please log out of the computers before you leave.

L5108.text: All vehicles, this is Convoy Commander. Truck four has a flat tire and has pulled onto the shoulder about two miles back. The recovery team is already with them, and they expect to be moving again in about twenty minutes. We will not wait here on the highway. Continue to the next rest area at mile marker eighty-six, park in the truck lot, and stay with your vehicles. Use the time to check your own tires and fluids. We'll leave together once truck four catches up. Over.

L5109.text: Attention, athletes. Sign-ups for the winter intramural basketball league are open now through November tenth at the main gym's front desk. Each unit may enter one team of up to twelve players, and all players must be assigned to that unit. Games will be played on Tuesday and Wednesday nights, beginning in December. A coaches' meeting will be held on November fifteenth, and every team must send at least one representative, or it will lose its place in the league. Team shirts will be provided by the gym.

L5110.text: Welcome to the auto skills center. You can work on your own car here, but there are a few rules. Every customer must watch a short safety video the first time, and you'll need to show your ID to check out tools. The lifts may only be used after an employee has trained you on them. Used oil goes in the tanks behind the building; never pour it down the drains. Bays can be reserved for up to four hours at a time, and we close at seven, so plan your work accordingly.

L5111.text: Hello, families. Registration for summer day camp at the youth center opens Monday, March third, at seven a.m. Spaces fill quickly, so we suggest signing up online rather than waiting in line at the center. Before your child can register, his or her sports physical and shot records must be up to date in our system. Camp runs Monday through Friday for ten weeks, and you may choose individual weeks. Children of deploying parents may register one week early, starting February twenty-fourth.

L5112.text: Good morning, and welcome to forklift operator training. This course lasts three days. Today you'll be in the classroom, learning the controls and the safety rules. Tomorrow we move to the warehouse, where you'll practice lifting empty pallets. On the last day, you'll take a written test in the morning and a driving test in the afternoon, and you must pass both to get your license. Steel-toed boots are required on days two and three, so if you don't have a pair, let me know before lunch today.

L5113.text: Hi, Mr. Brooks, this is Diane from Oak Ridge Apartments. Your lease ends on June thirtieth, and we'd love to have you stay. If you renew for another year, your rent will go up by only twenty-five dollars, and we'll replace the carpet in your bedroom at no cost. If you'd rather move out, we need written notice at least sixty days before the lease ends. Since you mentioned you might get orders this summer, I can also add a military clause to the lease. Please call me back by Friday.

L5114.text: Welcome to Crystal Cavern. Before we head down, a few things you should know. The tour lasts about ninety minutes and includes more than three hundred steps, so if you have heart or knee problems, you may want to take our shorter tour instead. The temperature inside stays around fifty-five degrees all year, so you'll want a jacket. Please don't touch the rock formations, because oils from your skin can stop them from growing. Photos are fine, but no flash, since it disturbs the bats.

L5115.text: Soldiers who are leaving the installation, here's what you need to know about turning in your field gear. Appointments at the central issue facility are required and can be made online up to two weeks ahead. All items must be clean and dry; anything that's dirty will be refused, and you'll have to come back another day. If something is missing or damaged, you can either replace it with an identical item or pay for it at the finance office. Bring your hand receipt and a copy of your orders.

L7201.text: Mr. Delgado, could I come by on Wednesday at two to talk about my essay?
I'm teaching then. Would Thursday at a quarter to three suit you? My last class ends at two thirty.
Yes, that's fine. I'll be at your office then.

L7202.text: Sergeant Hale, I'm sorry, but my report isn't ready. I spent all of Monday at the clinic with a fever.
I see. Did you bring a note from the doctor?
Yes, here it is. Could I have until Friday to finish the report?

L7203.text: My laptop crashed this morning, and the help desk says the hard drive is dead.
Oh no. Did you lose the training schedule you were working on?
Luckily, no. I'd saved a copy on the shared drive last night, so I only lost some old photos.

L7204.text: Corporal Tran, I need your signature here to show that you got your moving allowance.
I'd rather wait. I haven't checked my bank account yet, so I'm not sure the money has arrived.
All right. Look online tonight and come back tomorrow.

L7205.text: Should we drive all the way to the stadium for Saturday's game?
Parking there costs thirty dollars. Let's take my car to the train station and ride the train from there.
Good idea. The stadium is right next to the last stop anyway.

L7206.text: The internet in my room has been down since lunch. Should I call the help desk?
Before you do that, make sure all the cables on the back of the router are plugged in tightly.
Good point. My roommate moved the desk yesterday.

L7207.text: Can I leave my car here while I'm at the dental clinic? My appointment could take three hours.
The sign says there's a two-hour limit, and the military police check often.
Then I'd better use the big lot behind the PX instead.

L7208.text: Are you going to sign up for the evening Spanish class on base?
I'd rather take the online version. My shifts change every week, and I want to study whenever I'm free.
That makes sense. You can go at your own pace that way.

L7209.text: Have you seen the new sunglasses I bought on Saturday? I left them on the coffee table.
Sorry, Mom. My friend Kevin borrowed them for our beach trip, and he dropped them in the ocean.
Well, he'd better buy me another pair.

L7210.text: My daughter wants to join the rugby team instead of the soccer team this fall.
Just so you know, rugby players get hurt a lot more often than soccer players do. My nephew broke his collarbone.
Hmm. I'll talk to her coach about safety first.

L7401.text: Don't go by the clock over the orderly room door; it gains a few minutes every week.

L7402.text: Corporal Baines found a hole in the fuel line no bigger than a pinhead, but it was enough to cause the leak.

L7403.text: Is Lieutenant Okafor still in her office? I need her signature on this leave request.
Hurry, then. She's about to head out to the airfield for the rest of the day.

L7404.text: Do I need to pack my poncho for the hike this afternoon?
Leave it here. The forecast says sunny and dry all day, though it'll be pretty windy up on the ridge.

L7405.text: Would you put in for an assignment on the Gulf Coast?
No way. I can't stand humid weather, even if the beaches are beautiful.

L7406.text: The big gray dog that sleeps by the motor pool gate looks fierce, but it's completely harmless.

L7407.text: Nobody can rent a kayak at the base marina without first showing identification to the attendant.

L7408.text: Major Lindqvist trusts the evening news on Channel Four because its reporting is completely objective.

L6016.text: Each evening this week has been a few degrees colder than the one before, and the first frost is expected soon.

L6017.text: Every Sunday, Specialist Ortega makes a long-distance call from the day room to her grandmother, and they talk for an hour.

L6018.text: Corpsman Dalton explained that the kidney is an organ that cleans the blood and removes extra water from the body.

Not yet. He asked me to come back around three o'clock.

The cold snap last weekend finished them off.

L6063.text: The leaves by the window are drooping, and the soil in the pot looks cracked and dry.

Oh, thank you! I'll go turn them off before the battery dies.

A new landfill, I heard. The garbage trucks will start using it next spring.

L6083.text: The old switch on my desk lamp finally broke, so I'm stopping at the hardware store for a new one tonight.

L6084.text: The camp's portable heaters burn kerosene, so Sergeant Kline drove into town for two more cans before the cold front arrived.

L6085.text: My grandfather and his old army buddy have corresponded for forty years, and they have never missed a month.

L6090.text: The pharmacy is right around the corner from the clinic, so it only takes a minute to walk there.

No problem. The one across the street should have it, and it's open late.

Perfectly? They're far too small. My toes can't even move.

I'll sign up if you do it, too.

Its capacity. We need to keep drinks cold for about sixty people.

My field is meteorology, ma'am. My office is in the little tower by the runway.

It was canceled, so I'm checking out this morning and flying home.

L6131.text: Isn't this a wonderful old ballad?
The tune is, but I don't care for the way the orchestra plays it. It's too fast.

I felt the same. The story simply stops in the middle of the action.

L6251.text: The upper deck of the ferry was closed because of the wind, so we found seats on the lower deck near the engines.

L6252.text: Ever since their argument over the schedule, Specialist Ortiz has been avoiding Sergeant Hall by using the back stairs.

L6253.text: We regret that your luggage was lost on the connecting flight, and we will deliver it to your hotel when it's found.

L6254.text: We can't put off the generator repair any longer; the next storm could cut the power for days.

L6255.text: Captain Moss strolled to the coffee machine and took a clean mug down from the shelf.

L6256.text: Why did the military police put a barricade across the road near the flooded hangar?

Eleven hours with only two stops. I can barely keep my eyes open.

Yes, I booked a seat on the ferry. It leaves the port at six in the morning.

Please set out the forks, knives and spoons next to each plate.

L6261.text: Is the bug spray the quartermaster gave us any good?
It's remarkably effective. I haven't seen a single mosquito all week.

Of course. Take your time; I'm in no hurry.

L6263.text: The radio in the office won't turn on at all. Did somebody drop it?
No, the fuse blew when the storm knocked out the power.

L6264.text: Is the present for your niece ready to go in the mail?
Almost. I'm still wrapping it, and then I'll write the address.

No problem. I'll keep my voice down too.

If you want everyone to go quiet. He's such a wet blanket.

L6268.text: Sergeant Okoro is going to bake several loaves of bread in his own kitchen for Friday's retirement party.

I wish it were noon already; I skipped breakfast this morning.

Not a chance. Hand me your flashlight, would you?

L6925.text: Would you like a glass of lemonade?
Yes, please, with plenty of ice; it's ninety degrees out there.

L6926.text: Should we eat at the Italian place or the Mexican one tonight?
Either is fine with me; it's your call.

L6927.text: Could you pass this message on to the duty sergeant when he comes in?
Sure, I'll make sure he gets it first thing.

L6928.text: Are you ready to start, Lieutenant?
Almost. Let me just put my notes on the podium and test the sound system.

L6929.text: Which way does the trail go from here?
Give me a second; I'm still checking the compass on my watch.

L6930.text: I've been looking all morning for a report on winter driving safety.
There's one in the safety office binder on the second shelf.

L6931.text: Where should we pitch the tents tonight?
That flat spot by the river looks good, away from the wind.

L6932.text: Good morning, travelers: for the next fifteen minutes only, every sandwich at the snack bar comes with a free drink.

L7083.text: Corporal Vance has to renew his driver's license by Friday; otherwise he won't be allowed to drive any unit vehicles.

L7086.text: My brother caught a serious illness while he was stationed overseas, and the doctors kept him in the hospital for a month.

L7097.text: Our barracks are right next to the dining facility, the gym and the laundry, so living here is very convenient.

L7099.text: While cleaning out the old shed, Specialist Hoyt stepped on a rusty nail and had to get a tetanus shot at the clinic.

L7100.text: Nobody had looked at the results, because the envelope on the commander's desk was still sealed.

L7105.text: Please accept this small plant as a token of our thanks for all the extra hours you worked on the project.

L7106.text: The road crew worked from sunrise until sunset all week, and by Friday they were completely worn out.

L7107.text: Airman Hale is a conscientious clerk: he double-checks every report and never leaves a task half finished.

L7108.text: Sorry, Sergeant, I blew it at the checkpoint this morning; I forgot my ID card and held up the whole line.

L7110.text: The two visitors who were held at the gate will be released as soon as the guards finish checking their papers.

L7111.text: When the toddler pulled its tail, the puppy bit his hand, though it barely left a mark.

L7113.text: Our neighbor talks to his lawn mower and waters the sidewalk every night; I'm afraid he has a screw loose.

L7114.text: The two squadrons argued for weeks about the shared parking lot, but a meeting with the housing office helped them negotiate their differences.

L7115.text: After a twenty-minute nap in the shade, Corporal Pike woke up feeling refreshed and ready for the afternoon drills.

L7116.text: Don't try to cross the creek on foot; the current is very swift after last night's rain.

L7117.text: Frequent phone calls during the lesson were a real detriment to the training, so the instructor banned phones.

L7118.text: After the flood relief mission, the medics had to replenish their stock of bandages before the next call.

L7119.text: Ms. Dunham, a civilian, manages the new fitness center on base, so she decides its hours and hires its staff.

L7120.text: The commissary sold out of brisket before noon, so Sergeant Ruiz had to change the main dish for Saturday's cookout.

L7121.text: The mechanic extended the tow cable by another ten feet so it could reach the truck stuck in the ditch.

L7122.text: Ferry service to the island has been suspended until the storm passes, so the supply boats will wait in port.

L7123.text: Attention, please: the driver of the white van parked by the fuel depot must move it immediately, because this is a restricted area.

L7124.text: The family next door has three boys, so on Saturdays you can hear a soccer ball hitting their garage door all afternoon.

L7125.text: Flying is my husband's job, not his hobby; for fun he builds tiny ship models at the kitchen table.

L7126.text: I don't need a laptop myself, Specialist, but my brother might be interested in yours if the price is right.

L7127.text: I can't stay out late tonight, because my roommate Tessa has an early shift and she is a very light sleeper.

L7128.text: Excuse me, ma'am, which way is the records office? I've already walked up and down this hallway twice.

L7129.text: I spent all morning looking for the maintenance manual for our generator, and finally found it under a pile of old maps.

L7130.text: These peaches are wonderfully sweet, and they're half price today, so I think I'll pick up another bag.

L7131.text: Our helicopter had to fly low the whole way because of heavy clouds, so we never saw the mountains.

L7132.text: Some people laughed when Sergeant Hobbs sold his sports car for his daughter's tuition, but I think that was sensible.

L7211.text: Will your son be in the school band again this fall, Sergeant Ruiz?
Yes, but he wants a change. Last year he kept the beat from the back row, and now he'd like to learn the trumpet.
That's quite a switch. Brass instruments demand a lot of breath control.

L7212.text: The youth swim program costs a hundred and forty dollars for the whole season.
That's more than I planned to spend. Is there any help for military families?
If your spouse is deployed, the recreation office may cover the entire fee. Just bring a copy of the orders.

L7213.text: Did you see the notice about the new pool schedule that starts next month?
I did. Weekdays stay the same, but Sundays will run from noon to four instead of from eight to six.
That's a shame. I always swim at eight, right when the doors open.

L7214.text: Starting Monday, the snack bar near the flight line will stay open until ten at night.
That's three hours later than it closes now, isn't it?
Yes, and the crews on the late shift have asked for that for a long time.

L7215.text: Does the movie theater on post stay open late?
Not really. Sunday through Thursday it closes at nine, but on Fridays the last show ends at midnight, and on Saturdays at eleven.
I'll probably go on Saturday, since I work early on Fridays.

L7216.text: Instructors can borrow as many books as they like, but students are limited to eight at a time.
I'm a student, but my instructor asked me to get books for the whole class.
Then bring his card with a signed note, and I can scan them under his name.

L7217.text: I'd like to borrow the orbital sander from the self-help center to refinish my table.
Sure. Hand tools can go home for two weeks, but power tools are only lent for the weekend.
That's fine. I only need it on Saturday afternoon.

L7218.text: Is the education center open on weekends? I need to prepare for a certification exam.
On weekdays it closes at ten, but on Saturdays it opens at one in the afternoon and stays open until midnight.
Perfect. I'll go right after my morning shift.

L7219.text: Sergeant, the supply room doesn't have my size in the new cold-weather boots.
Fill out a request slip at the counter. The depot in the next state ships what we're missing, usually within a week.
Good, I'll do it now. I can wait a week.

L7220.text: Do you want to reserve the quiet room for this afternoon, Corporal?
Yes. I have to rehearse my farewell speech out loud, and I don't want an audience yet.
Understood. I'll put you down from two to four.

L7221.text: The director just told us to sit down with any student who has missed more than three classes.
I know. He wants us to find out what's wrong and give advice before it becomes a bigger problem.
Fine, but I'll need extra time in my schedule for those meetings.

L7222.text: Colonel Hirsch looked worried at the staff meeting. What was bothering him?
He's concerned about how many trainees are failing the swim test. Almost a third of last month's class didn't pass.
No wonder he wants extra practice sessions on weekends.

L7223.text: How many classes can I miss before it counts against me?
If you're absent more than fifteen percent of the course, you have to take the whole course over.
Then I can't afford any more sick days this month.

L7224.text: Another candy wrapper on the floor in the hallway! Who does this?
I don't know, but there's a trash can every ten steps along this corridor.
Exactly. Nobody can say they had to carry it far.

L7225.text: Did you read the new rule at the dining facility about leaving trays on the tables?
Yes. Whoever does it can be told to wipe down every table in the building after lunch.
That seems fair. Maybe people will finally stack their trays.

L7226.text: Which of our teams came home with the first-place trophy from the regional contest?
Not the band, which took third, and not the drill team, which finished second. The winners were the ones who made the judges ask for seconds.
Ha! I should have guessed. Their chili is famous.

L7227.text: Did you hear what the visiting general said about the graduating class?
Yes. He told the commandant they were polite, sharp and well prepared, and that he'd be glad to have them in his unit.
That's a great compliment. They practiced for weeks.

L7228.text: What was the colonel's talk about this morning? I missed it.
Mostly dates. Family day is on the fourth, the parade is in May, and inspection week begins in June.
Then I'd better write those down before I forget.

L7229.text: The captain just announced that final exams start Monday and graduation rehearsal is next Thursday.
Already? It feels like we only just arrived.
Eleven weeks went by fast. Soon we'll all be heading to our new units.

L7230.text: Every year our parents arranged the family trip, but this time they want us to handle everything.
Fine by me. I'll look at flights if you look at hotels.
Deal. Mom and Dad only have to show up at the airport.

L7231.text: How did your parents react when you said you'd plan the reunion yourself?
They weren't thrilled. Dad kept saying it's a lot of work, but in the end they agreed to let me try.
That sounds like a fair compromise.

L7232.text: Have you ever organized a big event before?
Last spring I planned my uncle's retirement party for eighty guests, including the music and the food.
Then a reunion should be easy for you.

L7233.text: How much money do we have for the trip?
Our two families saved seven thousand dollars altogether, and we agreed to split it evenly.
Good. Then we can start looking at prices.

L7234.text: When we were kids, a week at the lake cost our parents about two hundred dollars.
These days a week at the same lake costs five times that.
And we thought two hundred was a fortune back then.

L7235.text: Do you still have that old blue tent from our camping trips?
Of course. I put it up in the backyard every June, and the kids refuse to sleep anywhere else.
Then I'd better borrow it for the weekend.

L7236.text: Our family has four people, and your family has three.
Don't forget my mother. She's coming too, as long as she gets a seat on the plane.
Then I'd better look for a van with plenty of room.

L7237.text: Once we get to the national park in Colorado, what would you like to do?
I'd love to spend whole days walking the mountain trails with a backpack and a camera.
I'd rather rent a boat, but I'll gladly come along.

L7238.text: The unit's holiday party budget is five thousand dollars, isn't it?
Yes, and the hall rental alone will cost twenty-two hundred.
Then let's see what the food and music will add up to.

L7239.text: This will be our fifteenth summer at the lake with your family.
Fifteen years! We started when the kids were babies.
And now they're teenagers who complain that it's boring.

L7240.text: I called you three times last night. Where were you?
At my brother's. By the way, I still have the jacket you lent me back in college.
Keep it. You've been borrowing my things since we shared a dorm room.

L7241.text: Your nephew just hit the winning shot again. Where does he get that talent?
He takes after his dad. Sergeant Webb was the star of his unit's team for years.

L7242.text: The electrician fixed the hallway lights in under an hour, but she had to order a new switch for the stairwell.

L7243.text: Our weather station sits so high on the ridge that supplies arrive only by whirlybird, once a week.

L7244.text: Does your brother still work for the shipping company downtown?
He did until March. Now he's a flight mechanic at the base.

L7245.text: What's that sound? It's coming from the hallway.
Sounds like the alarm is going off. Somebody must have pushed the wrong button.

L7246.text: When our mechanics order a micrometer, they care less about its size or price and more about its precision.

L7247.text: I'm tired of eating the same sandwiches at the dining facility; let's order a pizza instead.

L7248.text: Is it really October already? The leaves on the parade field are just starting to change.
Yes, and by the end of the month they'll all be on the ground.

L7249.text: Is there any sugar left for the coffee?
Hardly any. I used most of it in the cookies this morning.

L7250.text: Pickleball has become very popular on base lately, and the courts behind the gym are full every evening.

L7251.text: When Corporal Reyes read the letter about his promotion, he cried like a baby, though he was smiling the whole time.

L7252.text: A toddler can't cook, get dressed or cross the street alone, so an adult has to stay close by at all times.

L7253.text: My handheld radio is dead again. Do you have a spare battery?
Check the supply cage. They keep a box of them next to the flashlights.

L7254.text: The water in the Great Salt Lake is so salty that visitors can lie back and read a newspaper without sinking.

L7255.text: Why is Sergeant Amato so grumpy this morning?
She skipped dinner and breakfast, and she keeps grumbling that she could eat a horse.

L7256.text: Private Ito's barracks is only a stone's throw from the chow hall, so he is first in line every morning.

L7257.text: Pack plenty of sunscreen for the beach exercise; without it, you'll be as red as a lobster by noon.

L7258.text: I got this jacket for fifteen dollars at the thrift shop, and honestly, it was a real steal.

L7259.text: Are you coming to the movie after chow tonight?
Not tonight. I'd rather take a long walk around the track to work off dinner.

L7260.text: I can't read the first line of your report. What happened?
I made a mistake and crossed it out, but I didn't have a clean sheet to start over.

L7261.text: Where's Airman Pierce? She missed morning formation.
She's at the dental clinic. A sharp pain in a back tooth kept her up all night.

L7262.text: Did the general say anything to you after the ceremony?
Not a word. He just smiled and gave me a little wave as his car went by.

L7263.text: I can do the inspection on the ninth, the twelfth or the twentieth. Which suits you?
I'm at a conference until the tenth, and the twentieth is my daughter's recital.

L7264.text: Your dog seems to tire easily lately. Is he okay?
The vet says his heart is weak, so he can't run the way he used to.

L7265.text: The whole squadron has been looking forward to the long weekend for weeks, so everybody is cheerful today.

L7266.text: The fog was so thick last night that Sergeant Bell could barely see the hood of his own truck.

L7267.text: The tank is almost empty. Should I put the whole can of fuel in at once?
No. Pour it a little at a time, or it will spill all over the engine.

L7268.text: How much are those two shirts on the rack by the door?
They're fifteen dollars each, but the second one is half price today.
In that case I'll take both of them.

L7269.text: Are you going to Lieutenant Mills's retirement party on Saturday?
I wouldn't miss it. I'm even bringing my wife and a homemade cake.

L7270.text: The next town is sixty kilometers away, and the convoy averages thirty kilometers an hour on this road.

L7271.text: After the twelve-mile road march, Private Dale was so worn out that he fell asleep on the bus before it left.

L7272.text: Who decides which driver gets which truck each morning?
Staff Sergeant Moreno does. She plans every trip on the big board in the dispatch office.

L7273.text: I heard Sergeant Ortiz's wife went to the hospital on Tuesday night.
She did. Their son was born early Wednesday morning, and both of them are doing fine.

L7274.text: Why are those teenagers running up and down the bleachers with trays?
The stadium hired them. They carry hot dogs and cold sodas to the fans in their seats.

L7275.text: Corporal Fisk's drawers are full of old coins from a dozen countries, and he trades them at the hobby shop every Saturday.

L7276.text: Does Captain Boyd ever take his wife out to restaurants?
Rarely. He'd much rather cook for her on the patio than wait for a table anywhere.

L7277.text: Specialist Burns dropped a heavy toolbox on his toes this morning, and now he can hardly get his boot on.

L7278.text: Why did the convoy stop at the overpass?
The sky ahead turned nearly black and the wind kicked up dust, so the lead driver didn't want to drive into a storm.

L7279.text: Did the search team find the two hikers?
Yes, near the river. They had wandered off the marked trail and couldn't find their way back.

L7280.text: Since we installed double-pane windows, the house stays warm in January, and our heating bill dropped by a third.

L7281.text: How did Staff Sergeant Cole's food truck do this summer?
Great. After paying for everything, he still put eleven thousand dollars in the bank.

L7282.text: Where was Lieutenant Gomez sitting during the briefing?
In the row in front of mine, so all I could see was the back of his head.

L7283.text: Even though it was below freezing, Sergeant Ames left his heavy jacket in his locker and walked to the gate in his shirt.

L7284.text: At the airport, Master Sergeant Hill realized his passport had expired, so he couldn't board the flight to Germany.

L7285.text: Master Sergeant Obi has composed more than thirty marches for the base band, and several are played at ceremonies.

L7286.text: The dining facility posts its menu daily, but the main dishes change only weekly, so don't expect much variety.

L7287.text: What can I get you, Colonel? Tonight's special is pork chops with rice.
I'll have the chops, please, well done.

L7288.text: Our pilots must get permission before flying over the lake, because the airspace above it belongs to Canada.

L7289.text: Gas prices climbed all through the summer, but after the refinery reopened last week, they dropped back to where they were in May.

L7290.text: Where's Airman Park? His mother called twice.
Out in the garage with his head under the hood. There are engine parts all over the driveway.

L7291.text: The party store fills the balloons with helium, which is lighter than air, so they float up to the ceiling.

L7292.text: How bad was the storm last night on the north side of the base?
Terrible. Roofs were torn off, trees came down on two cars, and the power was out until noon.

L7293.text: Whose umbrella is this one by the door?
It belongs to the new captain. She forgot it after the staff meeting.

L7294.text: Why are you standing in line at the licensing office on your day off?
My driver's license ran out last month, and the late fee goes up every week I wait.

L7295.text: Even when the alarm sounded during his briefing, Captain Stone didn't miss a beat and led everyone outside in single file.

L7296.text: A farmer discovered the cave in nineteen thirty-one while he was searching the hills for a lost cow.

L7297.text: Attendance at tomorrow's safety briefing is mandatory for every driver, and nobody will be excused except for medical reasons.

L7298.text: Private Cho complains that his tent leaks, the heater is broken, and he hasn't had a hot meal in days.

L7299.text: Are you going to see your brother in Alaska next year?
I'd love to, but only if my leave gets approved. Nothing is certain yet.

L7300.text: It's already dark at five. When did that happen?
Every year in November. The daylight keeps shrinking until the shortest day in December.

L7301.text: Do you feel like going bowling tonight?
Honestly, I'd rather catch the new movie at the base theater.

L7302.text: Private Hayes has an appointment with the barber at noon, so he'll be back after lunch.

L7303.text: Apart from the rain on Sunday, the soldiers enjoyed their weekend at the lake.

L7304.text: The mayor announced that he won't run again and will leave office when his term ends in May.

L7305.text: Each hiker who reaches the summit adds one more rock to the pile beside the trail marker.

L7306.text: How was the safety lecture this afternoon?
Two hours of slides with no breaks. I nearly fell asleep.

L7307.text: Sergeant Burke will be heading out shortly, so if you need his signature, get it now.

L7308.text: Is Corporal Shaw coming to the farewell party on Friday?
He was thinking about it, but he finally decided to skip it.

L7309.text: Lieutenant Cho considered taking the boat out on Saturday, but the strong wind kept her ashore.

L7310.text: The parade practice has stopped because of the thunderstorm, but it will resume at five o'clock.

L7311.text: The yellow sign by the bridge says 'Caution: Ice on Road' from November to March.

L7312.text: Before the vet examines the angry dog, his assistant puts a muzzle on it so nobody gets bitten.

L7313.text: How much rope do we have left on the spool?
Maybe nine feet, not much more than that.

L7314.text: Kevin was afraid to sing in the talent show because he thought his sister would make fun of him.

L7315.text: When the window broke, Specialist Ford took the blame, even though his roommate had thrown the ball.

L7316.text: The tailor took up my new dress pants two inches because they were dragging on the floor.

L7317.text: Please shut the gate behind you when you leave, or the horses will wander onto the road.

L7318.text: At the commissary, a young man will bag your groceries and help you carry them to your car.

L7319.text: How is Sergeant Cruz doing after his knee surgery?
The doctors expect him to be back on his feet in a few weeks.

L7320.text: Did you hear that your transfer to Germany was approved?
Yes, and what a relief; I'd been worrying about it for months.

L7321.text: In the valley, good farmland was scarce, so many young families moved west to find their own.

L7322.text: What did you and your old roommate talk about all evening?
Mostly the good old days at the academy and the friends we've lost touch with.

L7323.text: The tall one by the door, wearing a navy cap and a coat to match.

L7324.text: How do you like the iced tea I made?
It's good, but it could use a little more sugar.

L7325.text: The heat was so intense that one of the runners passed out and had to be carried to the medical tent.

L7326.text: The staff meeting has been pushed back to three o'clock because the colonel's flight is late.

L7327.text: When does your cousin arrive from Texas?
Sometime the month after Thanksgiving, just in time for the holidays.

L7328.text: How much did you pay for that used car?
Way too much. The salesman lied about the miles, and the engine died a week later.

L7329.text: Lieutenant Gomez was given a medal for organizing the rescue during the flood last spring.

L7330.text: Why do you always go to the lake after work?
The quiet water helps me relax after a stressful day.

L7331.text: Before he became a teacher, Mr. Dunn served one term as president of the city council.

L7332.text: How old was your daughter when you moved to Japan?
Let's see, she's sixteen now, and we moved four years ago.

L7409.text: The new recruits were so excited. Captain Reyes opened the control tower to them for an hour this afternoon.
Lucky them. Last year she turned away the whole class because of a security alert.

L7410.text: Specialist Ortiz turned down my invitation to the cookout because she still has a report to finish.

L7411.text: Is the repair crew still working in the training center?
They are, but Sergeant Ibe wants them gone by noon, because the general's party arrives at one.

L7412.text: How many manuals do you bring to the engine course now? It used to be six.
They cut the list in half this term.

L7413.text: Stop by my desk and look at the duty roster draft. I think Specialist Kerr is scheduled twice on Saturday.
Thanks for catching that. I'll go through it right now.

L7414.text: Staff Sergeant Pike can't join the morning run for three weeks, because the cast on his ankle has to stay on.

L7415.text: Did you read the notice? Starting Monday, nobody may park behind the dining facility.
That's going to cause trouble. Where will the cooks leave their cars?

L7416.text: Sergeant Alvarez slipped into the briefing a few minutes late and quietly took a seat near the door.

L7417.text: Staff Sergeant Gill never reads the front page; he turns straight to the box scores and the league standings.

L7418.text: Before leaving on his weekend trip, Corporal Davis stopped at the credit union to cash his paycheck.

L7419.text: Since the kitchen was closed, Airman Fontaine ate cold cuts and cheese on rye bread at her desk.

L7420.text: I'm ordering a flight suit for the new pilot, so how tall is he?
Around six foot four, though he's pretty thin.

L7421.text: Major Ito planned to drive to the coast at dawn, but the fog was so thick that he decided to wait.

L7422.text: The Costa twins look so much alike that even their squad leader says he can't tell them apart.

L7423.text: Did your truck make that grinding noise on the way here?
Not while I was driving. I only heard it after I parked and switched off the engine.

L7424.text: The new fuel tanks are made of an alloy, which makes them strong but much lighter than steel.

L7425.text: Did the guard at the border keep your passport?
No. He went through it page by page, then handed it back without stamping anything.

L7426.text: The shuttle from the airfield was due at half past six, but it pulled in twenty minutes late.

L7427.text: Specialist Coles noticed water seeping out of the pipe under the sink and set a bucket beneath it.
